Methods of finding square roots are ways to calculate the main square root of a number. Arithmetically, it means finding a number that, when multiplied by itself, equals the given number. Algebraically, it means solving the equation x² = s, where s is the given number. Geometrically, it means finding the length of a square's side when you know its area. Every real number has two square roots, but the principal root is always non-negative. Most of these roots are irrational numbers, meaning they have endless, non-repeating decimals. Thus, their exact values can only be approximated. Even for perfect square integers, exact results might require many steps to find. A continued fraction can represent a square root of a rational number, often showing a repeating pattern. This is similar to how some rational numbers have repeating decimals. Common methods involve starting with a guess and refining it. One popular method is Newton's method, which uses derivatives from calculus. Other methods, like paper-and-pencil synthetic division, don't need a starting guess. Sometimes, you need the integer square root, which is the nearest integer. This might need a different approach. The choice of method depends on accuracy needed, effort, and available tools. Methods can be for mental math, paper and pencil, or computer programs. Finding square roots has a long history, starting with ancient Babylonians. Modern methods developed after the adoption of Arabic numerals in Europe. Today, most computing devices have fast and accurate square root functions.

Thomas Hitzlsperger, born on April 5, 1982, is a German director of football and former soccer player who played as a midfielder. Since February 2019, he has been the head of sports at VFB Stuttgart. As a player, he started his career with Aston Villa in England (with a short loan to Chesterfield), then returned to Germany to play for Stuttgart, where he won the Bundesliga in 2007. In 2010, he joined Italian side Lazio before moving back to England to play for West Ham United the same year. He also had short stints with Wolfsburg and Everton. Hitzlsperger played for the German national team, earning 52 caps and participating in the 2006 World Cup and Euro 2008. Due to injuries, he retired from soccer in September 2013. After retiring, he came out as gay, becoming one of the most prominent male soccer players to do so.

Antonia Margaret Caroline Fraser, born on August 27, 1932, is a British author. She writes history books, novels, biographies, and detective stories. She is the wife of Harold Pinter, who won the 2005 Nobel Prize in Literature. Before his death in 2008, she was also known as Lady Antonia Pinter.

The head of the government in the Republic of Turkey from 1920 to 2018 was called the prime minister. In Turkish, this is "Türkiye Cumhuriyeti başbakanı." The prime minister led a group of different political parties in the Turkish parliament and also led the government team. In telecommunications networks, a node is a point where information is redistributed or a place where communication starts or ends. The definition of a node can vary depending on the network and layer of protocol. A physical network node is an electronic device connected to a network that can create, receive, or send information. Passive distribution points like distribution frames or patch panels are not considered nodes.

Hypothyroidism, or underactive thyroid, is a condition where the thyroid gland doesn't make enough thyroid hormone. This can cause symptoms like feeling cold, tiredness, constipation, slow heart rate, depression, and weight gain. Sometimes, there may be swelling in the front part of the neck due to a goiter. Untreated hypothyroidism during pregnancy can affect the baby's growth and intellectual development. The most common cause worldwide is too little iodine in the diet. In areas with enough iodine, Hashimoto's thyroiditis is the most common cause. Other causes include previous radioiodine treatment, injuries to certain parts of the brain, some medicines, a lack of a working thyroid at birth, or past thyroid surgery. To confirm hypothyroidism, doctors check thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and thyroxine levels in the blood. Treating hypothyroidism involves taking thyroid hormone, usually levothyroxine. Doctors adjust the dose based on symptoms and hormone levels. Taking thyroid medication during pregnancy is safe. About one billion people worldwide don't get enough iodine in their diet. In the U.S., hypothyroidism affects about 0.3% to 0.4% of people. Subclinical hypothyroidism, a milder form, affects about 4.3% to 8.5% of people. More women than men get hypothyroidism, and it's more common in older people. Dogs, cats, and horses can also get hypothyroidism, though less frequently. The word "hypothyroidism" comes from the Greek words "hypo-" meaning reduced, "thyreos" for shield, and "eidos" for form.

Jens Spahn, born on May 16, 1980, is a German politician. He is the federal minister of health in the fourth Merkel cabinet. He is a member of the lower house of the German parliament, the Bundestag, for Steinfurt I – Borken I. He is part of the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) of Germany, which works with the Social Democratic Party (SPD) to run the government. Spahn joined the CDU in 2002 when he was 22 years old and was the youngest member of the CDU in the Bundestag. He has served in the 15th, 16th, and 17th Bundestags. He is one of the main people who support changing the pension system in Germany. He is part of the health committee of the 17th Bundestag and leads a group that talks about health and health policies. He also speaks for the CDU/CSU health group in the Bundestag. In 2018, when Angela Merkel said she would not run again for the CDU leadership, Spahn wanted to be her replacement. He did not win in the first vote. In February 2020, when Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer decided to step down, Spahn said he would not try to be the leader but would support Armin Laschet instead.
Barnas is a commune in Ardèche, which is in the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region of southern France. The people who live there are called Barnassiens or Barnassiennes.

Jesse & Joy is a Mexican pop duo formed in 2005. Jesse, born on December 31, 1982, and Joy, born on June 20, 1986, are brother and sister. They were born in Mexico City. Jesse and Joy have made four studio albums, one live album, and one EP for Warner Music Latin. They have toured internationally. Ghost Whisperer is an American TV show about supernatural things. It was on CBS from September 23, 2005, to May 21, 2010. The show tells the story of Melinda Gordon, played by Jennifer Love Hewitt. She can see and talk to ghosts. Melinda tries to live a normal life, running an antique store and being married. She helps ghosts solve their problems and move on to another world. Her job is hard and sometimes people don't believe in her abilities. The ghosts she encounters are sometimes mysterious or scary, and Melinda has to find clues to help them. The show was made by John Gray and produced by Sander/Moses Productions and Jennifer Love Hewitt, working with ABC Studios and CBS Television Studios. CBS stopped the show on May 18, 2010, after five seasons.

Carthage is a village in the town of Wilna, in Jefferson County, New York, United States. In 2010, it had 3,747 people. The village is named after the ancient city of Carthage in Tunisia. Carthage is located at the southern part of Wilna town and is east of Watertown.

Leendert "Leen" Verbeek, born on March 5, 1954, is a Dutch politician. He has been the king's commissioner of Flevoland since 2008. Verbeek is a member of the Labour Party (PvDA). Before this, he was the mayor of Purmerend from 2003 to 2008. Verbeek grew up in Eindhoven. He attended MULO (which is like VMBO) and spent a year in high school in the United States. He then studied at the Academy for Educational Labour in Baarn. Later, he worked as a youth worker in Leiden. After working for ten years, Verbeek started his political career. He became an alderman in Houten from 1989 to 1996. Seven years later, in 2003, he became the mayor of Purmerend. Between his roles, he was the director of a company he created. In December 2007, Verbeek and Rob van Gijzel ran for mayor of Eindhoven. A vote was held, but they did not get enough votes, so van Gijzel became mayor instead. In November 2008, Verbeek left his job as mayor of Purmerend to become the king's commissioner for Flevoland.

Dawlish is a seaside town in Teignbridge, Devon, near Exeter and Torquay. In 2018, it had about 16,000 people. More houses are being built there, especially in the north and east. Dawlish used to be a small fishing place. In the 18th century, it grew into a popular seaside town. Its neighbor, Teignmouth, also became well-known as a seaside resort in the 19th century.

Wilhelm Keitel was born on September 22, 1882, and died on October 16, 1946. He was a German field marshal and a war criminal during World War II. Keitel led the High Command of the Armed Forces (OKW) during the war. He signed many orders that caused very brutal and illegal actions during the war. Keitel started his career in the military when he was appointed as the head of the armed forces office at the Reich Ministry of War in 1935. In 1938, when Hitler took control of the Wehrmacht, he replaced the ministry with the OKW, making Keitel its chief. His colleagues in the military didn't like him because he always agreed with Hitler. After the war, Keitel was tried by the International Military Tribunal in Nuremberg. He was found guilty of crimes against humanity, crimes against peace, criminal conspiracy, and war crimes. Keitel was sentenced to death and was executed by hanging in 1946.

Mária Pozsonec was a Slovenian politician who was Hungarian. She was born on January 16, 1940, in Dolga Vas, near Lendava, which was then in the Drava Banovina of Yugoslavia (now in Slovenia). She came from Hungarian parents. Pozsonec went to high school in Subotica, Serbia, and studied teaching at the University of Maribor in Slovenia. She worked as a teacher in Prekmurje, her home region. In the 1980s, she became an activist for the Hungarian minority in Slovenia. In April 1990, she was elected to the National Assembly as the representative of the Hungarian national community. She was re-elected four times, in 1992, 1996, 2000, and 2004. In 2008, she lost her seat to László Göncz. Pozsonec also served as the vice-mayor of Lendava from November 2006 to November 2011. She passed away on April 3, 2017, at the age of 77.

Magnús Eiríksson was born on June 22, 1806, in Skinnalón, in Norður-Þingeyjarsýsla, Iceland, and died on July 3, 1881, in Copenhagen, Denmark. He was an Icelandic theologian. He lived during the same time as Søren Aabye Kierkegaard and Hans Lassen Martensen, who also worked in Copenhagen. Eiríksson often criticized the church's teachings, especially those about the Trinity and Christ being divine. In his later work, he emphasized that God is one, and Jesus led people as a prophet and teacher. Because of his views, some people called him a "pioneer" or "precursor" to the Unitarian movement in Denmark.

The heat index (HI) combines air temperature and humidity to show how hot it feels in the shade. It's also called "felt air temperature," "apparent temperature," "real feel," or "feels like." For example, at 70% humidity, the heat index can be higher. The human body cools itself by sweating. Sweat evaporates and takes heat away from the body. But high humidity makes sweat evaporate slower. This means the body gets less cool, and feels hotter. How hot it feels is personal. People may feel it differently because of their body shape, how much they drink, being pregnant, going through menopause, or taking certain medicines. Scientists measure this based on how people say they feel at different temperatures and humidities. The heat index is based on shady areas. In sunny areas, the temperature can feel much hotter than the heat index suggests. For people who are active or exercising, the heat index might not show how hot they actually feel.

David, in the Hebrew Bible, was the third king of the united kingdom of Israel and Judah, succeeding Ish-bosheth. According to the Books of Samuel, David started as a young shepherd and gained fame as a musician. He later killed the Philistine champion Goliath, became Saul's favorite, and a close friend to Saul's son Jonathan. Saul, fearing David might take his throne, turned against him. After Saul and Jonathan died in battle, David was made king. As king, he conquered Jerusalem, brought the Ark of the Covenant to the city, and continued Saul's kingdom. During his rule, David had an affair with Bathsheba, leading to the death of her husband, Uriah. David's son Absalom rebelled against him. David fled Jerusalem but returned after Absalom's death to rule. God refused David the chance to build the temple because he had caused much bloodshed. Before he died, David chose Solomon as his successor. In prophetic literature, David is seen as an ideal king and the ancestor of a future messiah. Many psalms are attributed to him. Historians agree David likely existed around 1000 BCE, with little certainty about his life. The Tel Dan stele, an ancient inscription, mentions "House of David." David is widely discussed in Jewish traditions and is mentioned in the New Testament. Early Christians saw Jesus as a descendant of David. The Quran also describes David as a major prophet, and he appears in Islamic traditions. David's character has inspired art and literature for centuries.

Tyrus Raymond Cobb, nicknamed the Georgia Peach, was an American baseball player. He was born in Narrows, Georgia, and played for the Detroit Tigers for 22 seasons, becoming the team's player-manager for the last six. He ended his career with the Philadelphia Athletics. Cobb received the most votes on the first Baseball Hall of Fame ballot in 1936, with 98.2% of the votes. In 1999, he was ranked third on a list of the 100 greatest baseball players. He set 90 MLB records during his career. Cobb had the highest career batting average and most career batting titles. He also held many other records, including the most career hits, runs, and games played. His legacy includes a college scholarship fund for Georgia residents, supported by his investments in Coca-Cola and General Motors. Despite this, Cobb faced allegations of racism and violence, mostly from biographies written after his death. Cobb was known for conflicts but supported black players joining the major leagues and was a philanthropist.

Liu Shaoqi, born on November 24, 1898, and died on November 12, 1969, was a Chinese leader. He was an important politician and thinker. From 1954 to 1959, he was the chairman of the NPC Standing Committee. From 1956 to 1966, he was the first vice chairman of the Communist Party of China. Liu was also the President of the People's Republic of China from 1959 to 1968. During this time, he worked on rebuilding the Chinese economy. For 15 years, Liu was one of the most powerful people in China, after Mao Zedong and Zhou Enlai. Mao originally wanted Liu to take his place. However, in the early 1960s, Liu did not agree with Mao. From 1966, Mao started criticizing and removing Liu. Liu stopped appearing in public in 1968. Mao called Liu the "commander of China's bourgeoisie headquarters," saying Liu was the main "capitalist-roader" and a traitor to the revolution. Liu died because of harsh treatment during the Cultural Revolution. However, in 1980, Deng Xiaoping's government said Liu was rehabilitated. A special memorial service was held for him.

The Oriental Library is Japan's largest library for Asian studies and one of the world's five largest. It is in Tokyo. This library also works as a research center focused on Asian history and culture. It has helped develop Asian studies by collecting books and other materials and publishing research by Japanese scholars. Now, it has around 950,000 books, organized using Asian, Western, and Japanese languages.

Elizabeth Welter Wilson lived from April 4, 1921, to May 9, 2015. She was an American actress who acted for almost 70 years. She played important roles in movies and on TV. Wilson was honored by being added to the American Theater Hall of Fame in 2006.
George Shaw, born on December 10, 1751, and died on July 22, 1813, was an English botanist and zoologist.

The ruby slippers are special shoes worn by Dorothy in the 1939 movie "The Wizard of Oz," starring Judy Garland. They are very valuable because they are famous. Several pairs were made for the film, but the exact number is unknown. Five pairs have survived. One pair was stolen from a museum in 2005 and was found again in 2018. In the original book, Dorothy wore silver shoes, but they were changed to red for the movie. This was done to make the shoes look better using new technology called technicolor. Film writer Noel Langley suggested this idea.

The Wilmington Insurrection of 1898, also known as the Wilmington Massacre or the Wilmington Coup, happened in Wilmington, North Carolina, on November 10, 1898. This event is seen as a key moment in post-Reconstruction North Carolina politics. It led to stricter racial segregation and limited African American voting rights in the South, a trend that began after Mississippi's new constitution in 1890, which made it harder for people to vote. Laura Edwards wrote in "Democracy Betrayed" (2000) that what happened in Wilmington proved that "whiteness" was more important than the legal rights African Americans had under the Fourteenth Amendment. Initially, local white newspapers called the event a race riot caused by black people. However, as more facts came out, people started seeing it as a "coup d'état," meaning a group of white supremacists violently took over the government. Multiple reasons led to this. Some say it was the only such incident in American history, where elected officials were removed by a mob. The event was the result of a plan by white southern Democrats. They led a group of 2,000 white men to take over the city government. They expelled black and white political leaders, destroyed black citizens' property and businesses, including the city's only black newspaper, and killed between 60 and more than 300 people.

Chemical stability, when used in chemistry, means that a chemical system is in its lowest energy state or in chemical equilibrium with its environment. This equilibrium can be dynamic, with atoms or molecules changing forms, but the overall number in a particular form stays the same. This stability will last indefinitely unless the system changes. A chemical system can include changes in the phase of matter or a series of chemical reactions. If changing from state A to state B increases Gibbs energy, then state A is more thermodynamically stable than state B.

Sara Shahi, born on January 10, 1980, is an actress of Iranian and Spanish ancestry. She played Carmen in "The L Word" in 2008, Kate Reed in "Fairly Legal" from 2011 to 2012, and Sameen Shaw in "Person of Interest." She also starred as Detective Dani Reese in "Life" and had a supporting role in "Alias." In 2018, she was in "Reverie." In 2019, she appeared in a few episodes of "City on a Hill" on Showtime and seven episodes of "The Rookie" as Jessica Russo.

Vikram Chatterjee is a Bengali film actor. He first appeared in a small role in Mainak Bhowmik's 2012 movie "Bedroom" and quickly gained attention. In the same year, he played the main role in "Elar Char Adhyay," based on Rabindranath Tagore's novel "Char Adhyay." Soon after, he acted in "Ami Aar Amar Girlfriends" and "Hoichoi." His career took a big step forward in 2013 with a realistic movie "Mistake," directed by S.K. Bangalore. This movie was well-received and helped him become a leading actor in Bengali films. He is famous for his role in "Ichchenodi," where he played the main character Anurag, and he has many fans because of the show's success. Vikram also starred in the movie "Shaheb Bibi Golaam," where his performance of the character Zico was highly praised. In 2013, he took part in the reality show "Bigg Boss Bangali" as a contestant. His recent performances in "Khoj," directed by Arko Ganguly, and "Meghnad Badh Rahasya," directed by Anik Datta, have been well-received by both critics and audiences.

Como, an Italian football club founded in 1907, is based in Como, Lombardy. The team's color is royal blue. Como played in Serie A in 2002-03. Then, they lost two consecutive promotions, ending up in Serie C2 by 2005. Due to financial issues, they were even banned from Italian professional football. Later, they joined Serie D, the top level for non-professional football, in 2007-08 and won promotion back to Serie C2. In 2016, Como went bankrupt again. A new company restarted the club in 2017 and they played in Serie D until 2018.

Ronald Johnson was born on October 17, 1947, and died on November 10, 2018. He was an American football running back. Johnson played college football at the University of Michigan from 1966 to 1968. In 1967, he set a Michigan school record by running for 270 yards in a single game. In 1968, he was the first African-American to be the captain of a Michigan football team. He set an NCAA record by rushing for 347 yards in one game and broke Big Ten conference records with 92 points scored and 1,017 rushing yards in seven conference games. He also set Michigan records with 2,524 career rushing yards, 19 rushing touchdowns in a season, and 139.1 rushing yards per game in 1968. Johnson played in the National Football League (NFL) for seven seasons from 1969 to 1975. He was the first New York Giants player to rush for 1,000 yards in a season, doing so in 1970 and 1972. He also led the NFL in rushing attempts in both 1970 and 1972. Johnson retired as a player in 1976, was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 1992, and became the chairman of the National Football Foundation in 2006. He was diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease in 2008 and passed away in 2018. Johnson's brother, Alex Johnson, was the 1970 American League batting champion.

The Ron, Ronic, and Ron–fyer languages belong to group A.4 of the West Chadic branch of the Afro-Asiatic language family. They are spoken in Plateau State, North-Central Nigeria. These languages have been greatly affected by the Tarok language.

Montgomery County is in the central part of Missouri. As of 2010, it had 12, 236 people. The county seat is Montgomery City. It was named after Richard Montgomery, who died in 1775 during the American Revolutionary War while trying to capture Quebec City in Canada. The county has a winery branch in New Florence and is part of the Missouri Rhineland. It is roughly between Columbia and St. Louis.

Eric Peter Brewer, born on April 17, 1979, is a former professional ice hockey defenceman. He played in the NHL for 16 seasons, ending his career with the Toronto Maple Leafs. Brewer was an NHL all-star and won an Olympic gold medal. Brewer began his career as a junior ice hockey player, being named to the WHL West Second All-Star Team. He was also on the WHL Western Conference roster for the 1998 all-star game but missed it due to an injury. Selected in the 1997 NHL draft, he was chosen fifth overall by the New York Islanders. Over his 16-year NHL career, Brewer played for the Islanders, Edmonton Oilers, St. Louis Blues, Tampa Bay Lightning, Anaheim Ducks, and Toronto Maple Leafs. He was the captain of the Blues for two years. Brewer also played for the Prince George Cougars in the WHL and the Lowell Lock Monsters in the AHL. In 1999, he was chosen for the Prince George Cougars' all-time team. Brewer represented Canada in eight international events, winning three ice hockey world championship gold medals and one World Cup of Hockey gold medal. He won his Olympic gold medal at the 2002 Winter Olympics. For this, he was inducted into the BC Sports Hall of Fame with his teammates in 2003.

The Creation Museum is in Petersburg, Kentucky, USA. It is run by Answers in Genesis (AIG), a Christian organization. The museum teaches a young Earth creationist view, based on a literal reading of the Bible. It opened on May 28, 2007, and cost 27 million dollars, raised by private donations. The museum includes a special effects theater, a planetarium, a dinosaur skeleton, and an insect collection. As AIG’s headquarters, it has about 300 employees. Workers must sign a faith statement agreeing with AIG’s beliefs. The museum shows humans and dinosaurs living together and claims the Earth is about 6,000 years old, opposing evolution. Scientists and educators criticize the museum for incorrect science and worry it might harm science education. Some say it harms Christianity and believers by rejecting scientific agreement. Many Americans believe in young Earth creationism, making the museum popular. It is controversial and has been discussed by museum experts and culture watchers. Some museum study scholars, like Gretchen Jennings, say creationist exhibits don’t connect well with modern knowledge and don’t meet museum standards.

Alingsås VBK is a volleyball club in Alingsås, Sweden. It was founded on June 1, 1961. The club joined the Swedish Volleyball Federation on December 19, 1961. Alingsås VBK won the Swedish women's national championship in 1971.

"Koi... Mil Gaya" is a 2003 Indian Hindi science fiction movie. It was directed by Rakesh Roshan and is the first film in the Krrish series. The movie came out on August 8, 2003, with main actor Hrithik Roshan and supporting actresses Preity Zinta and Rekha in it. "Koi... Mil Gaya" won a National Film Award for best film on social issues. It was also shown at the Jerusalem Film Festival and Natfilm Festival in Denmark. The film got awards like Best Picture, Best Director (Rakesh Roshan), and Best Actor (Hrithik Roshan) from big movie award ceremonies, such as Filmfare Awards, IIFA Awards, and Screen Awards. It led to two more movies in the Krrish series—Krrish and Krrish 3. The film also inspired a children's TV show called J Bole Toh Jadoo, which aired on Nickelodeon India. "Koi... Mil Gaya" has some similarities with the 1982 Hollywood movie E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial and the film The Alien by Satyajit Ray. However, director Roshan said it's not like an Indian version of E.T., as the story is more like The Alien, about an alien meeting a boy who has some intellectual challenges.

The Canary Islands, also called "the Canaries," are a Spanish group of islands and the southernmost part of Spain's autonomous regions, located in the Atlantic Ocean, west of Morocco. They are part of Macaronesia and are one of eight regions with special recognition of historical nationality by the Spanish government. The largest eight islands, from biggest to smallest, are Tenerife, Fuerteventura, Gran Canaria, Lanzarote, La Palma, La Gomera, El Hierro, and La Graciosa. There are also many smaller islands like Alegranza, Isla de Lobos, Monte Clara, Roque del Oeste, and Roque del Este. The Canary Islands have a subtropical climate, with warm summers and mild winters. They are a popular tourist destination, attracting over 12 million visitors each year, especially to Tenerife, Gran Canaria, Fuerteventura, and Lanzarote. The islands include important natural attractions such as Maspalomas in Gran Canaria and Teide National Park and Mount Teide, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Mount Teide is the third tallest volcano in the world, measured from its base on the ocean floor. The Canary Islands are the southernmost region of Spain and the largest and most populated archipelago of Macaronesia. Historically, they were seen as a bridge between Africa, North America, South America, and Europe. In 2019, the islands had a population of 2,153,389, with the largest concentrations in Tenerife (43%) and Gran Canaria (40%). The capital cities are shared between Santa Cruz de Tenerife and Las Palmas de Gran Canaria. Las Palmas de Gran Canaria has been the largest city since 1768, except for a brief period in the 1910s. Before 1927, Santa Cruz de Tenerife was the sole capital of the Canary Islands. In 1927, the province of the Canary Islands was split into two provinces. The autonomous community of the Canary Islands was established in 1982, with its capital shared between Santa Cruz de Tenerife and Las Palmas de Gran Canaria. San Cristóbal de La Laguna, the third largest city on Tenerife, is a World Heritage Site and home to the "Consejo Consultivo de Canarias," the supreme consultative body of the Canary Islands. The islands were a key stop for Spanish galleons on their way to the Americas during the time of the Spanish Empire.

yellowcake, also called urania, is a powder made from uranium. It comes from processing uranium ores after mining. Yellowcake is made when uranium is refined, but before it's turned into fuel or enriched. Different ores require different methods to make yellowcake. Usually, yellowcake is produced by breaking down and chemically treating uranium ore. It's a coarse powder that smells strong and doesn't dissolve in water. Yellowcake contains about 80% uranium oxide and melts at about 2880°C.

The Arctic National Wildlife Refuge (ANWR or Arctic Refuge) is in northeastern Alaska, United States. It covers a large area in the Alaska North Slope region. ANWR is the biggest national wildlife refuge in the country, slightly bigger than the Yukon Delta National Wildlife Refuge. It is run from offices in Fairbanks. The refuge has many kinds of plants and animals, including polar bears, grizzly bears, black bears, moose, caribou, wolves, eagles, lynx, wolverines, martens, beavers, and migratory birds. These animals depend on the refuge. Just across the border in Yukon, Canada, are two Canadian national parks, Ivavik and Vuntut.

The Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) is a group that represents music companies in the U.S. Its members are record labels and distributors who make, produce, and sell most of the legally sold music in the country. The RIAA has its main office in Washington, D.C. It was created in 1952. At first, its job was to handle copyright fees and issues, work with unions, and study the music industry and rules from the government. Early standards set by the RIAA included the equalization curve for recording, the format of stereophonic grooves, and the sizes of 33 1/3, 45, and 78 rpm records. Today, the RIAA's main tasks include spending over $6 million each year on U.S. lobbying since 2001. It also manages sound recordings collectively and certifies gold and platinum albums and singles in the U.S.

Deer Island is a small community in Columbia County, Oregon, United States. In 2010, it had 294 people living there. It is near Columbia City, to the north-northwest. Deer Island has a post office with the zip code 97054.

Origin of Symmetry" is the second album by the English rock band Muse. It came out on June 18, 2001, through Mushroom Records and Taste Media. The album's title and theme come from ideas in Michio Kaku's book "Hyperspace." The album did well in the UK, reaching third place on the UK Albums Chart and getting BPI Platinum status. Four singles were released: "Plug in Baby," "New Born," "Bliss," and "Hyper Music" and "Feeling Good.
Craig is a city in Plymouth County, Iowa, United States. It had 89 people living there in 2010. The town of Craig became a city in Plymouth County on April 26, 1911.

Beam bridges, also called stringer bridges, are simple structures supported by an abutment or pier at each end. They do not transfer moments, so they are known as "simply supported" bridges. The simplest beam bridge could be a log, a wood plank, or a stone placed across a stream. For modern infrastructure, they are usually built with steel or reinforced concrete, or a mix of both. The concrete can be reinforced, prestressed, or post-tensioned. Modern examples include girder, plate girder, and box girder bridges. These bridges can be built with many beams side by side with a deck on top or with main beams supporting a deck between them. The main beams can be -beams, trusses, or box girders, which can be half-through or braced to create a through bridge. Since no moments are transferred, these bridges cannot support horizontal forces like arch bridges. This has led to innovative designs such as lenticular trusses and bow string arches. Beam bridges can have multiple simply supported spans supported by piers, like the Feiyunjiang Bridge in China. Unlike truss bridges, beam bridges have no built-in support, so they rely solely on piers. The farther apart the supports are, the weaker the bridge becomes. Therefore, beam bridges usually don't span more than a certain distance. However, they can still be used to cross great distances by joining several beam bridges together, creating a continuous span.

Lupita Nyong'o, born on March 1, 1983, is a Kenyan-Mexican actress and author. She was born in Mexico City where her father, Peter Anyang' Nyong'o, was teaching. After living in Kenya from the age of one, she studied in the United States, earning a degree in film and theatre from Hampshire College. Nyong'o started her career as a production assistant. She acted in her first short film, "East River," in 2008 and later starred in the TV series "Shuga" from 2009 to 2012. In 2009, she also made a documentary called "In My Genes." After that, she studied acting at Yale. In 2013, she starred in "12 Years a Slave," where she played Patsey, and was praised for her performance. She won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress and became the first Kenyan and Mexican actress to win this award. Nyong'o made her Broadway debut in 2015 and was nominated for a Tony Award. She also voiced characters in "Star Wars" and "The Jungle Book." In 2018, she acted in "Black Panther" and in 2019 in "Us," both critically acclaimed films. She supports historic preservation and fights against sexual harassment and for women's and animal rights. In 2014, she was named the most beautiful woman by People. Nyong'o also wrote a children's book called "Sulwe" in 2019, which became a best-seller. She was nominated for an Emmy in 2019 for narrating a documentary series. In 2020, she was listed as one of Africa's 50 most powerful women by Forbes.

Carlo Caffarra was an Italian church leader. He served as the archbishop of Bologna from 2003 to 2015 and retired then. Before that, he was the president of the Pontifical John Paul II Institute for Studies on Marriage and Family from 1981 to 1995. He was also the archbishop of Ferrara-Comacchio from 1995 to 2003. Pope Benedict XVI made him a cardinal in 2006.

Rachel Marilyn Lloyd, born Laird on January 3, 1929, and passing away on September 19, 2018, was an American politician and businesswoman. She worked in the United States House of Representatives from 1975 to 1995.

Mallemort is a small town in southern France, in the Bouches-du-Rhône department. It is situated near the Durance River, below the Luberon mountain range. The town is away from the main highway, but it's close to Arles, Saint-Rémy, and Salon-de-Provence.

James Stephen Fossett, born on April 22, 1944, and died on September 3, 2007, was an American businessman. He was also a record-setting aviator and adventurer. Fossett flew solo around the world in both a balloon and a fixed-wing aircraft. He made his fortune in financial services and broke five world records for nonstop circumnavigation of the earth: as a solo long-distance balloonist, a sailor, and a solo fixed-wing aircraft pilot. He was a member of the Royal Geographical Society and the Explorers Club, setting over 100 records in different sports. At the time of his death, 60 of his records were still standing. He broke three out of seven absolute world records for fixed-wing aircraft with his Virgin Atlantic GlobalFlyer. In 2002, he received the Royal Aero Club Gold Medal. He was inducted into the National Aviation Hall of Fame in 2007. Fossett went missing on September 3, 2007, while flying a small aircraft in the desert between Nevada and California. Search efforts were unsuccessful, and he was declared legally dead in the following year. In September 2008, a hiker found Fossett's identification cards in the Sierra Nevada mountains, leading to the discovery of his plane's wreckage. Only two large bones, likely scattered by animals, were found near the crash site.

Charlie Countryman, originally called The Necessary Death of Charlie Countryman, is a 2013 American-Romanian romantic drama. Fredrik Bond directed it and wrote it. Shia LaBeouf, Evan Rachel Wood, and Mads Mikkelsen star in the film. The movie premiered at the 2013 Sundance Film Festival on January 21, 2013, and competed at the 63rd Berlin International Film Festival. It was released in the United States on November 15, 2013, and in the United Kingdom on October 31, 2014.
Termen is a town in the Brig district of Valais in Switzerland.

Happy Valley Shanghai is an amusement park in China. It is in Songjiang District, not far from downtown Shanghai. The park covers a large area. It opened on August 16, 2009. This is the fourth Happy Valley theme park.

In 2003, the Pacific hurricane season had no major hurricanes, which hadn't happened since 1977. That year, many tropical storms affected Mexico. The most notable ones were Hurricanes Ignacio and Marty, which caused 14 deaths and about $1 billion in damage. Three other storms, including two hurricanes, and three Atlantic storms also affected Mexico. The only other significant storm was Hurricane Jimena, which passed near Hawaii, the first to do so in years. The season began on May 15 in the Eastern Pacific and June 1 in the Central Pacific, ending on November 30. Usually, most tropical storms form in these areas during these months. In total, 16 tropical storms formed, 7 became hurricanes, which is typical. The storms caused $129 million in damage and 23 deaths.

A trauma center is a hospital that treats people with serious injuries, like falls, car accidents, or gunshot wounds. Sometimes, a trauma center just means an emergency room without special services. In the U.S., to become a trauma center, a hospital must meet rules set by a group called the American College of Surgeons and pass an inspection. Each state decides how to give official status to trauma centers. Trauma centers have different levels: Level I is the best, and Level III is the lowest. Higher-level trauma centers have more specialists and better equipment. Lower levels can only treat and stabilize injuries before sending patients to a higher-level center. Running a trauma center costs a lot, especially in rural areas. The number of patients can change a lot, without warning. Trauma centers often have a landing pad for helicopters to bring in patients from remote areas faster. This can mean better care than going to a closer hospital by ambulance. The level of trauma care can greatly affect a patient's recovery and whether they need to go to a higher-level center.

Panphagia is a type of dinosaur that lived about 231 million years ago during the Carnian age of the Late Triassic period. It was found in what is now northwestern Argentina. Its fossils were discovered in the La Peña member of the Ischigualasto formation in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión basin. The name "Panphagia" means "all to eat" in Greek, as scientists believe it ate everything. This dinosaur is one of the earliest known dinosaurs and shows how early sauropodomorph dinosaurs might have changed their diet.

Harry Gulkin was born on November 14, 1927, and died on July 23, 2018. He came from Montreal, Quebec, Canada. Harry worked as a film and theatre producer, arts director, and project manager. He produced the film "Lies My Father Told Me," which won a Golden Globe.

Stewart-Haas Racing is an American professional stock car racing team that competes in several NASCAR series. The team is owned by Tony Stewart and Gene Haas. It was created in 2002 as Haas CNC Racing. In 2009, Tony Stewart joined the team and got a 50% share. The team has its main office in Kannapolis, North Carolina, near Charlotte Motor Speedway. It also shares a location with the Haas F1 Team, but they are separate for legal reasons. In the NASCAR Cup Series, Stewart-Haas Racing uses four Ford Mustang GT cars: No. 4 with Kevin Harvick, No. 10 with Aric Almirola, No. 14 with Clint Bowyer, and No. 41 with Cole Custer. In the Xfinity Series, they run one Ford Mustang full-time for Chase Briscoe. In the K & N Pro Series West, they run No. 41 Ford part-time with Aric Almirola. The Xfinity team works with Biagi-DenBeste Racing. From the start until 2016, they used Chevrolet engines and chassis from Hendrick Motorsports. In 2017, they started working with Roush-Yates Engines and switched to Ford engines, building their own chassis. Stewart-Haas Racing has won in all three national touring divisions, making them one of the few teams to do so.
Bernard Greenhouse was born on January 3, 1916, and died on May 13, 2011. He was an American cellist. He was also one of the people who started the Beaux Arts Trio.

Sridevi came in is an Indian Tamil drama. It stars Ananya, Nandhan Loganadhan, Lasya Nagraj, Meera Krishnan, and Devi Priya. The show is a remake of a Kannada serial called Lakshmi Baramma. Sridevi came in replaced Enga Veetu Mapillai and aired on Colors Tamil from April 18, 2018, to June 28, 2019.

Ryan Zinke, born on November 1, 1961, is an American businessman and politician. He was the U.S. Secretary of the Interior in the Trump administration from 2017 to 2019. Before that, he was a U.S. Representative for Montana's at-large congressional district from 2015 to 2017. He also served in the Montana Senate from 2009 to 2013, representing the 2nd district. Zinke played football at the University of Oregon and got a degree in geology. He also has a master's degree in business and global leadership. He was a U.S. Navy SEAL from 1986 to 2008, retiring as a commander. He is the first Navy SEAL to serve in the U.S. House of Representatives. In Congress, he supported using ground troops in the Middle East against ISIS and opposed the Affordable Care Act, some environmental rules, and giving state governments federal land. Trump chose Zinke to be the U.S. Secretary of the Interior. Zinke's role included opening more federal lands for oil, gas, and mineral exploration. Some of his expenses, like expensive flights, caused questions and were looked into by a government group. A news report in 2018 talked about these issues. Later, the investigation was sent to the Justice Department. Trump said Zinke would leave his job on January 2, 2019, and David Bernhardt would replace him.
The COVID-19 pandemic was found in the Republic of the Congo in March 2020.

Ingrid Victoria Sofia Louise Margareta, born on March 28, 1910, and who passed away on November 7, 2000, was the Queen of Denmark from 1947 to 1972. She was married to Crown Prince Frederick of Denmark and they had three daughters: Queen Margrethe of Denmark, Princess Benedikte of Sayn-Wittgenstein-Berleburg, and Queen Anne-Marie of Greece. In 1947, when her husband became King Frederick IX upon his father's death, Ingrid became queen. As queen, she made changes to Danish court life, making it less formal and more relaxed. King Frederick IX died in 1972, and Queen Margrethe succeeded him. Additionally, Ingrid was the paternal aunt of King Carl XVI Gustaf of Sweden.

Hillside Lake is a small community in Dutchess County, New York, United States. It had 1,084 people living there in 2010. Hillside Lake is part of the Poughkeepsie–Newburgh–Middletown, NY metropolitan statistical area. It is also part of a larger area called the New York–Newark–Bridgeport, NY-NJ-CT-PA combined statistical area.

The Great Wave, also known simply as the Wave, is a famous woodblock print by Japanese artist Hokusai. It was published between 1829 and 1833, during the late Edo period. This print is the first in Hokusai's series "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji." It is his most well-known work and often considered one of the most recognized pieces of Japanese art globally. The image shows a huge wave that looks threatening to three boats off the coast of Sagami Bay (in Kanagawa Prefecture) while Mount Fuji can be seen in the background. It is sometimes thought to be a tsunami, but it is more likely a large rogue wave. Like the other prints in the series, this one depicts the area and activities around Mount Fuji under different conditions. Throughout the series, Berlin blue pigment is used dramatically.

Owls are birds from the strigiformes order, which has over 200 species. Most owls are solitary and active at night. They have an upright posture, a large head, binocular vision, binaural hearing, sharp talons, and silent flight feathers. Not all owls fit this description: the northern hawk-owl is active during the day, and the burrowing owl lives in groups. Owls mostly hunt small animals like mammals, insects, and other birds. Some species catch fish. They can be found in all parts of the world except for polar regions and some remote islands. Owls belong to two families: the true owl family (Strigidae) and the barn-owl family (Tytonidae). A group of owls is called a "parliament."

Kenneth Gary Albert, born on February 2, 1968, is an American sportscaster. He is the son of sportscaster Marv Albert and the nephew of sportscasters Al Albert and Steve Albert. Kenneth is unique as he does the play-by-play for all four major professional sports leagues in the U.S. and Canada: the NFL, NBA, MLB, and NHL.

Chattanooga was a pop group made up of the Mia, Ackie, and Clara Kempff sisters from Halmstad, Sweden. They had some success in music charts in the early 1980s. In 1982, they sang "Hallå Hela Pressen" in a competition called Melodifestivalen and came in 4th place. In 2004, the sisters came together again to sing "Hallå Hela Pressen" with Nina and Kim.

The Malagasy Wikipedia is a version of Wikipedia in the Malagasy language. It was launched in April 2004 and has articles. Currently, it ranks 63rd in the world by the number of articles. There are 3 administrators, 13,671 registered users, and 25 active users on this Wikipedia.
The 970s decade started on January 1, 970, and ended on December 31, 979.

A record chart, also known as a music chart, ranks songs based on certain criteria over a period. Different criteria like sales, radio play, downloads, and streaming are used worldwide. Some charts focus on specific types of music or areas. Most often, these charts look at weekly data. Longer charts for years or decades are made from weekly ones. Weekly charts help show song success. TV and radio shows often list music chart songs.
