Robert DeRoy Windham, known as Blackjack Mulligan, was an American professional wrestler, writer, and former football player. He was born on November 25, 1942, and passed away on April 7, 2016. His sons are Barry and Kendall Windham. Mike Rotunda's wife is his daughter. He is also the grandfather of Bray Wyatt and Bo Dallas on his mother's side.
Sidney Haight was born on August 21, 1847, and died on September 17, 1918. He received the Medal of Honor during the American Civil War for his actions during the Siege of Petersburg.

Antonio Tavaris Brown Sr., born on July 10, 1988, is an American football wide receiver. He is currently a free agent. He grew up in Liberty City, Miami, and attended Miami Norland High School where he played both football and track. Brown played college football at Central Michigan University and was an All-American as a punt returner in 2008 and 2009. He was chosen as a sixth-round pick by the Pittsburgh Steelers. During his rookie season in 2010, Brown set a record by having the most receptions in the league. In his first season with the Steelers, the team reached Super Bowl XLV but lost to the Green Bay Packers. He had 16 receptions for 167 yards in 10 games. In his second NFL season, Brown became the first player to have over 1,000 receiving and return yards in the same year. For this achievement, he was chosen for the 2012 Pro Bowl as a punt returner. In 2013, he was the only receiver to record at least 50 yards in every game of an NFL season. Despite his continued success, including leading the league in receptions and receiving yards in 2014 and 2017, and receiving touchdowns in 2018, his relationship with the Steelers became difficult, especially with quarterback Ben Roethlisberger. Brown asked for a trade. In 2019, he was traded to the Oakland Raiders, making him the highest-paid receiver in the league. However, his time with the Raiders was brief, and after off-field issues, including a confrontation with the general manager, Mike Mayock, he was released without playing a regular-season game. Brown then signed with the New England Patriots but was cut after appearing in just one game. At the time, the NFL was investigating sexual assault allegations against him.

Jan Hus (also known as John Hus or John Huss) was born in Husinec, Bohemia, in 1369 and died on July 6, 1415. He is sometimes called "Ioannes Hus" or "Johannes Huss" in historical texts. Hus was a Czech theologian and philosopher who worked to reform the Church and inspire Hussitism, a key influence on Protestantism. He is seen as the second church reformer, coming after John Wycliffe. Hus taught important ideas that affected western European states, leading to the creation of a reformed religious group in Bohemia. Later, Martin Luther was influenced by his teachings. Hus studied to become a priest to escape poverty. He moved to Prague and supported himself by singing and working in churches. His studies and commitment were praised. After becoming a priest, he started preaching in Prague. Hus criticized the Catholic Church, including its views on church structure, buying of church positions, the Eucharist, and other religious topics. When Pope Alexander V sided with Bohemian church leaders against Hus and his followers, Hus was excommunicated. He continued to preach. Later, he also criticized the new Pope, John XXIII, for selling indulgences. His excommunication was strengthened, and he lived in exile for two years. The Council of Constance asked Hus to come and explain his views. He was arrested and put in prison. When asked to change his ideas, he replied, "I would not abandon the truth for a chapel of gold." Refusing to recant, he was imprisoned again. On July 6, 1415, he was executed by burning for disagreeing with the Catholic Church. After Hus's death, his followers, known as Hussites, refused to accept another Catholic king. They defeated five papal crusades between 1420 and 1431 in what became known as the Hussite Wars. The Bohemian and Moravian populations remained majority Hussite until the 1620s. At that time, a Protestant defeat in the Battle of the White Mountain led to the area coming under Habsburg rule for 300 years, forcing a return to Catholicism.
Browning is a village in Schuyler County, Illinois, United States. In the year 2000, it had 130 people living there.

megaraptor, meaning "giant thief," is a type of large meat-eating dinosaur that lived during the late Cretaceous period, specifically in the Turonian and Coniacian ages. Its fossils have been found in the Patagonian Portezuelo Formation in Argentina. Initially, scientists thought it was similar to a large dromaeosaur-like coelurosaur. However, recent studies and discoveries about related dinosaurs have classified megaraptor either as a very early tyrannosauroid or a very early coelurosaur.

Los Osos is a place without its own government. It is part of San Luis Obispo County, California, near the Pacific Ocean. It uses zip codes 93402 and 93412, and the phone area code is 805. In 2010, there were 14,276 people living there.
Most of the 35 streams are small and only last for a short time. They get water from melting snow until late April. Some streams only flow in winter and dry up during the summer.

The Arc de Triomphe de l'Étoile is a famous monument in Paris, France. It stands at the end of the Champs-Élysées, in the middle of Place Charles de Gaulle, which used to be called Place de l'Étoile because it has twelve roads that radiate out like the points of a star. The Arc de Triomphe is in three different neighborhoods: the 16th (south and west), the 17th (north), and the 8th (east). The Arc de Triomphe honors soldiers who fought for France in the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars. It lists all French victories and generals on its walls. Below the main part of the monument lies the tomb of an unknown soldier from World War I. It is part of the "historic axis," a line of important monuments and streets from the Louvre Museum to the Grande Arche de la Défense. The Arc de Triomphe was designed by Jean Chalgrin in 1806. It shows French young men without clothes fighting German soldiers with beards. The Arc de Triomphe is very tall, 50 meters high, 45 meters wide, and 22 meters deep. Its main vault is 22 meters high and 14.6 meters wide. Three weeks after a big parade in 1919, a pilot flew his plane under the main part of the Arc de Triomphe. The Arc de Triomphe was the tallest arch until 1938 when a bigger arch was built in Mexico City. In North Korea, there is an arch that is even taller, and there is another tall arch near Paris that looks like the Arc de Triomphe.
founex is a town in the nyon district of the vaud canton in switzerland.
A carapace is the upper part of the shell in animals like crustaceans, arachnids, and turtles. In turtles and tortoises, the bottom part is called the plastron.

The exabyte is a unit for measuring digital information. In the international system of units (SI), the prefix "exa" means multiplying by one billion billion (10 to the power of 18). So, one exabyte equals one quintillion bytes. The unit symbol for the exabyte is EB. A related unit is the exbibyte, which is based on a binary system and is about 15% larger than one exabyte.

Amite County is in Mississippi, near Louisiana. In 2010, it had 13, 131 people. The main town is Liberty. The county is named after the Amite River, which goes through it. Amite County is part of the Micropolitan Statistical Area around McComb.

The Whopper is Burger King's famous sandwich and related products. It was introduced in 1957 and has changed over time, with different sizes and bread. Burger King says it is "the home of the Whopper" in its ads, stores, and special Whopper Bar. Competitors make similar sandwiches to compete. Burger King sells different Whopper versions for different times or places. The company often makes special Whopper promotions and jokes. They have registered many global trademarks to protect the Whopper.

ibk sundsvall was a floorball club in sundsvall, Sweden, started in 1986. The men's team played in Sweden's top floorball division in the 1990s. In 2006, the club joined with ibk nordic to become sundsvall city. In 1991, the club also played soccer in division 6 for men.

Vanzone con San Carlo is a municipality in the province of Verbano-Cusio-Ossola, in the Piedmont region of Italy. It is located northeast of Turin and west of Verbania. Vanzone con San Carlo borders these municipalities: Antrona, Schieranco, Bannio Anzino, Calasca-Castiglione, and Ceppo Morelli.

Giuseppina Bozzacchi, born on November 23, 1853, was an Italian ballerina. At 16, she created the role of Swanhilda in Léo Delibes' ballet "Coppélia" while performing with the Paris Opera Ballet. Bozzacchi was born in Milan and went to Paris to study with Mme Dominique. Choreographer Arthur Saint-Léon and director Émile Perrin looked for someone to play Swanhilda. They tried ballerinas Léontine Beaugrand and Angelina Fioretti, but neither was suitable. The favorite ballerina was preparing for the role in 1868 but fell ill. In 1869, Saint-Léon and Perrin found 16-year-old Bozzacchi. She performed Swanhilda for the first time on May 25, 1870, in front of Emperor Napoleon III. She did well and repeated the performance in the following weeks. In July, France and Prussia had a dispute over Spain's throne, leading to France declaring war. Bozzacchi danced Swanhilda for the last time on August 31, 1870, as the Paris Opera closed due to the Franco-Prussian War. The opera stopped paying salaries, and Bozzacchi, weakened by hunger, fell ill. She got smallpox and fever and died on her 17th birthday morning. She was buried at the Montmartre Cemetery in Paris.

Dark Souls is a 2011 action role-playing game made by FromSoftware and released by Namco Bandai Games. It is the second game in the Souls series, following Demon's Souls. The story takes place in a fictional kingdom called Lordran. Players control a cursed, undead character on a journey to learn about their future. A version for Windows was released in August 2012, adding more content. In October 2012, extra content called "Artorias of the Abyss" was available for other platforms. Critics thought the game's combat was deep and its levels complex. However, some found it too hard. The Windows version got less praise due to technical problems. By April 2013, the game sold over two million copies. Two sequels came out in the mid-2010s, and a remastered version was released in 2018.

Three 6 Mafia is an American hip hop group from Memphis, Tennessee. They formed in 1991. At first, they made horror-themed underground rap music. Later, they became popular with more people. Their 1995 album "Mystic Stylez" is still widely liked today. They have made music with different record labels, including Prophet Entertainment, Hypnotize Minds, Relativity, Loud, and Columbia Records. Two of their albums became platinum: "Costello" in 2000 and "Most Known Unknown" in 2005. The song "Stay Fly" from "Most Known Unknown" was very popular. In 2006, they won an Academy Award for the best original song "It's Hard Out Here for a Pimp" from the movie "Hustle & Flow." Their latest album "Last 2 Walk" came out in 2008. As of 2016, they have sold 5.5 million albums worldwide.

Lewis Michael Eisenberg, born on October 12, 1942, is an American financier and investor. He is the United States Ambassador to Italy. Eisenberg helped start and led a private investment company called Granite Capital International Group. He has been involved in American politics for many years and held important roles, such as the chairman of the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey. He was in this role during the 2001 attack on the World Trade Center. In July 2017, Donald Trump nominated Eisenberg to be the United States Ambassador to Italy. The U.S. Senate confirmed him in August 2017.

Kublai was the fifth khagan of the Mongol Empire, ruling from 1260 to 1294. He became the first emperor of the Yuan Dynasty in China in 1271. Kublai was the fourth son of Tolui and grandson of Genghis Khan. He took power in 1260 after his older brother Möngke and had to defeat his younger brother Ariq Böke in 1264. This made the empire less united. Kublai had control mainly in China and Mongolia, but still had some influence in other parts of the empire. His territory stretched from the Pacific Ocean to the Black Sea, from Siberia to Afghanistan. In 1271, Kublai established the Yuan Dynasty, which controlled present-day Mongolia, China, Korea, and nearby areas. He became the first non-Han ruler to conquer all of China by 1279. Kublai's royal portrait was part of an album of Yuan emperors and empresses, now in the National Palace Museum in Taipei. The color white, Kublai's royal color, was also the color of the Yuan Dynasty.
Lisa Latrello Blunt Rochester (born on February 10, 1962) is an American politician. She has been a U.S. representative since 2017. She belongs to the Democratic Party.

The 2003 invasion of Iraq was the first part of the Iraq War. It started on March 19, 2003 (air) and March 20, 2003 (ground) and lasted for more than a month, including 26 days of fighting. Troops from the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Poland invaded Iraq. On May 1, 2003, U.S. President George W. Bush said the main fighting was over. After that, the Coalition Provisional Authority was set up, leading to the first Iraqi election in January 2005. U.S. forces stayed in Iraq until they left in 2011. The U.S. and its allies sent 177,194 soldiers into Iraq. About 130,000 were from the U.S., 45,000 from the U.K., 2,000 from Australia, and 194 from Poland. Other countries also helped. Before the invasion, 100,000 U.S. soldiers were in Kuwait. The coalition got support from the Peshmerga in Iraqi Kurdistan. Bush and Blair said they wanted to make Iraq give up weapons of mass destruction, stop supporting terrorism, and free the Iraqi people. Some people thought the U.S. was reacting to the September 11 attacks. In a survey, 64% of Americans supported the idea of fighting Iraq, but many wanted to try talking first. Some long-time U.S. friends, like France, Canada, Germany, and New Zealand, were against the war. They said there was no proof of weapons of mass destruction. They also argued that invading Iraq wasn't justified because UN reports said there wasn't enough evidence. In February 2003, before the invasion, about 3 million people protested in Rome against the war. The U.S.-led forces attacked the Iraqi government palace in Baghdad on March 20, 2003. The next day, they started attacking Basra. U.S. special forces landed in the Persian Gulf to secure Basra. Meanwhile, the main invasion force moved south, fighting in Nasiriyah on March 23. Air strikes across Iraq caused confusion in the Iraqi army, making it hard for them to fight effectively. On March 26, U.S. forces were dropped near Kirkuk, where they joined Kurdish rebels to secure the north. By April 9, the main coalition forces had taken Baghdad. They also captured Kirkuk on April 10 and Tikrit on April 15. Saddam Hussein and his leadership went into hiding as the coalition finished occupying the country. On May 1, President George W. Bush declared the main fighting was over, ending the invasion and starting the occupation period.

The South African Republic, also called the Transvaal Republic or the Zar, was an independent state from 1852 to 1902. It was located in what is now South Africa. In the first Boer War, the Republic defeated the British Empire. The republic stayed independent until the end of the Second Boer War on May 31, 1902. During this war, the British used a policy called scorched earth and set up concentration camps for captured Boer women and children, causing over 27,000 civilian deaths. After the war, the area that was the Zar became the Transvaal colony. During World War I, there was an attempt to recreate the republic in an event known as the Maritz Rebellion. The land that was once the Zar now includes parts of Gauteng, Limpopo, Mpumalanga, and North West provinces in northeastern South Africa.
Farid Abedi was born on August 28, 1977, in Firouzabad. He is an Iranian football player. Currently, he plays for Bargh Shiraz in the Azadegan League.
Italy has taken part in every Military World Games since the first one in 1995.

A euphemism is a gentle word or expression used instead of one that might be upsetting or bring up unpleasant thoughts. Some euphemisms are meant to be funny, while others use mild, non-offensive terms to make certain ideas seem less important. These terms can be used to hide rude words or talk about private or sensitive subjects, like disabilities, sex, going to the bathroom, or death, in a polite manner.

The flag of Saint Lucia has a blue background with a yellow triangle in front of a black triangle that has white edges. It was adopted in 1967 to replace the British blue ensign with the colony's arms. Since Saint Lucia became an associated state of the UK that year, this flag has been used. While the overall design hasn't changed, some details have been modified over time.

College Station is a city in Brazos County, Texas. It is in the central part of Texas, in the Brazos Valley region, near the Texas Triangle. College Station is north of Houston and northeast of Austin. In 2010, it had about 93,857 people, and by 2019, the number increased to around 117,911. College Station and Bryan together make the Bryan-College Station area, which had about 273,101 people in 2019. College Station is where Texas A&M University's main campus is located. The city got its name and started because of the university being near a railroad. As a land-, sea-, and space-grant institution, Texas A&M does a lot of research, with projects funded by groups like NASA, the National Institutes of Health, and the National Science Foundation. Because of Texas A&M, College Station was called the most educated city in Texas by "Money" magazine in 2006, and the 11th most educated city in the United States.
Giornico is a town in the Leventina district, which is in the Ticino canton of Switzerland.

The governor of Vermont is the leader of the state's government. The person who holds this job is chosen by voting directly every two years in years with even numbers. Vermont and New Hampshire are the only states that hold governor elections every two years, unlike the other 48 U.S. states which do it every four years. There is no limit on how many terms a Vermont governor can serve. If no candidate gets at least 50% plus one vote, the Vermont legislature will choose the governor. The current governor of Vermont is Republican Phil Scott. He took office on January 5, 2017, becoming Vermont's 82nd governor.
Great Romania, which means "România Mare" in Romanian, can refer to:

Eino Tamberg was born on May 27, 1930, and passed away on December 24, 2010. He was an Estonian composer whose music is played all over the world. Tamberg composed operas, including "Cyrano de Bergerac," four symphonies, and several concertos. He taught music composition at the Estonian Academy of Music for many years.
Jefferson County is the name of 26 counties and one parish in the United States.

An editorial is a written piece in a newspaper or magazine, often by the top editors, without a name. In the U.S., such pieces are called "leading articles," while in the U.K., they're called "leaders." Some newspapers put these under an "opinion" section, like The New York Times and The Boston Globe. Editorials can include pictures, usually in the form of cartoons. Newspapers usually write editorials on specific topics, based on what they think is important for their readers. These are often published on a page called the "editorial page." This page also has letters from people who read the newspaper. The page next to it, called the "op-ed" page, has writings from people not connected to the newspaper. Sometimes, an editorial might appear on the front page of a newspaper, but this happens rarely. In some countries like Denmark, Spain, Italy, and France, it's more common. Newspapers often don't put the editor's name on editorials, so readers focus on the issue, not the writer. However, the editor, who oversees the writing, is known. While the editor might not write the editorial, they are responsible for it. When a newspaper changes, like The Press in New Zealand which switched to a smaller size in 2018, they might publish old editorials to show how their views have changed. For example, they once said women would prefer staying at home instead of voting. In fashion magazines, "photo-editorials" are features with large photos, often on one theme, like a designer or model, without much text.
Blingel is a commune in the Pas-de-Calais department, which is in the Hauts-de-France region of northern France.

The Citadel Center is a 580 ft (177m) tall skyscraper in Chicago's Loop area. It is at 131 S. Dearborn St., Chicago, Illinois 60603. A Spanish architect, Ricardo Bofill, designed it. As of fall 2018, it was the 57th tallest building in Chicago, and it will soon be the 60th tallest. Completed in 2003, it has 37 floors above ground and 3 below (a total of 40 floors). It covers 1,536,548 square feet. It was certified as LEED Gold in 2017. In 2018, a special copy of the Winged Victory of Samothrace, a famous sculpture, was shown in the lobby but removed later. The original is at the Louvre Museum. The lobby had a curved wall made of red padauk wood. The Citadel Center was the first building in Chicago to use a raised-floor pressurized plenum system, allowing better climate control with adjustable floor diffusers.

Balaguer is the capital of the "comarca" of Noguera, in the province of Lleida, Catalonia, Spain. It is next to the River Segre, which flows into the Ebro. The town has a small area to the east that is not part of the main region. Balaguer became the new capital in 1106 when Count Ermengol VI of Urgell took it from the Moors. It stayed the capital for the counts of Urgell. There is a Gothic bridge, "Ponte Sant Miquel," over the Segre River. This bridge was destroyed in the Battle of Cap de Pont during the Spanish Civil War in 1938 and was rebuilt later. Another old building is the Santa Maria Church, which is higher up from the city. It is next to a well-preserved wall from the 15th century. The historic part of the town is on the right side of the Segre River. After the Spanish Civil War, a new bridge was built on the left side, leading to a newer part of the town being developed. During the Spanish Civil War, General Franco's forces came into Catalonia through Balaguer's bridgehead in 1938.

Luke Isaac Moore, born on February 13, 1986, is an English former professional footballer who played as a striker. He represented England's under-21 team. Luke is the younger brother of Stefan Moore, who was also a professional footballer.

Percy Bysshe Shelley (4 August 1792 – 8 July 1822) was a famous English poet from the Romantic period. He was known for writing both beautiful short poems and deep philosophical ones. Despite not being famous during his life, he was recognized for his poetry after he died. Shelley was part of a group of important poets and writers, including Lord Byron, John Keats, and Mary Shelley, who wrote visionary works. Shelley's best-known poems include "Ozymandias," "Ode to the West Wind," "To a Skylark," "Music, When Soft Voices Die," "The Cloud," and "The Masque of Anarchy." He also wrote plays and long, philosophical poems such as "Prometheus Unbound," which is considered his greatest work. Shelley's friends included important thinkers like his father-in-law, the philosopher William Godwin, and Leigh Hunt. Most publishers refused to print his works because of fear of legal trouble. During his time, his poetry was read secretly by many, but his work is now widely appreciated. Shelley's ideas influenced other famous thinkers, including Karl Marx and Mahatma Gandhi. He was a role model for many poets, such as Robert Browning and Dante Gabriel Rossetti. People who admired him include Oscar Wilde, Thomas Hardy, and Isadora Duncan. Shelley's writings on nonviolence also inspired Henry David Thoreau's "Civil Disobedience." His influence on poetry and ideas has grown over time and continues to be important today.
Saint- Jean- sur- Erm is a former town in Mayenne, a place in northwestern France. On January 1, 2017, it became part of a new town called Blandouet- Saint- Jean.

The Flint River is a river in Georgia, the U.S. state. It flows from the west part of Georgia, starting from the Piedmont region south of Atlanta. The river continues south to the wetlands near the Gulf Coast in southwestern Georgia. Together with the Apalachicola and Chattahoochee rivers, it forms the ACF basin. In its upper part, through the Red Hills of the Piedmont, the river is especially beautiful and flows freely. Historically, it was also known as the Thronateeska River.
drowned in sound, or dis, is a UK-based music website funded by Silentway, an artist management company. It was started by Sean Adams. The site has reviews, news, interviews, and discussion forums.

Hydrography is the study of measuring and describing the physical features of oceans, seas, coastal areas, lakes, and rivers. It also helps predict changes over time. The main goal is to ensure safe navigation. It supports many other activities too, such as economic development, security, defense, research, and protecting the environment.
lay-lamidou is a commune in Pyrénées-Atlantiques, a department in southwestern France.

The Amu Darya, also known as the Amu, Amo, or Amudaryo river, is a major river in Central Asia and Afghanistan. It starts in the Pamir Mountains, north of the Hindu Kush. The Amu Darya is formed by the Vakhsh and Panj rivers joining in the Tigrovaya Balka nature reserve on the border between Afghanistan and Tajikistan. The river flows northwest into the southern part of the Aral Sea. In its upper part, the river forms part of Afghanistan's northern border with Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan. In ancient times, the river marked the boundary between Greater Iran and Turan, which roughly corresponds to present-day Central Asia.

Tanuja, known as Tanuja, is an Indian actress who mainly works in Hindi films. She is part of the Mukherjee-Samarth family, with parents being actress Shobhna Samarth and producer Kumarsen Samarth. She married filmmaker Shomu Mukherjee, and they have two daughters, actresses Kajol and Tanisha. Tanuja won two Filmfare Awards. She is famous for her roles in films such as "Memdidi" (1961), "Chand Aur Suraj" (1965), "Baharen Phir Bhi Aayengi" (1966), "Jewel Thief" (1967), "Nai Roshni" (1967), "Jeene Ki Raah" (1969), "Haathi Mere Saathi" (1971), "Anubhav" (1971), "Mere Jeevan Saathi" (1972), and "Do Chor" (1972). Her scenes with actors Sanjeev Kumar, Rajesh Khanna, and Dharmendra were popular in the late 1960s and early 1970s.
The 20th century BC lasted from 2000 BC to 1901 BC.
Rebergues is a town in the Pas-de-Calais department, which is in the Hauts-de-France region of France.

A structure is an arrangement and organization of parts in an object or system. Material structures can be man-made, like buildings and machines, or natural, like living things, minerals, and chemicals. Abstract structures include things like computer data and musical forms. Structures can be organized in different ways, like a hierarchy (where things are arranged in levels), a network (where things are connected in many ways), or a lattice (where things are connected to their nearest neighbors in space).

Hipparchus of Nicaea, also called Hipparchos, was a Greek astronomer, geographer, and mathematician. He is known as the founder of trigonometry and famous for discovering precession of the equinoxes by accident. Born in Nicaea (now Iznik, Turkey), he may have died on Rhodes, Greece. He worked as an astronomer from 162 to 127. Considered the greatest ancient astronomer, Hipparchus created accurate models for the sun and moon. His achievements may have included the first reliable method to predict solar eclipses. He also measured Earth's precession and compiled the first comprehensive star catalog. Hipparchus developed trigonometry and trigonometric tables. He might have invented the astrolabe and armillary sphere, tools he used to create his star catalog.

In meteorology, visibility measures how far you can see clearly. It is reported in surface weather observations and METAR codes, using meters or statute miles, depending on the country. Visibility affects traffic on roads, sailing, and aviation. Meteorological visibility looks at how clear the air is. It doesn't change based on whether it is dark or light.
The Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium are in Brussels, Belgium. These museums have more than 20,000 drawings, sculptures, and paintings from the early 15th century to today.

Cara McCollum was born on February 6, 1992, and passed away on February 22, 2016. She was an American journalist. She worked as the lead news anchor for SNJ Today, starting in July 2015. Cara was also Miss New Jersey 2013 and competed in Miss America 2014.

On November 14, 2017, some soldiers from the Zimbabwe Defence Forces (ZDF) went to Harare, the capital of Zimbabwe. They took control of the Zimbabwe Broadcasting Corporation and other important areas of the city. The next day, the ZDF said they weren't trying to take over the government. President Robert Mugabe was safe, but the ZDF would deal with "bad people" around Mugabe who were causing problems in the country. The day before the soldiers moved to Harare, there was tension in Mugabe's party. Emmerson Mnangagwa, a former vice-president, and Grace Mugabe, the president's wife, were fighting over who would become the next leader. Zuma, the president of South Africa, called Mugabe and was told Mugabe was under house arrest but was okay. On November 19, ZANU–PF, the ruling party, removed Mugabe as party leader and chose Mnangagwa instead. They gave Mugabe until November 20 to step down as president or face being removed from office. Mugabe did not resign. On November 21, a special meeting in parliament decided to remove him. That same day, Mugabe sent a letter to parliament, resigning as president. Phelekezela Mphoko, the second vice-president, became acting president. Mnangagwa became the new president on November 24, 2017.

Diomedes is a hero from Greek mythology. He took part in the Trojan War. He was born to Tydeus and Deipyle. Later, he became the king of Argos, following in his maternal grandfather A德鲁斯的生平可以简化如下： 德鲁斯是希腊神话中的英雄，参加了特洛伊战争。他出生于提底斯和狄皮耶。后来，他成了阿戈斯的国王，接替了他的外祖父阿德拉斯图斯。在荷马的《伊利亚特》中，德鲁斯被认为是特洛伊战争中最出色的战士之一，与阿基琉斯之后的阿吉斯和阿伽门农齐名。他后来在意大利建立了十多个城市。去世后，德鲁斯在意大利和希腊被作为神明祭祀，称呼有所不同。

Charles Henry Scherza was born on February 15, 1923, in Brandon, Manitoba. He played ice hockey professionally for 11 seasons in the American Hockey League. In 1949, he won the Calder Cup with the Providence Reds. Charles Scherza passed away on March 16, 2014, at the age of 91.

electromagnetic hypersensitivity (EH) is claimed sensitivity to electromagnetic fields. People with EH say they feel bad when exposed to these fields. There is no scientific proof for EH, and it is not recognized as a medical condition. Those who say they have EH often feel unwell at very low levels of electromagnetic fields. These levels are much lower than the maximum allowed by safety standards. In tests, many people who think they are sensitive cannot tell the difference between being exposed and not being exposed to electromagnetic fields. A study in 2011 looked at many medical research papers and found no strong evidence that symptoms are caused by electromagnetic fields. Some people who think they are sensitive to electromagnetic fields might try to reduce their exposure or use alternative medicine. Government agencies have punished companies that sell devices to protect against electromagnetic radiation, because these claims were false.

Hannes Schäfer, born on October 2, 1965, in Göttingen, Germany, is a German bass guitarist, singer, and doctor. He started his musical career with a punk band called "Defekt" in 1982, playing bass and singing. From 1985 to 1987, he was in a jazz rock band named Cit. During this time, he also worked as a studio musician at Stakkato Studio Hannover. In 1987, Hannes founded the rock band Fury in the Slaughterhouse in Hanover. He played bass there until 1996, when he left. Christian Deker replaced him. Schäfer's band won six gold records for their albums "Fury in the Slaughterhouse" (1988), "Mono" (1992), and "The Hearing and the Sense of Balance" (1995). The band sold about three million records and CDs during his time with them. In 1995, they won the most important musical award in Germany, the "Comet," as the best rock act of the year. Schäfer played over 1,400 concerts with more than five million people as a member of Fury in the Slaughterhouse. He performed at three farewell concerts in Hanover in August 2008 and one more in May 2011, with over 40,000 spectators. After leaving the band in 1996, he studied medicine and became a gynaecologist. Today, he works in his own clinic in Hanover, Germany.
Erin Richards, born on May 17, 1986, is a Welsh actress, director, and writer. She is famous for playing Molly Hughes in the TV show "Breaking In" and Barbara Kean in "Gotham."

Fabio Cudicini was born on October 20, 1935. He was an Italian goalkeeper who played from 1955 to 1972. He was one of the tallest goalkeepers of his time, standing at a height of 6 feet 6 inches. Although he never played for the Italian national team, Cudicini is considered one of the best goalkeepers of his generation and one of Italy's best goalkeepers ever. He is mostly remembered for his successful and dominant time with A.C. Milan. He helped the club win the 1969 European Cup, among other titles. Cudicini is celebrated for his achievements with A.C. Milan.

Hoyt Patrick "Pat" Taylor Jr. was born on April 1, 1924, and died on April 22, 2018. He was an American politician and lawyer. Pat Taylor served as the speaker of the North Carolina House of Representatives and as the 26th lieutenant governor of North Carolina.

Igor Nikolayevich Rodionov, born on December 1, 1936, and died on December 19, 2014, was a Russian general and Duma deputy. He was known for his strict political stance and his role as the head of the Defense Ministry of the Russian Federation. Rodionov served as a Soviet army officer in various locations, including East Germany, Czechoslovakia, and the Far East. In 1970 to 1973, he led a motorized rifle regiment in the 24th motorized rifle division, also known as the "Iron Division," in the Carpathian Military District. Later, he commanded the 17th motor rifle division in the same district. From 1983 to 1985, he was the commander of the 5th army in the Far East Military District, and in 1985 to 1986, he led the 40th army in Afghanistan. Rodionov was in charge of a violent crackdown during the April 9 protests in Tbilisi in 1989. He was blamed for the deaths of 19 people and injuries to hundreds. He was then reassigned to the General Staff Academy. However, it's believed he was used as a scapegoat, as the orders came from Defense Minister Yazov, at the request of local communist party officials. From 1989 to 1996, Rodionov was a People's Deputy and head of the General Staff Academy. In 1996, Russian President Boris Yeltsin replaced Defense Minister Pavel Grachev with Rodionov. Rodionov had written many military articles and came from the General Staff Academy, where he had analytical experience, something Grachev lacked. During his term, Rodionov tried to reform the military but believed in maintaining the Cold War perspective, seeing Russia as an adversary of the West. He changed his mind about whether to restructure the army based on Russia's new situation or continue the Soviet model. Yeltsin dismissed Rodionov because he refused to give civilian control to the Defense Council and had disputes with Yuriy Baturin over military spending. Rodionov continued to be a member of the State Duma from 1999, representing the Rodina faction. He served on the National Security Committee and chaired the Professional Union of Military Personnel. He was buried at the Federal Military Memorial Cemetery in Moscow Oblast after his death.

Ravi Shankar, born Robinndro Shauknor Chowdhury (later spelled Ravindra Shankar Chowdhury in Sanskrit), was born on April 7, 1920, and passed away on December 11, 2012. Known as Pandit (master), he was an Indian musician and composer of Hindustani classical music. He became famous for playing the sitar in the latter half of the 20th century and influenced many musicians worldwide. In 1999, he received India's highest civilian honor, the Bharat Ratna. Shankar came from a Bengali Brahmin family in India. He started dancing but gave it up in 1938 to study sitar playing under Allauddin Khan. After finishing his studies in 1944, he worked as a composer, creating music for the "Apu trilogy" by Satyajit Ray, and was the music director of All India Radio in New Delhi from 1949 to 1956. In 1956, he began touring Europe and the Americas, playing Indian classical music and making it more popular in the 1960s through teaching, performances, and collaborations with violinist Yehudi Menuhin and Beatles guitarist George Harrison. His influence on Harrison helped popularize Indian instruments in Western pop music during the latter half of the 1960s. Shankar also engaged with Western music by writing compositions for sitar and orchestra. He toured the world in the 1970s and 1980s. From 1986 to 1992, he served as a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha, the upper house of the Indian Parliament. He continued performing until the end of his life.
Dhillon is a tribe of Jat people found among Sikhs in Punjab, India. Notable people with the name Dhillon may or may not be part of this tribe.

Joan Mari Torrealdai Nabea was a Basque writer, journalist, and sociologist. He lived from November 24, 1942, to July 31, 2020. He was from Forua, in the Biscay province of the Basque Autonomous Community, Spain. He was also a member of Euskaltzaindia, the Royal Academy of the Basque Language.

Cosmology, from the Greek words "kosmos" meaning "world" and "-logia" meaning "study of," is a part of astronomy that looks at how the universe began and has changed over time, from the big bang to now and even the future. It is the study of the universe's start, its big structures, and its movement, and what might happen to it in the end. People like scientists, especially astronomers and physicists, and philosophers, including those who think about the nature of space and time, study it. The word "cosmology" first appeared in English in 1656 in Thomas Blount's "Glossographia," and later in 1731, it was used in Latin by the philosopher Christian Wolff in "Cosmologia Generalis." Religious or mythological cosmology deals with stories about how the universe was created and beliefs about the end of the world, found in religious and mythological writings. Physical cosmology focuses on the universe's laws and is studied by scientists and philosophers. Because physical cosmology shares some areas with philosophy, it might include ideas that aren't always testable. Unlike astronomy, which studies single stars and planets, cosmology looks at the universe as a whole. Modern cosmology is mainly based on the big bang theory, which tries to combine what we know about the universe with our understanding of tiny particles. The big bang theory, with its explanation of dark matter and dark energy, is described by theoretical astrophysicist David N. Spergel as a "historical science" because the further back in space we look, the further back in time we are seeing due to how fast light travels.

L'Ile-Saint-Denis is a town near Paris. It is in the northern part of Paris. The town is close to the center of Paris. Ile-Saint-Denis is on an island in the Seine River, which is why it is called Ile-Saint-Denis.

El Paso County is one of 64 counties in Colorado. In 2010, it had 622, 263 people. This made it the second most populated county in Colorado, after Denver. The county seat is Colorado Springs, the second largest city in Colorado. El Paso County is part of the Colorado Springs Metropolitan Statistical Area. Since 1871, El Paso County has usually voted for the Republican candidate. The last Democrat to win was Lyndon B. Johnson in 1964. Democrats won El Paso County four other times, and the Populist Party won in 1892 with James B. Weaver. In 2004, Colorado Springs and El Paso County created the Pikes Peak Rural Transportation Authority (PPRTA). They also put a 1% sales tax towards improving transportation. Since 2003, the area has made progress on transportation, like the completion of Cosmix in 2007 and the I-25 interchange with Highway 16 in 2008. In 2012, the county voted to legalize marijuana. On March 12, 2019, the county voted to become a Second Amendment sanctuary.
Hand County is in South Dakota, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 3,431 people. Miller is the county seat.
Mary Ann Mobley was born on February 17, 1937, and died on December 9, 2014. She was an American actress and TV personality. She also won the Miss America title in 1959.

Mallory Hagan was born on December 23, 1988. She is an American politician and used to be a beauty queen. She won Miss America 2013 while being Miss New York 2012. Hagan moved to New York in 2008 after her first year at Auburn University. Before winning Miss America, she was also Miss Brooklyn 2010, Miss Manhattan 2011, and Miss New York City 2012. She was a first runner-up twice in Miss New York. In Alabama, she was the runner-up in the Miss Alabama's Outstanding Teen program. As Miss Chattahoochee Valley 2007, she won a talent competition. She won Miss America by talking about child sexual abuse, because her family had a history with it. She also talked about gun control, saying that violence should not be used to fight violence. In 2018, she tried to become a congressperson as a Democrat in Alabama's 3rd congressional district, which includes her hometown of Opelika.

Irony, in simple terms, is a situation where what seems to be true or expected is actually different. There are different types of irony, such as verbal, dramatic, and situational. These types are often used to stress a point. In sarcasm, a form of verbal irony, the opposite of the truth is stated to emphasize a message. Other forms of irony include dialectic and practical irony.

Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne is an expansion for a real-time strategy game by Blizzard Entertainment, released on July 1, 2003, for Microsoft Windows and Mac OS X. It continues the story from the main game and features two new main characters, Maiev Shadowsong and Kael'thas, along with the returning character Arthas. It also includes a new orc campaign. The expansion introduces new units, buildings, and heroes, two new races, and some game changes. Sea units return, and Battle.net adds clan features and more maps. Development began in October 2002, and the expansion was announced in January 2003. Public tests allowed 20,000 players to try new features. The game received good reviews, with praise for mission design and new units, though some criticized graphics and voice-acting. By August 15, 2003, it sold over one million copies.

Tom Adams, born on March 9, 1938, and passed away on December 11, 2014, was an English actor. He acted in adventure, horror, and mystery films and appeared in several TV shows. He is most famous for playing Daniel Fogarty in "The Onedin Line," in multiple series.
Saint-Gervais-en-Belin is a town in the Sarthe department, which is in the Pays-de-la-Loire region of western France.

Wood fuel, like firewood or charcoal, is a type of fuel. It can be in various forms such as chips, pellets, or sawdust. The specific form used depends on factors like where it comes from, how much there is, how good it is, and how it will be used. In many places, wood is an easy-to-find fuel. You can just pick up dead wood without any tools. However, special tools like skidders and splitters are used in bigger wood production. Sawmill waste and leftover materials from construction can also be used as fuel. Making fire was a crucial discovery for humans. People have used wood for heating for a very long time, even before civilization began. Neanderthals are believed to have used it too. Today, burning wood is the most common way to use solid fuel for energy. It can be used for cooking and heating, and sometimes to power steam engines or generate electricity. You can use wood indoors in a furnace, stove, or fireplace, or outdoors in a campfire or bonfire.
Daluis is a town in the Alpes-Maritimes area of France, in the southeast. It is at the end of the Gorges de Daluis and is by the River Var.

Villedieu is a town in Vaucluse, which is in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region of southeastern France. A local story says that penitents asked Alice Colonieu to make a statue of the Virgin Mary. They wanted her to put the statue on the back of a house in Villedieu. The statue, in the Renaissance style and decorated with a king scallop, is still visible in Villedieu today and is known as the "Virgin of the Smile."
Abdulhussain Abdulredha was a Kuwaiti actor. He was born on July 15, 1939, and died on August 11, 2017.
Lenox is a city in Taylor and Adams counties, in the state of Iowa. In 2010, the city had 1,407 people.

The Ontario New Democratic Party (NDP) is a social-democratic political party in Ontario, Canada. Led by Andrea Horwath since March 2009, the party is now the official opposition following the 2018 election. It is part of the federal New Democratic Party. The NDP was formed in October 1961 from the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation (Ontario section) and the Ontario Federation of Labour. For many years, the NDP was the most successful provincial NDP branch outside the party's western part. Under its first leader, Donald C. MacDonald, the party had a breakthrough in the 1967 election, winning 20 seats. Stephen Lewis became the leader in 1970 and guided the party to official opposition status in 1975, the first time since the 1940s. After a poor performance in 1977, including losing second party status, Lewis stepped down in 1978, and Michael Cassidy became the new leader. Cassidy led the party through one election in 1981, but the performance was poor, and he resigned. In 1982, Bob Rae became the leader. Under his leadership, the NDP held the balance of power in 1985 by signing an agreement with the Liberal government. After the 1987 election, the NDP became the official opposition again. The 1990 election surprisingly resulted in the NDP forming the government for the first time, becoming the first NDP provincial government east of Manitoba. However, the economy was in a recession, and the party lost power in 1995. Rae stepped down in 1996. Howard Hampton was elected leader in 1996 and led the party through three elections. Hampton's leadership saw the NDP lose official party status twice—after the 1999 and 2003 elections. The party regained status after the 1999 election when the government changed rules, and again after winning several by-elections in the 2000s. After the 2007 election, the NDP maintained its status. Hampton stepped down in 2009, and Andrea Horwath became the new leader after winning the leadership in 2009. Under Horwath, the party had good performance in the 2011 and 2014 elections, winning 17 and 21 seats respectively. Horwath's leadership also saw the NDP form the official opposition with 40 seats after the 2018 election.

Carlos Rojas Hernández, also known as Carlos "Cuco" Rojas, was born on March 28, 1954, in San Martín, Meta, Colombia. He was a Colombian harpist and songwriter of joropo music. He also led the Colombian band Cimarron. He passed away on January 10, 2020.

Hans von Borsody, born on September 20, 1929, and died on November 4, 2013, was a German film actor. He came from a family with Hungarian roots and an artistic background. His father, Edvard, was a film director, and his uncle Julius was a set designer. His daughter Suzanne is also an actress. At the age of three, his family moved to Berlin, and they became German citizens. Borsody was married four times: to Karin Dittmann, Rosemarie Fendel, Alwy Becker, and Heide Keller.

Kiel is the capital and largest city in Schleswig-Holstein, a state in northern Germany. In 2016, it had 249,023 people. Kiel is about north of Hamburg. Being near the Baltic Sea and Jutland, Kiel is a big maritime city. It hosts many sailing events, like Kiel Week, the world's largest. Kiel is also famous for the Kiel mutiny during World War I, when sailors refused to sail ships. This led to the fall of the German Kaiser and the start of the Weimar Republic. The 1936 and 1972 Olympic sailing events were held in Kiel Bay. Kiel is a major shipbuilding city. It has the Geomar-Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research, part of the University of Kiel. Kiel is an important transportation hub because of the Kiel Fjord and Kiel Canal. Many ferries leave from Kiel. Cruise ships also visit the city. Kiel has a long history, starting in the 13th century as a Danish village. It became part of Germany in 1871. In 2005, Kiel's income per person was higher than Germany's average and 159% of the European Union's average.

Armùngia is a municipality in the province of South Sardinia, in the Italian region of Sardinia. It is located northeast of Cagliari. Armùngia borders the municipalities of Ballao, San Nicolò Gerrei, Villaputzu, and Villasalto.

The Avenger is the second full-length album by the Swedish death metal band Amon Amarth. It was released on September 2, 1999, by Metal Blade Records. This album featured new members, Johan Söderberg and Fredrik Andersson, completing the band's lineup until 2015. It came in a digipak version with a bonus track called "Thor Arise," which was a re-recording of the title track from their first demo. The album was also released as an LP. In 2005, Metal Blade Records re-released it on picture LP, with only 500 copies. In 2009, a deluxe edition was released, including a remastered album and a bonus CD of the entire album performed live in Bochum, Germany.

Saat bhai champa and sat bhai chompa are popular folk tales in Bengal, a region in eastern India. The story was first published in 1907 by Dakshinaranjan Mitra Majumder in a book called Thakurmar Jhuli. Rabindranath Tagore, a famous writer who won the Nobel Prize, wrote the introduction to this book. In 1944, a man named Bishnu Dey published a more detailed version of the story under the name "Sat Bhai Champa." Several movies were made based on the story. The 1968 movie Sat Bhai Chompa is considered one of the top ten Bangladesh films of all time by the British Film Institute.

Demetria Dyan McKinney, born on August 27, 1979, is an American actress and singer-songwriter. She was in a TV show called "Tyler Perry's House of Payne" from 2006 to 2012. There was a new version of this show planned for 2020. She also acted in other shows. She was a regular character in "The Ricky Smiley Show" on TV One, and in "Saints & Sinners," a soap opera on Bounce TV. She was also in a horror show called "Superstition" on SYFY. On stage, she played Coretta Scott King in a rhythm and blues opera called "I Dream" in 2010. She also performed as Deena Jones in "Dreamgirls" in 2012. In 2017, she starred as Whitney Houston in a TV One film called "Bobbi Kristina." That same year, she released her first album titled "Officially Yours."

Tropical Storm Cristobal was a weak storm that moved slowly in the western Atlantic Ocean before being absorbed by another weather system. It was the third named storm of the 2002 Atlantic hurricane season. Cristobal formed on August 5 near South Carolina from the same weather trough that created Tropical Storm Bertha. The storm moved southeast slowly at first and remained disorganized. It had maximum winds of 50 mph (85 km/h). On August 8, it no longer had the features of a tropical cyclone. Its leftovers brought some rain to Bermuda. The storm combined with high pressure to cause three drownings on Long Island due to strong currents.

The maize weevil, also known as the greater rice weevil, is a type of beetle found in the Curculionidae family. It is present in many tropical areas around the world and in the United States. This beetle is a significant problem for maize crops. It attacks both growing crops and stored cereal products like wheat, rice, sorghum, oats, barley, rye, buckwheat, peas, and cottonseed. The maize weevil also damages other stored or processed cereal products, such as pasta, cassava, and coarse, milled grains. It can even eat fruits stored in warehouses, like apples.
Villeneuve-sur-Fère is a village in the Aisne department, which is in Hauts-de-France, in northern France.

Gustav Metzger was born on April 10, 1926, in Nuremberg and died on March 1, 2017, in London. He was an artist and activist. Metzger developed the idea of auto-destructive art and created the art strike. He worked with John Sharkey to start the Destruction in Art Symposium in 1966. People recognized Metzger for his protests in both politics and art.
Gido Kokars was born on August 16, 1921, and passed away on March 10, 2017. He was a Latvian conductor. His twin brother, Imants Kokars, was also a conductor.
Suvarna Sahakari Bank was a private co-operative bank in India. It was based in Pune, Maharashtra. The bank started in 1969 and stopped operating in 2009.

Fiorello Henry La Guardia, born Fiorello Enrico La Guardia, was an American politician. He served as the 99th mayor of New York City from 1934 to 1945 for three terms. He was a pro-New Deal liberal progressive Republican. Before becoming mayor, he was elected to Congress in 1916, 1918, and from 1922 to 1930. Short and energetic, he loved attention and is considered one of the greatest mayors in American history. Standing only 5 feet 2 inches tall, he was nicknamed "The Little Flower." La Guardia, a Republican, was very popular in New York in the 1930s. He supported President Franklin D. Roosevelt and in return, Roosevelt provided funding for the city and cut off support for La Guardia's enemies. La Guardia improved New York City by unifying the transit system, building low-cost housing, creating parks and playgrounds, constructing airports, reorganizing the police force, and defeating the Tammany Hall political system. He also made jobs based on merit instead of personal favors. He hosted a radio show called "Talk to the People" from 1941 to 1945. A strong leader, La Guardia was seen as slightly controlling but effective. He won elections against the corrupt Tammany Hall system, led during the Great Depression and World War II, and brought in programs to help people. He supported immigrants and minorities and was backed by President Roosevelt. Known as a reform mayor, he helped end corruption, brought in experts, and improved the city for its citizens. His administration opened new groups to politics and gave New York its modern infrastructure.

Sobek, also known as Sebek, was an ancient Egyptian god with a complex nature. He was linked to the Nile crocodile or the West African crocodile and could be shown as a crocodile or a human with a crocodile head. Sobek was connected to pharaohs, fertility, and strong soldiers. He was also a protective god, often called upon to guard against dangers from the Nile.

Charlotte - Jeanne Béraud de la Haye de Riou lived from October 4, 1738, to February 6, 1806. She was a lover of Louis Philippe d'Orléans, Duke of Orléans. Louis Philippe later married, but King Louis XV did not allow Charlotte to become the Duchess. Charlotte wrote and acted in some plays. She was known as "Madame de Montesson."

VHF Omni-directional Range (VOR) is a radio navigation system for airplanes. It helps pilots find their position and stay on course by receiving signals from ground stations. VOR uses frequencies from 108.00 to 117.95 MHz in the VHF band. Developed since 1937, it became the standard air navigation system worldwide by 1946. Around 2000, about 3,000 VOR stations operated globally, with 1,033 in the U.S. by 2013, reduced to 967, as GPS became more common. A VOR ground station sends a rotating signal 30 times per second, pointing to magnetic north. It also sends a steady signal. The difference in signal timing helps find the direction from the station to the plane. Two VOR radials can pinpoint the aircraft's location. VOR signals can travel up to 200 miles. Each station sends a VHF signal with the navigation part, station identifier (a three-letter code in Morse), and sometimes voice messages like station name, advisories, or live broadcasts.

A cave or cavern is a natural space underground big enough for a person. They often form due to weathering and can go deep into the ground. The term "cave" can also describe smaller openings like sea caves, rock shelters, and grottos, but strictly, a cave has a wider bottom than its opening. Rock shelters, on the other hand, are narrower at the top than at the bottom. Studying and exploring caves is called speleology. Recreational visits or exploration of caves is sometimes called caving, potholing, or spelunking.
The Chevrolet Trax is a small crossover SUV made since 2013. It uses the GM Gamma II platform. This platform is also used for the Chevrolet Aveo, Sonic, and Opel Mokka, as well as the Buick Encore.

Lev Semyonovich Vygotsky, born in 1896 and died on June 11, 1934, was a Soviet psychologist. He wrote about how children grow and develop. He looked at many topics from different angles as his ideas changed over time. One of his students was Alexander Luria. Vygotsky introduced the idea of the "zone of proximal development" (ZPD). This idea explains the difference between what a student can do alone and what they can do with help from someone who knows more. He saw ZPD as a way to measure skills that are developing, in addition to just looking at how well a learner does on their own. Vygotsky also studied how language and thoughts are connected, how language develops, and how people grow through actions and relationships in their social and cultural environment. Many scholars argue about Vygotsky's work and are trying to better understand his original ideas.

Giovanni Boccaccio, born on June 16, 1313, and died on December 21, 1375, was an Italian writer and poet. He was also friends with Petrarch. Boccaccio wrote important books like "The Decameron" and "On Famous Women." He wrote most of his stories in the Tuscan language. He also wrote some works in Latin. Boccaccio's writing was different because his dialogue was very realistic, unlike the usual formulaic characters and plots from medieval writers.

A Roman legion was a large military group in the Roman army. The word "legio" comes from "legere," which means "to choose." In the older Roman times, a legion had about 4,200 foot soldiers and 300 horse soldiers. During later times, it grew to have around 5,200 foot soldiers and 120 additional helper soldiers.

Bombadier Transportation is a German part of the Bombadier Inc. company. It makes and fixes train equipment. The company's main office is in Berlin, Germany. They have offices in many places around the world. Bombardier Transportation makes trains, train engines, and parts for trains. In February 2020, they had about 36,000 workers in 63 places around the world.

Glenn Brydson, nicknamed "Swampy," was born on November 7, 1910, and died on December 9, 1993. He was a Canadian ice hockey player who played as a right winger. Brydson played eight seasons in the NHL, from 1930 to 1938. He played for the Montreal Maroons, St. Louis Eagles, New York Rangers, and Chicago Black Hawks. After leaving the NHL, he played five seasons in the International American Hockey League, which later became the American Hockey League. He played for the New Haven Eagles, Indianapolis Capitals, Springfield Indians, and Pittsburgh Hornets. Brydson played senior hockey briefly before retiring in 1942. He is buried at Park Lawn Cemetery in Toronto.

Meadowbank Stadium, also known as the Meadowbank Sports Centre, was a multi-purpose sports facility in Edinburgh, Scotland. Built on the site of older sports venues, it hosted the 1970 Commonwealth Games and the 1986 Commonwealth Games, becoming the first venue to host the games twice. The stadium was also used for football. From 1974 to 1995, it was the home of Meadowbank Thistle, a Scottish football league team. From 1996, it became the home ground for Edinburgh City, a senior non-league football team. In 2016, after Edinburgh City joined the Scottish Professional Football League, league football returned to Meadowbank. The Meadowbank complex also hosted Leith Athletic, which played on the adjacent Meadowbank 3G artificial pitch since 2013. In early 2019, the sports centre was demolished, and construction began on a new facility. Meadowbank Stadium was also used for rugby, being the home venue of Edinburgh Rugby from 2002 to 2004.

Fernando Sebastián Aguilar CMF was a Spanish cardinal in the Roman Catholic Church. He was also the Archbishop Emeritus of Pamplona y Tudela. Pope Francis made him a cardinal on February 22, 2014. He was born on December 14, 1929, and died on January 24, 2019.

Janet Gray Hayes was born on July 12, 1926, in Rushville, Indiana. She earned her bachelor's degree from Indiana University and later studied at the University of Chicago. Hayes moved to San Jose, California, in 1956 with her husband, who was a doctor. She joined the San Jose City Council in 1971 and became a Democrat. Hayes was the first woman elected as the mayor of San Jose in 1975, and she served two four-year terms until 1983. She was also the first woman elected as mayor of a major U.S. city with over 500,000 people. Hayes passed away on April 26, 2014, in Saratoga, California, due to a stroke.

Egg donation is when a woman gives her eggs to help another woman have a baby using assisted reproduction. For this, doctors use a lab to fertilize the eggs. Sometimes, unfertilized eggs are frozen for later use. Egg donation is part of third-party reproduction, using assisted reproductive technology. In the U.S., the American Society for Reproductive Medicine and the Food and Drug Administration have guidelines. Similar rules exist in other countries. However, in the U.S., egg donation agencies can choose to follow these guidelines or not.

This is a list of important people from Afghanistan. Afghanistan includes many different ethnic groups. The country's borders have changed over time. This list mostly includes people from the current Afghanistan, except for some Pashtuns who lived in regions not controlled by Afghanistan at certain times. It also includes people from before the current borders who were not Pashtuns but were important to Afghanistan's history. Faridoon Angar is one of them.
This article lists cities in Jordan.
farschweiler is a town in the trier-saarburg district, which is in rhineland-palatinate, a state in germany.
Feldbrunnen-St. Niklaus is a municipality in the Lebern district, in the canton of Solothurn, Switzerland.

Nathaniel Dwayne Hale, known as Nate Dogg, was an American singer, rapper, and songwriter born on August 19, 1969, and died on March 15, 2011. He was famous for his smooth voice, which he used to create memorable hooks in many rap songs, especially in the 1990s during the G-funk era in the West Coast. Nate was part of 213, a group formed in 1990 with Snoop Dogg and Warren G. After Snoop joined Death Row Records, Nate contributed to Dr. Dre’s first album, "The Chronic" (1992), and Snoop’s debut, "Doggystyle" (1993). His biggest musical success came in 1994 with the song "Regulate," which he wrote with Warren G and reached number two on the Billboard Hot 100. Nate also had 16 hits on the Billboard Hot 100 as a featured artist, including one that reached number one on 50 Cent’s "21 Questions" in 2003. In December 2007, Nate had a stroke that weakened his left side but left his mind and voice unaffected. He had another stroke several months later. Nate passed away from heart failure at the age of 41 in 2011.
Inō Tadataka, born on February 11, 1745, and died on May 17, 1818, was a Japanese surveyor and cartographer. He is famous for creating the first map of Japan using modern surveying methods.

Hevrin Khalaf, also known as Khelef, was born on November 15, 1984, and died on October 12, 2019. She was a Kurdish-Syrian politician and civil engineer. Khalaf worked in Rojava for many years and became the secretary general of the Future Syria Party. She was killed by Turkish-backed fighters called Ahrar al-Sharqiya near the M4 motorway, south of Tell Abyad, during a Turkish offensive in northeastern Syria in October 2019.

Clarke County is in the northeast of Georgia, U.S. The 2010 census showed 116, 714 people lived there. The county seat is Athens, which is combined with Clarke County. Athens-Clarke County is part of the Athens-Clarke County, Georgia metropolitan statistical area. This area is also part of the Atlanta-Athens-Clarke County-Sandy Springs, Georgia combined statistical area.
Sant'Antonio means Saint Anthony in Italian. It usually refers to places named after Saint Anthony of Padua or Saint Anthony Abate.

Popeye the sailor is a fictional American cartoon character created by Elzie Crisler Segar. He first appeared in the comic strip "Thimble Theatre" on January 17, 1929. Popeye became the main character, and the strip's title later changed to "Popeye." Segar's "Thimble Theatre" was already running for 10 years when Popeye debuted, but Popeye quickly became the star, and the strip gained popularity in the 1930s. After Segar died in 1938, the strip continued with help from his assistant, Bud Sagendorf. Hy Eisman now writes and draws the Sunday edition, while daily strips are old stories by Sagendorf. In 1933, Max Fleischer made Popeye into cartoon shorts for Paramount Pictures. These cartoons were very popular, and Fleischer continued making them until 1957. The cartoons are now owned by Turner Entertainment and distributed by Warner Bros. Popeye has also appeared in comic books, TV shows, video games, advertisements, and products like spinach and candy cigarettes. A live-action film about Popeye was made in 1980, starring Robin Williams. Charles M. Schulz said Popeye was a perfect comic strip. In 2002, TV Guide ranked Popeye as the 20th greatest cartoon character of all time.

Stickney Township is one of 29 townships in Cook County, Illinois, USA. According to the 2010 census, its population was 40,772. About 71% of these people live in Burbank, which has a population of 28,925. Township offices are located at 5635 W. State Road in Burbank. Other small towns in the township are Stickney, with 6,786 people, and Forest View, with 698 people. There is also part of Bedford Park, mainly industrial, and some small areas of Bridgeview. Unincorporated communities in the township include Central Stickney and Nottingham Park. The borders of Stickney Township are roughly Pershing Road (39th Street) to the north, Cicero Avenue to the east, 87th Street to the south, and Harlem Avenue to the west. However, it does not include parts of Garfield Ridge and Clearing, which include Chicago Midway International Airport. The area between Laramie and Cicero avenues is included up to 35th Street.

The Yalobusha River is a river in north-central Mississippi, United States. It is a major part of the Yazoo River and, therefore, part of the Mississippi River watershed. The name "Yalobusha" comes from the Choctaw word "yalooboshi," meaning "little tadpole." The United States Board on Geographic Names chose this name in 1892. It has also been called "Yallabusha" and "Yellowbushy River."

A 1872 novel called "A Dog of Flanders" was written by Marie Louise de la Ramée, who used the pen name "Ouida." It tells the story of a Flemish boy named Nello and his dog Patrasche, set in Antwerp. For many years, this story has been a favorite children's classic in Japan, Korea, and the Philippines. Several Japanese films and anime have been made based on the book since the 1980s. In the 1980s, the Belgian tourist board noticed how much visitors liked the story and created two monuments to honor it. One is a small statue of Nello and Patrasche in Hoboken, near Antwerp. The other is a commemorative plaque in front of Antwerp's cathedral, given by Toyota. Later, this plaque was replaced by a marble statue of the two characters, covered with a stone blanket, created by artist Batist Vermeulen.

LVMH Moët Hennessy – Louis Vuitton SE, also known as LVMH, is a French company based in Paris. It was created in 1987 when Louis Vuitton, founded in 1854, joined with Moët Hennessy. The latter was formed from the merger of Moët & Chandon, which makes champagne, and Hennessy, which makes cognac. LVMH manages about 60 smaller companies that each handle famous brands, with a total of 75 brands. These smaller companies are often run separately under six main groups: fashion, wine and spirits, perfumes and cosmetics, watches and jewelry, selective distribution, and other activities. One of LVMH's oldest brands is the wine producer Château d'Yquem, which has been around since 1593.

Ross Batty, born on September 20, 1986, in England, used to go to Barnard Castle School. He plays rugby union as a hooker. Currently, he plays for Bath in the Aviva Premiership. He often plays in the scrum for Bath after joining from Rotherham in 2010. On February 2, 2018, he celebrated his 150th appearance for Bath, including cup matches. On April 25, 2019, he signed a new contract with Bath. The contract's length was not disclosed. He spent nine seasons with Bath until the end of the 2018-2019 season.

Bastendorf is a small town in Tandel, a commune in northeastern Luxembourg. The town has 371 people. Until January 1, 2006, Bastendorf was its own commune in the canton of Diekirch. On that date, Bastendorf joined with the commune of Fouhren to form the new commune of Tandel, which is in Vianden. This new commune was created by a law passed on December 21, 2004.

Karnes County is in Texas, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 14,824 people. Karnes City is the county seat. The county is named after Henry Karnes, who fought in the Texas Revolution. There was a train line that passed through Karnes County, connecting San Antonio to Corpus Christi.
corpe is a town in the Vendée department, which is in the Pays de la Loire region of western France.

Sir Run Run Shaw, born in 1907 and died in 2014, was known as Shao Yifu and Siu Yat-fu. He was a very important person in the entertainment world in Asia. He started the Shaw Brothers Studio, a big movie company in Hong Kong. He also helped make TVB, a major TV company in Hong Kong. Sir Run Run Shaw donated lots of money to schools in Hong Kong and mainland China. More than 5,000 buildings in Chinese colleges are named after him. He also created the Shaw Prize for astronomy, life science, and mathematics.
Ōshima, Oshima, Ōshima, or Ohshima can all refer to the same place.

Swisscom AG is a big telecommunications company in Switzerland. Its main office is in Worblaufen, near Bern. The Swiss government owns 51% of Swisscom AG. Swisscom controls 60% of the mobile market, 67% of broadband, and 33% of TV telecommunication in Switzerland. Its Italian branch, Fastweb, serves 16% of private clients and 29% of corporate clients in Italian broadband and also offers mobile services. Switzerland set up its first telegraph network in 1852, followed by telephones in 1877. In 1920, these networks joined with the postal service to form PTT (Postal Telegraph and Telephone). PTT struggled to create its own digital network, but it was the first to launch a digital exchange in 1986. Swisscom pioneered mobile services called Natel A in 1978 and later offered a digital service called Natel D in 1993. In 1997, the Swiss telecommunications market opened up, and PTT was turned into Swisscom through a partial privatization. The Swiss government now owns 51% of Swisscom. Swisscom owns the Natel brand, known only in Switzerland. In 2001, 25% of Swisscom mobile was sold to Vodafone. Swisscom later bought a majority stake in Fastweb, an Italian telecom company, and invested in areas like hospitality, cloud services, and billing. New services in digital and IT areas aim to help Swisscom earn more money and offset losses from its traditional core business.

k's choice is a Belgian rock band from Antwerp. They started in the mid-1990s. The main members are brothers Sam Bettens (lead vocals, guitar) and Gert Bettens (guitar, keyboard, vocals). They also have Bart Van Liedekx (bass), Tom Lodewyckx (lead guitar), Reinout Swinnen (keys), and Wim Van der Westen (drums). The band has made albums that sold many copies, reaching gold and platinum status.

Abdullah Hamid Ali Al-Hamid, also known as Abu Bilal, was a Saudi poet, Arabic professor, and human rights activist. He co-founded the Saudi Civil and Political Rights Association (ACPRA). Al-Hamid was arrested multiple times for asking for a constitutional monarchy in Saudi Arabia. In May 2005, he was jailed for seven years for "opposing the ruler." He was freed in August 2005 due to a pardon. In 2008, he was put in jail again for four months because he supported a women's protest. The women were showing support for their detained relatives outside a prison in Buraidah, Saudi Arabia. In 2018, he received the Right Livelihood Award, along with other activists and Waleed Abulkhair, for their work to change Saudi Arabia's political system based on human rights.

Observation is actively gathering information from a primary source. In living beings, this involves using the senses. In science, observation also means using tools to see and record data. The term can also mean any data collected during a scientific activity. Observations can be qualitative, noting only if a property is present or absent. They can also be quantitative, giving a number by measuring or counting.
