UK garage, or ukg, is a type of electronic music that started in England in the early 1990s. It mixes styles like garage house, R&B, jungle, and dance-pop. UK garage has a rhythmic beat with shuffled drums and hi-hats, cymbals, and snares. Sometimes, it includes unusual kick drum patterns. The songs also often have chopped-up, stretched or changed pitch vocal samples. The tempo is usually about 130 beats per minute. UK garage led to other styles like speed garage and 2-step. By the mid-2000s, it was mostly replaced by bassline, grime, and dubstep. UK garage's decline in the mid-2000s led to the creation of UK funky, a closely related style.
Fowler is a town in Center Township, Benton County, Indiana, United States. In 2010, it had 2,317 people. It is in the Lafayette, Indiana, area.
Oppen is a municipality in Gros-de-Vaud district, which is in the canton of Vaud in Switzerland.

Louis Antoine Godey was born on June 6, 1804, and died on November 29, 1878. He was an American editor and publisher. He is famous for starting "Godey's Lady's Book," which was the first successful American magazine for women about fashion.

Mikhail Bakunin, a Russian revolutionary and anarchist, was born and died in 1876. He is considered one of the most influential figures in anarchism and a key founder of the social anarchist tradition. Bakunin grew up in Pryamukhino, a family estate in Russia. He studied in Moscow and Berlin, hoping to become a scholar. In Paris, he met Karl Marx and Pierre-Joseph Proudhon, who greatly influenced him. His activism led to his expulsion from France for opposing Russia's occupation of Poland. In 1849, he was arrested for participating in the Czech rebellion and deported to Russia, where he was imprisoned and later exiled to Siberia. He escaped to the United States, then to London, where he worked on a journal called "Kolokol" (The Bell) with Alexander Herzen. In 1863, Bakunin joined the Polish insurrection but failed to reach it. Instead, he spent time in Switzerland and Italy. In 1868, he joined the International Working Men's Association, leading an anarchist faction that grew in influence. The 1872 Hague congress was a struggle between Bakunin and Marx. Bakunin argued for the state to be replaced by self-governing workplaces and communes, while Marx wanted to use the state to bring about socialism. Bakunin was expelled from the association for maintaining a secret organization within it. From 1870 until his death in 1876, Bakunin wrote "Statism and Anarchy" and "God and the State," and continued to support European worker and peasant movements. In 1870, he was involved in an insurrection in Lyon, France, and later sought to join an anarchist insurrection in Bologna, Italy, but his health forced him to return to Switzerland in disguise. Bakunin is remembered as a major figure in anarchism, opposing Marxism, especially the dictatorship of the proletariat. His book "God and the State" has been widely translated. He influenced later thinkers like Noam Chomsky, Peter Kropotkin, and Errico Malatesta.

The Parliament of Albania, or Kuvendi, is the main group of representatives for the people of Albania. It makes laws for the country. There are at least 140 members who are chosen by a secret vote. They serve for four years. The Parliament is led by a Speaker and at least one Deputy Speaker. Elections follow a system where parties are represented proportionally. The Parliament can change Albania's borders and the constitution. It also approves the government, watches how the government works, starts and stops wars, and makes budgets. It helps decide elections, calls for public votes, and gives pardons. The Parliament also chooses the President. When the Parliament is first elected, the first meeting happens within 20 days, with the President as the Speaker. Laws passed by the Parliament are published in the Official Journal of Albania. The first known Parliament in Albania was in Lezhë in 1444. This group, called the League of Lezhë, was formed by Gjergj Kastrioti Skënderbeu to fight against the Ottoman Empire.
Leslie Orgel, a British chemist, lived from January 12, 1927, to October 27, 2007. He is famous for his ideas about how life began.
pettefaux is a town in the Pas-de-Calais area, which is in Hauts-de-France, a region in France.

Tapioca is a starch from the cassava plant's roots. The cassava plant, also called manioc, is native to Brazil's north and central-west regions. Its use spread to South America and was taken by Portuguese and Spanish colonizers to West Indies, Africa, and Asia. The plant is a perennial shrub that thrives in tropical areas. Cassava can grow well in poor soils, unlike many other crops. While tapioca is a main food for millions in tropical areas, it only provides carbohydrates and lacks protein, vitamins, and minerals. In other places, tapioca is used to make foods thicker.
Flavio Bucci was an Italian actor, voice actor, and film producer. He was born on May 25, 1947, and died on February 18, 2020.
Zoran "Bata" Mirković was born on September 21, 1971. He is from Serbia. He used to be a football player. Now, he is a manager.
Carhaix-Plouguer is a town in Finistère, which is in Western Brittany, France.
Shadow Hills is a neighborhood in the Verdugo Mountains and the northeastern part of San Fernando Valley, which is in Los Angeles, California.

".with my own eyes" is a song by German group sash! It came out on September 4, 2000, through x-it records. This was the third single from their third album, "trilenium." Finnish singer inka auhagen performs on the song. The song did well in several European countries and peaked at number 10 on the uk singles chart. It was sash! 's last top 10 hit on that chart until 2008.

"Just a Girl" is a song by American band No Doubt from their 1995 album "Tragic Kingdom." It was released as the first single on September 21, 1995, and written by Gwen Stefani and Tom Dumont, produced by Matthew Wilder. This song also appears in their 2003 album "The Singles 1992–2003." It is a new wave song about Stefani's experiences as a woman and her challenges with strict parents. It was Stefani's first solo song without her brother's help. Critics praised the song for its feminist lyrics and Stefani's voice. "Just a Girl" was a hit, reaching number 23 on the Billboard Hot 100 and the top ten in several countries, including Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, Norway, Scotland, and the United Kingdom. The music video, directed by Mark Kohr, shows Stefani singing in a clean restroom while the male band members play their instruments in a dirty one. The men eventually join her in the restroom and dance together. Stefani wore a popular outfit in the video. No Doubt performed "Just a Girl" in many concerts, including the Tragic Kingdom World Tour (1995–1997), part of the 2002 Rock Steady Tour, and the 2016 This Is What the Truth Feels Like Tour. The song's title inspired Stefani's 2018–2020 residency in Las Vegas. It has been covered and used in other songs by various musicians.

The anus is an opening at the end of an animal's digestive system opposite the mouth. Its main job is to control the removal of feces, which are the leftover semi-solid wastes from food digestion. These leftovers can include undigestible parts, such as bones, or indigestible plant materials like cellulose. The anus also helps get rid of toxic materials that were eaten and dead or extra gut bacteria. Some animals, like amphibians, reptiles, and birds, use a single opening called the cloaca for waste, mating, and egg-laying. Monotremes, a type of mammal, also have a cloaca. Marsupials have a single opening for both solid and liquid waste, and a separate part for reproduction. Most placental mammals, which include many common animals like dogs and cats, have separate openings for pooping, peeing, and reproduction. The development of the anus was a significant step in the evolution of animals. It seems to have evolved independently at least twice, once in protostomes and once in deuterostomes. This development also helped other important changes like the bilateral body structure, the coelom, and metamerism, where the body is made up of repeated segments that can specialize, like in the heads of insects.

A lawn mower, also called a grass cutter, is a machine with spinning blades to cut grass. The height of the cut grass can be set by design or adjusted by the operator. The blades can be powered by pushing the mower, a battery, or a small engine. Manual mowers are pushed by people, while self-propelled or ride-on mowers are easier to use. Robotic mowers can operate automatically or by remote control. Two types of blades are used. Rotary mowers have one blade spinning vertically, while cylinder mowers have a horizontal spinning blade assembly with a cutting bar. There are different kinds of mowers for different sizes of lawns. Small, push mowers are for small residential areas. Larger push mowers or electric mowers are for bigger lawns. Ride-on mowers, resembling small tractors, are for very large lawns. Large multi-blade mowers attached to tractors are used for big grass areas like golf courses and parks.
Alma is a village in Marion County, Illinois, United States. It used to be called Mound City and Rantoul. According to the 2000 census, the population was 386 people.
cyclostome is a word used in biology. It comes from the Greek words "round" and "mouth." It has a few different meanings.

Emalain Kudo Kabua, born in February 1928, was the first lady of the Marshall Islands. She was the wife of former Marshall Islands president Amata Kabua and the mother of President-elect David Kabua. Emalain Kabua was the first and only first lady of the Marshall Islands from 1979 to 1996. She also designed the flag of the Marshall Islands.

The Jurassic period lasted about 56 million years, from the end of the Triassic period to the start of the Cretaceous period. It was part of the Mesozoic era, known as the age of reptiles. The Jurassic period began with a major extinction event. During this time, two other smaller extinction events also happened: one in the early Jurassic (Pliensbachian-toarcian extinction), and another at the end (Tithonian event). However, these weren't as severe as the "big five" mass extinctions. The Jurassic period is split into three parts: early, middle, and late. In terms of rocks, it is divided into lower, middle, and upper layers. The name "Jurassic" comes from the Jura Mountains in Europe, where rocks from this period were first found. By the start of the Jurassic, the supercontinent Pangaea was breaking into two landmasses: Laurasia to the north and Gondwana to the south. This created more coastlines, making the climate more humid and replacing many deserts with rainforests. On land, life changed too. Dinosaurs and their relatives became more dominant, replacing the Triassic fauna. The first birds also appeared, evolving from a branch of theropod dinosaurs. Lizards and early mammals, including primitive placentals, also appeared. Crocodilians started living in water. In the oceans, marine reptiles like ichthyosaurs and plesiosaurs were common, while pterosaurs were the main flying creatures.

Chakotay is a fictional character in the American science fiction TV series "Star Trek: Voyager." He was played by Robert Beltran and was the first officer on the USS Voyager. Chakotay is the first Native American main character in the Star Trek series. This was done by the show's producers to inspire Native Americans, just as Uhura inspired African Americans. The producers worked with Jamake Highwater to create the character. Chakotay's tribe wasn't named at the start of the series, but this was fixed in a later episode. He first appeared in the pilot episode and was in the main cast until the end of the series. He was in a main storyline with his love, Seska, until her death. In an episode, Chakotay was against working with the Borg, which could have been dangerous. By the end of the series, he and Seven of Nine had a romantic relationship. After the ship returned, Chakotay became its captain. However, his relationship with Seven ended. Some critics thought Chakotay's Native American background was too stereotypical. He was criticized for representing Native American traditions in a way that wasn't accurate. But, he was also seen as a positive role model for Native Americans in science fiction.

Desoto is a city in Dallas County, Texas, in the United States. In 2010, it had 49,047 people. Desoto is a suburb of Dallas. It is part of the Best Southwest area, which includes Desoto, Cedar Hill, Duncanville, and Lancaster.

Canillo is a parish in Andorra. It is also the main town of the parish. The parish is known as the religious center of Andorra. It has a sanctuary and chapel dedicated to Our Lady of Meritxell, who is the patron saint of Andorra. The parish is home to Sant Joan de Caselles, one of the best-preserved Romanesque churches in the Pyrenees. As of 2011, the parish had 4,826 people living there. Despite being a tourist destination, the parish still has many traits related to livestock and agriculture.

A defoliant is a chemical used to make leaves fall off plants. People use defoliants to remove weeds in farms and gardens. This helped increase food production during the mid-20th century. Defoliants were also used in wars to make food crops and hiding places unavailable to enemies. This happened in the Malayan Emergency and the Vietnam War.

Mount Jackson is a town in Shenandoah County, Virginia, United States. In 2010, it had 1,994 people. Travelers on I-81 can easily find Mount Jackson. Exit at 273, and you will see a water tower painted like a basket of apples; it was recently painted. For those not on the highway, Mount Jackson has a history as an important commercial and railroad center in the area. It also has connections to the Civil War and is part of a historic district listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

Washoe County is in North Carolina, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 13,228 people. Its main city is Plymouth. The county started in 1799 from part of Tyrrell County. It's named after George Washington. Washoe County has three towns: Plymouth, Roper, and Creswell. Plymouth is the main town. The county is famous for its farms, forests, and lakes. The Roanoke River and Albemarle Sound are on its north side. Lake Phelps, 16,000 acres, is in Creswell and part of Pettigrew State Park. Somerset Place, a historic plantation, is also there. In the south of the county, the Pungo area of the Pocosin Lakes National Wildlife Refuge is known for good bear watching. The area is famous for having the world's biggest black bears. The North Carolina Black Bear Festival happens in June in Plymouth.

Philip Kotler, born on May 27, 1931, is an American marketing author, consultant, and professor. He taught at the Kellogg School of Management at Northwestern University from 1962 to 2018. Kotler defined the marketing mix. He wrote over 80 books, including "Marketing Management," "Principles of Marketing," "Kotler on Marketing," "Marketing Insights from A to Z," and "Winning Global Markets." Kotler described strategic marketing as the connection between what society needs and how industries respond. He helped create social marketing to encourage healthier and safer lifestyles. Kotler also introduced the ideas of demarketing, prosumers, atmospherics, and societal marketing. Many scholars consider him the father of modern marketing. His recent work focuses on economic justice and problems with capitalism. He published "Confronting Capitalism: Real Solutions for a Troubled Economic System" in 2015, "Democracy in Decline: Rebuilding Its Future" in 2016, and "Advancing the Common Good" in 2019. He also wrote "Brand Activism: From Purpose to Action" in 2018.

Joseph Patrick Kennedy III, born on October 4, 1980, is an American lawyer and politician. He has been serving as a U.S. representative since 2013. Kennedy works for the Democratic Party and represents a district from Boston's western suburbs to the state's south coast. He used to work as an assistant district attorney in Massachusetts, specifically in Cape and Islands, and Middlesex County, before becoming a congressman. Kennedy is the son of U.S. Representative Joseph P. Kennedy II, a grandson of U.S. Senator and former Attorney General Robert F. Kennedy, and a grandnephew of President John F. Kennedy and U.S. Senator Ted Kennedy. He is also a great-grandson of Joseph P. Kennedy Sr., who was the U.S. ambassador to the United Kingdom. Kennedy was born in Boston and grew up in the area with his twin brother, Matthew Rauch Kennedy. After graduating from Stanford University with a bachelor’s degree, he served in the Peace Corps for two years in the Dominican Republic. He then earned his law degree from Harvard Law School in 2009. In early 2012, Kennedy left his job as an assistant district attorney to run for the U.S. House of Representatives seat that Barney Frank was leaving. Kennedy took his seat in January 2013 and now serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce. In September 2019, Kennedy announced he would run for the Democratic nomination in the 2020 Massachusetts U.S. Senate election, competing against incumbent Edward Markey.

Safety was Coldplay's first public release. It was recorded in May 1998 over a weekend. The band and their manager, Phil Harvey, paid around £1500 for it. Only about 50 copies were given to record stores. Most of the copies went to record companies and the band's friends and family. The songs on this release later appeared unchanged on other Coldplay releases. "Bigger Stronger" and "Such a Rush" are on "The Blue Room EP," while "No More Keeping My Feet on the Ground" was the B-side of the "Yellow" single. The cover photo of Chris Martin, the lead singer, was taken by John Hilton, a friend of the band.

Shemiranat County is in Tehran Province, Iran. The capital is Shemiran, part of Tehran City. In 2006, the county had 37,778 people living in 11,178 families. For census, Shemiran and Tajrish are included in Tehran City. Shemiranat County has two districts: Rudbar-e Qasran and Lavasanat. The county includes four cities: Tajrish, Fasham, Shemshak, and Lavasan.

1600 Penn is an American TV show. It's about a family living in the White House who have problems. The main actors are Jenna Elfman, Bill Pullman, and Josh Gad. Josh Gad, along with Jason Winer and Jon Lovett, created the family and the show's main format. NBC decided to make more episodes in May 2012. The show came on in December 2012 and ended in March 2013. NBC stopped the show after just one season in May 2013.

The Barents Sea is a part of the Arctic Ocean, near Norway and Russia. It is split between Norwegian and Russian waters. This sea is also called the Murman Sea among Russians. The current name honors Willem Barentsz, a Dutch sailor. It is a shallow sea, with an average depth. It is important for fishing and searching for oil and gas. The Barents Sea is next to the Kola Peninsula, the edge of the Norwegian Sea, and some islands like Svalbard, Franz Josef Land, and Novaya Zemlya. Novaya Zemlya, which connects to the Ural Mountains, separates it from the Kara Sea. Because of global warming, the sea ice is melting, and the water is less layered. This could change weather in Europe and Asia.

A migraine is a type of headache that happens often, feels strong to very strong, and usually affects one side of the head. These headaches pulse and can last from a few hours to three days. People with migraines might feel sick, throw up, and be sensitive to light, sound, or smells. Physical activities can make the pain worse. Before a headache, some people experience an aura, which is a brief period of visual disturbance. Migraines may run in families and are more common in women after puberty. The risk usually goes down during pregnancy and after menopause. No exact cause is known, but they might involve brain nerves and blood vessels. Treatment often starts with simple pain relievers like ibuprofen or acetaminophen, plus medication for nausea, and avoiding triggers. For those who don’t respond to these, specific drugs like triptans or ergotamines can be used, sometimes with caffeine. Medications to prevent attacks include metoprolol, valproate, and topiramate. About 15% of people have migraines, which start in puberty and peak in middle age. They are a major cause of disability. An early description of migraines is found in the Ebers Papyrus, written around 1500 BC in ancient Egypt. The word "migraine" comes from the Greek "hemikrania," meaning "pain on one side of the head."

Hashish, or hash, is a drug made from the resin of the cannabis plant. People typically smoke it in a pipe, bong, vaporizer, or joint, or they can eat it after a process called decarboxylation. Hashish isn't flammable on its own, so it's often mixed with other herbs. Its names can vary by region. Hashish is a concentrate made from the plant’s sticky, resinous part called trichomes. According to the 1961 UN Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, hashish is defined as "the separated resin, whether crude or purified, obtained from the cannabis plant." It usually contains more tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and other cannabinoids than regular cannabis. Hashish can be solid or a paste-like substance. Its color varies from light to dark brown, or even yellow, tan, black, or red. The process and leftover plant material affect its appearance. In Europe in 2011, hashish purity ranged from 4% to 15%. Between 2000 and 2005, about 18% of cannabis seizures were hashish. In 2008, hashish was the main form of cannabis used in Europe, while herbal cannabis was more common in North America.

A SIM card is a small chip used in mobile phones and some computers to store important information. This includes your unique ID number and a key to help verify your identity when you use a mobile device. Some SIM cards can also keep contact details. GSM phones always need a SIM card, while CDMA phones only require one for newer, LTE-capable models. SIM cards can also be used in satellite phones, smartwatches, computers, or cameras. SIM cards are like tiny smart cards with contacts and semiconductors. They are easy to transfer between devices. The first UICC smart cards were the size of credit cards, but they became smaller over time. Each SIM card has a unique serial number (ICCID), your ID number (IMSI), security details, temporary network information, a list of available services, and two passwords: one for everyday use (PIN) and one to unlock the PIN (PUK). In Europe, the serial SIM number (SSN) sometimes has a related number, like an international article number (IAN) or European article number (EAN), needed when you sign up for prepaid phone services online.

Habib Mohebian, known as Habib, was an Iranian singer-songwriter born on September 27, 1947, in Tehran, Iran. He started to love music and the guitar in his final years of high school. In a national contest run by the Iranian radio and TV, he was selected among 16 candidates. After training for two years, he joined the military. While serving, he continued to perform in military clubs and at other events. He later lived in the western and eastern Azerbaijan provinces and moved to Tehran. He then went to the United States but returned to Iran in 2009. Habib passed away on June 10, 2016, in Ramsar, Mazandaran, Iran, due to a heart problem.

Guanajuato is a city and municipality in central Mexico. It is the capital of the state with the same name. It is part of the Bajío region. The city is in a narrow valley with narrow, winding streets. Most streets are narrow alleys that cars cannot pass through, and some are long staircases going up the mountains. Many city streets are partly or fully underground. The historic center has small plazas and old buildings, like mansions, churches, and civil structures, made of pink or green sandstone. The city grew because of the many minerals in the nearby mountains. During the colonial period, it was one of the most important cities due to its rich mines. One mine, La Valenciana, produced a lot of silver. The city has a mummy museum with naturally mummified bodies found in the cemetery between the mid-19th and 20th centuries. It also hosts the International Cervantino Festival, which brings artists and performers from around the world and Mexico. Guanajuato was the site of the first battle of Mexico's independence war. This battle was between newly formed Mexican fighters and royalist troops. The city became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1988.

Caniformia is a group within the carnivores. This group includes animals like dogs, bears, wolves, foxes, raccoons, badgers, seals, and mustelids. Seals, walruses, and sea lions are also part of this group. Caniformia mainly came from North America and northern Eurasia. This group is different from Feliformia, which includes cats and their relatives. Feliformia mainly came from Africa and southern Asia.

Florence County is in South Carolina, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 136, 885 people. The county seat is Florence. Florence County is part of the Florence, South Carolina metropolitan area. About 60% of the county's population lives in urban areas.

Adam Lyons Schlesinger was an American singer-songwriter who also played the bass, guitar, keyboard, and drums. He won three Emmy awards, a Grammy award, and the ASCAP Pop Music Award. He was nominated for Academy, Tony, and Golden Globe awards. Schlesinger was part of the bands Fountains of Wayne, Ivy, and Tinted Windows. He also wrote songs and produced for the Brooklyn-based synth-pop duo Fever High. He grew up in Manhattan and Montclair, New Jersey. Schlesinger passed away during the COVID-19 pandemic due to complications from the virus.
The Manitoba Liberal Party is a political party in Manitoba, Canada. It started in the late 1800s, after the province was created in 1870.

Jerry Heller, born on October 6, 1940, and died on September 2, 2016, was an American music manager and businessman. He was famous for managing N.W.A and Eazy-E, who were important early rap artists. In the 1960s and 1970s, he helped bring Elton John and Pink Floyd to America for their first big tours. He also worked with many other artists like Journey, Marvin Gaye, and Van Morrison. During the mid-1980s, he worked with R&B and hip-hop artists such as Michel'le and World Class Wreckin' Cru. Heller played a big part in the development of West Coast rap by managing Ruthless Records with Eazy-E and signing artists like N.W.A, the D.O.C., and Bone Thugs-n-Harmony.

Dwijen Sharma was born on May 29, 1929, and died on September 15, 2017. He was a naturalist and science writer from Bangladesh. In 1987, he received the Bangla Academy Literary Award. In 2015, the government of Bangladesh awarded him the Ekushey Padak for his contributions to language and literature.

Patrick Alan Nunelee was an American businessman and politician. He served as a U.S. representative from 2011 until he died in 2015. Before that, he worked in the Mississippi State Senate from 1995 to 2011, representing the 6th district. He belonged to the Republican Party.

Kathleen Marie Ireland, born on March 20, 1963, is an American model and actress who became an author and entrepreneur. She was a supermodel in the 1980s and 1990s, famous for being in 13 straight "Sports Illustrated" swimsuit issues. In 1993, she started a brand marketing company called Kathy Ireland Worldwide (KIWW). Thanks to her business career, she became very rich. By 2015, she had a personal fortune of $420 million. In 2012, products from her company were worth $2 billion.

Atal Bihari Vajpayee, born on December 25, 1924, and died on August 16, 2018, was an Indian leader. He was the Prime Minister of India three times: first for 13 days in 1996, then for 13 months from 1998 to 1999, and finally for a full term from 1999 to 2004. Vajpayee was a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the first BJP leader to complete a full term as Prime Minister. He was also a poet and writer. Vajpayee was in the Indian Parliament for more than 50 years, elected ten times to the Lok Sabha and twice to the Rajya Sabha. He represented Lucknow and left politics in 2009 because of health problems. He was one of the founders of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh (BJS), which later became the BJP. Vajpayee was the BJP's first president from 1968 to 1972. In 1977, he became the Minister of External Affairs when Morarji Desai was Prime Minister. He left this job in 1979, and the government ended soon after. Vajpayee was among those who started the BJP in 1980. During his time as Prime Minister, India did some important tests in 1998. Vajpayee tried to befriend Pakistan by traveling to Lahore in a bus in 1999 to meet Nawaz Sharif. After the Kargil War in 1999, Vajpayee met with Pervez Musharraf to improve relations and invited him to Agra for a summit. In 2014, Narendra Modi's government said December 25, Vajpayee's birthday, would be Good Governance Day. In 2015, Vajpayee was given India's highest honor, the Bharat Ratna, by President Pranab Mukherjee. Vajpayee passed away in 2018 due to old age.

Mashhad, also spelled Masht or Meshad, is the second-largest city in Iran and the capital of Khorasan-e Razavi province. It is located in the northeast of the country. In 2016, it had a population of 3,001,184, including Mashhad Taman and Torqabeh areas. The city is famous for the shrine of Imam Reza, the eighth Shia Imam, who was buried there. Many pilgrims visit this shrine every year. The Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid is also buried there. Mashhad has been ruled by different groups over time. During the Mongol period, it was quite prosperous. The city is also called the City of Ferdowsi, after the Iranian poet who wrote the "Shahnameh." Some important Iranian poets and artists, such as Mehdi Akhavan-Sales and Mohammad-Reza Shajarian, come from Mashhad. Ferdowsi and Akhavan-Sales are buried in Tus, an ancient city near Mashhad. On October 30, 2009, Iran's president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad declared Mashhad as "Iran's spiritual capital."

Angalifu (pronounced "ang-uh-leef-oo") was a northern white rhinoceros. He lived from around 1970 until December 14, 2014. At the time of his death, there were only six northern white rhinoceroses left in the world. Angalifu was one of two male rhinoceroses alive, and the only one in North America. He lived longer than his male friend Sudan, but not as long as females Najin and Fatu. Angalifu was born in the wild around 1970. He was captured and taken to the Khartoum Zoo in Sudan. In 1990, he was moved to the San Diego Zoo Safari Park. He lived there until he died of old age in 2014, at 44 years old.

Central Connecticut State University (CCSU) is a public university in New Britain, Connecticut. It was founded in 1849 as the State Normal School and is Connecticut's oldest publicly funded university. CCSU has four schools: the Ammon College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences, the School of Business, the School of Education and Professional Studies, and the School of Engineering, Science, and Technology. CCSU has 11,822 students, including 9,546 undergraduates and 2,276 graduate students. More than half of the students live off-campus, and 96 percent are Connecticut residents. The university is part of the Connecticut State Colleges and Universities system, which includes Eastern, Western, and Southern Connecticut State Universities. Together, these universities have a combined student body of 32,722.

The House of Savoy is a royal family that began in 1003 in a place called Savoy. Over time, the family became more powerful. They started by ruling a small area north of Italy and eventually controlled the Kingdom of Sicily from 1713 to 1720. After that, they got to rule Sardinia directly. From a branch called Savoy-Carignano, the House of Savoy helped Italy become united in 1861. They ruled Italy as kings from 1861 until 1946. They also briefly ruled Spain in the 1800s. The kings of Italy from the House of Savoy were Victor Emmanuel II, Umberto I, Victor Emmanuel III, and Umberto II. Umberto II was king for only a few weeks before Italy became a republic after a vote in 1946.

In 1976, voters in the Democratic Party chose their candidate for the U.S. presidential election. Former Georgia governor Jimmy Carter won. This was decided through primary elections and caucuses. The final selection happened at the 1976 Democratic National Convention in New York City, which took place from July 12 to July 15.

Georg Solti, born György Stern in Budapest on October 21, 1912, was a Hungarian-born British conductor. He is best known for his work with opera companies in Munich, Frankfurt, and London, and as the music director of the Chicago Symphony Orchestra for many years. Born in Budapest, he studied music with Béla Bartók, Leó Weiner, and Ernesto Dohnányi. In the 1930s, he worked as a répétiteur at the Hungarian State Opera and at the Salzburg Festival with Arturo Toscanini. His career was interrupted when he fled Hungary in 1938 due to increasing anti-Jewish laws. He found refuge in Switzerland during World War II, where he worked as a pianist. In 1946, he became the musical director of the Bavarian State Opera in Munich. In 1952, he moved to Frankfurt, where he remained until 1961. He became a citizen of West Germany in 1953. In 1961, he became the musical director of the Royal Opera Company in London, improving its standards. He became a British citizen in 1972. From 1969 to 1991, he was the music director of the Chicago Symphony Orchestra. He also served as the music director of the Orchestre de Paris from 1972 to 1975 and the principal conductor of the London Philharmonic Orchestra from 1979 to 1983. Known for his intense performances early in his career, Solti's conducting style became more mellow later. He recorded many works multiple times and made over 250 recordings, including the famous complete set of Wagner's "Ring des Nibelungen." His "Ring" recordings were voted the greatest ever made in polls by Gramophone magazine in 1999 and the BBC's Music Magazine in 2012. Solti received numerous Grammy Awards during his career. He passed away on September 5, 1997.

Justin Wakeland High School is a public high school in Frisco, Texas. It is a 5A school according to the University Interscholastic League. It belongs to the Frisco Independent School District and is one of ten high schools in the district. The school opened in 2006. Most sophomores and juniors came from Frisco High School because the city and district expanded. New freshmen usually come from Griffin Middle School, Cobb Middle School, and some from Staley Middle School. In 2015, the school met standards set by the Texas Education Agency.

An oil is a thick, liquid substance that does not mix with water and mixes with other oils. Oils have a lot of carbon and hydrogen and can catch fire easily. They also help things stick to surfaces. Most oils are made from fats and are liquid at room temperature. Oils can come from animals, plants, or oil drilled from the ground. Some oils are easy to evaporate, while others are not. People use oils for many things. For food, there is olive oil. For heating, there is heating oil. Some oils, like mineral oil, are used for medicine. Motor oil helps machines move smoothly. Oils are also used to make paints and plastics. In some religions, special oils are used in ceremonies to make them pure.

Roberto Farias was born on March 27, 1932, and passed away on May 14, 2018. He was a Brazilian film director, producer, and screenwriter. During his career, he directed 15 films. His 1982 film "Pra Frente, Brasil" was shown at the 33rd Berlin International Film Festival. Farias's brother, named Reginaldo Faria (his surname originally had no 's'), is also a film director and actor.
Bollène (in Provencal, "bouleno") is a town in the Vaucluse department, which is in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region of southern France.

Sarrebourg is a town in the Moselle department, in Grand Est, northeastern France. It is near the upper part of the Saar River. In 1895, a place where ancient people worshipped was found in Sarrebourg at the entrance to a path from the Vosges mountains.

Keminmaa is a municipality in Finland. The municipality has a population of ( ). It covers an area of which is water. The population density is not specified. Neighboring municipalities are Kemi, Simo, Tervola, and Tornio.

Noel George Williams, born on September 19, 1943, and better known as King Sporty, was a DJ, reggae musician, and record producer. He worked for the Tashamba and Konduko labels. King Sporty is famous for writing the song "Buffalo Soldier," which became popular because of Bob Marley.

In Norse cosmology, Niflheim, which means "world of mist," is a location that sometimes overlaps with Niflhel and Hel. The name "Niflheim" is found in two sources: "Gylfaginning" and "Hrafnagaldr Óðins." Niflheim was mainly a cold and icy realm, with frozen rivers like Élivágar and the well of Hvergelmir from which all rivers came. According to "Gylfaginning," Niflheim was one of two primordial realms that came from Ginnungagap, the space between ice and fire. The other realm was Muspelheim, the realm of fire. The creation began when the waters from Niflheim mixed with the heat from Muspelheim, forming a "creating steam." Later, Niflheim became the home of Hel, a goddess and daughter of Loki. It was also the afterlife for people who did not die a heroic or notable death.
A sloppy Joe is a sandwich made with ground beef or pork, onions, tomato sauce or ketchup, and seasonings. It is served on a hamburger bun. This dish came from the United States in the early 1900s.
Paul Malékou was born on November 17, 1938. He became the foreign minister of Gabon in 1968. He was born in Fougamou, Gabon. From 1975 to 1983, he worked as the director-general of Asecna.

The Reinheitsgebot is a set of rules about beer ingredients in Germany. It limits what can be used. The most famous version was made in Bavaria in 1516. However, similar rules existed before 1516. Modern rules are different from the 1516 Bavarian ones.

John "Ace" Cannon, born on May 5, 1934, and died on December 6, 2018, was an American musician who played the tenor and alto saxophone. He performed and toured with Bill Black's band from Hi Records, and later began his solo career in 1961. His first solo album, "Tuff," reached number 17 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 in 1962. The following year, his single "Blues (Stay Away from Me)" climbed to number 36. In April 1965, he released "Ace Cannon Live," recorded in Hi's studio with a live audience, which Pesce claims was the first album of its kind. Cannon was honored by being inducted into both the Rock and Soul Hall of Fame and the Rockabilly Hall of Fame in 2000. In 2007, his hometown, Calhoun City, Mississippi, celebrated the first annual Ace Cannon Festival. He was also inducted into the Mississippi Musicians Hall of Fame in 2008. After traveling and entertaining fans worldwide for many years, he moved back to Calhoun City in the late 1980s, where he lived until his death. Ace Cannon passed away at his home on December 6, 2018, at the age of 84.

an Buruk, born on October 19, 1973, is a Turkish football manager and former player. He currently manages Istanbul Başakşehir in Süper Lig. As a midfielder, he played for Galatasaray, Inter Milan, Beşiktaş, and Istanbul B.B. He also played for the Turkey national team 56 times.
George Foster Peabody was an American banker and philanthropist. He lived from July 27, 1852, to March 4, 1938.

Michael Corbett Shannon, born on August 7, 1974, is an American actor, producer, director, and musician. He was nominated twice for the Academy Award for best supporting actor for his roles in "Revolutionary Road" (2008) and "Nocturnal Animals" (2016). Shannon was also nominated for a Screen Actors Guild award and a Golden Globe for his role in "99 Homes" (2014), and received a Tony Award nomination for best featured actor in a play for "Long Day's Journey into Night" (2016). He started his acting career in 1993 with "Groundhog Day" and gained more recognition for his role in "8 Mile" (2002). Shannon can play different types of roles, from comedies to dramas. Some of his films include "Pearl Harbor" (2001), "Bad Boys II" (2003), "Bug" (2006), "Before the Devil Knows You're Dead" (2007), "The Black Dahlia" (2006), "The Iceman" (2012), "Premium Rush" (2012), "Man of Steel" (2013), "The Shape of Water" (2017), and "Knives Out" (2019). He often works with director Jeff Nichols, appearing in all his films: "Shotgun Stories" (2007), "Take Shelter" (2011), "Mud" (2012), "Midnight Special," and "Loving" (both 2016). Shannon is also famous for his role as Nelson Van Alden in the HBO series "Boardwalk Empire" (2010–2014), for which he was nominated for three Screen Actors Guild awards.

Osama Bin Laden, the founder of Al-Qaeda, was killed on May 2, 2011, in Pakistan. The operation began around 20:00 UTC on May 1 and was carried out by U.S. Navy SEALs. The SEALs worked with other special forces from the CIA and JSOC. Bin Laden was found in Abbottabad, Pakistan. After his death, his body was taken to Afghanistan for identification and was later buried at sea. Al-Qaeda confirmed his death and vowed revenge. Some groups in Pakistan also vowed retaliation. Most Americans supported the operation, but many in Pakistan and some others criticized it. There were questions about whether Bin Laden should have been captured alive, and no evidence was shown to the public. Pakistan formed a commission to investigate the incident, which revealed the military and intelligence had failed to find Bin Laden for nine years. The report was leaked to Al Jazeera in 2013.

Suzy Delair, born Suzette Pierrette Delaire on December 31, 1917, and passed away on March 15, 2020, was a French actress, dancer, singer, and comedian who performed in vaudeville shows.

Gary Charles Peters Sr., born on December 1, 1958, is an American politician. He has been a U.S. senator from Michigan since 2015. A Democrat, he was a U.S. representative from 2013 to 2015. The district he represented included parts of Detroit and other cities. Before Congress, Peters worked in the Navy, was an investment advisor for 22 years, and taught for a short time. He was on the Rochester Hills city council from 1991 to 1995 and served in the Michigan Senate from 1995 to 2002. In 2002, he ran for Michigan attorney general but lost. Peters then worked as a lottery commissioner from 2003 to 2008. He quit this job to run for Congress. In 2014, Peters was elected to the U.S. Senate seat. He won the Democratic primary and beat the Republican candidate in the general election. He was the only new Democrat to win a Senate election that year.
A playwright writes plays.

A text editor is a computer program used to change plain text. Some people call these programs "notepad" software, like Microsoft Notepad. Text editors come with operating systems and are used in software development. They can be used to edit files, such as configuration files, documentation files, and programming code.

Hans Gericke was a German architect and urban planner. He worked as the deputy director from 1953 to 1958 for the Institutes for the Theory and History of Architecture at the German Academy of Architecture. In 1965, he became the chief architect of East Berlin in East Germany. This city is now called Berlin, Germany. Many organizations honored him for his work. He was born in Magdeburg, Province of Saxony, in the Prussian part of the German Empire. Gericke died on February 15, 2014, at the age of 101.

UNSW is a public research university in Sydney, Australia. It is called UNSW Sydney since 2017. In 2012, it had the highest ATAR scores in New South Wales and attracted many top students. The university started in 1949. In 2020, it was ranked 4th in Australia and 43rd in the world. It has nine faculties and offers bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees. Its main campus is in Kensington, near Sydney's city center. Some parts of the university, like the Creative Arts Faculty, UNSW Art & Design, are in Paddington. The UNSW Canberra campus is at the Australian Defence Force Academy in Canberra. There are also subcampuses in the Sydney CBD, Randwick, and Coogee. Research stations are spread across New South Wales. UNSW is part of the Group of Eight, a group of top research universities in Australia, and Universitas 21, a global network of universities. It works with over 200 universities worldwide.
Sigourney is a city in Keokuk County, Iowa, United States. In 2010, it had 2,059 people. The city is also the county seat of Keokuk County.

Hurricane Maria was a very strong category 5 hurricane that hit Dominica, St. Croix, and Puerto Rico in September 2017. It caused a lot of damage and was the worst natural disaster in recorded history for those islands. Maria was also the deadliest Atlantic hurricane since 2004. It was one of the ten strongest Atlantic hurricanes and the strongest tropical cyclone globally in 2017. It was the 13th named storm, the 8th consecutive hurricane, the 4th major hurricane, the 2nd category 5 hurricane, and the deadliest storm of the very active 2017 Atlantic hurricane season. At its strongest, the hurricane caused huge destruction and many deaths in the northeastern Caribbean. This made recovery harder in areas already damaged by Hurricane Irma. The total damage was estimated at over $91.61 billion, mainly in Puerto Rico, ranking it as the third-costliest tropical cyclone on record. Maria began as a tropical wave and became a tropical storm on September 16, east of the Lesser Antilles. Favorable weather conditions let the storm quickly get stronger as it approached the islands. Maria became a category 5 hurricane just before hitting Dominica on September 18, the first category 5 hurricane to strike the island. It weakened slightly after hitting Dominica but reached its strongest point over the eastern Caribbean with winds of 175 mph and a pressure of 908 mbar. On September 20, an eye wall replaced the hurricane's core, weakening it to a high-end category 4 hurricane when it hit Puerto Rico. Further interaction with land weakened the hurricane, but it regained some strength after moving northeast of the Bahamas. Moving slowly north, Maria gradually weakened to a tropical storm on September 28. Embedded in the westerlies, it accelerated eastward, becoming extratropical on September 30 and dissipating by October 2. Maria caused terrible damage across Dominica, leaving communication networks down. Most buildings and infrastructure were destroyed, and much of the island's vegetation was cleared. Guadeloupe and Martinique also faced widespread flooding, damaged roofs, and uprooted trees. Puerto Rico suffered catastrophic damage and a major humanitarian crisis; most of its population faced flooding and a lack of resources, made worse by slow relief efforts. The storm caused the worst electrical blackout in U.S. history, and in June 2018, thousands of homes and businesses still had no power. Maria was the third consecutive major hurricane to hit the Leeward Islands in two weeks, following Hurricane Irma, which hit several islands, and Hurricane Jose, which passed close by, bringing strong winds to Barbuda. In August 2018, Puerto Rico revised its official death toll from 64 to 2,975, making the total death toll 3,059: around 2,975 died in Puerto Rico, 65 in Dominica, 5 in the Dominican Republic, 4 in Guadeloupe, 4 in the contiguous United States, 3 in the U.S. Virgin Islands, and 3 in Haiti. Maria was the deadliest hurricane in Dominica since 1834 and the deadliest in Puerto Rico since 1899. The initial death count in Puerto Rico was 64 but was revised after studies estimated between 1,400 and 5,740 deaths. The official estimate of 2,975 deaths is based on a study commissioned by the Puerto Rico governor, where researchers at George Washington University developed models to estimate excess mortality due to Maria, including both direct and indirect deaths. The discrepancy with the initial death count was due to "lack of awareness of appropriate death certification practices after a natural disaster" among physicians reporting deaths to vital statistic agencies.

The bishop is a piece in chess. Each player starts with two bishops. One bishop is placed between the knight and the king. The other bishop is placed between the queen and the knight. For white, the starting squares are c1 and f1. For black, the starting squares are c8 and f8.

Alexander Pope (born May 21, 1688, died May 30, 1744) is considered one of the best English poets, especially from the early 1700s. He is famous for writing satirical and conversational poetry like "The Rape of the Lock," "The Dunciad," and "An Essay on Criticism," and for translating Homer's works. After Shakespeare, Pope is the second most quoted writer in English, with some of his poems becoming common sayings (e.g., "damning with faint praise"). He was very skilled in the heroic couplet. Pope faced many challenges in his life. He and his family were Catholics, which brought them trouble. After King James II left the throne, laws restricted their activities, stopping them from living near London and attending school or university. Pope mostly educated himself, with his aunt teaching him to read and learn languages like French, Italian, Latin, and Greek. At six, he discovered Homer. As a child, he survived being trampled by a cow but later struggled with a serious health condition that troubled him his whole life. In 1709, Pope published "Pastorals," his first major poems, which made him famous. By age 23, he had written "An Essay on Criticism," which was well-received. This essay helped him make friends like Joseph Addison and Richard Steele, who worked on "The Spectator." Critic John Dennis was upset with Pope and disliked him for the rest of his life. Dennis and Pope often criticized each other in their writings. In 1712, Pope wrote "The Rape of the Lock." The poem was inspired by a real incident where Lord Petre cut a lock of Miss Arabella Fermor's hair. Pope used this as a subject for a witty, playful epic that highlighted issues like individualism and consumerism. In 1717, a collection of Pope's poems was published, including new poems about love. Pope never married but had strong connections with Lady M. Montagu and Martha Blount. He wrote popular poems about both. Pope was known for his sharp satires. He made enemies among critics, politicians, and other important figures. In his later years, he mostly revised and expanded his work "The Dunciad." He died in 1744, saying he was dying from many good symptoms.
Macaye is a commune in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department, which is in southwestern France.

Victor Amadeus II, born on May 14, 1666, and died on October 31, 1732, ruled as Duke of Savoy from 1675 to 1730. He also had other titles, like Marquis of Saluzzo and Prince of Piedmont. Louis XIV planned his marriage to keep French influence in Savoy, but Victor Amadeus broke away later. When he became duke, his mother, Marie Jeanne Baptiste of Nemours, acted as regent. She lost power in 1684. Victor Amadeus fought in a war and in 1713 became King of Sicily. He had to give this up and instead became King of Sardinia. He left art and buildings in Turin, including new palaces and a church.

Antonio Maceda Francés was born on May 16, 1957. He is a retired Spanish footballer. Even though he was a central defender, he was famous for scoring goals. He began his career with Sporting de Gijón and ended with Real Madrid. He suffered a lot from injuries at Real Madrid. Maceda played for Spain nearly 40 times. He also represented Spain in two World Cups and Euro 1984.

Johan Cédric Micoud, born on July 24, 1973, is a former French professional footballer. He mostly played as an attacking midfielder. People thought he was a skilled midfielder and very good at taking corners and free kicks. Micoud played for 16 years professionally. He played in Italy and Germany, besides France. He also wore the French national team jersey 20 times. Micoud helped France in the 2002 World Cup and Euro 2000, and France won the Euro 2000 tournament.

The Delaware River is a big river on the east coast of the United States. It flows through four states: Delaware, New Jersey, New York, and Pennsylvania. The river starts in the Catskill Mountains in New York and goes into Delaware Bay. Its water then enters the Atlantic Ocean near Cape May in New Jersey and Cape Henlopen in Delaware. Not including Delaware Bay, the river is long. The Delaware River is part of the "Great Waters" recognized by the America's Great Waters Coalition. It has two main branches that start in the Catskill Mountains in New York. One branch starts near Mount Jefferson and the other at Grand Gorge. The branches join near Hancock and then flow south. The river forms borders between states and meets the tide at Falls of the Delaware. It helped the growth of cities like Philadelphia and Camden by being used for shipping. Before European settlers arrived, the Lenape Native Americans lived near the river. They called it Lenapewihittuk or the largest river in their land. In 1609, a Dutch expedition led by Henry Hudson visited the river. Hudson’s discoveries helped Dutch colonization of North America in the 17th century. Early Dutch and Swedish settlers lived along the lower part of the river and called it the "South River." After the English took control in 1664, the river was renamed "Delaware" after Sir Thomas West, 3rd Baron De La Warr, who was the first royal governor of the Virginia colony.

Noam Chomsky, born on December 7, 1928, is an American linguist, philosopher, and political activist. He is often called "the father of modern linguistics" and is a major figure in analytic philosophy. Chomsky is also one of the founders of cognitive science. He teaches at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the University of Arizona. He has written over 100 books on topics like linguistics, politics, and war. Chomsky was born to Jewish immigrants in Philadelphia. He was interested in anarchism from young age, influenced by alternative bookstores in New York. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania and later developed the theory of transformational grammar, earning his doctorate in 1955. That year, he started teaching at MIT, and in 1957, he published "Syntactic Structures," a book that changed how language is studied. From 1958 to 1959, he was a fellow at the Institute for Advanced Study. Chomsky created or helped create several theories, including universal grammar, generative grammar, the Chomsky hierarchy, and the minimalist program. He was against linguistic behaviorism, especially the work of B. F. Skinner. In 1967, Chomsky wrote "The Responsibility of Intellectuals," which opposed U.S. involvement in the Vietnam War. He was arrested for his activism and was on President Richard Nixon's enemies list. He continued his work in linguistics and also became involved in the linguistics wars. With Edward S. Herman, he wrote "Manufacturing Consent," a book on media criticism. Chomsky also supported efforts to stop the Indonesian occupation of East Timor. Chomsky has taught at the University of Arizona since 2017. He is one of the most cited scholars alive, influencing many academic fields. He has criticized U.S. foreign policy, neoliberalism, and state capitalism. His ideas are important in the anti-capitalist and anti-imperialist movements, but he has also faced criticism.

Frederick Nelson Pyatt, born on September 9, 1953, is a former professional ice hockey player from Canada. He was born in Port Arthur, Ontario. In 1973, Pyatt was chosen by the Detroit Red Wings of the National Hockey League and the Minnesota Fighting Saints of the World Hockey Association. He also played for the Washington Capitals and Colorado Rockies. Pyatt is the father of Jesse and former NHL players Tom and Taylor Pyatt.
Higden is a town in Cleburne County, Arkansas, United States. In 2010, the town had 120 people.

The health services functional constituency, formerly known as the health constituency, is part of Hong Kong's Legislative Council elections. It was first created for the 1988 Legislative Council election. This group includes health-related professionals. It has one of the bigger groups of voters among functional constituencies. The pro-democracy camp has held the seat since it was created.
Plougastel-Daoulas is a commune in Finistère, which is in Brittany, a region in northwestern France.

Hara Pattanaik, also known as Hari Patnaik, was born on October 12, 1958, and passed away on January 13, 2015. He was an Odia film actor, director, and writer. Pattanaik acted in more than 60 Odia movies and directed about 19 films. He helped introduce other actors like Anubhav Mohanty, Sabyasachi Mishra, and Babushaan. Pattanaik died because of cancer.

Wandsworth is a borough in southwest London. It is part of inner London. Wandsworth is next to Lambeth to the east, Merton and Kingston upon Thames to the south, Richmond upon Thames to the west, and across the River Thames, it borders Hammersmith and Fulham, Kensington and Chelsea, and Westminster. Wandsworth's local government is the Wandsworth London Borough Council.

The Pauline epistles, also known as Paul's letters, are thirteen books in the New Testament that some people think Paul wrote. However, the authorship of a few is unsure. These letters are some of the earliest Christian documents and give insight into early Christian beliefs and problems. As part of the New Testament's canon, they are important for Christian teachings and ethics. The letter to the Hebrews, though not named after Paul, was traditionally seen as written by him. But since the 16th century, most people believe it was not. Paul probably wrote seven letters, but four are likely fake (Ephesians, First Timothy, Second Timothy, Titus). Two others (Second Thessalonians, Colossians) are questionable. Some think Paul used a secretary to help write these letters. In most modern Bibles, Paul's letters come after the Acts of the Apostles and before the Catholic epistles. But some early Greek manuscripts put the general epistles first and the Pauline epistles last.

Halloween is an American horror series with eleven films, plus novels, comic books, merchandise, and a video game. The films mainly focus on Michael Myers, a serial killer who was put in a sanitarium as a child for killing his sister, Judith. Fifteen years later, Michael escapes to stalk and kill people in the fictional town of Haddonfield, Illinois, on Halloween. The original "Halloween," made in 1978, was written by John Carpenter and Debbie Hill, and directed by Carpenter. This film inspired many other scary movies. Eight more sequels followed. Michael Myers is the main bad guy in all the films except one. In 2007, Rob Zombie made a remake of the 1978 film. A sequel to this remake came out two years later. In 2018, a new film was released that continues the original story. In 2019, it was announced that two more films would follow the 2018 movie, called "Halloween Kills" and "Halloween Ends," which will come out in 2021 and 2022. The films earned over $640 million worldwide. The original film and the 2018 sequel got good reviews, but the other films were mixed or not well-received by both fans and critics.

Francis George Steiner, FBA (born April 23, 1929, died February 3, 2020), was a French-American who wrote about literature, language, and society. He also wrote about the effects of the Holocaust. People praised him as a "polyglot and polymath." A. S. Byatt, an English novelist, said he was like a "late, late, late renaissance man" and a "European metaphysician with an instinct for the driving ideas of our time." Harriet Harvey-Wood, who used to run literature at the British Council, said Steiner was a "great lecturer" who would give talks without notes. Steiner taught at the University of Geneva (1974-1994), University of Oxford (1994-1995), Harvard University (2001-2002), and was an extraordinary fellow at Churchill College, Cambridge, since 1969.

Anseba region is one of six administrative areas in northern Eritrea. Its capital and biggest city is Keren. The region gets its name from the Anseba River, which flows through most of it. The area has an average elevation, and May is the hottest month with temperatures reaching up to 40°C. The coldest months are December to February, when it can get very cold. It rains about 600 mm annually, which is good for farming. As of 2005, Anseba region had about 549,000 people, up from 484,200 in 2001, with a growth rate of 11.80 percent. The region covers 23,200 square kilometers, making a population density of 23.66 people per square kilometer. The country and region are governed by the People's Front for Democracy and Justice (PFDJ), which was originally called the Eritrean Liberation Front. Elections are held regularly, but only the PFDJ can contest them. Women and men of all ethnic and religious backgrounds can vote.

Jamstik is a brand of portable, app-connected guitars made by Zivix, a music technology company in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The guitars are made in the United States, designed in Minneapolis and produced by a contract manufacturer in South Dakota.

The House of Windsor is the royal family ruling the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth realms. In 1901, King Edward VII, who was the son of Queen Victoria and Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha, became the king after the House of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha took over the British throne from the House of Hanover. In 1917, to avoid negative feelings towards Germany during World War I, the royal family changed their name from Saxe-Coburg and Gotha to Windsor. Four British monarchs from the House of Windsor have ruled since then: George V, Edward VIII, George VI, and Elizabeth II. The current head of the family is the monarch of sixteen countries, including the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Jamaica, Barbados, the Bahamas, Grenada, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Tuvalu, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Belize, Antigua and Barbuda, and Saint Kitts and Nevis. There are also three crown dependencies, fourteen British overseas territories, and two associated states of New Zealand.

Kimberley Gail Marsh, born on June 13, 1976, is an English actress and presenter. She became famous in 2001 when she won a spot in the band Hear'say by appearing on a reality TV show called "Popstars." Hear'say had some success, with two UK number-one singles and an album that topped the charts. In 2002, Marsh left the band to pursue a solo career. She released an album called "Standing Tall" in 2003, which reached number nine in the UK charts and produced two top-ten singles. From 2006 to 2019, she played Michelle Connor in the TV show "Coronation Street" on ITV. She won awards for her acting, including Best Newcomer at the 2007 British Soap Awards and the 2007 National Television Awards. In 2010, she competed on "Popstar to Operastar," a show where famous pop stars learned to sing opera, and came in fourth place.

WWE Raw is a professional wrestling TV show that airs on Monday nights from 8:00 to 11:00 PM EST on USA Network in the United States. It is also called Monday Night Raw or simply Raw. The show is part of a brand where WWE workers perform. It started on January 11, 1993, and is one of the main WWE shows, along with Friday Night Smackdown. WWE Raw is the longest-running weekly TV program. In 2000, Raw moved from USA Network to Spike TV, which used to be TNN. Raw came back to USA Network in 2005 and is still there. As of December 9, 2016, you can watch all Raw episodes on the WWE Network. New episodes are available for 30 days after they air. Since the first episode, Raw has been broadcast live in 208 different places, in 171 cities, towns, and 11 countries: the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Afghanistan, Iraq, South Africa, Germany, Japan, Italy, and Mexico.

The Animals are an English band that plays rhythm and blues and rock music. They formed in Newcastle upon Tyne in the early 1960s. In 1964, they moved to London after becoming famous. They were known for their strong, blues-like sound and a deep-voiced singer named Eric Burdon. Their most famous song was "House of the Rising Sun," which was also popular in the United States. They also made other hits like "We Got to Get Out of This Place," "It's My Life," "Inside Looking Out," "I'm Crying," and "Don't Let Me Be Misunderstood." The band made both tough rock songs and rhythm and blues music. They were part of a group of British bands that became popular in the United States. Throughout the 1960s, the band changed members and had problems with their managers. In the late 1960s, they performed as Eric Burdon and the Animals in California and made hits like "San Francisco Nights," "When I Was Young," and "Sky Pilot." Eventually, the band broke up. The original members, including Eric Burdon, Alan Price, Chas Chandler, Hilton Valentine, and John Steel, reunited once for a concert in Newcastle in 1968. They had brief reunions in 1975 and 1983. Since then, different members have come together under different names. The Animals were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1994.

Salt Lake County is in Utah, U.S. In 2010, it had about 1,029,655 people, and as of July 1, 2019, it had around 1,160,437, making it Utah's most populous county. Its main city, Salt Lake City, is both the county seat and the state capital. Salt Lake County was created in 1850. It is the 37th most populous county in the U.S., and along with Denver County, El Paso County in Colorado, and Clark County in Nevada, it's one of the few counties in the Rocky Mountains in the top 100. Salt Lake County is also one of the largest counties in Utah, with a population of 700,000 or more. It covers the Salt Lake Valley and parts of the surrounding mountains, including the Oquirrh Mountains to the west and the Wasatch Range to the east. The northwestern part of the county includes some of Great Salt Lake. Salt Lake County is famous for its ski resorts, and Salt Lake City hosted the 2002 Winter Olympics. Salt Lake County is the central part of the Salt Lake City metropolitan area.

Charles Edward Daniels, born on October 28, 1936, and died on July 6, 2020, was an American singer, songwriter, and musician. He was famous for his music in southern rock, country, and bluegrass. He is most known for his country music hit "The Devil Went Down to Georgia." Daniels began his singing and musical career in the 1950s. He was honored when he was added to the Cheyenne Frontier Days Hall of Fame in 2002, the Grand Ole Opry in 2008, the Musicians Hall of Fame and Museum in 2009, and the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2016.

Sirdavidia is a type of flowering plant. It belongs to the annonaceae family. It was described on February 4, 2015. It was discovered by Thomas L.P. Couvreur from France's Institute of Research for Development, Raoul Niangadouma from the Herbier National du Gabon, Bonaventure Sonké from the University of Yaoundé, and Hervé Sauquet from Université Paris-Sud. The plant was named after Sir David Attenborough. The specific species called Sirdavidia solannona was found in Gabon's Crystal Mountains National Park on November 15, 2013. It was found between 300 and 600 meters above sea level. The name "solannona" was chosen because the flowers look like those of "solanum" plants.
Angkaliya Curtis, born around 1928, is an Australian Aboriginal artist. She paints animals from the central Australian desert.
32 is the number that comes after 31 and before 33.

La Bollène-Vésubie is a town in the Alpes-Maritimes department of Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur in southeastern France. The people who live there are called bollénois. In the Niçois dialect of langue d'oc, the town is called La Boulèna, and the people are called lu boulenasc.

Silent Hill: Downpour is a survival horror video game. Vatra Games made it, and Konami Digital Entertainment published it. It's the eighth game in the Silent Hill series and came out in March 2012. The game is set in Silent Hill, a made-up American town. The story follows a man named Murphy Pendleton, who goes to the town and enters a different world. He uncovers hidden memories. The game is played from a third-person view and in 3D. Critics had mixed opinions. They liked the scary atmosphere and the story. But they thought the monster designs and combat could be better. They also had issues with the game's performance. Since its release, a fix has improved these problems.

Toypurina lived from 1760 to 1799. She was a medicine woman from the Tongva nation, also called Gabrieliño. This name came from their connection to San Gabriel Mission. Toypurina was against Spanish missionaries who came to California. In 1785, she planned a rebellion against San Gabriel Mission. She recruited people from six of the eight villages involved in the attack.

Wii Music is a music video game made by Nintendo for the Wii. It came out in Japan and North America in October 2008, and in Europe and Australia a month later. This game is part of the Touch! Generations and Wii series. In Wii Music, players control a virtual band. They choose instruments and play by moving the Wii Remote and Nunchuk. Unlike games like Guitar Hero or Rock Band, there's no scoring; players can experiment with different ways to play songs. Nintendo advertised Wii Music as a way to experience music without expensive lessons at home. It was one of the first games shown for the Wii, being playable at E3 in 2006, and then presented more in 2008. Reviews were mixed to positive. It scored 64.34% on Gamerankings and 63 on Metacritic. Criticism was about its simple gameplay, not very precise controls, and its use of mostly public-domain music. It's seen as the least successful game in the Wii series, selling 2.65 million copies worldwide by March 2009.

Uses and gratifications theory (UGT) helps understand why and how people choose specific media to meet their needs. This theory looks at what people do with media rather than what media does to people. Media is a common product, and audiences are its users. UGT is a way to understand media use from the audience's point of view. It assumes that people are active in choosing media to satisfy their needs, like gaining knowledge, relaxing, socializing, having fun, or escaping. Unlike some other theories, UGT says audiences are responsible for selecting media that give them satisfaction. Media companies compete with other sources for viewers' attention. UGt gives communication experts a view to understand how and why people choose media.

Liberty X, originally called Liberty, was a British-Irish group with members Michelle Heaton, Tony Lundon, Kevin Simm, Jessica Taylor, and Kelli Young. The group formed after the five contestants from the TV show "Popstars" who didn't join Hear'say. Liberty X had ten big hits in the UK and some popular songs worldwide. Their first album, "Thinking It Over," came out in May 2002. It had a big hit called "Just a Little." Their second album, "Being Somebody," released in November 2003, didn't do as well. The group stopped performing after sales went down, but they made a final album called "X" in October 2005. Liberty X broke up in early 2007, but not officially, because they were still popular. In 2008, they performed together one last time in Belfast. In 2012, Liberty X reunited for a TV show called "The Big Reunion." The show aired from January to March 2013, leading up to a big concert at the Hammersmith Apollo in February. Tony Lundon said this would be their last performance together. After the show, the group announced they had a new management company, 365 Artists Management, for their future plans.

'Splosion Man is a 2.5D action platform game made by Twisted Pixel Games for the Xbox 360. You can download it from Xbox Live Arcade. It came out on July 22, 2009, during the 2009 Xbox Live Summer of Arcade. In the game, you control 'Splosion Man, who can explode himself. He needs to go through obstacles and traps to exit the laboratory called Big Science. Players liked 'Splosion Man so much that it was voted the best original game for Xbox Live Arcade in 2009. IGN ranked it 11th among the top 25 Xbox Live Arcade games ever. In 2009, it sold 13th in overall sales and by the end of 2011, over 487,000 copies had been sold. A sequel called 'Ms. Splosion Man' was released on July 13, 2011.

Hanau is a town in the Main-Kinzig-Kreis, in Hesse, Germany. It is 25 km east of Frankfurt am Main and part of the Frankfurt Rhine-Main region. Hanau is a major transport center because of its railway station and port on the River Main. The town is famous for being the birthplace of the Grimm brothers and Franciscus Sylvius. Since the 16th century, it was a center for working with precious metals, with many goldsmiths. Hanau is also home to Heraeus, one of Germany's largest family-owned companies. During World War II, Hanau lost much of its old buildings. In 1945, a British air raid caused a firestorm, killing one-sixth of the remaining population and destroying 98 percent of the old city and 80 percent of the town overall. In 1963, Hanau hosted the third Hessentag state festival. Until 2005, it was the administrative center of Main-Kinzig-Kreis. On February 19, 2020, a gunman attacked two hookah lounges in Hanau, killing nine people from outside Germany before shooting his mother and himself.

Joseph René Marcel Pronovost, born on June 15, 1930, and passed away on April 26, 2015, was a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman and coach. He played 1,206 games over 20 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL) for the Detroit Red Wings and Toronto Maple Leafs from 1950 to 1970. A top defenceman, he was named to four NHL All-Star teams and played in 11 All-Star games. Pronovost was on four Stanley Cup championship teams with the Red Wings, including the first in 1950. He won another Stanley Cup with the Maple Leafs in 1967. In 1978, he was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame as a player. Pronovost began coaching in 1969. He coached the junior Hull Olympiques and Windsor Spitfires for several seasons. He was the head coach of the Chicago Cougars in the World Hockey Association's first season, 1972-73, and coached 104 games for the Buffalo Sabres between 1977 and 1978. He was also an associate coach for the Red Wings for a short time. From 1990 to 1995, he worked for the NHL Central Scouting Bureau. Pronovost then became a scout for the New Jersey Devils, where he was part of three Stanley Cup championship teams, including the last one in 2003. His 53-year span between his first and last championship is a record for the Stanley Cup.

Barsha Lekhi, born on May 5, 1993, in Saptari, Nepal, is a beauty queen and environmental activist. She won the title of Miss Nepal 2016. In 2016, she also won the Missosology People's Choice Award. She represented Nepal at the Miss International 2016 contest in Japan on October 27, 2016. Barsha studied environmental science at Patan Multiple Campus. She has worked for the Nefin-REDD/CC Partnership Program. Currently, she is studying for her master's degree in environmental science at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

The Standard Model of particle physics describes three of the four fundamental forces in the universe: electromagnetic, weak, and strong interactions. It does not include gravity. This model classifies all known elementary particles and was developed in the latter half of the 20th century by many scientists. By the mid-1970s, the model was fully formed after experiments confirmed the existence of quarks. Later, the discovery of the top quark (1995), the tau neutrino (2000), and the Higgs boson (2012) supported the model further. The model accurately predicts properties of weak neutral currents and the W and Z bosons. While it is believed to be self-consistent and has had great success in making accurate predictions, it does not explain everything. It doesn’t explain why matter predominates over antimatter, doesn’t include gravity, and can't fully explain the universe’s accelerating expansion, which might be due to dark energy. It also doesn’t have a particle that matches all the properties of dark matter observed in the universe. The model doesn’t explain why neutrinos change between types and why they have mass. The development of the Standard Model was driven by both theoretical and experimental physicists. For theorists, the model is a good example of a quantum field theory that shows various phenomena like spontaneous symmetry breaking and non-perturbative behavior. It serves as a basis for creating more complex models that include new particles, extra dimensions, and more elaborate symmetries to explain phenomena not fully covered by the Standard Model, such as dark matter and neutrino oscillations.

Vincenzo Bettiza was born on June 7, 1927, and died on July 28, 2017. He was an Italian novelist, journalist, and politician who was born in Yugoslavia.

Robie Creek is a place in Boise County, Idaho, United States. In 2010, it had 1,162 people living there. Robie Creek has a park with swimming, a play area for children, and a place to launch and dock boats. There are toilet facilities, but no cell phone service.
