In quantum field theory, the Casimir effect and Casimir–Polder force are physical forces caused by a quantized field. These forces were predicted by Dutch physicist Hendrik Casimir in 1948. In 1997, a direct experiment by S. Lamoreaux measured the force to within 5% of the theory's prediction. The Casimir effect happens because conductors and dielectrics change the energy of the electromagnetic field. Since the energy value depends on the shapes and positions of these materials, the Casimir effect results in a force between them. Any material that can support oscillations has a similar effect to the Casimir effect. For example, beads on a string or plates in turbulent water or gas can illustrate this force. In modern physics, the Casimir effect is important in the chiral bag model of nucleons. It is also significant in some aspects of micro- and nanotechnologies.
John Samuel Mbiti was a Kenyan-born Christian philosopher and writer. He was an ordained Anglican priest and a canon.
Babbie is a town in Covington County, Alabama, United States. In 2010, it had 603 people. Babbie became a town in 1957.
The central pier is one of three piers in Blackpool, England. It was built in 1868.

William Friedkin, born on August 29, 1935, is an American director, producer, and screenwriter. He is famous for making movies in the 1970s as part of the "New Hollywood" movement. Starting his career with documentaries in the early 1960s, Friedkin is well-known for directing the action movie "The French Connection" in 1971 and the scary movie "The Exorcist" in 1973. "The French Connection" won five Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Director. "The Exorcist" also got Friedkin nominated for Best Director. Other films he directed include "The Boys in the Band" in 1970, "Sorcerer" in 1977, "Cruising" in 1980, "To Live and Die in L.A." in 1985, "Bug" in 2006, and "Killer Joe" in 2011.

"What I've Done" is a song by Linkin Park. It came out as the first single from their album "Minutes to Midnight" in 2007, and it's the sixth track. The song is in the key of G minor. It was released as a radio single on April 1, 2007, and as a digital download on April 2. A CD single came out on April 30. The live version of "What I've Done" was nominated for "Best Hard Rock Performance" at the 2010 Grammy Awards but didn't win. It also became the main theme of the 2007 science fiction movie "Transformers" and was on the "Minutes to Midnight" album. The song was certified five times platinum by the RIAA, making it Linkin Park's most successful song in terms of sales, even though it might not be the most famous. It was featured in the video game "Guitar Hero World Tour" and later included in a Linkin Park DLC pack for "Rock Band 3" in January 2011. The song is also a bonus track for the UK version of "Iridescent." Currently, an instrumental version of the song is used by Sky UK for their interactive services.

Wittmund is a "landkreis" (district) in northwest Lower Saxony, Germany. It is located in East Frisia, by the North Sea. To the east and clockwise around it are the districts of Friesland, Leer, and Aurich.

A combatant is someone who can fight in a war. The Geneva Conventions, a set of rules, say that soldiers are combatants. They have the right to fight. They can be attacked by the other side because of their role, to stop them from helping their team. If caught, combatants are prisoners of war. All soldiers must follow war rules. Breaking these rules doesn't mean they lose their right to fight or to be treated as prisoners.

Oliver Burgess Meredith (November 16, 1907 – September 9, 1997) was an American actor, director, producer, and writer. He worked for over 60 years and was called "a skilled actor" and "one of the best actors of the century." Meredith was part of the Actors Studio and won several Emmy Awards. He was the first male actor to win the Saturn Award for best supporting actor twice and was nominated for two Academy Awards. Meredith was famous for his roles as George Milton in "Of Mice and Men" (1939), Ernie Pyle in "The Story of G.I. Joe" (1945), and the narrator in "A Walk in the Sun" (1945). He was known later for appearing in "The Twilight Zone" and playing the villain the Penguin in the TV series "Batman" (1960s) and boxing trainer Mickey Goldmill in the "Rocky" films. For his roles in "The Day of the Locust" (1975) and "Rocky" (1976), he was nominated for an Academy Award for best supporting actor. He also starred in comedy films like "Foul Play" (1978) and fantasy movies such as "Clash of the Titans" (1981). Throughout his career, he narrated many films and documentaries, including one in 1983. Meredith also acted in many important plays, like those by Shakespeare, O'Neill, and Beckett.

Melissa Ellen Gilbert, born on May 8, 1964, is an American actress, director, producer, and former president of the Screen Actors Guild. She began acting as a child in the late 1960s, appearing in commercials and TV shows. From 1974 to 1984, she played Laura Ingalls Wilder on the TV series "Little House on the Prairie." During this time, she also appeared in popular TV movies like "The Diary of Anne Frank" and "The Miracle Worker." As an adult, Gilbert continued her acting career in TV movies and made guest appearances. She also did voice work for animations, like playing Barbara Gordon/Batgirl. From 2009 to 2010, she acted in "Little House on the Prairie, the Musical." In 2012, she competed on "Dancing with the Stars." Gilbert was the president of the Screen Actors Guild from 2001 to 2005. Her autobiography, "Prairie Tale: A Memoir," came out in 2009. She also wrote a children's story, "Daisy and Josephine," and a cookbook, "My Prairie Cookbook: Memories and Frontier Food from My Little House to Yours," in 2014. In 2016, Gilbert tried to become a U.S. Representative for Michigan's 8th district as a Democrat but dropped out due to injuries from a 2012 accident.

Eduardo Horacio Laborde was born on October 19, 1967, and died on February 4, 2015. He was an Argentine rugby player. He played three games for the national team, called "Los Pumas," in the 1991 Rugby World Cup. He died in Pinamar, a coastal town, when his bicycle crashed into another vehicle.

Actinium is a chemical element with the symbol Ac and atomic number 89. It was discovered by André-Louis Debierne in 1899. Friedrich Oskar Giesel isolated it later in 1902, but didn't know it was already known, and named it emanium. Actinium was the first to give its name to the actinide series, a group of 15 similar elements between actinium and lawrencium. Sometimes, it is considered the first of the 7th-period transition metals. Actinium is a soft, silvery-white metal that quickly reacts with air and moisture. A white coating of actinium oxide forms, stopping further reaction. Actinium mostly forms compounds with a +3 oxidation state. Actinium is found in small amounts in uranium and thorium ores. It has two main isotopes: Ac-227, which decays with a half-life of 21.772 years, emitting beta and sometimes alpha particles; and Ac-228, which decays with a half-life of 6.15 hours, emitting beta particles. One ton of natural uranium contains about 0.2 milligrams of actinium-227, and one ton of thorium contains about 5 nanograms of actinium-228. Actinium is hard to separate from ores due to its similar properties to lanthanum. It is produced in small amounts in a nuclear reactor. Because it is rare, expensive, and radioactive, actinium is not used much in industry. It is used as a neutron source and in radiation therapy.

Churdan is a city in Greene County, Iowa, United States. In 2010, the city had 386 people.

Robert Brown was born on March 19, 1923, and died on January 15, 2020. He was a Scottish football player and manager. Brown played as a goalkeeper for Queen's Park, Rangers, and Falkirk. He also made five international appearances for the Scotland team. After his playing career, he managed St. Johnstone and the Scottish national team from 1967 to 1971. In 2015, Brown was inducted into the Scottish Football Hall of Fame.

West Hanningfield is a small village and civil parish in South Essex, England. It is near Chelmsford, the county town. The village is in the Chelmsford borough and part of the Rayleigh parliamentary constituency. It is north of Hanningfield Reservoir. Neighboring villages include South Hanningfield, Stock, Rettendon, and East Hanningfield. It is also close to the Chelmsford areas of Galleywood and Great Baddow. The local pub is called the Three Compasses. There is a primary school, a village hall, and a hairdresser in the village. Lord Hanningfield, a former leader of Essex County Council, lives there. The St Mary and St Edward Church, in the village's east, is a Grade II* listed building from the 12th century, with changes in the 18th and 19th centuries. It has a wooden tower thought to date back to the early 13th century, with trees cut down between 1382 and 1414. The church bells from 1676 are a rare example of a complete 17th-century set, though not used now. The Church Buildings Council considers them historically important.
Marie Dubois, born Claudine Lucie Pauline Huzé on January 12, 1937, died on October 15, 2014. She was an actress from Paris and France.

Charles Joseph Scarborough, born on April 9, 1963, is an American cable news host. He currently co-hosts "Morning Joe" on MSNBC with his wife, Mika Brzezinski. Before that, he hosted "Scarborough Country" on the same network. He was also a lawyer and a politician. He served in the United States House of Representatives from 1995 to 2001, representing Florida's 1st district as a Republican. Scarborough also worked as a visiting fellow at the Harvard Institute of Politics at the Harvard Kennedy School of Government. In 2011, he was named one of the most influential people in the world by Time magazine.

North Mississippi Allstars is an American southern rock/blues band from Hernando, Mississippi. They started in 1996. The band has two brothers: Luther Dickinson, who plays guitar, upright bass, and sings, and Cody Dickinson, who plays drums, keyboards, and an electric washboard, and also sings. Duwayne Burnside, who used to play second guitar with the band, is R. L. Burnside's son and played on some of their songs.

Alaska Airlines is a big American airline based in Seattle, Washington. It is the fifth largest airline in the United States by the number of planes, passengers, and destinations. Alaska Airlines, along with its partner airlines Horizon Air and SkyWest Airlines, offers many routes within the United States, especially from the Pacific Northwest and Alaska to over a hundred destinations, including Hawaii, Canada, Costa Rica, and Mexico. The airline operates from five main hubs, with the primary one in Seattle/Tacoma. Alaska Airlines is not part of any major airline alliance but plans to join Oneworld by the end of 2020. As of 2020, it has more than 16,000 employees and is known for having the highest customer satisfaction among traditional airlines for twelve years in a row.
The Bari province was in the Apulia region of Italy. Its capital was Bari. It had an area and 1,594,109 people in 2005. On January 1, 2015, it became the Metropolitan City of Bari.

Gameshark is a brand for video game cheat devices used on various console systems and Windows computers. Currently, Mad Catz owns the Gameshark brand. They made Gameshark products for Sony PlayStation, Xbox, and Nintendo consoles. Players use cheat codes from Gameshark discs or cartridges. They load these into the console's memory. When a game is played, the cheats are activated.

The 2018 FIFA World Cup qualification UEFA Group B was one of nine UEFA groups. It included six teams: Portugal, Switzerland, Hungary, Faroe Islands, Latvia, and Andorra. The draw for the group stage was on July 25, 2015, at the Konstantinovsky Palace in St. Petersburg, Russia. Portugal won the group and qualified directly for the 2018 FIFA World Cup. Switzerland came second and qualified for the play-offs. They won against Northern Ireland and qualified for the tournament as well.

Jump blues is a fast version of blues music, often played by small groups with horn instruments. It was popular in the 1940s and influenced rhythm and blues and rock and roll. People started listening to jump blues again in the 1990s, during a swing revival.

Edmond Mairé was a French labor union leader. He worked from 1971 to 1988 as the secretary general of the French Democratic Confederation of Labour (CFDT). Mairé did not like strikes and believed workers and bosses should share work more equally.

A Hilbert space, named after David Hilbert, is a mathematical concept that extends the idea of a two- or three-dimensional space to spaces with any number of dimensions, finite or infinite. It uses vector algebra and calculus methods, just like the familiar plane and space, but in any dimension. A Hilbert space has a special measurement tool called an inner product, allowing us to measure lengths and angles. Moreover, it is complete, meaning it includes all the limits needed to use calculus techniques. Hilbert spaces naturally appear in mathematics and physics, especially in function spaces. They were first studied by David Hilbert, Erhard Schmidt, and Frigyes Riesz in the early 1900s. These spaces are crucial in partial differential equations, quantum mechanics, signal processing, heat transfer, and thermodynamics. John von Neumann introduced the term "Hilbert space" for this abstract idea. Examples include spaces of square-integrable functions, sequence spaces, and spaces of generalized functions. Hilbert spaces help us visualize concepts like the Pythagorean theorem and the parallelogram law. We can also use perpendicular projections, like "dropping the altitude" of a triangle, for optimization problems. Each element in a Hilbert space can be described by its coordinates, much like specifying a point in the plane. In some cases, especially with infinite dimensions, we can think of a Hilbert space as a space of infinite sequences that are square-summable. Linear operators on a Hilbert space are transformations that stretch the space in different perpendicular directions.
Annapolis is a place in Crawford County, Illinois, United States. It is north-northwest of Robinson. Annapolis has a post office with the zip code 62413. As of 2010, the population was 55.

Nelson Lagoon is a small place in Alaska, in a area called Aleutians East Borough. In 2010, there were 52 people living there, which is less than the 83 people in 2000. Nelson Lagoon was created around 1960 and is one of the newest communities in the area. It is the only Aleut settlement near the Bering Sea. The community is located on the northern side of the Alaska peninsula, on a narrow sand spit that separates the lagoon from the Bering Sea. Nelson Lagoon is part of an area known for fishing, especially salmon. In the late 1990s, the community built a dock, boat ramp, harbormaster's office, and warehouse. The place has good facilities for boats and storage. There is also a 4,000-foot-long runway made of gravel, which allows planes to land regularly. In March 2016, Nelson Lagoon was covered in a layer of ash during a big eruption of Mount Pavlof, a nearby mountain.

The president of the Republic of Crimea was the leader of the Crimean Republic from February 16, 1994, to March 17, 1995. The position was removed because it went against Ukraine's constitution. Crimea had its first presidential election on January 16, 1994. In the second round, held on January 30, 1994, Yuriy Meshkov, a pro-Russian politician, won with 72.9% of the votes. Only Yuriy Meshkov was the president of the Republic of Crimea.

Susanna "Susan" Kohner, born on November 11, 1936, is an American former actress who worked in films and TV. She is famous for her role as Sarah Jane in the movie "Imitation of Life" (1959). For this role, she was nominated for an Oscar and won a Golden Globe. In the film, she played a light-skinned Black woman who "passed" for white as a child and young adult. After Susanna married menswear designer and writer John Weitz in 1964, she stopped acting to focus on her family. Her two sons, Paul and Chris Weitz, became film directors, producers, screenwriters, and sometimes actors.

Euro disco is a type of electronic dance music from Europe that came from disco in the late 1970s. It mixes pop and rock with a continuous dance vibe. Many euro disco songs have English lyrics, but singers often speak different languages. Euro disco includes styles like space disco and italo disco. These styles became less popular after 1986, giving way to electronic rock and hi-nrg. However, there was a small revival of italo disco in the late 1990s.

Quorn is a small town in the Flinders Ranges, north of South Australia, northeast of Port Augusta. In, the town had 1,230 people, mostly living in its center. Quorn is the main town in the Flinders Ranges Council area. It is part of the Stuart state district and Grey federal district. Known for its pretty buildings and history, Quorn attracts tourists and film crews. It is also the end of the Pichi Richi Railway.

St. Paul is a town in southern Madison County, Arkansas, United States. In 2010, it had 113 people. It is near the northwest Arkansas region. St. Paul was created in 1887 when a train line reached that area.

Sometimes written as Gumpei Yokoi, he was a Japanese video game designer. He worked for Nintendo for a long time. He created the Game & Watch handheld system. He also invented the "cross" shaped control pad. He originally designed the Game Boy. He produced several popular and well-reviewed video game franchises, like Metroid and Kid-Icarus.

The use of toxic chemicals as weapons dates back many years. The first large-scale use happened during World War I. These chemicals were mainly used to make defenders feel scared, hurt, and kill them. The gas clouds moved slowly, making them effective against those who were stuck in a fixed position. Different types of weapons were used, including tear gas to temporarily disable people, and deadly gases like phosgene, chlorine, and mustard gas. Gas attacks were a major part of the first global and total war of the 20th century. About 90,000 people died from gas attacks, while over 1.3 million were injured. Unlike other weapons, gas could be countered with masks. As gas use increased in the later part of the war, its effectiveness decreased. The widespread use of these chemical weapons and advances in explosives led some to call World War I "the chemist's war." This period also saw the creation of weapons of mass destruction. The use of poison gas by all major countries during World War I was considered a war crime because it broke the 1899 Hague Declaration and the 1907 Hague Convention, which banned the use of toxic gases in warfare. The horror caused by gas attacks led to less use during World War II.
Dows is a city in Franklin and Wright counties, in the state of Iowa. In 2010, the city had 538 people living there.

Metropolis is a city in Massac County, Illinois, United States. It is near the Ohio River. According to the 2010 census, Metropolis has 6,537 people. Metropolis is the county seat. It is also part of the Paducah, KY-IL micropolitan area, which is in southern Illinois.

Thomas Hodgkin was born on August 17, 1798, and died on April 5, 1866. He was a British doctor who is known for being one of the most important pathologists of his time and for his work in preventive medicine. Hodgkin is famous for describing Hodgkin's disease, a type of lymphoma and blood disease, in 1832. His work helped pathologists start to take an active part in patient care. He worked at Guy's Hospital with other doctors like Thomas Addison and Richard Bright.

Chaim Yisroel Belsky, born on August 22, 1938, and died on January 28, 2016, was an American rabbi. He was an expert in Orthodox and Haredi Judaism and lived in Brooklyn, New York. Belsky taught at Yeshiva Torah Vodaas and led summer camps run by Agudath Israel of America. He worked for over 28 years as a top advisor on food preparation rules for the Orthodox Union. Belsky was known for his wide knowledge of religious teachings and his deep understanding of many subjects. He faced criticism for comments he made about a Jewish camp counselor accused of sexual abuse.

Football is the most popular sport in Austria. The Austrian Football Association, known as "ÖFB," was founded in 1904 and has been part of FIFA since then. Despite its popularity, Austria's national team hasn't done well in tournaments except for a successful period in the early 1930s. In 2016, Austria played in their first European Championship as a qualifier but came last and couldn't advance. Before that, they only played in the European Championship in 2008 when they were co-hosting with Switzerland. Even then, they were eliminated early. In the World Cup, Austria did better, finishing fourth in 1934 and third in 1954. Otherwise, they didn't enter (1930), didn't qualify (1966, 1970, 1974, 1986, 1994, 2002, 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018), withdrew (1938, 1950, 1962), or were eliminated early (1958, 1978, 1982, 1990, 1998).

Milan Michálek, born on December 7, 1984, is a professional ice hockey player from Czech Republic. He plays as a left winger and is currently not signed to any team. He last played for the Toronto Maple Leafs in the National Hockey League (NHL). He was chosen as the sixth player overall in the 2003 NHL Entry Draft by the San Jose Sharks. His older brother, Zbyněk Michálek, is also a professional ice hockey player. Zbyněk played as a defenceman and last played in the NHL with the Arizona Coyotes organization.

Gemiliano "Mel" Campos López, Jr. (born September 1, 1935, died January 1, 2017), was a Filipino politician. He was the mayor of Manila from 1986 to 1987 and from 1988 to 1992. He was also an assemblyman in the Batasang Pambansa of the Philippines from 1984 to 1986. Additionally, he was the former chairman of the Philippine Sports Commission.
Saint-Paul-Mont-Penit is a commune in Vendée, which is in the Pays de la Loire region of western France.

Hainan Airlines Co., Ltd. (HNA) is based in Haikou, Hainan, China. It is the largest civilian airline with a majority state ownership in China. HNA is the fourth-largest airline in China by the number of airplanes and the tenth-largest in Asia by the number of passengers. It flies from 500 routes in and out of Hainan and nine other cities on the mainland. Its main airport is Haikou Meilan International Airport. HNA also has hubs in Beijing Capital International Airport and Xi'an Xianyang International Airport. It has several important cities. HNA is a Skytrax 5-star airline.

The 2000 municipal elections in Halifax Regional Municipality, Nova Scotia, Canada, were held on October 21, 2000. These elections happen every four years since 1996, when Halifax, Dartmouth, Bedford, and parts of Halifax County joined together. The Regional Council has 23 councillors and a mayor. All positions were up for election that year. There are no political parties at the municipal level in Nova Scotia, so candidates run independently.

Leon Norman Cohen was born on September 21, 1934, and died on November 7, 2016. He was a singer, songwriter, poet, and novelist from Canada. His work often talked about religion, politics, feeling alone, being sad, love, relationships, losing things, and dying. Cohen was given important honors like being inducted into the Canadian Music Hall of Fame and the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. He also received the Companion of the Order of Canada, a very high honor. In 2011, he won awards for his writing. Before becoming a musician, Cohen wrote poems and novels in the 1950s and early 1960s. He started his music career in 1967 at 33 years old. His first album, "Songs of Leonard Cohen," came out in 1967. He followed with more folk music albums like "Songs from a Room" in 1969, "Songs of Love and Hate" in 1971, and "New Skin for the Old Ceremony" in 1974. In 1977, his album "Death of a Ladies' Man," created by Phil Spector, had a different sound. In 1979, "Recent Songs" blended Cohen's style with jazz and other music. His most famous song, "Hallelujah," came out in 1984. In 1988, "I'm Your Man" marked his move to using synthesizers. In 1992, "The Future" had sad words about politics and society. "Ten New Songs" in 2001 was a big hit. His 11th album, "Dear Heather," came out in 2004. In 2012, 2014, and 2016, he released "Old Ideas," "Popular Problems," and "You Want It Darker," the last one just three weeks before he died. His last album, "Thanks for the Dance," was released after he died in 2019.

Russian Mission is a city in Alaska. It was once a place where Russian fur traders did business in 1842. After Russia sold its land to the United States in 1867, the city was named Russian Mission in the early 1900s. Today, alcohol cannot be sold there. In 2000, 296 people lived in Russian Mission. By 2010, the population had grown to 312.

Ningbo is a city in northeast Zhejiang province, People's Republic of China. Formerly known as Ningpo, it is a sub-provincial city. Ningbo includes the urban areas, three satellite cities, and several rural counties, some of which are islands in Hangzhou Bay and the East China Sea. Its port, the Port of Ningbo–Zhoushan, is one of the busiest in the world. Ningbo has its own planning status. As of 2010, the total population was 7.6 million, with 3.5 million in the urban areas of Ningbo proper. To the north, Hangzhou Bay separates Ningbo from Shanghai. To the east lies Zhoushan in the East China Sea. To the west and south, Ningbo borders Shaoxing and Taizhou. Ningbo is where Chiang Kai-Shek, a Chinese nationalist leader, was born.

George Dureau, born on December 28, 1930, and died on April 7, 2014, was an American artist. His work focused on charcoal sketches and black and white photographs of poor white and black athletes, dwarfs, and amputees. Robert Mapplethorpe is said to have been inspired by Dureau's photos of amputees and dwarfs. These photos showed the subjects as both vulnerable and strong, playful and serious, complex and fully human.

The Boutonne is a long river in western France, in the Deux-Sèvres and Charente-Maritime areas. It starts in a village called Chef-Boutonne. The river flows mostly in a southwest direction. It joins the Charente River near Cabariot, as a smaller river branching to the right into the larger Charente.

Sewage, or domestic wastewater, is the water used by a community. It includes greywater from sinks, bathtubs, showers, dishwashers, and washing machines, and blackwater from toilets, along with soaps, detergents, and toilet paper. Sewage can go into a sewer that carries it away, or into an onsite sewage facility. In some sewers, it mixes with surface runoff. Most wastewater globally is not treated and ends up polluting the environment, especially in low-income countries. About 90% of the world's wastewater is released untreated. In many developing countries, wastewater from homes and industries often goes directly into the environment without treatment. The term "sewage" is older and is being replaced by "wastewater." In American English, "sewage" and "sewerage" are often used interchangeably. However, in American technical contexts, "sewerage" refers to the system that handles sewage.
Athies is a town in the Pas-de-Calais region of northern France.

In Ireland, "gaeltacht" refers to areas where Irish is commonly spoken at home. Gaeltacht districts were officially recognized in the 1920s, early days of the Irish Free State. This happened after a movement to revive the Irish language. The government wanted to bring back Irish as the main language. Today, it's noticed that the gaeltacht is facing language decline. A 2015 study found that only 21 out of 155 electoral divisions in the gaeltacht are where Irish is used daily by more than two-thirds of people. Some experts say this is a critical level for a language to survive.

Domecy-sur-le-Vault is a commune in the Yonne department, which is in Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, a region in central France. This commune is famous for the Château de Domecy-sur-le-Vault.

Cozy Powell, born Colin Trevor Flooks, was an English rock drummer. He was born on December 29, 1947, and passed away on April 5, 1998. Powell played drums for many famous rock bands and artists, including the Jeff Beck Group, Rainbow, Gary Moore, Robert Plant, Brian May, Whitesnake, Emerson, Lake & Powell, and Black Sabbath. He appeared on at least 66 albums and contributed to many others. Many rock drummers consider him very influential.
Strausberg is a town in Brandenburg, Germany. It is 30 kilometers east of Berlin. Strausberg has 25,594 people living there, making it the biggest town in the Märkisch-oderland district.

Shawn Colvin, born on January 10, 1956, is an American singer-songwriter and musician. She has been making solo music for many years. Colvin is most famous for her song "Sunny Came Home," which won a Grammy Award in 1997.

Jack Hobbs, known as Sir John Berry Hobbs, was born on December 16, 1882, and died on December 21, 1963. He was a famous English cricket player who played for Surrey from 1905 to 1934 and for England in 61 test matches between 1908 and 1930. He was called "the master" and is considered one of the best cricket batsmen ever. He scored 61,760 runs and made 199 centuries in first-class cricket. Hobbs was a right-handed batsman and a medium pace bowler. He was also good at fielding, especially at the cover position. Born poor, Hobbs wanted to play cricket. His early batting was not good, but he improved in 1901 and was noticed by local teams. In 1903, he joined Surrey with support from an England batsman, Tom Hayward. His first-class debut came in 1905, and he scored 88. A century in his next game made him a successful county player. Hobbs made his test debut in 1908, scoring 83. His success, especially against South African spin bowlers, made his place in the team secure. By 1911-12, he scored three centuries against Australia and was judged the world's best batsman. Hobbs played attacking, dynamic cricket until 1914. After World War I, he maintained his reputation in 1919 and continued to score many runs. He returned after a difficult season in 1921 and played more cautiously. He scored a lot in test and domestic cricket until he stopped playing. Hobbs was known for his fast footwork, ability to play different shots, and good ball placement. He was one of the first batsmen to succeed against tricky spin bowlers. He mixed classical shots with effective defense. He was successful on difficult pitches. Hobbs played with several openers, including Tom Hayward, Andy Sandham, Wilfred Rhodes, and Herbert Sutcliffe. His partnership with Sutcliffe remains one of the best in test cricket history. Hobbs was close to his wife Ada, who lived for 56 years. They lived comfortably from his Surrey wages, commercial endorsements, and shop profits. After cricket, Hobbs worked in journalism. He was knighted in 1953, the first professional cricketer to receive this honor. Hobbs spent his later years taking care of Ada. He died at 81, just a few months after her in 1963.
Riceville is a city in Howard and Mitchell counties, in the state of Iowa. In 2010, the city's population was 785.

A reasonable accommodation is a change made to a system to ensure fairness for an individual based on their proven need. The need can be different for each person. Accommodations can be about religion, physical or mental issues, emotions, school, or work, and are often required by laws. Different countries have their own systems for reasonable accommodations. The United Nations uses this term in a rule called the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. It says that not providing accommodations is discrimination.

William John Fairbairn, born on January 7, 1947, played ice hockey as a right wing. He played in the NHL for 10 seasons. Fairbairn mainly played for the New York Rangers. Later, he played for the Minnesota North Stars and the St. Louis Blues. He retired early in the 1978-79 NHL season. Fairbairn scored 162 goals during his career.

Rockville is a village in Vernon, a town in Tolland County, Connecticut, United States. The population was 7,474 in 2010. It became a city in 1889. Since 1965, Rockville has been combined with Vernon.

The Central Bohemian region is an administrative area in the Czech Republic, located in the central part of Bohemia. Prague, the capital city of the Czech Republic, is in the center of this region. However, Prague is not part of this region but is a separate region. This region is in the middle of Bohemia and covers a large area of 11,014 km², which is almost 14% of the total area of the Czech Republic. It surrounds Prague and borders seven other regions: Liberec (north), Hradec Králové (northeast), Pardubice (east), Vysočina (southeast), South Bohemia (south), Plzeň (west), and Usti nad Labem (northwest).
Bournos is a commune in southwestern France. It is in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department.

The Berlin State Opera is a famous building on Unter den Linden Boulevard in Berlin's historic center. It was built between 1741 and 1743, following designs by Georg Wenzeslaus von Knobelsdorff, under King Frederick the Great's instructions. The opera house, once called the Royal Prussian Opera House, was damaged in World War II bombing. After the war, from 1951 to 1955, it was restored and became part of the Forum Fridericianum square. Known as "Lindenoper," it is the first theater in the city that stands alone as a big, impressive building.
Joseph Bonnel was a French football player who played as a midfielder. He was part of the French team in the 1966 FIFA World Cup. He scored 3 goals in that year.

Kieren John Perkins, OAM, was born on August 14, 1973. He is an Australian former competitive swimmer. Perkins won four Olympic medals and held world records in three swimming events. Known as one of the world's best long-distance swimmers, he won two Olympic gold medals in the 1500-meter freestyle in 1992 and 1996, and a silver medal in 2000.

Heidi Alexander was born on April 17, 1975. She is a British Labour Party politician. She works as the deputy mayor of London for transport with Sadiq Khan. She is also the deputy chair of transport for London. Alexander served as a member of parliament (MP) for Lewisham East from the 2010 general election. She left this position in May 2018 to join Sadiq Khan's team. In September 2015, she became the shadow secretary of state for health. However, she left this role on June 26, 2016.

Fernando Bernabé Agüero Rocha was born on June 11, 1917, in Managua, Nicaragua, and died on September 27, 2011. He was a Nicaraguan politician and the founder of the Social Conservative Party in 1988. In 1967, he ran for president as part of the Conservative 1966 National Opposition Union (UNO). During his campaign, one of his rallies in Managua was violently stopped. Later, in 1971, he signed a controversial pact called the Kupia Kumi with Anastasio Somoza Debayle.

Ahmed Osman, born on January 3, 1930, was the prime minister of Morocco from November 2, 1972, to March 22, 1979. He was married to Princess Lalla Nuzha, a sister of King Hassan II, from 1964 to 1977. Ahmed Osman founded the National Rally of Independents. He held several important positions: secretary general of the Ministry of National Defence from 1959 to 1961, ambassador to the Federal Republic of Germany from 1961 to 1962, and to the United States from 1967 to 1972. From 1962 to 1964, he served as the under secretary of the Ministry of Mines and Industry. He was president of the Moroccan General Navigation Company from 1964 to 1967 and prime minister from 1972 to 1979. He became the president of the National Rally of Independents in 1977 and the president of the National Assembly from 1984 to 1992.

Binoculars or field glasses are two telescopes placed side-by-side and aligned to point in the same direction. They allow the viewer to use both eyes when looking at distant objects. Most binoculars are handheld and use both hands, but their sizes vary. Some are small like opera glasses, while others are larger and mounted on stands. Unlike a single telescope, binoculars provide a three-dimensional image. For closer objects, the two slightly different views seen by each eye create a sense of depth.

Tondiarpet taluk is a part of Chennai city district in Tamil Nadu, India. It was created in December 2013 from the old Fort-Tondiarpet area. It includes the Tondiarpet neighborhood.

Australian convict sites are a world heritage property. There are 11 old prison places. They were built by the British Empire between the 18th and 19th centuries. These sites are on good land along the coast of Sydney, Tasmania, Norfolk Island, and Fremantle. They show "the best surviving examples of large-scale transportation of convicts and the spread of European power through convict labor." Each site was first added to Australia's national heritage list. Then, they became part of the world heritage list. Planning began in 1995. A nomination was first made in January 2008. The nomination failed, and it was changed later.
Brooks County is the name of two counties in the United States.

Joel Murray was born on April 17, 1963. He is an American actor. He played important roles in TV shows like "Mad Men," "Grand," "Love & War," "Dharma & Greg," and "Shameless." He also appeared in movies such as "God Bless America" and "Monsters University."
Serrières-de-Briord is a commune in Ain, which is in eastern France.

The Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks is an action-adventure game made by Nintendo for the Nintendo DS. It was part of the Legend of Zelda series and came out worldwide in December 2009. In 2016, it was re-released on the Wii U's virtual console. Like earlier games, Spirit Tracks uses a cel-shaded art style. The main character, Link, travels on a train with a cannon, just like in Phantom Hourglass. Players can also control phantoms and play a flute called the spirit flute. Spirit Tracks is the first Zelda game with different endings that change Link's final result.

William Frederick Frazer was born on July 8, 1960, and died on June 28, 2019. He was from Northern Ireland and supported people who were hurt by violence from Irish Republican groups. Frazer started and led a group called Families Acting for Innocent Relatives. He was also involved in the Love Ulster campaign and later with protests at Belfast City Hall. In 2019, a journalist named Mandy McAuley said that the Ulster Defence Association got weapons from the Ulster Resistance in the late 1980s. McAuley claimed that Frazer was in charge of giving out those weapons. She said that many people confirmed this. These weapons were connected to at least 70 murders by paramilitary groups.

The Terminal is a 2004 American movie. Steven Spielberg directed it and starred Tom Hanks, Catherine Zeta-Jones, and Stanley Tucci. The story is about an Eastern European man who gets stuck in John F. Kennedy Airport in New York. He can't enter the United States, and he can't return to his home country because of a problem there. The movie is partly based on a real story about a man who stayed in a Paris airport for 18 years. After finishing another film, Spielberg decided to make this movie to make people laugh, cry, and feel good about the world. They built a whole airport set inside a hangar because no airport wanted to help. Most of the outside shots were filmed at a Montreal airport. The movie came out in North America on June 18, 2004. People had mixed feelings about it, but it made a lot of money, earning $77.9 million in the U.S. and $219.4 million worldwide.

Ringmaster is the second album by the American hip hop group Insane Clown Posse. It was released on March 8, 1994, by Psychopathic Records. The group made the album in 1993 at the Tempermill studio. In the album's lyrics, the leader of the carnival is like one of the judges of your soul in the afterlife. This character is created from the listener's own bad actions. Ringmaster was the first album by Insane Clown Posse that was made just by producer Mike E. Clark. He worked with the group for many years. The album also has guest appearances by Capitol E and Jumpsteady. The song "Ringmaster" was reissued by Island Records in 1998 and got a gold certification from the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). The original version of the album also got a gold certification in 2004.

Cristian Eugen Chivu, born on October 26, 1980, is a former Romanian football player. He usually played as a left back, but he could also play as a central defender. He started his career at FCM Reșița, his hometown club. In 1998, he moved to FC Universitatea Craiova. A year later, he joined Ajax in the Netherlands. As captain at Ajax, his performance helped him transfer to Roma for €18 million in 2003. At Roma, he won the Coppa Italia in his last of four seasons there. He then transferred to Internazionale, where he stayed until retiring in 2014. During his time at Internazionale, he won three big trophies: the Italian league, the Italian cup, and the UEFA Champions League in 2010. He played for Romania 75 times between 1999 and 2010 and was part of their teams for the 2000 and 2008 European Championships. After retiring, he became a football analyst for Italian TV stations Sky Sport and now Fox Sports. He also works as a technical observer for UEFA.

Hammurabi was the sixth king of the Babylonian dynasty, coming from the Amorite tribe. He ruled from around 1792 BC to 1750 BC. His father, Sin-muballit, stepped down due to poor health. During his reign, Hammurabi conquered Elam and cities like Larsa, Eshnumna, and Mari. He made Ishme-dagan I, the king of Assyria, pay tribute, and forced his son Mut-ashkur to do so. This made almost all of Mesopotamia part of Babylonian rule. Hammurabi is famous for the Code of Hammurabi, which he said came from Shamash, the Babylonian god of justice. Unlike earlier codes, it focused more on punishing the person who did the crime, not just helping the victim. It had specific punishments for different crimes and said that people were innocent until proven guilty. Even though the punishments were very strict by today’s standards, they were meant to stop people from taking revenge. The Code of Hammurabi and the Law of Moses in the Bible share many similarities. Hammurabi was seen as a god during his life. After he died, he was remembered as a great conqueror who spread civilization and made everyone honor Marduk, the main Babylonian god. His military achievements became less important over time, and he was seen more as a lawgiver. For ancient Mesopotamians, his time was used as a reference for events in the distant past. Even after his empire fell, he was still seen as a good king, and many rulers claimed him as an ancestor. Hammurabi was found by archaeologists in the late 1800s and is important in understanding the history of laws.

Townsville is a city on Australia's northeastern coast. It is the biggest city north of the Sunshine Coast, with about 180,820 people as of June 2018. Locals call it the unofficial capital of North Queensland. Townsville has many government, community, and business offices for the northern part of the state. It is in the dry tropics region near the Great Barrier Reef. Townsville is also an important industrial city. It has one of the world's largest zinc refineries and other factories. The city's port is growing to allow bigger ships from Asia and the world's largest passenger ships to visit. Its location near Asia and trading partners like China makes it increasingly important. Popular places to visit include The Strand, a long tropical beach and garden area; Riverway, a park next to Ross River; Reef HQ, a big aquarium with native plants and animals from the Great Barrier Reef; the Museum of Tropical Queensland, which shows relics from a sunken British warship; Castle Hill, a big hill that is a popular exercise spot; the Townsville Sports Reserve; and Magnetic Island, a nearby island mostly protected as a national park.

A resistance movement is when some people in a country try to oppose the government or an occupying force, and work to cause trouble. They might use peaceful ways, like civil resistance, or use force, whether with weapons or not. In some cases, a resistance group might use both methods. This can happen in different areas or phases of a country. Since 1899, there has been debate about whether armed resistance movements are legal. The first major set of rules for war, called the Hague Convention, was made that year. A part of these rules, called the Martens Clause, tried to balance the viewpoints of powerful countries and smaller ones. Recently, the Geneva Conventions in 1977 mentioned that people fighting against colonial rule, foreign occupation, or racist regimes might be lawful combatants. The rules can be unclear, making it hard to decide if a resistance movement is lawful. A government might call a resistance group a terrorist based on whether they think the group's members are legal fighters and have the right to resist. In the end, deciding if a resistance movement is lawful is a political choice.

Schifflange is a commune and town in southwestern Luxembourg. It is part of the canton of Esch-sur-Alzette. The town of Schifflange, located in the west of the commune, has 9,332 people. Schifflange became separate from the commune of Esch-sur-Alzette on August 15, 1876. The law to create Schifflange was made on July 6, 1876.

A corroboree is a general term for an Australian Aboriginal meeting. It can be a special ceremony, a happy celebration, or even related to war. The British settlers in Sydney first used this word, coming from the Dharug language. Corroborees usually have dancing, music, special clothes, and sometimes body decorations. Now, people also use the word for any big, loud gathering.

Holley is a small community in Santa Rosa County, Florida. As of 2019, it had 2,425 people living there. Florida State Road 87 goes through Holley. Holley is usually seen as part of the larger community of Navarre. Holley is part of the Holley-Navarre census area. It also uses the Holley-Navarre fire and water systems. People in Holley vote in Navarre’s election district. Some of the main areas in Holley are Gordon Evans Road, Nelson Street, and Bob Tolbert Road. These areas are growing quickly.

The new academy prize in literature was created in 2018. It replaced the Nobel Prize in Literature, which was not given that year and was delayed until 2019. The winner was chosen on October 12, 2018. The new academy was closed in December 2018. They asked the public to vote on 47 writers nominated by Swedish librarians. The final four were Maryse Condé, Neil Gaiman, Haruki Murakami, and Kim Thuy. Murakami then asked to withdraw his name, saying he preferred to focus on writing. Maryse Condé won the prize. In 2018, the new academy was formed as a non-profit group. It was not connected to the Nobel Foundation or the Swedish Academy.

Mahmoud Abdelrazek Hassan Fadlala, known as Shikabala, was born on March 5, 1986. He is an Egyptian professional footballer who plays for Zamalek in the Egyptian Premier League and the Egyptian national team. Shikabala started playing for Zamalek when he was young and has been with the club for many years. He is considered one of Zamalek's legends. He has also played for other clubs like PAOK and Sporting CP. Shikabala usually plays as a right-winger, but he can also play as a central attacking midfielder or a left winger.
Guerbigny is a commune in the Somme department, which is in Hauts-de-France in northern France.

Merrimack County is in the state of New Hampshire, U.S. In 2010, it had 146, 445 people, which made it the third-largest county in New Hampshire. The main city, Concord, is the capital of New Hampshire. Merrimack County was created in 1823 from parts of Hillsborough and Rockingham counties. It is named after the Merrimack River. Concord is part of the Merrimack, NH micropolitan area, which is part of the larger Boston-Worcester-Providence area. In 2010, the center of New Hampshire was in Merrimack County, in Pembroke town.

"Time of the Season" is a song by the British rock band The Zombies. It is on their 1968 album "Odessey and Oracle." The song was written by the keyboard player Rod Argent and recorded at Abbey Road Studios in August 1967. More than a year after it was first released, the track became a surprise hit in the United States. It reached number three on the Billboard Hot 100 and number one on the Cashbox chart. It has become one of The Zombies' most popular and recognizable songs.

Stagecoach Group is a transport company based in Perth, Scotland. It runs buses, express coaches, and a tram service in the United Kingdom. It used to operate in many places including Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, and Oceania. It is listed on the London Stock Exchange.

State of Georgia is an American TV show. It features Raven-Symoné, Majandra Delfino, and Loretta Devine. The show is about Georgia, played by Raven-Symoné, an actress with a big personality, and her best friend Jo, played by Majandra Delfino, who is a science geek. They both try to succeed in New York City. The show was on ABC Family from June 29 to August 17, 2011. The first episode had 1.32 million viewers. ABC Family stopped the show on September 16, 2011, because it wasn't doing well.

Roman Stanley Gribbs was born on December 29, 1925, and died on April 5, 2016. He was an American politician. Gribbs was the mayor of Detroit from 1970 to 1974. Later, he became a judge on the Michigan Court of Appeals. Gribbs was the last mayor of Detroit who was white, as the city was becoming mostly black during his time. Detroit elected Mike Duggan as mayor in 2013.

Loretta Lynn, born on April 14, 1932, is an American country music singer and songwriter. She has had a long career, spanning 60 years. Some of her famous songs include "You Ain't Woman Enough (To Take My Man)", "Don't Come Home A-Drinking (With Lovin' on Your Mind)", "One's on the Way", "Fist City", and "Coal Miner's Daughter". Lynn was in a biographical film with the same name in 1980. She has won many awards and is known for being a pioneering artist in country music. Lynn received awards from both the Country Music Association and the Academy of Country Music as both a duet partner and an individual artist. She is the most awarded female country recording artist and the only female ACM artist of the decade (1970s). Lynn has 24 number one hit singles and 11 number one albums. She continues to perform, appear at the Grand Ole Opry, and release new albums.

Chiang Ching-kuo, born on April 27, 1910, and died on January 13, 1988, was a Taiwanese politician. He was the son of Chiang Kai-shek, the former president. Ching-kuo held many important jobs in the Republic of China government. He was the premier from 1972 to 1978 and became president in 1978 until he died in 1988. Chiang went to the Soviet Union when he was a teenager in 1925. His father's party, the Nationalists, and the Communist Party were allies then. Ching-kuo studied there but had to work in a steel factory in the Ural Mountains when the Nationalists broke their alliance with the Communists. There, he met and married Faina Vakhreva. In 1937, when war with Japan was likely, he was sent to China. His father began to trust him during the war and gave him more responsibilities, including running administration. After Japan lost the war, Ching-kuo cleaned up corruption in Shanghai with tough methods. The Communists' victory in 1949 forced the Chiang family and their government to move to Taiwan. Ching-kuo was first in charge of the secret police from 1965 to 1969, where he used strict methods to control people. He then became Minister of Defense from 1969 to 1972, Vice-premier from 1972 to 1975, and finally premier from 1975 to 1978. After his father died in 1975, Ching-kuo led the Nationalist Party as chairman. He was elected president in 1978 and again in 1984. During his time as president, the government became more open and allowed some political disagreement. Ching-kuo worked to win the support of Taiwanese people and reduced the favoritism for those who moved from the mainland. At the end of his life, he relaxed controls on media and allowed more Taiwanese people to have important positions, including his successor, Lee Teng-hui.
Maizery was a former commune in the Moselle department in northeastern France. In June 2016, it became part of a new commune called Colligny-Maizery. In 2017, its population was 182.

Squash is a game where two players hit a small, rubber ball against the walls of a four-walled court using racquets. They take turns hitting the ball to the court's walls. The goal is to make the ball go in a way the other player can't return. Squash is played by around 20 million people in more than 185 countries. A group called the World Squash Federation organizes the sport. They are recognized by the International Olympic Committee but squash is not in the Olympics yet. People who love squash are working to get it included in future Olympic games.

The Eastern Chalukyas, also called the Chalukyas of Vengi, ruled parts of South India from the 7th to the 12th centuries. They began as governors of the Chalukyas of Badami in the Deccan region. Later, they became an independent power and ruled the Vengi area in present-day Andhra Pradesh until 1189 CE. Initially, their capital was in Vengi (modern Pedavegi near Eluru). Later, it moved to Rajamahendravaram (modern Rajahmundry). The Eastern Chalukyas were often involved in wars with the powerful Cholas and Western Chalukyas over control of Vengi. For about 500 years, they ruled Vengi and helped unify the region. This period also saw the growth of Telugu culture, literature, poetry, and art.

Sidney Sheldon was an American writer, director, and producer born on February 11, 1917, and died on January 30, 2007. He worked in Broadway plays and motion pictures in the 1930s. His work "The Bachelor and the Bobby-Soxer" (1947) was a successful comedy that won him an Oscar in 1948. He then moved to television, creating shows like "The Patty Duke Show" (1963-66), "I Dream of Jeannie" (1965-70), and "Hart to Hart" (1979-84). After turning 50, Sheldon began writing best-selling romantic suspense novels, including "Master of the Game" (1982), "The Other Side of Midnight" (1973), and "Rage of Angels" (1980). He wrote 18 novels that sold over 300 million copies in 51 languages. Sheldon is often mentioned among the top ten best-selling fiction writers of all time.
