The University of Costa Rica, in Spanish "Universidad de Costa Rica" (UCR), is a public university in Costa Rica, a country in Central America. Its main campus, called Ciudad Universitaria Rodrigo Facio, is in San Pedro Montes de Oca, a city in the province of San José. It was first created as the "Universidad de Santo Tomás" in 1843 and is the oldest and largest higher education institution in Costa Rica. UCR is also the most important research university in Costa Rica and Central America, and one of the most prestigious and recognized in Latin America. About 45,000 students study there each year.

On a sailing boat, a forestay is a rope that helps keep the mast from falling backward. It is attached either at the top of the mast or, in some cases, about one-eighth to one-fourth of the way down from the top. The other end of the forestay is tied to the front part of the boat, called the bow. Often, a sail is connected to the forestay. This sail can be a jib or a genoa. In a cutter rig, sails called jibs are attached to stays in front of the forestay, which may extend from the mast to a part of the boat called a bowsprit. The sail connected to the forestay is then called a staysail. The forestay can be made of materials like stainless steel wire, solid stainless steel rod, carbon rod, or a strong plastic called ultra high molecular weight polyethylene on fast racing boats. On older boats, it might be made of galvanized wire or natural fibers.

A video game developer makes video games, like a software developer but with a focus on games. This can be one person doing everything or a big company with different people working on different parts, such as coding, design, art, and testing. Many game developers get help from companies that fund and market their games. Some developers work alone or in small groups, making what we call indie games. Developers can make games for different devices, like game consoles (such as Nintendo Switch, Xbox One, and PlayStation 4), computers, or phones. They can also specialize in certain types of games, like role-playing games or shooter games. Some developers change games from one device to another or translate games into different languages. Occasionally, they do regular software development work too. Game publishers often have their own development teams, like EA Canada or Activision. But they are still called publishers because their main job is publishing games. Some developers work independently, like the company that made the Halo series for Xbox.

Paul Gust Vallas, born on June 10, 1953, is an American politician. He used to be the superintendent of the Bridgeport public schools and the Recovery School District of Louisiana. He was also the CEO of the School District of Philadelphia and the Chicago Public Schools. Additionally, he worked as the budget director for the city of Chicago. In 2002, Vallas tried to get the Democratic nomination for governor of Illinois but was unsuccessful. In 2014, he ran for lieutenant governor with then Governor Pat Quinn, but they lost to the Republican candidates Bruce Rauner and Evelyn Sanguinetti. In 2019, Vallas tried to become the mayor of Chicago. He got ninth place in the first round with 5.43% of the vote and did not advance to the runoff. He then supported Lori Lightfoot for the position.

Devonté Hynes, born David Joseph Michael Hynes on December 23, 1985, is an English singer, songwriter, record producer, and director. He was part of the band Test Icicles from 2004 to 2006, playing guitar, synthesizer, and singing occasionally. The band released one full album in 2005. Hynes then released two solo albums as Lightspeed Champion between 2008 and 2010. Later, he made music as Blood Orange, releasing four albums between 2010 and 2018. He has also worked with many other artists like Tinashe, Solange Knowles, Connan Mockasin, Tei Shi, Sky Ferreira, FKA Twigs, HAIM, Florence and the Machine, Carly Rae Jepsen, Diana Vickers, The Chemical Brothers, Kylie Minogue, A$AP Rocky, Mac Miller, Blondie, and Mariah Carey.

James Henry Hammond was born on November 15, 1807, and died on November 13, 1864. He was from South Carolina and worked as an attorney, politician, and planter. Hammond served as a U.S. representative from 1835 to 1836, as the 60th governor of South Carolina from 1842 to 1844, and as a U.S. senator from 1857 to 1860. He was known as one of the main supporters of slavery before the American Civil War. Through his marriage, Hammond owned a large area of land, several plantations, houses, and more than 300 slaves. He was also related to Wade Hampton II and his children through his wife's family. Hammond was their uncle. Hammond was accused of raping four of Wade Hampton II's teenage nieces. This scandal was made public, but it didn't stop him from being elected as a U.S. senator later.

Shawnee is a city in Pottawatomie County, Oklahoma, United States. The population was 29,857 in 2010, which is 4.9% more than 28,692 in 2000. Shawnee is part of the Oklahoma City-Shawnee area. It is also the county seat of Pottawatomie County. Shawnee is the main city of the Shawnee micropolitan area. It is about 45 minutes east of downtown Oklahoma City and can be reached via Interstate 40. Additionally, it is 112 miles east-northeast from the McClellan-Kerr Arkansas River Navigation System, which connects to the Gulf of Mexico.
Pleasant Hill is a city in Polk County, Iowa, United States. In 2010, it had 8,785 people. It is in the Des Moines–West Des Moines area. In July 2005, it got a zip code, 50327.

The monarchy of Belgium is a constitutional, hereditary, and popular monarchy. The current monarch is called the "King" or "Queen of the Belgians" and is the country's head of state. Belgium has had seven kings or queens since it became independent in 1830. The current monarch, King Philippe, became king on July 21, 2013, after his father gave up the throne.

Hoyerswerda is a big town in the Bautzen district of Saxony, a state in Germany. It is in a region called Upper Lusatia, where some people speak Sorbian, an additional language besides German. Hoyerswerda has two parts: the old town, with old houses and things to see, and the new town, which is more modern and colorful. Before it was renovated, there were many apartment blocks. The area around the town has many lakes, marshes, and waterways because it is in Lusatia. This attracts holidaymakers and people who like cycling and inline skating, as there are paths by the lakes.

Aurelius Ambrosius, known as Ambrose in English (397 AD), was the bishop of Milan. He was a theologian and one of the most important religious leaders in the 4th century. Ambrose became bishop unexpectedly in 374 after people chose him. As bishop, he fought against a religious group called Arians and tried to help resolve a conflict between Emperor Theodosius I and a man named Magnus Maximus. It is said that Ambrose promoted a singing style called "antiphonal chant," where the choir sings in response to each other. He also wrote a song called "Veni Redemptor Gentium" for Christmas. Ambrose had a big influence on another important church leader, Augustine of Hippo (354-430). Western Christianity considers Ambrose one of its four main teachers. He is a saint in the Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Anglican, and some Lutheran churches. He is also the patron saint of Milan.
Burgistein is a town in the Thun district, which is in the canton of Bern, Switzerland.
Kellinghusen is a town in the Steinburg district of Schleswig-Holstein, a state in Germany.

Cearbhall Ó Dálaigh (born on February 12, 1911, and died on March 21, 1978) was an Irish politician who belonged to Fianna Fáil. He also worked as a judge and a barrister. Ó Dálaigh served as Ireland's fifth president from December 1974 to October 1976. He worked as a judge at the European Court of Justice from 1973 to 1974, Ireland's Chief Justice from 1961 to 1973, a judge at the Supreme Court from 1953 to 1973, and Ireland's Attorney General from 1946 to 1948 and from 1951 to 1953. Sometimes, his name was spelled as Carroll O'Daly, which he used during his legal career.

The Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARM) was a special area in the Philippines. It covered five provinces where many Muslims lived: Basilan (without Isabela City), Lanao del Sur, Maguindanao, Sulu, and Tawi-Tawi. ARM was the only region in the Philippines with its own government. Its main city, Cotabato, was not part of its area. ARM existed from 2006 until 2008, when a province called Shariff Kabunsuan was removed. This happened because a big court said the law that created it was not correct. In 2012, President Benigno Aquino III said they wanted peace in ARM and planned to change its name to the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region. In 2018, President Rodrigo Duterte signed a new law called the Bangsamoro Organic Law. This new law created a new area called the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM). ARM was officially ending after this new law was accepted on January 25, 2019. BARMM will take its place.
Michel Jeury, born on January 23, 1934, and passed away on January 9, 2015, was a French writer of science fiction. He was famous in the 1970s. He also wrote using a fake name, Albert Higon.

The flag of Myanmar, also called Burma, was adopted on October 21, 2010. It replaced the old flag used since 1974. Changes to the country's name and new rules were also made in 2008. The new flag has three horizontal stripes: yellow, green, and red. In the middle, there is a white star with five points. The colors mean different things: yellow stands for unity, green for peace, and red for bravery.

The Song of Songs, also known as the Song of Solomon or Canticles, is a special book found in the Ketuvim, or "Writings," part of the Hebrew Bible and the Old Testament. It is unique because it does not talk about laws, covenants, or the God of Israel, nor does it discuss wisdom like other books such as Proverbs or Ecclesiastes. Instead, it is about love and celebrates romantic and sexual relationships between two lovers, showing them praising and yearning for each other. Other women in Jerusalem act like an audience, making the story more engaging for the reader. In modern Judaism, the Song of Songs is read during the Sabbath, specifically on Passover, which celebrates the start of the grain harvest and commemorates the Exodus from Egypt. In Jewish tradition, it is seen as an allegory of the relationship between God and Israel, while Christianity sees it as an allegory of Christ and his "bride," the Church.

The G7 is a group of seven major developed countries. These countries are Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States. They are among the largest economies in the world. As of 2018, these seven countries have 58% of the global net wealth ($317 trillion) and over 46% of the global GDP based on nominal values. They also have more than 32% of the global GDP when measured by purchasing power parity. The European Union is invited to participate in G7 meetings. Each year, the G7 hosts a summit with the leaders from these seven countries.
Ayub Awista (born around 1979) is an Afghan writer. He also started the Afghan Youth Sports Exchange in the United States.

Page County is in Iowa, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 15, 932 people. The county seat is Clarinda. It was named after Captain John Page of the 4th U.S. Infantry, who died in the Battle of Palo Alto.

Orestes "Minnie" Miñoso, born Saturnino Orestes Armas Miñoso Arrieta, was a Cuban professional baseball player. He began his career in the Negro Leagues in 1946 and was an All-Star third baseman for the New York Cubans. In 1948, he joined the Cleveland Indians, a Major League Baseball team. He later became an All-Star left fielder for both the Cleveland Indians and the Chicago White Sox. Miñoso was the first black Cuban in Major League Baseball and the first black player for the White Sox. He played as a rookie in 1951 and was one of the first Latin American players in an MLB All-Star game. Miñoso played as an American League All-Star for seven seasons and won three gold gloves in his 30s. He batted over.300 for eight seasons. He led the American League in triples and stolen bases three times each, and in hits, doubles, and total bases once each. Miñoso and Willie Mays, with 179 and 167 stolen bases respectively, are credited with bringing speed as an offensive weapon to baseball in the 1950s. He was known for reaching base, leading the American League in times hit by pitch ten times, and holding the league record for career times hit by pitch from 1959 to 1985. As a defensive standout, he led American League left fielders in assists six times and in putouts and double plays four times each. Miñoso was very popular and dynamic, helping the Chicago White Sox become a top team in the 1950s and 1960s. He held the White Sox record for career home runs from 1956 to 1974. He left the major leagues after the 1964 season but played and managed in Mexico until 1973. He later returned to the White Sox as a coach and made brief, public appearances in 1976 and 1980. He became the third player to get a hit after the age of 50 and the second player to appear in the major leagues in five decades. His White Sox uniform number 9 was retired in 1983, and a statue of him was unveiled at U.S. Cellular Field in 2004. Miñoso was elected to the Cuban Baseball Hall of Fame in Exile in 1983 and to the Mexican Professional Baseball Hall of Fame in 1996. In 2014, he was on the National Baseball Hall of Fame's Golden Era Committee election ballot for possible hall of fame consideration in 2015. He and other candidates, including former White Sox teammate Billy Pierce and other former Cuban players Tony Oliva and Luis Tiant, did not get inducted in 2015.

Maaloula, or Maʿlūlā, is a town in the Rif Dimashq governorate in Syria. It is about 56 kilometers northeast of Damascus. The town is built in the mountains, more than 1,500 meters above sea level. Maaloula is one of three villages where people speak Western Neo-Aramaic. The other two villages are Jubb'adin and Bakhah, which are nearby.

Barrie is a city in central Ontario, Canada. It sits on Kempenfelt Bay, part of Lake Simcoe. Barrie is a separate city, not part of Simcoe County. It's in a historically important area called Huronia and is in the densely populated Greater Golden Horseshoe region. As of 2016, Barrie had 141,434 people, making it the 34th largest city in Canada. The Barrie Census Area had 197,059 people, 21st in Canada. Barrie has grown a lot recently because many people from Toronto use it as a home. The city has good jobs and affordable homes. Go Transit offers daily train service to and from Toronto. Barrie is north of Toronto, northeast of Detroit, and west of Ottawa. It was first settled during the War of 1812 as a supply base. It got its name in 1832 after Sir Robert Barrie. The population grew a lot in the 1980s and 1990s, going from 38,423 in 1981 to 128,430 in 2006. Barrie now has tall buildings by the lake and beaches. It's a popular tourist spot with ski areas nearby. The city's economy includes education, healthcare, technology, and manufacturing. The Royal Victoria Regional Health Centre is the biggest employer. Retail in Barrie has grown a lot, thanks to new shopping areas. Barrie has cold, snowy winters and hot, humid summers.
Lie Sang Bong is a Korean fashion designer. His designs have been worn by famous singers and actors like Beyoncé, Rihanna, Lady Gaga, and Lindsay Lohan.

The River Shannon is the longest river in Ireland. It covers an area that makes up one-fifth of Ireland's total land. The river divides the western part of Ireland (mainly Connacht) from the eastern and southern parts (Leinster and most of Munster). County Clare is an exception, as it is west of the river but belongs to Munster province. The Shannon is a significant barrier, with fewer than thirty-five crossing points from Limerick in the south to Dowra in the north. The river is named after a Celtic goddess called "Sionna." Since ancient times, the Shannon has been an important waterway, first mapped by Ptolemy, a Greek-Egyptian geographer. The river flows south from a lake in County Cavan, then turns west and empties into the Atlantic Ocean through a long estuary. Limerick city is where river water meets the sea water in the estuary. East of Limerick, the Shannon is tidal up to the base of the Ardnacrusha dam.
Faverolles is a commune in Aisne, which is in Hauts-de-France in northern France.

Irma Schultz Keller, born on October 1, 1965, is a Swedish actress and pop singer. She has acted in many Swedish movies and TV shows. She also appeared in American productions, like the horror movie "The Resurrection of Michael Myers Part 2" and the miniseries "Xerxes." Keller studied mime and acting at the Swedish National Academy and graduated in 1999. In 2007, she and Uno Svenningsson performed the song "God Morgen" in Melodifestivalen. They entered as Uno & Irma but lost to Sonja Alden in the first round and were eliminated from the contest.
Afrodisiac can mean: A substance or food believed to increase sexual desire.

The Fahrenheit scale is a temperature system created by physicist Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit in 1724. It uses the degree Fahrenheit (symbol: °F) as its unit. The freezing point of a mixture of brine (water, ice, and ammonium chloride) was set at 0 °F, and his estimate of the human body temperature was 96 °F. He also set a middle point at 32 °F for ice water. Today, the Fahrenheit scale is formally defined by two key points: water freezing at 32 °F and boiling at 212 °F, both at sea level and standard pressure. This scale was the first standardized temperature system widely used but is now used mainly in the United States, its territories, and a few other places like Palau, Federated States of Micronesia, Marshall Islands, the Cayman Islands, and Liberia. In some Caribbean and Central American countries, both Fahrenheit and Celsius are used, especially for weather reports. In the UK, both scales are sometimes given together. Most countries use the Celsius scale, renamed from the centigrade scale in 1948 to honor Anders Celsius.

Diana Serra Cary, born Peggy-Jean Montgomery on October 29, 1918, and known as Baby Peggy, was an American child film actress, performer, author, and silent film historian. She was the last living silent film star from Hollywood and the last person with a big career in silent films. Baby Peggy was also the last person to meet President Calvin Coolidge during his presidency. Along with Jackie Coogan and Baby Marie, she was one of the top child stars in Hollywood during the silent film era. Between 1921 and 1923, she made more than 150 short films for the Century Film Corporation. In 1922, she got over 1.2 million letters from fans. By 1924, she was called "the million dollar baby" because she earned $1.5 million a year. Although she was famous and rich as a child, she became poor later and worked as an extra in the 1930s. Since she was young, she loved writing and history. In her later life, she became an author and silent film historian under the name Diana Serra Cary. She wrote several books, including a historical novel called "The Drowning of the Moon." She also helped protect the rights of child actors.

In 1685, King James II of England met Michael Shen Fu-tsung, a Chinese man. The king liked him so much that he had a painting made and put it in his bedroom. The painting is still at Windsor Castle. Shen also visited Oxford, helping to organize Chinese books in the Bodleian Library. In 1681, Shen left China with Philippe Couplet, a Jesuit, to travel in Europe. They wanted to promote the Jesuit mission and ask the Pope for help. They took five Chinese candidates for the priesthood, including Wu Li and Shen Fuzhong. Only Shen Fuzhong joined Couplet on his trip. Shen met King James II because the king was a Catholic, and Catholic and Jesuit priests were welcome at court. But in 1688, King James II was replaced by William III, who was Protestant. That meeting was special because it led to the famous painting, "The Chinese Convert," made by Sir Godfrey Kneller.

Knott's Berry Farm is a theme park in Bueno Park, California. It is owned by Cedar Fair and was the twelfth-most-visited theme park in North America in 2018. It gets about 4 million visitors each year. The park has 40 rides, such as roller coasters, family rides, dark rides, and water rides. The park started in the 1920s as a roadside berry stand. Walter Knott ran it on State Route 39 in California. By the 1940s, they added a restaurant, shops, and attractions, like a ghost town, to keep more visitors happy. Over the next two decades, the site became a modern amusement park. They started charging admission in 1968. In 1997, Cedar Fair bought the park for $300 million. Two years earlier, in 1995, the Knott's food business was bought by Conagra, Inc.
Ahmed Ben Bella was an Algerian politician, soldier, and revolutionary born on December 25, 1916. He became the first president of Algeria from 1963 to 1965 and lived until April 11, 2012.

Enrique Floriano Millán was born on October 9, 1982, in Lorca, Murcia. He is a swimmer from Spain who has vision problems. He competes in a special category for swimmers with severe visual impairment, called B2/S12.

SUVa is the capital and biggest city in Fiji. It is on the southeast coast of the island of Viti Levu, in the Rewa province, central division. In 1877, they chose SUVA as the capital because the former main European settlement at Levuka was too small. In 1882, the government moved from Levuka to SUVA. According to the 2017 census, SUVA city had 93,970 people. With nearby areas, the greater SUVA area had 185,913 people. SUVA, along with nearby towns Lami, Nasinu, and Nausori, has about 330,000 people, which is more than a third of Fiji's population. SUVA is a big city for politics, business, and culture in Fiji. It's also the main economic and cultural center for the South Pacific, hosting many important offices and missions. The city has a lively arts scene and is growing as a fashion center in the region.

In the United States, state courts handle most civil and criminal cases. These courts deal with disputes related to a U.S. state. Federal courts, which have a smaller number of cases and fewer staff, focus on different types of cases. State courts are common law courts. They follow the laws and rules set by their state’s constitution, state laws, and previous decisions by courts in their state. They also use federal laws when necessary. In most cases, a single judge decides cases, especially in trials. However, decisions from lower courts can be reviewed by a panel of a state court of appeals. There is also a highest court for appeals in each state, called the state supreme court, which oversees the entire court system. For cases involving federal laws, the state's highest court’s decision (including their refusal to hear appeals) can be appealed to the United States Supreme Court, which can choose whether to hear the case or not.

Vancouver is a big city in western Canada, in the lower mainland of British Columbia. In 2016, it had 631,486 people, up from 603,502 in 2011. The greater Vancouver area had 2,463,431 people, making it the third-largest city in Canada. It has the highest number of people living in a small area in Canada, with over 5,400 people per square kilometre. This makes it the fifth-most crowded city with over 250,000 people in North America. Vancouver has many different cultures and languages: 52% of its people speak English as a second language, 48.9% speak neither English nor French, and 50.6% belong to minority groups. It is often named as one of the best cities in the world for living and quality of life. The city planned to become the greenest city in the world by 2020. Vancouver was originally called Gastown and started as a small settlement near a tavern built in 1867. It changed its name to Vancouver in 1886 due to a deal with the Canadian Pacific Railway. The city's big port on the Pacific Ocean became important for trade between Asia, Europe, and eastern Canada. Vancouver has hosted many big events, including the 1954 Commonwealth Games, Expo 86, and the 2010 Winter Olympics. Forestry is its biggest industry, but tourism and film production are also important. Many film studios are in Vancouver and nearby Burnaby, making it one of North America's largest film production centers.

Snow Patrol's third studio album, "The Final Straw," was released in the UK and Ireland on August 4, 2003. It came out in the U.S. in 2004. This album was important because it helped the band become famous in other countries. Five singles were taken from the album over 14 months. It was the first album with lead guitarist Nathan Connolly and the last with bassist Mark McClelland. In 2004, the album was re-released in the UK with two extra tracks, but only the original version was sent to the U.S. The album was also available on SACD and dualdisc with 5.1 surround mixes.

Sorel Etrog was an artist, writer, and philosopher born in Romania and later lived in Israel and Canada. He was born on August 29, 1933, and passed away on February 26, 2014. Sorel is best known for his sculptures, which are modern art works.

Naughton is a village and used to be its own civil parish, but now it's part of Nedging-with-Naughton in the Babergh district of Suffolk, England. It's northwest of Ipswich and southwest of Stowmarket. Historically, it was part of the Cosford hundred in Suffolk. In 1935, Naughton joined with Nedging to form Nedging-with-Naughton. In 1931, the village had 98 people. Naughton is where two roads meet: the Whatfield road from the southwest and the New road from the southeast. There is a 14th-century church called St. Mary's in the center of the village, just west of where these roads meet.

Washburn County is in Maine, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 32, 856 people, which is the smallest county in Maine. The main town is Machias. The county started in 1789. It borders New Brunswick in Canada. Some say it's called "Sunrise County" because it's the easternmost point in the U.S. and might be where the sun first rises in the 48 states. Many small towns near the sea have small fishing businesses. Tourism is important but not as much as in other parts of the state. Blueberries are very important for the economy.

The Camp David Accords were political agreements signed by Egyptian President Anwar Sadat and Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin on September 17, 1978. They negotiated secretly at Camp David for 12 days. President Jimmy Carter of the United States witnessed the signing at the White House. The second agreement, "A Framework for the Conclusion of a Peace Treaty Between Egypt and Israel," led to the 1979 Egypt-Israel Peace Treaty. Sadat and Begin received the 1978 Nobel Peace Prize for their work. The first agreement, "A Framework for Peace in the Middle East," focused on Palestinian territories but was not part of the Palestinian negotiation process. It was criticized by the United Nations. Historian Jørgen Jensehaugen notes that by January 1981, when Carter left office, the first agreement was already facing criticism.

Richard Lester, born on January 19, 1932, is a retired American film director who now lives in the United Kingdom. He is famous for directing the Beatles in the 1960s and for his work on Superman movies in the 1980s. Lester is also an honorary associate of the London Film School.
The Royal New Zealand Navy (RNZN) is part of New Zealand's military. It has ships called "Warriors of the Sea of New Zealand." Right now, they have eight ships in their fleet.

The Detroit Pistons are an American professional basketball team based in Detroit. They play in the National Basketball Association (NBA) and are part of the Eastern Conference Central Division. Their home games are at Little Caesars Arena in midtown Detroit. The team was founded in Fort Wayne, Indiana, as the Fort Wayne Pistons in 1941. They were in the National Basketball League (NBL) and won championships in 1944 and 1945. In 1948, they joined the Basketball Association of America (BA). The NBL and BAA merged to form the NBA in 1949, and the Pistons became part of this new league. In 1957, the team moved to Detroit. The Pistons have won three NBA championships: in 1989, 1990, and 2004.

Maximilian Kolbe, born Rajmund Kolbe on January 8, 1894, and later venerated as Saint Maximilian Kolbe, was a Polish Catholic priest and Franciscan friar. He volunteered to die in place of another prisoner at Auschwitz, a German death camp in occupied Poland during World War II. Kolbe was active in promoting the veneration of the Virgin Mary and founded a monastery near Warsaw. He also ran several organizations and publications. Pope John Paul II canonized Father Kolbe on October 10, 1982, and declared him a martyr of charity. The Catholic Church honors him as the patron saint of amateur-radio operators, drug addicts, political prisoners, families, journalists, prisoners, and the pro-life movement. John Paul II called him the "apostle of consecration to Mary." His feast day is on August 14, the day he died.

The Renault Fr1 was a single-decker bus made by Renault Trucks in France from 1987 to 1997. It had a 6-cylinder Renault engine with an 9,834 cc displacement. The bus came in three types: TE, TX, and GTX. It could have either 1 or 2 doors. In 1997, the bus was redesigned and called the Renault Iliade.

Snakes are long, legless, meat-eating reptiles. They are cold-blooded like other lizards and covered in scales. Many snake species have more movable jaws than lizards, allowing them to eat prey larger than their heads. Their organs, like kidneys, are stacked one on top of the other because of their narrow bodies. Most snakes have only one working lung. Some have tiny vestigial claws near the back. Lizards, without legs or with small legs, have developed many times into legless forms. They are similar to snakes, but some have eyelids and ears. Snakes live almost everywhere except Antarctica, including most small land areas. There are over 3, 600 snake species in more than 20 families, ranging from very small to very large. The first snake fossils date back millions of years. Scientists believe snakes evolved from lizards that could burrow or live in water, possibly during the Jurassic period. The diversity of snakes increased after a major extinction event around 66 million years ago. The oldest written records of snakes come from an ancient Egyptian text called the Brooklyn Papyrus. Most snakes are not venomous, but those that are use venom to catch prey, not to protect themselves. Some venom can hurt or even kill humans. Nonvenomous snakes usually swallow their prey alive or squeeze them to kill.

Kambaata is a highland East Cushitic language, part of the larger Afro-Asiatic family. It is spoken by the Kambaata people. There are dialects like Kambaata, Tambaro, Alaba, and K'abeena. Kambaata is one of Ethiopia's official languages. It has many verbal affixes, which cause many sound changes. The language follows a subject-object-verb order. Kambaata includes five vowels (which are either long or short), ejectives, a retroflexed implosive, and a glottal stop. Some parts of the Bible, including the New Testament and parts of the Old Testament, have been translated into Kambaata. Initially, these translations used the Ethiopian syllabary (New Testament in 1992), but later, they were republished using Latin letters to fit new policies.

Sandpipers are a large group of wading birds, part of the family Scolopacidae. They include species called sandpipers, as well as others called curlew and snipe. Most sandpipers eat small insects or worms they find in the mud or soil. Different types of sandpipers have differently shaped beaks, which helps them feed in the same areas without competing for food. These birds have long bodies and legs, and narrow wings. Their beaks are usually thin, but the shape and length can vary. Sandpipers are small to medium-sized, ranging in size. They use their sensitive beaks to feel for food in the mud. Their feathers are mostly plain, with brown, gray, or streaked patterns. However, some species have brighter colors during breeding season. Most sandpipers make their nests in open areas and defend their territory with flying displays. They typically lay 3 to 4 eggs in a simple ground scrape. The baby sandpipers are able to move around soon after hatching.
Lantsch/Lenz is a municipality in the Albula region of the canton of Graubünden in Switzerland. Most people there speak Romansh.

Denis Farkasfalvy was born on June 23, 1936, and died on May 20, 2020. He was a Hungarian-American Catholic priest and monk in the Cistercian order. He was also an abbot, theologian, author, and translator.

Olga Maria Elisabeth Schwarzkopf, born on December 9, 1915, and died on August 3, 2006, was a German-born Austro-British soprano. She was very famous for singing lieder and performing in Viennese operettas, as well as in the operas of Mozart, Wagner, and Richard Strauss. After stopping performing, she taught singing around the world. Many people think she was one of the greatest sopranos of the 20th century.

The Sri Lankan civil war was a conflict in Sri Lanka from 1983 to 2009. It started on July 23, 1983, with the Tamil Tigers, led by Velupillai Prabhakaran, fighting against the Sri Lankan government. They wanted to create an independent Tamil state called Tamil Eelam in the north and east of Sri Lanka due to discrimination against Tamils by the government, which included several violent events in the years after Sri Lanka gained independence from Britain in 1948. After 26 years of fighting, the Sri Lankan military defeated the Tamil Tigers in May 2009, ending the war. The war caused many problems for Sri Lanka's people, environment, and economy. It is estimated that around 80,000 to 100,000 people died during the conflict. The number of civilian deaths was even higher. At the beginning of the conflict, the Sri Lankan forces tried to take back areas captured by the Tamil Tigers. The Tamil Tigers, known as the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), were listed as a terrorist group in 32 countries, including the United States, India, Canada, and European Union countries. The Sri Lankan government forces were also accused of human rights abuses. After fighting for two decades and failing four times to reach a peace agreement, a ceasefire was declared in December 2001. However, fighting resumed in late 2005, and the Sri Lankan government launched several military attacks against the Tamil Tigers in 2006, driving them out of the eastern part of the country. In 2007, the government moved its attacks to the north. They ended their ceasefire agreement on January 2, 2008, saying the Tamil Tigers had violated it over 10,000 times. With the help of destroyed arms-smuggling ships and a crackdown on Tamil Tiger funding, the Sri Lankan forces took control of all areas previously held by the Tamil Tigers, including their capital and military bases. In May 2009, the Tamil Tigers admitted defeat. After the Tamil Tigers were defeated, they stopped demanding a separate state and agreed to a federal solution. In May 2010, President Mahinda Rajapaksa created a commission to look into the conflict. Since the end of the civil war, Sri Lanka has faced criticism for human rights violations, including war crimes. The Tamil Tigers were known for carrying out attacks, like suicide bombings. The Mullivaikkal remembrance day is observed annually by Sri Lankan Tamils to honor those who died in the final stages of the civil war, which ended on May 18, 2009. In January 2020, President Gotabaya Rajapaksa claimed that more than 20,000 abducted Sri Lankan Tamil civilians were dead.

The team captain of a soccer team is a player chosen to lead the team on the field. They are often one of the more experienced players or someone who can greatly affect the game. The team captain usually wears an armband to show they are the leader.
Mitrovoça, which comes from the name "Saint Demetrius" or "Sveti Dimitrije" (in Cyrillic: "Свети Димитрије"), might be called:

A rhetorical question is one where the person asking doesn't expect a direct answer. Often, it’s used to start a discussion or to show the speaker's opinion. For example, "Can't you do anything right?" is asked not to find out if the person can do things right, but to suggest they can't.
Morrowcourt is a commune in Aisne, which is in Hauts-de-France, in northern France.

Piedmont blues, also called east coast or southeastern blues, is mainly about a guitar playing technique called the piedmont fingerstyle. This style uses a thumb to create a steady beat on the bass strings while the other fingers play a more rhythmic melody on the higher strings. It sounds a bit like ragtime or stride piano. This style was named by blues researcher Peter B. Lowry, who shared credit with Bruce Bastin, another folklorist. The piedmont style differs from others, especially Mississippi delta blues, because of its ragtime-like rhythm.
Moore Haven is a city in Florida, United States. It is the county seat of Glades County. The population was 1,680 in 2010. Moore Haven is on the southwest side of Lake Okeechobee.

In the 1980 Democratic presidential primaries, voters chose the nominee for the Democratic Party's presidential candidate. Incumbent President Jimmy Carter was chosen as the nominee through primary elections and caucuses. These events led to the 1980 Democratic National Convention in New York City from August 11 to 14. Carter had a strong challenge from Senator Ted Kennedy of Massachusetts. Kennedy won 12 contests and got over seven million votes. He did not give up hope of winning the nomination until the second day of the convention. This was the last election where an incumbent president's party nomination was contested before the convention.

Sin City is a series of comic books by American writer-artist Frank Miller. The first story appeared in "Dark Horse Presents Fifth Anniversary Special" in April 1991. It continued in issues 51 to 62 of "Dark Horse Presents" from May 1991 to June 1992, under the title "Sin City." There are several other stories of different lengths that followed. The stories are set in a city called Basin City and share many characters. A movie version of Sin City, directed by Robert Rodriguez and Frank Miller, came out on April 1, 2005. A sequel was released on August 22, 2014. Dimension Films is making a new TV series based on Sin City. Stephen L'heureux, who worked on the second film, will oversee the series with Frank Miller, the creator of Sin City. The new TV series will have new characters and timelines, and it will be more like the original comic books rather than the movies.

Villach is the seventh-largest city in Austria and the second-largest in Carinthia. It is a key traffic hub for southern Austria and the Alpe-Adria region. The population of Villach is 61,887. Together with other Alpine towns, Villach is part of the Alpine Town of the Year association. They work to promote sustainable development in the Alpine Arc. Villach became the first town to receive the title of Alpine Town of the Year in 1997.

Lindsey Nelson was born on May 25, 1919, and passed away on June 10, 1995. He was an American sportscaster known for announcing college football and New York Mets baseball. Nelson worked with the Mets for 17 years and with the San Francisco Giants for three years. He covered college football for 33 years, including 26 Cotton Bowls, five Sugar Bowls, and four Rose Bowls. He also announced Notre Dame games for 14 years. Nelson is part of 13 separate halls of fame. Fans remember him as a talented broadcaster and an enthusiastic sports lover. His colorful jackets and lively broadcasts made him one of the top sportscasters in the industry.

Brooke Christa Shields, born on May 31, 1965, is an American actress and model. She started as a child model and was famous when she was 12 for playing a child prostitute in the movie "Pretty Baby" (1978). The film is set in New Orleans at the beginning of the 20th century. Shields became well-known for this role and kept modeling until her late teenage years. She also acted in movies like "The Blue Lagoon" (1980) and "Endless Love" (1981). In 1983, she stopped modeling to go to Princeton University, where she studied languages and got a degree. In the 1990s, Shields returned to acting and appeared in smaller roles in movies. She also acted in TV shows like "Suddenly Susan" (1996-2000), where she was nominated for two Golden Globes, and "Lipstick Jungle" (2008-2009). In 2017, she acted again in NBC's 19th season. Since 2014, Shields has been the voice of Beverly Goodman in the animated shows "Mr. Pickles" and "Momma Named Me Sheriff."

Lorenzo Cherubini, born on September 27, 1966, is known as Jovanotti. He is an Italian singer-songwriter and rapper. The name Jovanotti comes from "giovanotti," which means "young man" in Italian. At first, he used "Joe Vanotti" as his stage name, but a poster mistakenly called him "Jovanotti," and he kept the name. Jovanotti often uses the nickname "Jova" with his fans. He has a TV channel called Jova.tv, which started on October 2, 2014. Jovanotti's music style changed over time. He started with hip hop, rap, and disco but later included funk, world music, classical, and ska. His lyrics also became more about big ideas like philosophy, religion, and politics. He cares a lot about social and political issues. Some of his older songs sound like 1980s pop with many keyboards. He sings in Italian most of the time but also made a Spanish album with his biggest hits. Jovanotti performed on a charity album called "Red Hot + Rhapsody" in 1998, where he sang "I Got Rhythm." He also joined a charity concert with Luciano Pavarotti in 1996.
Vallorbe is a municipality in the Jura-Nord-Vaudois district, which is in the canton of Vaud in Switzerland.

Bettlach is a commune in Haut-Rhin department and Grand Est region of northeastern France.
Colcannon is a traditional Irish dish. It is made by mashed potatoes with kale or cabbage.

Potsdamer Platz is a big square and crossroads in the center of Berlin, Germany. It is south of the Brandenburg Gate and the Reichstag, near the southeast corner of the Tiergarten Park. The square is named after the city of Potsdam, southwest of Berlin. Potsdamer Platz was an intersection of rural roads that became one of Europe's busiest traffic spots in just over a century. During World War II, it was completely destroyed. After the war, during the Cold War, the Berlin Wall cut through where it used to be. Since Germany reunited, Potsdamer Platz has been rebuilt with big projects.

Sir John Grant McKenzie Laws lived from May 10, 1945, to April 5, 2020. He was a lord justice of appeal. He worked in this role from 1999 to 2016. He also taught at the University of Cambridge as the Goodhart visiting professor of legal science. Additionally, he was an honorary fellow of Robinson College, Cambridge.

Massimo Mattioli, born on September 25, 1943, and passed away on August 23, 2019, was an Italian artist and cartoonist. He started his career in 1965 by publishing "Vermetto Sigh" in the comic book "Il Vittorioso." Later, his work appeared in "Corto Maltese" and "Frigidaire." In 1968, he moved to London and made comics for "Mayfair" magazine. In the early 1970s, he created the character Pasquino for the "Paese Sera" newspaper. In 1973, he began working with "Il Giornalino," creating the character Pinky. In 1977, Mattioli, along with Stefano Tamburini, launched the underground magazine "Cannibale." The same year, "Cannibale" published the first adventure of Joe Galaxy. In 1982, he created the "Squeak the Mouse" series, which parodied "Tom and Jerry." Mattioli received several awards, including the French Prix Phenix in 1971 and the "Romics d'Or" in 2009.
Kensington is a town in Montgomery County, Maryland, United States. In 2010, it had 2,213 people. Greater Kensington includes the entire 20895 zip code and has 19,054 people.
Patrick Dennistoun McGorry, born on September 10, 1952, is an Australian psychiatrist. He is famous for creating early intervention services to help young people with mental disorders.

Fratton Park is a football stadium in Portsmouth, a city in the United Kingdom. It's where Portsmouth F.C. first played. Portsmouth F.C. was formed on April 5, 1898. Fratton Park is special because it's on an island, Portsea Island, unlike most other stadiums in the English Premier League. It was built in 1899 on a field that used to grow potatoes. It opened on August 15, 1899, and their first match there was on September 6, 1899, against Southampton F.C., with 4,141 people watching. The stadium is named after Fratton railway station, one mile west of where it is, to make it seem closer to the station. Its maximum capacity was 58,000 in 1935, but the record attendance was 51,385 in 1949. In 1996, the stadium became all-seated, reducing its capacity. Portsmouth fans call it "the old girl." In recent years, it's been called "Fortress Fratton" because it often has many fans and a strong football atmosphere. The stadium is in the St. James parish of Milton, Portsmouth.

Naomie Melanie Harris, born on September 6, 1976, is an English actress. She began her career as a child, appearing in the TV show "Simon and the Witch" in 1987. In 2002, she played Selena in the movie "28 Days Later." She also acted as Tia Dalma, the witch, in the second and third "Pirates of the Caribbean" films. In 2013, she was in a film as Winnie Mandela. In 2012 and 2015, she played Eve Moneypenny in the "James Bond" movies "Skyfall" and "Spectre." She will reappear in the upcoming "James Bond" film "No Time to Die" in 2020. In 2016, she starred in "Moonlight," which got great reviews. Her performance there earned her nominations for the Golden Globe, BAFTA, and Academy Award for best supporting actress. In recognition of her work, Harris was named an Officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE) in the 2017 New Year Honours.

The grand tour was a tradition where wealthy young European men, usually from around 21 years old, would travel through Europe in the 17th and 18th centuries. They typically went with an adult, like a family member. This journey helped them learn about ancient and Renaissance art and culture, and meet other rich, polite people. It lasted from a few months to a few years. By the mid-18th century, it became common for people from the nobility in Central Europe as well. The tour included seeing important art and music. A guide called a cicerone was often hired. The grand tour became less popular as interest in classical culture faded, and easier travel options appeared. Even today, the idea of a grand tour influences travel choices and ideas about culture. It was less about scholarly study and more about enjoying cities like Venice and Rome. For artists, understanding art techniques was important, but the full grand tour experience was too expensive. Guides like Jonathan Richardson’s book helped make these trips more popular. In Rome, dealers like Thomas Jenkins sold and advised on buying ancient art. Souvenirs included coins and medals. Artists like Pompeo Batoni painted wealthy travelers among ancient Roman sites. Few went much south in Italy or to Greece.

The banker horse is a breed of wild horse living on barrier islands in North Carolina's Outer Banks. These horses are small, tough, and gentle. They came from domesticated Spanish horses that might have been brought to America in the 1500s. The horses could have become wild after surviving shipwrecks or being left on the islands by explorers led by Lucas Vázquez de Ayllón or Sir Richard Grenville. There are banker horses on Ocracoke Island, Shackleford Banks, Currituck Banks, Cedar Island, and in the Rachel Carson Estuarine Sanctuary. Although they can damage plants and ground-nesting animals, the horses are allowed to stay because of their history. They eat marsh grasses that provide them with water and food, and they also feed on temporary freshwater pools. To keep the population in check and avoid inbreeding, and to protect their habitat, the horses are managed by the National Park Service, the North Carolina state government, and some private groups. They are checked for diseases like equine infectious anemia. In 1996, a disease was found on Shackleford and quickly stopped. The horses are kept safe from traffic on North Carolina Highway 12. To limit the number of horses, some are adopted, and some are given birth control. Wild banker horses that are trained can be used for trail riding, driving, and sometimes for mounted patrols.

Miriam Margolyes, born on May 18, 1941, is a British-Australian actress and comedian. She started her career in theatre. She also acted in films and television shows. In 1993, she got a BAFTA award for her role in "The Age of Innocence" directed by Martin Scorsese. She is known for playing Professor Sprout in the "Harry Potter" movies. Margolyes has lived in England, Australia, and Italy for many years. She acted in plays in both England and Australia. For example, she was in the first Australian performance of a 2013 play. In 2013, she became an Australian citizen.
Chavenon is a commune in the Allier department, which is in Auvergne, in central France.

An eagle is a common name for many large birds of prey in the family Accipitridae. Eagles are part of several groups called genera, but not all are closely related. Most of the 60 eagle species are found in Eurasia and Africa. Outside this area, only 14 species of eagle can be found: 2 in North America, 9 in Central and South America, and 3 in Australia.

A chemical substance is a type of matter with a fixed composition and distinct properties. It cannot be broken down into its elements using physical methods, meaning chemical bonds must be broken. Chemical substances can be simple elements, compounds, or alloys. Sometimes, chemical elements are included in the definition, depending on the view of experts. Pure substances are called 'pure' to distinguish them from mixtures. Pure water is an example of a chemical substance, as it always has the same properties and the same ratio of hydrogen to oxygen, whether from a river or a lab. Diamond, gold, salt, and sugar are other commonly found pure substances. In practice, substances are never completely pure, and their purity depends on their intended use. Chemical substances can be solids, liquids, gases, or plasma, and change forms with temperature or pressure. Chemical reactions can combine or change these substances. Energy forms like light and heat are not considered chemical substances.

NBC is an American TV and radio network. It belongs to NBCUniversal, which is part of Comcast. NBC's main office is in New York City, but it has big offices in Los Angeles, Chicago, and Philadelphia. NBC is one of the biggest TV networks in the U.S. It is sometimes called the "Peacock Network," because of its peacock logo. The logo was first used in 1956 to show NBC's advancements in early color TV, and became the network's official symbol in 1979. NBC started in 1926 by RCA. At first, RCA was owned by General Electric (GE). In 1932, GE had to sell RCA and NBC because of antitrust laws. In 1986, GE bought NBC for $6.4 billion. Bob Wright became the CEO of NBC and held that position until 2007, when Jeff Zucker took over. In 2003, NBCUniversal was formed when Comcast combined its entertainment assets with GE. In 2011, Comcast got control of NBCUniversal. By 2013, Comcast owned all of NBCUniversal. After the Comcast merger, Steve Burke became the new CEO of NBCUniversal, replacing Jeff Zucker. NBC has 13 main stations and nearly 200 affiliates across the U.S. and its territories. Some of these affiliates are also available in Canada and Mexico via pay-TV providers or in border areas over-the-air. NBC also has agreements to use its brand on international channels in South Korea and Germany.

Multiple cameras are used in filmmaking and video production. Several cameras record or broadcast a scene at the same time. This method is called multi-camera or multicam. It is different from using just one camera.

Lopp Lagoon is a tidal lake near the westernmost tip of the Seward Peninsula in Alaska. Many creeks flow into it, but the most water comes from the Mint River. Some salt water from the Pacific Ocean enters the lagoon through several channels connecting it to the Bering Strait. It was named in 1900 for William Thomas Lopp, a missionary and leader of a relief expedition. Lopp Lagoon has historically been important for local people, providing salmon and waterfowl as food.

Paulo César Wanchope Watson, known as Paulo Wanchope, was born on July 31, 1976. He is a former Costa Rican footballer and former coach of the Costa Rica national football team. Wanchope is the second top scorer in Costa Rica's national team history, with 45 goals in 73 international matches. He scored against Brazil in 2002 and against Germany twice in 2006. These goals make him the top scorer for Costa Rica in the FIFA World Cup. He shares this record with Rónald Gómez.
Adams is a city in Adams County, Wisconsin. The population was 1,967 in 2010. It is in the town of Adams.
Clay County is in Indiana, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 26,890 people. The main town is Brazil. Clay County is part of the Terre Haute, Indiana, area.
Poygan is a town in Winnebago County, Wisconsin, United States. In 2010, the town had 1,301 people.

Port Vila, or simply Vila, is the capital and largest city of Vanuatu, located on the island of Efate. In 2009, the last census, Vila had 44,040 people. That's 35% more than in 1999, when the population was 29,356. In 2009, Vila's population made up 18.8% of Vanuatu's total population and 66.9% of Efate's population. Vila is on the south coast of Efate, in Shefa Province. It is Vanuatu's main economic and commercial center. The mayor of Vila is Erick Puyo Festa, from the Vanua'aku Pati party, who was elected in January 2018. His deputy is Jenny Regenvanu, from the GRAN MO JASTIS Pati. On March 13, 2015, Vila suffered significant damage from Cyclone Pam.

Rolf Leeser was born on June 4, 1929, in Essen, Germany. He played football for Ajax in the Netherlands from 1948 to 1954. Leeser joined Ajax's youth academy at 12 years old. He made his first professional game on September 19, 1948. He became a regular player during the 1951-52 season and played until April 1954, scoring six goals in 34 matches. Apart from football, Leeser was a fashion designer. He started Leeser B.V., a women's fashion company. He also helped redesign the Ajax logo, which has been used since 1990. Leeser passed away on March 21, 2018, at the age of 88. He was married to Anita B. Leeser-Gassan.
Brisbane is an Australian area for voting in the state of Queensland.

Municipios, or "municipios" in Spanish, are the second-level administrative divisions in Mexico. The first level is the "state," or "estado" in Spanish. As of September 2017, there are 2,448 municipalities in Mexico, not counting the 16 "delegaciones" of Mexico City. The political organization and responsibilities of municipalities are described in Article 115 of the 1917 constitution and further detailed in the state constitutions. Municipalities are different from cities, as some municipalities can be as large as states, whereas cities are measured in blocks.

Equivalent weight, also called gram equivalent, is the mass of a substance that will combine with or displace a fixed amount of another substance. The equivalent weight of an element is the mass that combines with or displaces 1.008 grams of hydrogen, 8.0 grams of oxygen, or 35.5 grams of chlorine. These values are found by dividing the atomic weight by the usual valence. For acid-base reactions, the equivalent weight of an acid or base is the mass that provides or reacts with one mole of hydrogen ions. For redox reactions, the equivalent weight is the mass that supplies or reacts with one mole of electrons. Equivalent weight has the same units as mass, unlike atomic weight, which is a ratio and has no units. Originally, equivalent weights were found through experiments. Now, they are derived from molar masses. The equivalent weight of a compound can be calculated by dividing its molecular mass by the number of positive or negative charges it forms when dissolved.

Pegomastax, named for its strong jaw, is a type of dinosaur found in South Africa. It lived during the early Jurassic period, about 200 to 190 million years ago. The partial skull of Pegomastax, including parts of the lower jaw and a toothless beak, was discovered in Voyizane, Joe Gqabi district, in the upper Elliot formation rocks. This specimen was found during an expedition from 1966 to 1967 but was only described in 2012 by Paul Sereno. The type species is "P. africana." Pegomastax was a small, parrot-like herbivore, measuring less than 60 cm in length. Its lower jaw was strong and had a short beak. Like other heterodontosaurids, Pegomastax had a large tooth at the start of its lower jaw, which may have been used for defense.

Andrés Muschietti, born on August 26, 1973, is an Argentine filmmaker. He gained fame in 2013 with the movie "Mama," which he made with his sister, Barbara Muschietti, and Neil Cross. They based "Mama" on a short film of the same name. At age 39, this film caught Guillermo Del Toro's attention, who later became its executive producer. Muschietti became even more well-known for directing two films in the "It" series. The first, "It" (2017), was an adaptation of Stephen King's novel and became the highest-grossing horror film ever. Its sequel, "It Chapter Two" (2019), was also directed by him. Both films were made by Warner Bros. and New Line Cinema. Muschietti will direct two upcoming films for Warner Bros.: "The Flash," starring Ezra Miller, set in the DC universe, and a live-action version of "Attack on Titan." He will also direct a Netflix remake of "The Howling."
Chamely Khatun, born on November 11, 1988, is a Bangladeshi cricketer. She plays for the Bangladesh national women's cricket team. She is a right-handed batswoman and a right-arm slow bowler.

Karl-Heinz von Hassel was a German actor born on February 8, 1939, in Hamburg. He died on April 19, 2016, at 77 years old. He appeared in over 100 films and television shows from 1960 to 2012. He trained for a business career but also took acting lessons. Starting in 1960, he performed on stage at different theaters. From 1966, he acted regularly on TV. He had important roles in movies directed by Rainer Werner Fassbinder. He was often cast as police officers but also played industrial workers. He passed away in Hamburg after a short illness.

Uddingston is a small town in South Lanarkshire, Scotland. It is located north of the River Clyde, southeast of Glasgow city center. Uddingston serves as a suburb for Glasgow, where people live but commute to work in the city.
Ismael Gómez Falcón was born on April 24, 1984. He is a Spanish football player who plays as a goalkeeper for Hércules CF.
Anizy-le-Grand is a commune in Aisne, which is in Hauts-de-France, a region in northern France. It became a commune on January 1, 2019, after Anizy-le-Château, Faucoucourt, and Lizy merged.

The Hanshin Tigers (Japanese: 阪神タイガース "Hanshin Taigāsu") are a professional baseball team in Japan. They play in the Central League and are based in Nishinomiya, Hyōgo Prefecture. The team is owned by Hanshin Electric Railway Co., Ltd., a company that is part of Hankyu Hanshin Holdings Inc. The Hanshin Tigers are one of the oldest professional baseball clubs in Japan. They first played in 1936 as the Osaka Tigers. They changed their name to Hanshin Tigers in 1961.

Dokaor Toongtong is a Thai singer from the Isan area. She sings luk thung and mor lam sing music. Her most popular songs are "Ber Tho Jao Choo," "Oak Hak Wan Hae Tiean," "Miea Kao," and "Rak Phay Thee Kaeng Saphue." She is sometimes called Aor or "Sao Sieng Sor," which means "beautiful voice."

Bad Doberan was a former district in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Germany. It was named after its largest town, Bad Doberan, where "bad" means "spa" in German. The district was around the city of Rostock and bordered the Baltic Sea to the north. It also bordered the former districts of Nordvorpommern, Güstrow, and Nordwestmecklenburg. In September 2011, the district was abolished. Its area is now part of the Rostock district.

Cylinder is a city in Palo Alto County, Iowa, United States. In 2010, the city's population was 88 people.
Trévoux is a town in the Ain department of eastern France. The people there are called Trévoltiens. It is near Lyon and is built on the steep left bank of the Saône River.

The Forlì-Cesena province is in the Emilia-Romagna region of Italy. Its capital is Forlì. As of 2016, the province had 394,273 people. It covers an area. The province includes 30 communes, and its president is Davide Drei. Even though it is near the independent republic of San Marino, Forlì-Cesena does not share a land border with it.

Efficiency means how well a task is completed using the least amount of resources. In simpler terms, it's about using inputs effectively to produce desired outputs with minimal waste. Efficiency is about doing things right, while effectiveness is about achieving the desired results, regardless of how it is done. A saying distinguishes them by saying, "efficiency is doing things right, while effectiveness is doing the right things." This means choosing the right goals is as important as the process. Efficiency is often mistaken for effectiveness. Efficiency can be measured as the amount of output compared to the resources used. This is usually expressed as a percentage. For example, if 100% of energy is used without any loss, then the efficiency is 100%. Some measurements like specific impulse are used when efficiency can't be expressed as a percentage. Businesses sometimes confuse efficiency with effectiveness. For instance, a company might produce a lot by making workers work longer hours, but this doesn't mean it's an efficient process. Similarly, a company might use more energy per product to achieve high production numbers, which is effective but not efficient. Efficiency can be measured by the formula: efficiency (r) = output (p) / input (c). In energy conversion, for example, useful work output (p) is compared to high-temperature heat input (c). Efficiency can never be more than 100% due to the conservation of energy.

In 2000, Louise, a UK singer, released her 10th solo song. This song was from her third solo album called "Elbow Beach." The song uses a part from a song called "Different Strokes" by Syl Johnson, which the Wu-Tang Clan also used. In the UK, the single reached number 13 on the charts.

The World Trade Organization (WTO) is an organization where countries make rules about buying and selling things between each other. It started on January 1, 1995, after a big meeting in Marrakesh, where 123 countries agreed. Before that, there was a different organization called GATT that began in 1948. The WTO has rules about selling goods, services, and ideas. It helps countries talk and decide about trade by giving them a set of guidelines. It also has a system to solve disagreements about following these rules. One rule is that countries should not treat other countries unfairly, but there are some exceptions for things like protecting the environment or national security. The WTO has a boss called the Director-General. As of now, his name is Roberto Azevêdo. He has a team of over 600 people working with him in Geneva, Switzerland. In 2013, all countries agreed on a new rule to make it easier to do trade, which was the first big agreement since the WTO began. In January 2017, countries changed an important rule about protecting inventions and ideas, which is the first change since the WTO started in 1995. Studies show that the WTO has helped trade grow. Without it, trade barriers would be much higher. Many trade agreements now mention the WTO, often many times, and sometimes copy parts of its rules directly.

Julian Clare May, born on July 10, 1931, and died on October 17, 2017, was an American writer of science fiction, fantasy, horror, science, and children's books. She also used different pen names. She is best known for her "Saga of Pliocene Exile" and "Galactic Milieu Series" books.

Maurice Petty was born on March 27, 1939, and passed away on July 25, 2020. He was an American NASCAR crew chief and engine builder for Petty Enterprises, which he helped own. He was inducted into the International Motorsports Hall of Fame in 2011. Later, in 2014, he was also enshrined in the NASCAR Hall of Fame. He was the first engine builder to be honored in the NASCAR Hall of Fame.
Saint-Julien-de-Mailloc was a small town in Calvados, which is in Normandy, a region in northwestern France. On January 1, 2016, Saint-Julien-de-Mailloc became part of a new town called Valorbiquet.

West Palm Beach is a city and the main town of Palm Beach County, Florida, United States. It is right west of Palm Beach, which is on a barrier island across Lake Worth Lagoon. In 2010, the population was 99,919. West Palm Beach is part of the Miami metropolitan area, which had about 6,158,824 people in 2017. It is the oldest city in South Florida, becoming a city two years before Miami in 1894. West Palm Beach is about north of Miami's downtown area.

Andromeda is one of the 48 constellations listed by Ptolemy, a 2nd-century astronomer. It remains one of the 88 modern constellations. Named for Andromeda, the daughter of Cassiopeia in Greek mythology, it was chained to a rock to be eaten by the sea monster Cetus. In the northern hemisphere, Andromeda is best seen in autumn evenings. It lies above the celestial equator and can be seen only north of 40° south latitude. It's a large constellation, with an area of 722 square degrees—over 1,400 times the size of the full moon and more than 10 times the size of the smallest constellation, Crux. Its brightest star, Alpha Andromedae, is part of Pegasus too. Gamma Andromedae is a colorful binary and popular among amateur astronomers. Beta Andromedae, slightly less bright, is a red giant visible to the naked eye. The Andromeda galaxy, or M31, is the largest and brightest deep-sky object in Andromeda. It's the closest spiral galaxy to the Milky Way and one of the brightest Messier objects. Other galaxies within Andromeda include M110, M32, and NGC 891. The Blue Snowball Nebula, a planetary nebula, is visible in a telescope. In Chinese astronomy, Andromeda stars were part of four different constellations with special meanings. In Hindu mythology, there's also a constellation related to Andromeda. The Andromedids, a weak meteor shower, are seen in November from Andromeda.

NCAA Division II (D-II) is a middle-level division in the National Collegiate Athletic Association. It offers a choice between the larger Division I, which has more funding, and the scholarship-free Division III. Before 1973, NCAA's smaller schools were in the College Division. In 1973, when the NCAA started using numbers for divisions, the College Division split. Schools that wanted to offer scholarships or compete against schools that did became Division II. Those that chose not to offer scholarships became Division III. Espn televises Division II football's championship game. Cbs shows men's basketball championships. Espn2 covers women's basketball championships. Stadium broadcasts six Division II football games on Thursdays during the regular season and one men's basketball game each Saturday during the regular season. In 2015, the official slogan for NCAA Division II became "Make it yours."
Bartholomäberg is a town and a popular place for tourists. It is in the Bludenz district of Vorarlberg, Austria.

A steel mill or steelworks is a factory where steel is made. It can be a complete plant that makes steel from starting materials like iron ore all the way to finished products. Or, it can be a plant that makes semi-finished steel products from melted iron or scrap metal.

The Screen Actors Guild (SAG) was a labor union in America for over 100,000 film and TV actors worldwide. In March 2012, SAG members voted to join with the American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (AFTRA) to form SAG-AFTRA. SAG’s goal was to make sure actors get fair pay, benefits, and working conditions. They also collect money when their recorded performances are used without permission and protect actors' rights. SAG was created in 1933 to help actors who had unfair, long-term contracts with movie studios. These contracts didn’t set work hours or rest times and could be renewed by the studios. They often controlled actors' personal lives. SAG was part of a larger group called the Associated Actors and Artists of America (AAAA), which includes other unions. SAG controlled movie performances while sharing TV, radio, internet, and new media roles with AFTRA. SAG had offices in major U.S. cities and gave out Screen Actors Guild Awards each year, which are seen as a sign of success before bigger awards like the Oscars. This award continues under the same name with SAG-AFTRA.

Thomas P. Tiffany was born on December 30, 1957. He is an American businessman and politician. Since 2020, Tiffany has been a U.S. representative for Wisconsin's 7th congressional district. He belongs to the Republican Party. Before this, Tiffany served in the Wisconsin State Assembly from 2011 to 2013 and the Wisconsin Senate from 2013 to 2020. Tiffany took over Sean Duffy's seat in Congress after winning a special election against Democrat Tricia Zunker.

Ronald Gabriel Palillo was an American actor and teacher. He was born on April 2, 1949, and died on August 14, 2012. He is most famous for playing the character Arnold Horshack in the TV show "Welcome Back, Kotter" from 1975 to 1979. Arnold Horshack was a silly, not very smart character that people liked.

Arch Enemy is a Swedish melodic death metal band from Halmstad. They were formed in 1995. The band members were from other groups like Carcass, Armageddon, Carnage, Mercyful Fate, Spiritual Beggars, The Agonist, Nevermore, and Eucharist. The band was started by Michael Amott from Carcass and Johan Liiva, who were also from Carnage. They have released ten studio albums, three live albums, three video albums, and four EPs. The band’s original singer was Johan Liiva. In 2000, he was replaced by Angela Gossow from Germany. Angela left the band in March 2014 to manage it and was replaced by Alissa White-Gluz from Canada.

The Canadian National Railway (CN) is a big train company in Canada. It is based in Montreal, Quebec. CN serves Canada and parts of the United States. It is the biggest railway company in Canada, both in size and money earned. CN's rail network stretches from the Atlantic Coast in Nova Scotia to the Pacific Coast in British Columbia, covering about 20,000 miles of track. In the late 20th century, CN grew by taking over other railroads like the Illinois Central. CN is a public company with about 24,000 workers. As of July 2019, its value was about $90 billion Canadian. CN used to be owned by the Canadian government. It became a private company in 1995. As of 2019, Bill Gates was the biggest shareholder of CN's stock. CN was called "CNR" from 1919 to 1960 and "CN" from 1960 until now.

Jefferson County is in the state of Iowa. In 2010, it had 16, 843 people. The county seat is Fairfield. Jefferson County was created in January 1839 and was named after President Thomas Jefferson. The area around Fairfield is considered a micropolitan statistical area.

Lester Bruce McDonald was born on September 19, 1914, and died on July 26, 1971. He was an American football player. McDonald played as an end in the National Football League (NFL). He played for the Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions, and Philadelphia Eagles. He also played college football at the University of Nebraska. In 1937, he was chosen as the eighth player in the first round of the NFL draft.
