Ivan Hašek, born on September 6, 1963, is a former professional footballer from Czech Republic. He played as a central midfielder. He played for Sparta Prague for 11 years, appearing in over 300 official games. Later, he managed the club. Hašek played for Czechoslovakia in the 1990 World Cup. He also became the president of the Czech Republic Football Association.
Billy used to be a commune in Calvados, which is in Normandy, a region in northwestern France. On January 1, 2017, it joined with other communes to form a new commune called Valambray.
glos is a commune in Calvados, which is in Normandy, a region in northwestern France.
Egliswil is a village and municipality in the district of Lenzburg, in the canton of Aargau, in Switzerland.

Katiti Aboriginal Land Trust (Katiti ALT) is a land trust for a piece of land in the southwest of Australia's Northern Territory. It is in an area called Petermann. The trust was created in 1980 through the Katiti Land Claim. The trust's owners are Pitjantjatjara, Yankunytjatjara, and Luritja people. The land is officially known as Northern Territory portion 1818. It is next to the larger Petermann Land Trust and the Uluṟu–Kata Tjuṯa National Park to the north and west. To the east and south, there are two farms called Curtin Springs and Mulga Park. The town of Yulara is not part of the land trust and is between the Katiti block and the Uluṟu–Kata Tjuṯa National Park. Katiti ALT is named after Katiti, a natural spring located near Lake Amadeus. This spring was first described by Baldwin Spencer and Francis James Gillen in 1894, who called it "Kurtitina." In 1903, Lawrence Wells and his team visited the spring, and Herbert Basedow later marked it as "Curtyteena" on his maps.

Kansas is split into 4 congressional districts. Each district has a representative in the U.S. House of Representatives. The number of districts hasn't changed since the 2010 census. From 2010 to 2018, all representatives were Republicans. But after the 2018 elections, one Republican lost to a Democrat. Now, Kansas has 3 Republican and 1 Democratic representative.

The Institute for Research on Public Policy (IRPP) is an independent, national, bilingual, and not-for-profit organization based in Montreal, Quebec. Its goal is to improve public policy in Canada by doing research, offering insights, and helping people talk about important issues. It publishes research that is reviewed by experts and organizes events like conferences, round tables, and discussions for different groups, including experts, policymakers, and the general public. The IRPP also publishes a magazine called "Policy Options." The IRPP focuses on four main topics: how Canada’s government is changing, how Canada can meet its innovation challenges, income inequality, and how global trade and production changes affect Canada’s economy. The IRPP was created in 1968 by Prime Minister Pierre Elliott Trudeau’s government. It receives funding from an endowment fund that includes contributions from federal and provincial governments and the private sector. The IRPP is registered as a charity and is legally incorporated in Canada. Anne McLellan is the chair of the board of directors, and Graham Fox is the president and CEO.

Air Dolomiti S.p.A. is an Italian airline based in Dossobuono, Villafranca di Verona, Italy. It has operating bases in Munich and Frankfurt airports in Germany. Air Dolomiti is completely owned by Lufthansa. The airline flies from various Italian cities to Munich and Frankfurt. Most of its flights use the Air Dolomiti brand and are shared with Lufthansa. A few flights use the Lufthansa brand.
David Wayne, born Wayne James McMeekan on January 30, 1914, and died on February 9, 1995, was an American actor. He worked in both stage and movies. His career lasted for more than 50 years.
Janine Sutto was born on April 20, 1921, and passed away on March 28, 2017. She was a Canadian actress and comedian who was born in France.

Antonino Rocca, born Antonino Biasetton, was born on April 13, 1921, and died on March 15, 1977. He was an Italian Argentine professional wrestler. He teamed with Miguel Pérez. After he died, he was added to the WWE Hall of Fame in 1995 and the Wrestling Observer Newsletter Hall of Fame in 1996.

Slim Harpo, born James Isaac Moore on January 11, 1924, and known for his stage name, was an American blues musician. He was famous for playing swamp blues. Slim Harpo was very successful, with his songs reaching the top of the R&B charts. Some of his biggest hits were "I'm a King Bee" in 1957, "Rainin' in My Heart" in 1961, and "Baby Scratch My Back" in 1966. This last song was also popular, reaching No. 16 on the US pop chart. He was a master of playing the harmonica, also called the harp.

The Celtic League is a group founded in 1961. It works to promote Celtic identity and culture in Ireland, Scotland, Wales, Brittany, Cornwall, and the Isle of Man. These places are known as the Celtic nations. The League especially wants to help these nations keep their Celtic languages. It also wants more self-rule and eventually independence for each nation. The Celtic League is recognized by the United Nations Economic and Social Council.

Lake Amadeus is a large salt lake in the southwest corner of Northern Territory, Australia. It is about north of Uluru, also known as Ayers Rock. To the northwest, there is a smaller lake called Lake Neale. Lake Amadeus is part of the Amadeus Basin. This basin was formed by erosion from the Petermann Orogeny, an ancient mountain-building process.

Ángela María Ponce Camacho is a Spanish model and beauty pageant winner. She won Miss Universe Spain in 2018. On June 29, 2018, Ponce made history by becoming the first openly transgender woman to win Miss Spain. She represented Spain in Miss Universe 2018 as the first openly transgender contestant. However, she did not advance to the finals.
Bolivia is divided into 1,374 cantons, which are below the municipal level.
Yupik can mean: Yup'ik (with the apostrophe) can mean:

Princeton is a city in Mercer County, West Virginia, United States. It is the county seat. The city is often called the "jewel of the south" or the "heart of Mercer County". In 2010, it had a population of 6,432. Princeton is part of the Bluefield, WV-VA micropolitan area, which has 107,342 people. The city has a baseball team called the Princeton Rays, which plays in the Appalachian League.

The Inca civil war, also called the Inca war of succession or the war of the two brothers, was fought between half-brothers Huáscar and Atahualpa. They were sons of Huayna Capac, who ruled the Inca Empire. The war began in 1529, after Huayna Capac died in 1527. Huáscar started the war, as he claimed the throne because he was fully Inca. Atahualpa was better at fighting and had more soldiers, who were placed in the north by their father. The details of the war vary. After Atahualpa won, Spanish forces, led by Francisco Pizarro, invaded. Pizarro captured and killed Atahualpa after receiving a ransom.

Raymond Poulidor, born on April 15, 1936, and died on November 13, 2019, was a French cyclist. He raced his whole career. Poulidor was known as "pou-pou." His career was good, even though he rode during the time of great riders Jacques Anquetil and Eddy Merckx. This made Poulidor popular because he was considered the underdog. He was called "the eternal second" because he never won the Tour de France, but he finished in second place three times and in third place five times, including when he was 40. He never wore the yellow jersey, which is for the overall leader, in the Tour de France, even though he finished 12 out of 14 times. However, Poulidor did win one grand tour, the 1964 Vuelta a España.

Electronic paper, also called electronic ink or electrophoretic display, shows text and images like normal ink on paper. Unlike regular flat screens that give off light, electronic paper reflects light, making it easier on the eyes and better for viewing from different angles. As of 2008, electronic displays had contrast similar to newspapers. Newer displays, made in 2008, had even better contrast. In bright sunlight, an ideal electronic paper display can still be read clearly. Many electronic paper technologies can show text and images without needing power. Flexible electronic paper uses plastic materials for the display. It's used in things like shelf labels, bus station timetables, billboards, smartphone screens, and e-readers that display digital books and magazines.
Torcy is a town in the Pas-de-Calais area of northern France.

Tali Tali Pompey was an Aboriginal artist from Central Australia. She began painting in 2002. Her work was soon included in important public galleries. She lived from about 1945/47 to November 16, 2011.

The Bridgeport Sound Tigers are a professional ice hockey team. They play in the American Hockey League (AHL). The Sound Tigers are connected to the New York Islanders in the National Hockey League (NHL). The Sound Tigers started playing in the 2001-02 season and were bought by the New York Islanders in 2004. The team is in Bridgeport, Connecticut, and they play their home games at the Webster Bank Arena.

Rutgerus Johannes Martinus van Nistelrooy, born on July 1, 1976, is a Dutch football coach and former player. He is currently coaching the PSV Eindhoven under-19s team and serves as an assistant manager for the Netherlands. A former striker, van Nistelrooy is often considered one of the best strikers of his generation. He is the top scorer in three separate UEFA Champions League seasons and is the sixth-highest goalscorer in the competition’s history, with 56 goals. He has also been the top scorer in three different European domestic leagues. Van Nistelrooy started his career with Den Bosch and then moved to Heerenveen. He gained attention while playing for PSV Eindhoven, where he won two Eredivisie titles. His goal-scoring record at PSV caught the attention of Manchester United, and he joined the team in 2001 for £19 million. At Manchester United, he was successful, winning the Premier League, FA Cup, Football League Cup, and FA Community Shield. He was also named Sir Matt Busby Player of the Year twice. During his time at Manchester United, he scored 150 goals in 219 games and became their all-time European goalscorer. However, he lost favor towards the end of his tenure. Real Madrid signed van Nistelrooy in 2006. Although he was injured at the end of his time there, he won La Liga twice and the Supercopa de España. He later joined Hamburg SV in the January transfer window of 2010 and moved to Málaga in the summer of 2011. Van Nistelrooy retired from football on May 14, 2012. Internationally, van Nistelrooy played for the Netherlands 70 times and scored 35 goals. He was part of the Euro 2004, 2006 World Cup, and Euro 2008 squads.

Fana Hlongwane is a South African politician and businessman. He was an adviser to South Africa's Defence Minister Joe Modise from 1995 to 1998. His companies, including Ngwane Defence, Truvelo, and Les Amis, are accused of receiving money from British Aerospace, which is believed to be bribes. The ANC is also said to have received these payments. In 2003, Swedish authorities claim that 24 million rand was paid to Hlongwane. A British Aerospace project manager paid 7 million rand to Hlongwane in 2007 through a company called Ivema, which Hlongwane partly owned.

Gopinath Pandurang Munde (born December 12, 1949, died June 3, 2014) was an Indian politician from Maharashtra. He was very popular and called a 'lokneta.' He was a senior leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and was a union minister for rural development and panchayati raj in Narendra Modi's cabinet. He held this position for a short time before his death in a road accident. Munde served as a member of Maharashtra's legislative assembly (MLA) for five terms from 1980 to 1985 and 1990 to 2009. He was the leader of the opposition in the assembly from 1992 to 1995 and was the deputy chief minister of Maharashtra from 1995 to 1999. He was elected to the Lok Sabha in 2009 and 2014 and served as the deputy leader of the BJP in the Lok Sabha. Munde was appointed to Modi's cabinet on May 26, 2014, but died a week later in New Delhi due to a road accident. Some media reports suggest he might have been murdered. He was the shortest-serving cabinet minister in India's history.

Mazdak, also known as Mazdak the Younger (died around 524 or 528), was a Zoroastrian priest and an Iranian reformer. He gained influence during the time of Sasanian Emperor Kavadh I. Mazdak said he was a prophet of Ahura Mazda and started programs to help people. Some see him as a early example of socialism.

Janne Persson, born on October 3, 1947, in Gothenburg, Sweden, is a Swedish pianist and singer. He had several hit songs in Sweden in the 1970s and 1980s. In 1980, he participated in Melodifestivalen with the song "Växeln Hallå" and came in second place. The following year, he performed "Rocky Mountain" and ended up third. For many years, Janne also played the piano for a group called "Vi i Femman." He sang with a vocal group named "Noviserna," which included Anna-Lisa Cederquist. The name "Lucas" came from a pop band in Gothenburg where he sang and played piano in the late 1960s. The band "Lucas" won Sveriges Radio's pop band competition in 1967 and had a hit song "Anti-Social Season." They also had a hit with "Go Now." In 2009, Janne appeared on Doobidoo on SVT, playing the piano and singing "Växeln Hallå." He also directs the choirs in Onsala and Mölnlycke.
Bulgarians are a group of people from Bulgaria and nearby areas. They are part of the South Slavic ethnic group.

My Family is a British sitcom created by Fred Barron. It was produced by DLT Entertainment and Rude Boy Productions and aired on BBC One for 11 series between 2000 and 2011. Christmas specials began in 2002. The show was ranked 24th in BBC’s “Britain’s Best Sitcom” in 2004 and was the most watched sitcom in the UK in 2008. By 2011, it was one of only twelve British sitcoms to reach 100 episodes. In 2020, BBC One started showing the series on Fridays at 8 pm, and all 11 series were available on BBC iPlayer. Set in Chiswick, West London, the show stars Robert Lindsay as Ben Harper, Zoe Wanamaker as Susan Harper, and Kris Marshall, Daniela Denby-Ashe, and Gabriel Thomson as their children Nick, Janey, and Michael. Janey left in 2002 but returned in 2004 and stayed until the end. Nick left in 2005 but appeared occasionally. The character of Abi, played by Siobhan Hayes, joined in 2002 and left in 2008. Roger and Alfie, played by Keiron Self and Rhodri Meilir, were introduced in 2003 and 2005, respectively.

James Barnes Wyngaarden was born on October 19, 1924, and died on June 14, 2019. He was an American doctor, researcher, and leader at a university. He helped write a important book about medicine called "Cecil Textbook of Medicine." He also led the National Institutes of Health from 1982 to 1989. He had four daughters and one son. Wyngaarden was part of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.

Pashupati Sharma is a Nepalese folk singer born on October 31, 1982, in Putalibazar Municipality, Ward 3, Syangja District, Nepal. In 2003, he moved to Kathmandu for his studies. Sharma started singing in a duet folk singing club called Saptakoshi Dohori Sanjh. He released his first official song in 2003. Sharma has sung over 1,000 songs in his career. His songs often talk about love, patriotism, and satire. In 2018, he released a song called "Chhata Harayo" with Devi Gharti Magar. One of his satire songs, "Lutna Sake Lut," was removed from YouTube. Sharma is considered a living legend in Nepal's folk music industry.

Sahibzada Mohammad Shahid Khan Afridi, known as Shahid Afridi or Boom Boom, was born on March 1, 1975. He is a famous Pakistani cricketer and used to be the captain of the Pakistan national cricket team. As an all-rounder, he was known for his bowling, which relied on changing the pace rather than spin. However, he was most famous for his aggressive batting. Afridi held the world record for the fastest ODI century in 37 deliveries and hit the most sixes in ODI cricket history. He considered himself a better bowler than a batsman and took over 350 wickets in ODI matches and 48 in Test matches. He also topped the chart for the most T20I wickets, with 98 from 99 matches. Afridi retired from international cricket on February 19, 2017, but made a brief comeback to play in a charity match in 2018. He officially retired again on May 31, 2018, at Lord's cricket stadium. On June 13, 2020, he announced he had tested positive for COVID-19 after experiencing severe body pain. Before contracting the virus, he helped people in remote areas of Balochistan during the lockdown.
Saul Asael Martinez Alvarez, born on January 29, 1976, is a Honduran football player. He plays as a forward for Miami United, which is in the fourth tier league in the USA.

The Rolling Stones released their album "Their Satanic Majesty's Request" in December 1967. It was their sixth album in the UK and their eighth in the US. Decca Records released it in the UK, while London Records did so in the US. This was their first album to have the same version in both countries. The title is a joke about the phrase "Her Britannic Majesty requests and requires." The band tried out new sounds for this album, including using instruments like the mellotron, adding unusual sounds, string music, and rhythms from Africa. They made the album without their usual manager and producer, Andrew Loog Oldham. The long recording process was filled with band members using drugs, going to court, and spending time in jail. The album's cover has a special picture designed by Michael Cooper. Critics had mixed opinions about the album. Some thought it copied the Beatles' work, especially their 1967 album "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band." However, the album has become better liked over time. After the album came out, the Rolling Stones went back to their blues music roots, playing simpler music.

Hadrian ruled Rome from 117 to 138. He came from a Roman family that moved from Italy to Spain. His father was important and a cousin of Emperor Trajan. Trajan's wife and a close friend of Trajan helped Hadrian get married to Traian's niece early in his career. Trajan and his wife supported Hadrian. When Trajan died, Trajan's wife claimed Trajan named Hadrian emperor right before he died. Rome's army and leaders accepted Hadrian, but some top leaders were killed shortly after, as they had opposed Hadrian. The senate was angry with Hadrian and never forgave him. Hadrian stopped Trajan's plans to expand the empire. Instead, he focused on strengthening borders and unifying the empire. He built Hadrian's Wall in Britain, which marked its northern edge. He traveled to most of the empire’s provinces, visiting specialists and administrators. He improved the army and built many temples and buildings. In Rome, he rebuilt the Pantheon and constructed the Temple of Venus and Roma. In Egypt, he might have rebuilt the Serapeum. He made Athens a cultural center and built many temples there. Hadrian was close to a young Greek man named Antinous, and Antinous' death led Hadrian to create a new religious cult. Hadrian successfully ended the Bar Kokhba revolt in Judaea. His last years were troubled by illness and more deaths of important people. He adopted Antoninus Pius as his successor, with Antoninus agreeing to adopt Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus. Hadrian died in Baiae in 138. Antoninus had Hadrian declared a god, though the senate was against it. Some say Hadrian was a good emperor, while others found him distant and strict. He is seen as complex, generous, and ambitious.

The dram is the money used in Armenia and Artsakh, a nearby country. It used to be divided into 100 luma. The word "dram" means "money" and is similar to words like "drachma" in Greek, "dirham" in Arabic, and "dram" as a unit of weight in English. The first dram coins were made between 1199 and 1375.

Rosemary Clooney, born on May 23, 1928, and passed away on June 29, 2002, was an American singer and actress. She became famous in the early 1950s with the song "Come on-a My House." Other popular songs she sang included "Botch-a-Me," "Mambo Italiano," "Tenderly," "Half as Much," "Hey There," and "This Ole House." She also performed jazz music. Her career slowed down in the 1960s because of personal problems like depression and drug use. In 1977, her career got better when Bing Crosby, her co-star in "White Christmas," invited her to perform with him at a show celebrating his 50 years in the entertainment industry. She kept making music until she died in 2002.

Eupen, a city and municipality in Belgium, is near the German border (Aachen) and the Dutch border (Maastricht). It's also close to the Ardennes forest, specifically the "High Fens" nature reserve. Eupen has been the capital of the Euroregion Meuse-Rhine since 1213, when it was part of the Duchy of Limburg. Its ownership changed hands several times—first to Brabant, Burgundy, the Holy Roman Empire, and France, and then to Prussia in 1815. Prussia later became part of the German Empire in 1871. After World War I, the Treaty of Versailles transferred Eupen and Malmedy from Germany to Belgium. German is the official language here, and the city is the capital for Belgium's German-speaking community. Eupen has a small university called "Autonome Hochschule in der Deutschsprachigen Gemeinschaft," which offers degrees in education and nursing. In 2010, Eupen's football team, K.A.S. Eupen, became the first from the German-speaking community to play in Belgium's top football league. On January 1, 2006, Eupen had 18,248 people living there, with 8,892 males and 9,356 females. The city covers an area of 104.12 km², giving it a population density of 175.90 people per km². Eupen is considered a Roman Catholic region in Belgium with conservative views.
The name Ana has been used for seven tropical cyclones in the Atlantic Ocean and one in the Central Pacific.
Alan Abel, born on August 2, 1924, and died on September 14, 2018, was an American hoaxer, writer, and filmmaker. He is famous for creating hoaxes that turned into big media events.

Lodano is a village in Vallemaggia, a district in Ticino, Switzerland. It was first mentioned in 1224 as "Lodino." In 1709, the village had 70 people. The population grew to 85 by 1801, 140 by 1850, and 141 by 1900. It then decreased to 134 in 1950 and 86 in 1970. After that, the population increased to 171 in 2000 and 191 in 2003. The village covers 13.76 square kilometers. In 2004, Lodano became part of the nearby village Maggia.
Salavre is a town in the Ain area of France, which is in the eastern part of the country.

A volcanic belt is a large area where volcanoes are active. Smaller areas of activity are called volcanic fields. These belts are found above zones with very high temperatures, where magma forms. This happens at depths between 10 and 50 kilometers along tectonic plate boundaries. Examples include the trans-mexican volcanic belt in Mexico and the northern cordilleran volcanic province in Canada. Ancient volcanic belts, now inactive, can be found in places like the Canadian shield. This region has over 150 old volcanic belts that are almost flat plains. They are very old, ranging from 600 to 1200 million years. These belts contain volcanic rocks and sometimes old sedimentary rocks, forming greenstone belts. Greenstone belts are believed to have formed at ancient ocean spreading centers and island arcs. The abitibi greenstone belt in Ontario and Quebec, Canada, is one of the largest. Unlike regular mountain ranges, volcanic belts have volcanoes instead of mountains formed by tectonic plate movement.

Ellen Schwiers was a German actress who performed on stage, in films, and on television. She was born on June 11, 1930, and died on April 26, 2019. She appeared in the first performances of plays by Dürrmatt and Frisch at the Schauspielhaus Zürich and played Buhlschaft in "Jedermann" at the Salzburg Festival. During her career, from 1949 to 2015, she acted in more than 200 films and TV shows, including popular series like "Tatort." She also directed plays, started a touring theatre company in 1982, and was in charge of a festival from 1984.

Deinocheiridae is a family of dinosaurs that lived in Asia and North America from about 115 to 69 million years ago. It was first named by Halszka Osmólska and Jan Roniewicz in 1970, with the type genus being Deinocheirus. In 2014, a study by Yuong-Nam Lee and others showed that Deinocheiridae was a valid family. They used new skeletons of Deinocheirus, Garudimimus, and Beishanlong to create a family tree. Beishanlong was the earliest, and Deinocheirus was the most advanced. Garudimimidae, named in 1981, is now considered a junior synonym of Deinocheiridae because Deinocheiridae includes the type genus of Garudimimidae. Deinocheiridae existed from 115 to 69 million years ago, with Beishanlong living from 115 to 100 million years ago, Garudimimus from 98 to 83 million years ago, and Deinocheirus from 71 to 69 million years ago. Other genera include Paraxenisaurus, and possibly Harpymimus and Hexing.

Italian (also "italiano") is a Romance language in the Indo-European family. It is one of the closest languages to Latin, which it evolved from through Vulgar Latin. Italian is an official language in Italy, Switzerland (in Ticino and parts of Graubünden), San Marino, and Vatican City. It has official status in Western Istria (parts of Croatia and Slovenia) and was once an official language in Albania, Malta, Monaco, Montenegro, and Greece. It is understood in Corsica and Savoie due to its similarity with Tuscany's dialect. Italian was also used in former Italian colonies in East Africa and North Africa, where it still plays a significant role. Large Italian communities speak it in the Americas and Australia. Italian is a major European language, used as one of the official languages in the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe and the Council of Europe. It is the second most widely spoken native language in the European Union, with 67 million speakers (15% of the EU population), and 13.4 million EU citizens speak it as a second language (3%). About 85 million people speak Italian worldwide. Italian serves as the main working language of the Holy See, acting as a common language in the Catholic Church hierarchy and as the official language of the Sovereign Military Order of Malta. It is known as the "language of music" due to its use in musical terms and opera, with many musical words coming from Italian. Italian became the official language of Italy after unification, based on Tuscan dialects spoken by the upper class in Florence. Its development was influenced by other Italian languages and, to a minor extent, Germanic languages of post-Roman invaders. Italian also borrowed learned words from Latin, its ancestor language, through written language, scientific terms, and the church's liturgical language. Throughout the Middle Ages and into the early modern period, literate Italians often used Latin, leading to the adoption of many Latin words into Italian. Unlike other Romance languages, Italian retains Latin's distinction between short and long consonants. Almost all native Italian words end with vowels, making Italian words easy to rhyme. Italian has a 7-vowel sound system; classical Latin had 10, with 5 short and 5 long sounds.

Chen Meng, born on January 15, 1994, is a Chinese table tennis player. She won the women's singles title in the ITTF World Tour Grand Finals in 2017, 2018, and 2019. She also got a silver medal in the women's singles at the 2019 World Championships. In 2011, she won the girls' singles title at the World Junior Table Tennis Championships.

Jõgeva county, or Jõgevamaa, is one of Estonia's 15 counties. It is in the eastern part of the country. It borders Ida-Viru county to the northeast, Lake Peipus to the east, Tartu county to the south, Viljandi county to the southwest, Järva county to the northwest, and Lääne-Viru county to the north.
Eastland is a city in Eastland County, Texas, United States. In 2010, it had 3,960 people. Eastland is also the county seat.

Grand Island is a town in Erie County, New York, United States. In 2010, it had 20,374 people, an increase of 9.41% from 2000. The town got its name from the French term "la grande île" because it is the largest island in the Niagara River and the third largest in New York. This name appears on the town's seal. Over its history, Grand Island was home to the Attawandaron nation and was claimed by French and English settlers. In 1945, a plan suggested making Grand Island part of a new world peace capital, located on the border between Ontario, Canada, and western New York. The UN headquarters would be on nearby Navy Island in Ontario. An artist’s drawing showed bridges connecting the island to both countries. However, the proposal was rejected in favor of the UN’s current headquarters in New York City. Grand Island is in the northwestern part of Erie County, near the Canada–US border, but there is no river crossing to Canada. It is northwest of Buffalo and south of Niagara Falls. Interstate 190 and New York State Route 324 pass through the town.

Margaret Higgins Sanger, born Margaret Louise Higgins on September 14, 1879, and later known as Margaret Sanger Slee, was an American activist for birth control, sex educator, writer, and nurse. She popularized the term "birth control," opened the first birth control clinic in the United States, and founded organizations that evolved into Planned Parenthood Federation of America. Sanger used her writings and speeches to promote her ideas. In 1914, she was prosecuted for her book "Family Limitation" under the Comstock Act and fled to Britain until it was safe to return. Her efforts helped legalize contraception in the U.S. Despite criticism from opponents of abortion, Sanger believed birth control was different from abortion and opposed abortion throughout most of her career. She is respected in the American reproductive rights movement. Sanger was criticized for supporting eugenics. In 1916, Sanger opened the first birth control clinic in the U.S., leading to her arrest for distributing information on contraception. Her trial and appeal caused controversy. Sanger believed women needed to choose when to have children for a more equal and healthier life. She also wanted to stop illegal abortions. She thought contraception was the best way to avoid them. In 1921, Sanger founded the American Birth Control League, which later became Planned Parenthood Federation of America. In New York City, she set up the first clinic with all-female doctors and another in Harlem with an advisory council and African-American staff. In 1929, she created the National Committee on Federal Legislation for Birth Control to push for legalizing contraception in the U.S. From 1952 to 1959, Sanger was president of the International Planned Parenthood Federation. She died in 1966 and is considered a founder of the modern birth control movement.
coustaussa is a commune in the aude department, which is in the occitanie region of southern france. The people who live there are called coustaussans.

Ștefan Andrei was a Romanian politician. He was born on March 29, 1931, and died on August 31, 2014. Andrei was a communist and served as Romania's minister of foreign affairs from 1978 to 1985. He was arrested after the 1989 revolution that removed Nicolae Ceaușescu from power.

Vulcanodon means "volcano tooth" and is a type of dinosaur from the early Jurassic period in southern Africa. The only known species is called Vulcanodon karibaensis. It was discovered in 1969 in what is now Zimbabwe. For a long time, it was thought to be the earliest-known sauropod. It was one of the most primitive sauropods found. Vulcanodon was a plant-eating, four-legged dinosaur with a long neck and tail. It was smaller than most other sauropods, measuring around 8 meters long. Fossils of Vulcanodon include parts of its pelvis, hind legs, forearms, and tail, but not its trunk, neck, or head. At first, scientists believed Vulcanodon was a prosauropod because it had knife-shaped teeth, which suggested it might have eaten both plants and meat. However, we now know these teeth belonged to a different dinosaur, possibly a meat-eater, that scavenged on Vulcanodon. Scientists now consider Vulcanodon a true sauropod. It is related to another dinosaur called Tazoudasaurus, and both are part of the Vulcanodontidae family.

The Texas Ranger division, often called the Texas Rangers and also known as "Los Diablos Tejanos" or "The Texan Devils," is a statewide police agency in Texas. Based in Austin, Texas, they investigate crimes like murder and political corruption, control riots, protect the governor, catch fugitives, and sometimes act like a military force. They were first unofficially created in 1823 by Stephen F. Austin and had their first leader, Captain Morris. In 1835, Daniel Parker officially formed them to guard the Mexican border. The Rangers were briefly dissolved after the Civil War but quickly reformed. Since 1935, they've been part of the Texas Department of Public Safety and act as Texas' state investigators. As of 2019, they have 166 members. The Rangers played key roles in important Texas history, such as preventing the assassinations of presidents William Howard Taft and Porfirio Díaz. They also dealt with famous criminals like John Wesley Hardin, Sam Bass, and Bonnie and Clyde. Many books have been written about the Rangers, both factual and fictional. The Lone Ranger, a well-known character, was inspired by Texas Rangers. The Texas Rangers are seen as important to Texas culture and are legally protected. There's a museum in Waco, Texas, called the Texas Ranger Hall of Fame and Museum, which honors their significance.

Santa Rosa is a city in Guadalupe County, New Mexico, United States. The 2010 census showed a population of 2,848. It is between Albuquerque and Tucumcari, near the Pecos River. Santa Rosa is where Interstates 40, U.S. Route 54, and U.S. Route 84 meet. The city is at the western edge of the Llano Estacado, also known as the "Staked Plains," in eastern New Mexico and west Texas.
Yeager is a town in Hughes County, Oklahoma, United States. The population was 75 in 2010. The town was developed early in the 1900s. Oil and gas helped the town grow, but it never had many people.
Here is a list of Guinea's presidents since the country gained independence from France in 1958, after saying no to joining the French community in a vote.

Johnnie Lee Cochran Jr. (born October 2, 1937, died March 29, 2005) was an American lawyer and civil rights activist. He is most famous for defending O.J. Simpson. Cochran helped Simpson and convinced a jury to find him not guilty in the deaths of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ron Goldman. Cochran used memorable sayings in his defense, like "If it doesn't fit, you must acquit!" He also represented Sean Combs, Michael Jackson, Tupac Shakur, Stanley Williams, Todd Bridges, Jim Brown, Snoop Dogg, Riddick Bowe, Reginald Oliver Denny, and Geromino Pratt. Cochran also helped Marion Jones when she was accused of using performance-enhancing drugs in high school. Cochran was skilled in court and was an early advocate for people hurt by the police.

Grandview Heights is a city in Franklin County, Ohio, United States. In 2010, it had 6,536 people. It started as part of Marble Cliff, one of the first suburbs of Columbus. Marble Cliff became a community in 1890 and was called "hamlet of Marble Cliff" when it was incorporated in 1901. Grandview Heights became a separate village in 1906 and a city in 1931. It has its own police and fire departments and runs its own school district. Marble Cliff shares these services with Grandview Heights.

Uppsala City IBK was a floorball club in Uppsala, Sweden. The men's team played in the Swedish top division during the 1990s. In the same decade, the women's team took the place of Storvreta IBK in the Swedish league system. During the 1996-1997 season, the women's team played well in the Swedish championship playoffs. They won the first semifinal game against Högdalens IBF, but lost the entire semifinal series.

Bernard le Bovier de Fontenelle, also known as Bernard le Bouyer de Fontenelle, was a French writer who lived from February 11, 1657, to January 9, 1757. He was an important member of three academies in France, part of the Institut de France. Fontenelle was famous for making science easier to understand during the Age of Enlightenment.
Hohentannen is a municipality in Weinfelden district, which is in the canton of Thurgau, Switzerland.
Neuenhof is a municipality in the Baden district of Aargau canton in Switzerland. It is situated in the Limmat Valley, also known as "Limmattal" in German.

Hurricane Hortense was the first strong hurricane to hit Guadeloupe and Puerto Rico since 1989. It was the second strongest hurricane of the 1996 Atlantic season. It was the eighth tropical storm, eighth hurricane, of that season. Hortense formed from a tropical wave in the Atlantic Ocean on September 3. It moved westwards for four days without getting stronger because of wind conditions. On September 7, it became a tropical storm and moved over Guadeloupe on September 8. It then crossed the Caribbean Sea. On September 9, it hit Puerto Rico and briefly touched the Dominican Republic. As it moved into the Atlantic, it got much stronger and reached a peak speed of 140 mph (Category 4) on September 13. After that, it weakened as it moved northeast. On September 15, it hit Nova Scotia, Canada, as a weaker Category 1 hurricane. It left about 50% of banana plants damaged in Guadeloupe and caused flooding on Martinique. In Puerto Rico, 11,463 houses were severely damaged, and about 1.4 million people lost electricity. The damage cost about $153.4 million. There were 19 deaths, mostly from flash floods. Hortense also caused some damage in the Bahamas, Turks and Caicos, and Bermuda. In Nova Scotia, it brought heavy rain and strong winds, causing many power outages and road damage. New Brunswick, Newfoundland, and Prince Edward Island also had some damage. The total damage in Atlantic Canada was about $3.64 million.

Mark Alan Webber, born on August 27, 1976, is an Australian former racing driver. He last competed in the FIA World Endurance Championship, driving for Porsche in the LMP1 class, where he won the championship in 2015. Webber won nine Formula One races and came third in the championship several times while driving for Red Bull Racing. Webber had success in Australia racing Formula Ford and Formula Holden before moving to the UK in 1995. He partnered with fellow Australian Paul Stoddart, who owned an F3000 team, and they eventually moved into Formula One when Stoddart bought the Minardi team. In 2000, Webber won the International F3000 season, beating then-19-year-old Fernando Alonso. Webber made his Formula One debut in 1998 for Minardi, scoring the team's first points in three years at home. Jaguar hired him as their main driver after his first season. During his two years with the team, Webber often qualified in the top two rows and outperformed his teammates. His first Formula One win was at the 2009 German Grand Prix, following second-place finishes at the 2009 Chinese, Turkish, and British Grands Prix. By the end of 2009, Webber had eight podium finishes, including another victory in Brazil. He added ten more podiums in 2010, including wins in Spain, Monaco, Britain, and Hungary. Webber finished the 2010 season third, having led for much of the time but losing out to teammate Sebastian Vettel in the final race. In 2011, Webber won the Brazilian Grand Prix again, finishing third behind Vettel and Jenson Button. However, he failed to win in the second half of the season after victories in Monaco and Britain, and his last grand prix win was in the British Grand Prix. He finished the 2011 season sixth. Webber was a long-time director of the Grand Prix Drivers' Association, a Formula One drivers' union. On June 27, 2013, he announced his retirement from Formula One at the end of the season. He began racing for Porsche in 2014, competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship in LMP1 sportscars. In November 2015, he became a World Endurance Champion, sharing the #17 car with Timo Bernhard and Brendon Hartley. Webber also raced with the #1 car in 2016. After retiring from Formula One, Webber joined the BBC F1 team as an occasional pundit and reporter from 2014 to 2015 and became a full-time pundit for Channel 4’s F1 coverage in 2016. On October 13, 2016, Webber announced his retirement from driving at the end of the 2016 season to take up a role with Porsche and focus on media roles for Channel 4’s F1 and WEC coverage.

Hämeenkoski was a former municipality in Finland. It merged with the municipality of Hollola on January 1, 2016. It was located in Southern Finland and part of the Päijänne Tavastia region. The municipality had a population, but the exact number is not given. Its area was and of that was water. The population density was unknown. Hämeenkoski spoke only Finnish. Lake Pääjärvi is near the border between Hämeenkoski and Hämeenlinna (formerly Lammi).

The M65 is a motorway in Lancashire, England. It starts just south of Preston and goes through the main junctions of the M6 and M61 motorways. It runs east past Darwen, Blackburn, Accrington, Burnley, Brierfield, and Nelson, and ends in Colne.

Al Jazeera, meaning "the peninsula" (referring to the Arabian Peninsula), is a Qatari state-owned broadcaster based in Doha, Qatar. It is part of the Al Jazeera Media Network. Initially, Al Jazeera was an Arabic news and current affairs satellite TV channel. It later grew into a network with many outlets, including internet and TV channels in multiple languages. Al Jazeera Media Network is a major global news organization with 80 offices around the world. The Arabic channel sometimes showed different opinions, which caused problems in some Gulf Arab countries. Al Jazeera was the only channel to cover the Afghanistan war live, making it well-known worldwide. Al Jazeera Media Network is a news channel for public benefit according to Qatari law. It gets money from the Qatari government but keeps its independence in making decisions. Some say it supports the Qatari government's views, but Al Jazeera also shows critical content. People think it has more Islamist views, supporting the Muslim Brotherhood, and a bias against Shia people. However, Al Jazeera claims it is fair and balanced, covering all sides of a debate. In 2017, during a crisis involving Qatar, some countries asked for Al Jazeera's closure. Other media supported Al Jazeera. Al Jazeera is seen as less religious and more moderate than some other groups.

Jimmy Wayne Jamison was an American musician, singer, and songwriter. He was born on August 23, 1951, and died on September 1, 2014. Jamison was the lead singer of the rock band Survivor. He was with the band from 1984 to 1989, then again from 1992 for a short time, from 2000 to 2006, and again from 2011 until he passed away. He is also famous for co-writing and performing the theme song "I'm Always Here" for the TV show Baywatch in the 1990s.

Ace of Base is a Swedish pop group. It was first made up of siblings Jonas Berggren, Linn Berggren, and Jenny Berggren, with Ulf Ekberg joining in 1990. They became very successful after their first album "Happy Nation" came out in 1992. This album, also known as "The Sign," sold nine million copies in the United States and was the best-selling album of 1994. It had three hit singles that reached number one on the Billboard charts: "All That She Wants," "The Sign," and "Don't Turn Around." They kept making hit songs in the 1990s, like "Beautiful Life," "Lucky Love," "Cruel Summer," and "Life Is a Flower." By 2002, they had sold 30 million copies of their first four albums, making them the third most successful Swedish group ever, after ABBA and Roxette. Despite not being active since 2012, the group hasn't officially broken up. They have released some demo tracks in recent years, including a compilation album called "Hidden Gems" in 2015. In 2020, they released a boxset with an expanded 2-disc edition. Jenny Berggren performs their hits in her solo concerts around the world.
Waltenschwil is a municipality in the Muri district of the Aargau canton in Switzerland.

The Democratic National Committee (DNC) is the governing body of the U.S. Democratic Party. It organizes the Democratic National Convention every four years. This convention picks a candidate for president and decides on the party's platform. The DNC helps party candidates, but it doesn't control elected officials. The committee's leader is chosen by the members. It also raises money for its work. The DNC was created at the 1848 Democratic National Convention. Its main partner is the Republican National Committee.

The title is a German translation of an old Norse phrase. In Norse mythology, this phrase refers to a big war among different beings and gods. This war leads to the world burning and being renewed. However, Wagner's version in his "Ring" series is different from the old Norse stories.

Jumanji is a 1995 American movie about fantasy and adventure. Joe Johnston directed it. It is based on a 1981 children's book by Chris Van Allsburg. The first movie in the Jumanji series, it was written by Van Allsburg, Greg Taylor, Jonathan Hensleigh, and Jim Strain. Stars include Robin Williams, Kirsten Dunst, David Alan Grier, Bonnie Hunt, Bradley Pierce, Jonathan Hyde, and Bebe Neuwirth. The story is about a magic board game. Each move in the game creates jungle dangers for the players. In 1969, a boy named Alan Parrish got stuck in the game with his friend Sarah Whittle. Twenty-six years later, two siblings, Judy and Peter Shepherd, find the game and start playing. Unknowingly, they let Alan out of the game. After finding Sarah, the four of them try to finish the game to fix the damage and return to normal. The movie came out on December 15, 1995. It got mixed reviews but was successful, making $263 million worldwide. It was the 10th highest-grossing film of 1995. The movie led to an animated TV show from 1996 to 1999 and was followed by a 2005 film and two direct sequels in 2017 and 2019. Columbia Pictures took over distribution for all the following films.

Extratropical cyclones, sometimes called mid-latitude or wave cyclones, are low-pressure areas that help drive the weather in many parts of the world. Along with high-pressure areas, which have anticyclones, they influence weather. Extratropical cyclones can cause different types of weather, from mild rain to strong storms. These large weather systems, called synoptic low-pressure systems, form in middle latitudes. Unlike tropical cyclones, they create quick temperature changes and differences in dew point around their centers, along weather fronts.

Mathieu Pierre Flamini was born on March 7, 1984. He is a French professional footballer and environmental entrepreneur. Flamini plays as a midfielder. He has played for several clubs, including Marseille in France, Arsenal and Crystal Palace in England, Milan in Italy, and Getafe in Spain. He also played for the France national team three times. Flamini co-founded GF Biochemicals, which is the first company in the world to produce large amounts of levulinic acid.

The Alþingi, or Icelandic Parliament, is Iceland's national legislature. It is the world's oldest surviving parliament. Founded in 930, it originally met at a place called "thing fields." Even after Iceland joined Norway in 1262, it continued to hold meetings there until 1800. It was restarted in 1844 and moved to Reykjavík, where it remains today. The present Alþingi building was built in 1881 using Icelandic stone. This parliament has 63 members, elected every four years by proportional representation. The current speaker is Steingrímur J. Sigfússon. According to Iceland's constitution, there are six electoral districts, which can increase to seven. The number of seats for each district is set by law, with no district having fewer than six seats. Parties getting more than 5% of the national vote get seats based on their proportion of the vote to ensure fair representation. If one district has fewer voters per member than another, the national electoral commission will adjust seat allocations to make it more equal.

Mneme is a small moon of Jupiter. It was found in 2003 by a team from the University of Hawaii, led by Scott S. Sheppard. At first, it was called S/2003 J 21. Mneme is about 2 kilometers in size and takes 640.769 days to orbit Jupiter. It is very far from Jupiter, at an average distance of 21,427,000 kilometers. Its orbit is tilted 148 degrees compared to Jupiter's equator. It moves at an average speed of 2.43 km/s. Mneme was named in March 2005 after Mneme, one of the three original Muses. Sometimes, people confuse Mneme with Mnemosyne, the mother of the Muses, who were the daughters of Zeus (Jupiter). Mneme is part of the Ananke group, a group of small moons that orbit Jupiter between 19.3 and 22.7 million kilometers, with inclinations close to 150 degrees.

Sigma Octantis, also written as σ Octantis and abbreviated as sig oct or σ oct, is the current south star. It is very close to the southern celestial pole, making it the pole star for the Southern Hemisphere. It is a solitary star in the southern circumpolar constellation of Octans. It is about 281 light-years away from Earth. Sigma Octantis is a giant star with a spectral type of F0 III. It is a Delta Scuti variable, with its brightness changing by about 0.03 magnitudes every 2.33 hours.

Matthew Nagy, born on April 24, 1978, is an American football coach and former quarterback. He is the head coach for the Chicago Bears in the NFL. As a quarterback, he played college football for the University of Delaware from 1997 to 2000 and set school passing records. After not getting an NFL contract, he played in the Arena Football League (AFL) for six seasons. He played for the New York Dragons, Carolina Cobras, Georgia Force, and Columbus Destroyers. After finishing his playing career, Nagy became an assistant coach with the Philadelphia Eagles in 2009. He worked there for five years, mostly in offensive roles under head coach Andy Reid. In 2013, when Reid moved to the Kansas City Chiefs, Nagy joined him as the quarterbacks coach. He held this position until 2016 when he was promoted to offensive coordinator. In 2018, Nagy became the head coach of the Chicago Bears. In his first year, he led the team to their first NFC North championship and playoff appearance since 2010.

Potosí is a department in southwestern Bolivia. It covers 118,218 km² and has 823,517 people (as of 2012). The capital is the city of Potosí. Most of the area is dry, mountainous land. To the west, there is a large plateau where the biggest salt flat in the world, Salar de Uyuni, is located. Cerro Potosí was very rich during the Spanish Empire. It provided a lot of silver, which was sent to Europe. Potosí is also where the San Cristóbal silver, zinc, and lead mines are. These mines were developed by Apex Silver Mines Limited, a company from Colorado, USA. In November 2008, the mines were sold to Sumitomo Corporation, a Japanese company.

Pind Dadan Khan tehsil is a part of Jhelum district in Punjab, Pakistan. Its headquarters is the town of Pind Dadan Khan, situated on the river Jhelum, about 22 kilometers from the M2 motorway. This area is famous for the Khewra Salt Mines, the largest salt mines in Asia, which have been in use for over 2000 years. There is also an underground mosque inside the mines. The region has a long history, dating back to the time of Alexander the Great. Jalalpur Sharif, a small town within Pind Dadan Khan, is said to be where Alexander the Great's horse, Bucephalus, is buried. Pind Dadan Khan gets its name from Dadan Khan, a devoted Sufi saint from the Awan tribe.

Bellaire is a village in Belmont County, Ohio, United States. It is part of the Wheeling, West Virginia, metropolitan area. Wheeling is located to the east of Bellaire across the Ohio River. The village had 4,278 people in 2010, its highest population was in 1920. Bellaire is next to the Ohio River. The Bellaire toll bridge, which is now closed, was used in the 1991 movie "The Silence of the Lambs." A curved bridge over the Ohio River, part of the B & O railroad, was featured in the 2010 film "Unstoppable." This bridge is a historic structure. A logo with the historic stone bridge is on official village documents and police uniforms. The logo was created by former resident Michael A. Massa, who also designed the Belmont County seal.
Lionel Guérin is a French CEO and politician.

An antimicrobial is something that kills tiny living things or stops them from growing. We can group these medicines based on the tiny living things they target. For example, antibiotics fight bacteria, and antifungals fight fungi. Antimicrobials can also be classified as either microbicidal, which means they kill microbes, or biostatic, which means they just stop them from growing. The use of these medicines to treat infections is called antimicrobial chemotherapy, while using them to prevent infections is called antimicrobial prophylaxis. Antimicrobial agents are of three main types. Disinfectants, like bleach, kill many microbes on surfaces to stop the spread of illness. Antiseptics are used on living tissue during surgery to reduce the risk of infection. Antibiotics fight microbes inside the body. Antibiotics were originally made from living microbes but now include synthetic ones too, like sulfonamides or fluoroquinolones. Today, the term "antibiotic" can mean any antimicrobial. Antibacterial agents can be further divided into two groups: those that kill bacteria, called bactericidal, and those that slow bacterial growth, called bacteriostatic. To better fight microbes, new antimicrobial technologies have been developed. These solutions can kill microbes immediately when they come into contact with them.
In June 2011, Shibasaki was chosen to be part of the Japan team that played against Peru. However, he did not get to play in the game.

In September 1944, a strong hurricane hit the eastern United States. It caused a lot of damage, especially in New England. Some effects were also seen in the Outer Banks, mid-Atlantic states, and the Canadian Maritimes. The 1944 hurricane was similar to the 1938 "Long Island Express," which is one of the worst storms in New England history. On September 4, a storm system appeared east of the Lesser Antilles but didn't become a hurricane until September 9, northeast of the Virgin Islands. The storm moved northwest and grew stronger. It reached its strongest on September 13, north of the Bahamas, after turning north. The next day, it passed the Outer Banks and landed on Long Island and Rhode Island as a weaker hurricane on September 15. After that, the hurricane changed into an extratropical storm. It continued moving northeast and merged with another extratropical system off Greenland on September 16.

Mostafa Pour-mohammadi was born on March 9, 1960, in Qom. He is an Iranian politician and prosecutor. Pour-mohammadi held important government positions. From 2005 to 2008, he was the Minister of Interior. He also served as Minister of Justice from 2013 to 2017. He is suspected of being involved in the 1988 massacre of Iranian prisoners.

The office of the prime minister in Prussia existed from 1848. In that year, King Frederick William IV created this office during the 1848–49 revolution. It ended in 1947 when the Allies abolished Prussia.
Sarat Pujari was born on August 8, 1934, and passed away on May 12, 2014. He was an actor, director, and producer in the Odia film industry, known as Ollywood. He came from Jhaduapada, Sambalpur.

John Dixon was born on February 20, 1929, and passed away on May 7, 2015. He was an Australian comic book artist and writer. He is best known for creating the comic strip "Air Hawk and the Flying Doctors," which was published from 1959 to 1986.

Wind power is using wind to make electricity through wind turbines. These turbines can also do other work, like grinding grains or pumping water. Wind power is a clean, renewable energy that is better for the environment than burning fossil fuels. Wind farms have many turbines that send electricity to the power grid. Onshore wind farms use less land and have less impact on the landscape compared to other power stations, but they need to be in open areas. Offshore wind farms make more steady power but are more expensive to build and maintain. Small onshore wind farms can provide energy for the grid or isolated areas. Wind is not always available, so it must be combined with other power sources or stored. In areas with more wind power, more conventional sources are needed to keep the grid stable. Techniques like using hydroelectric power, having extra capacity, and exporting electricity can help. Weather forecasts help prepare for changes in wind power production. In 2018, wind power made up 4.8% of the world's electricity, and the total capacity was 591 GW. In Europe, wind power supplied 15% of electricity in 2019, and at least 83 countries use wind power.

Jon Llewellyn Kyl, born on April 25, 1942, is an American politician. He was a U.S. senator for Arizona from 1995 to 2013 and again in 2018. Kyl was a Republican. He was a senator twice. During his first time, he served with John McCain. Kyl was the Senate minority whip from 2007 to 2013. Kyl was born in Nebraska and grew up in Iowa. His parents were John Henry Kyl and Arlene Griffith Kyl. He studied at the University of Arizona and became an attorney and lobbyist in Phoenix. In 1987, he was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives and served until 1995. In 1994, he was elected to the U.S. Senate and kept winning until 2013. In 2006, Time magazine named him one of America's ten best senators. In 2007, he was ranked as the fourth-most conservative U.S. senator by National Journal. He led Republican policy as the chairman of the Republican Policy Committee from 2003 to 2007 and the Republican Conference in 2007. In December 2007, he became the Senate minority whip. In February 2011, Kyl said he would not run for re-election in 2012 and planned to retire at the end of his third term. He said he would not run for any other office except the vice presidency if offered. After leaving the Senate in 2013, he worked as a lawyer and helped with Brett Kavanaugh's Supreme Court nomination. In September 2018, Kyl was chosen by Governor Doug Ducey to fill John McCain's Senate seat after McCain died. At a press conference, Kyl said he would not run for the remainder of the term after the 2020 special election. Kyl was the first person to return to the Senate by appointment since 1975. He left the Senate on December 31, 2018, and was replaced by Martha McSally.
Andelsheim is a town in Haut-Rhin, which is in Grand Est, in northeastern France.

Quintana Roo, officially called the Free and Sovereign State of Quintana Roo, is one of Mexico's 32 states. It has 11 municipalities and its capital is Chetumal. Located on the eastern part of the Yucatán Peninsula, Quintana Roo borders Campeche to the west, Yucatán to the northwest, and Belize to the south. It faces the Caribbean Sea to the east and the Gulf of Mexico to the north. The state used to share a border with Guatemala, but this ended in 2013. Quintana Roo includes famous cities like Cancún, islands such as Cozumel and Isla Mujeres, and towns like Bacalar, Playa del Carmen, and Akumal. It also has ancient Mayan ruins at Chacchoben, Cobá, Kohunlich, Muyil, and Tulum. The Sian Ka'an Biosphere Reserve is there too. The population is growing fast because of new hotels and more jobs. Many people move here from Yucatán, Campeche, Tabasco, and Veracruz. Quintana Roo often gets strong hurricanes because it is in a dangerous part of the coast. The most recent big one was Hurricane Dean in 2007.

Geoffrey L. Duncan, born on April 1, 1975, is an American businessman and politician. He is the 12th Lieutenant Governor of Georgia. Before this, he was a member of the Georgia House of Representatives. Duncan played college baseball for the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets. He then played professional baseball for six years until a shoulder injury made him stop. After that, he worked in business and was elected to the Georgia House of Representatives in 2012.

recruitment means finding and choosing people for jobs, either full-time or temporary, in a company. It can also involve picking individuals for unpaid roles. Managers, human resources experts, or recruitment specialists handle the process. Sometimes, public employment agencies, commercial recruitment companies, or specialized search firms assist too. Online tools and even artificial intelligence are used to help with recruitment.

The Belize Barrier Reef is a series of coral reefs along Belize's coast, mostly offshore. It's part of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef System, stretching from Cancún in Mexico to Honduras. This makes it the second-largest coral reef system in the world, after Australia's Great Barrier Reef. It's a top tourist attraction, with many people visiting for scuba diving and snorkeling. Almost half of Belize's 260,000 yearly visitors come here. The reef is important for fishing too. Charles Darwin called it "the most remarkable reef in the West Indies" in 1842. Belize has three Caribbean atolls: Turneffe Atoll, Glover's Reef, and Lighthouse Reef. Lighthouse Reef is the easternmost area for diving and is famous for the Great Blue Hole, discovered by Jacques Cousteau in 1970. Turneffe Atoll is near Belize City. The different reefs offer various diving spots, like walls, pinnacles, and reef flats over a large area of sea.
