Raiford Chatman "Ossie" Davis was an American actor, director, poet, playwright, author, and civil rights activist. He was born on December 18, 1917, and died on February 4, 2005. He was married to Ruby Dee, who also worked as an actress, until his death. They performed together often. Both Ossie and Ruby Davis were honored by the NAACP Image Awards Hall of Fame, received the National Medal of Arts, and were given Kennedy Center Honors. Ossie Davis was inducted into the American Theater Hall of Fame in 1994.
Helenburgh Football Club was a Scottish team from Helensburgh. They played in the Scottish Football League Third Division from 1923 to 1926.

Addison Mitchell McConnell Jr. (born February 20, 1942) is an American politician. He is Kentucky's senior U.S. senator and Senate majority leader. McConnell is the second Kansan to lead a Senate party and the longest-serving U.S. senator and Senate Republican leader from Kentucky. He was first elected to the Senate in 1984 and has been re-elected five times since. During the 1998 and 2000 election cycles, McConnell was the chairman of the National Republican Senatorial Committee. In the 108th Congress, he became majority whip and was re-elected to this role in 2004. McConnell was elected Senate minority leader in 2006 and held this position until 2015. In 2015, Republicans took control of the Senate, and McConnell became Senate majority leader. Early in his career, McConnell was known as a pragmatist and moderate Republican. However, he later shifted to the right. He opposed stricter campaign finance laws, leading to a Supreme Court ruling in 2010 that partially overturned the Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act (McCain-Feingold). During the Obama administration, McConnell often worked against major presidential initiatives, used the filibuster frequently, and blocked several of President Obama's judicial nominees, including Supreme Court nominee Merrick Garland. During the Trump administration, Senate Republicans, under McConnell's leadership, confirmed more judicial nominees than ever before. Notable among these were Neil Gorsuch and Brett Kavanaugh, who were both confirmed to the Supreme Court.

ReactOS is a free and open-source operating system for personal computers. It is designed to work like Windows Server 2003 and later versions. ReactOS might replace Windows and has information on parts of Windows that are not well understood. The project began in 1996. It is not complete yet and is only recommended for testing. Many Windows programs run on ReactOS, such as Adobe Reader 6.0 and OpenOffice. ReactOS is mainly written in C, but some parts, like the file explorer, are in C++. The operating system supports AMD64 processors. ReactOS works well with other open-source projects, especially Wine, which helps Unix-like systems use Windows programs.

Cosimo II de' Medici was the Grand Duke of Tuscany from 1609 to 1621. He was the older son of Ferdinando I de' Medici and Christina of Lorraine. For most of his twelve-year rule, he let his ministers handle the administration. He is famous for supporting Galileo Galilei, who was his childhood teacher.

Afrikan Tähti, known in Swedish as Den Försunkena Diamanten or Afrikas Stjärna, meaning "Star of Africa," is a Finnish board game designed by Kari Mannerla in 1951. It has been one of the most popular board games in Nordic countries for many years. The game was first published in Helsinki, Finland, in 1951. Kari Mannerla, inspired by stories of the world's largest diamond, the Star of Africa, created the game. He used an English map of Africa and chose exotic places. He drew random land, sea, and air routes on the map. An important feature of the game was that players could choose their routes instead of following a fixed path. Tokens were shuffled before each game and placed randomly on the board. Players didn't know what surprises were under each token. Robbers and horseshoes added excitement. "Afrikan Tähti" was Kari Mannerla's last game. He was 19 years old and thought it was special. He offered it to a publishing company. After some negotiations, he agreed to print 10,000 copies. He asked for separate negotiations for future prints. The publisher agreed, as board games were rarely printed again. Instead, they printed 10,000 more the following year, and more each year after that. Over 100,000 games were sold in seven years, a record even today. Afrikan Tähti has been one of the most sold board games in Finland for 65 years. It has been translated into 16 languages. It is very popular in Nordic countries, especially in Sweden, Norway, and Denmark, where it was marketed in 1960. In Sweden, it is called Den Försunkena Diamanten; in Norway, Den Forsunkena Diamanten; and in Denmark, Afrikas Stjerne. In Finland, over two million games have been sold, in Sweden and Norway almost one million, and in Denmark half a million. Internationally, over 4.5 million games have been sold. In his retirement, Kari Mannerla revived his old game Inkan Aarre, which has sold over 100,000 copies in Finland. Both games are now copyrighted to Kari Mannerla's five daughters.

Teruel Cathedral, also known as Catedral de Santa María de Mediavilla de Teruel, is a Catholic church in Teruel, a city in Aragon, Spain. It is dedicated to Mary and is an example of Mudéjar architecture. This church, along with others in the town and in the province of Zaragoza, is a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1986.

Romance is a strong feeling of love for someone or a strong attraction towards another person. It includes actions to show those feelings. The "Wiley Blackwell Encyclopedia of Family Studies" says that romantic love, which is based on mutual attraction between two people, can change how families and marriages work. This means romantic love can start the relationship between two people. Romantic love is important in Western countries and is needed to start a close relationship. It helps form the basis for the next steps in building a family. According to "Collins Dictionary," romantic love involves feeling very strongly about someone and seeing them as having special qualities, like being extra virtuous or beautiful. This love can be more important than other things. Romantic feelings often go with sexual attraction, but you can have romantic feelings without expecting a physical relationship. The word "romance" comes from medieval stories about knights, which idealized love.
Paiçandu is a city in Paraná state, in southern Brazil. It was founded in 1948 and became an independent city on November 19, 1960. In 2015, the population was 39,291. The city's area is 171.4 km².
Ælfweard was born around 902 and died on August 2, 924. He was the second son of Edward the Elder, Edward's second wife, Ælfflæd, gave birth to him.

An inventor creates or discovers new methods, forms, devices, or useful things. The word "inventor" comes from the Latin word "invenire," which means "to find." Patents were made to help inventors by giving them a temporary exclusive right to their inventions if these inventions are new, not obvious, and useful. While inventing is linked to science and engineering, inventors don't have to be engineers or scientists.
dastilbe was a type of prehistoric fish that no longer exists. It lived during the Aptian period.

Netball is a ball game for two teams of seven players each. It is very popular in countries like those in the Commonwealth, especially in schools, and is mainly played by women. More than 20 million people play netball in over 80 countries. Major leagues include the Netball Superleague in Great Britain, Suncorp Super Netball in Australia, and the ANZ Premiership in New Zealand. Major international competitions are the World Netball Championships every four years, the Commonwealth Games, and the yearly Quad Series and Fast5 Series. In 1995, netball was recognized by the International Olympic Committee but has not yet been part of the Olympics. Games are played on a rectangular court with goal rings at each end. Teams try to score by passing the ball and shooting it through the goal ring. Each player has a specific position and can hold the ball for only three seconds. The team with the most goals wins. Netball games last 60 minutes. Variations exist to make the game faster and more appealing. Netball developed from early basketball versions in England in the 1890s. By 1960, rules were standardized, and the International Netball Federation (INF) was formed. As of 2019, INF includes over 70 national teams divided into five regions.
There is an art museum in Kyoto, Japan. This museum is also called MOMAK, which stands for Museum of Modern Art, Kyoto.

The Škoda Fabia is a small car made by Škoda Auto in Czech Republic since 1999. It replaced the Škoda Felicia, which ended production in 2001. When it first came out, the Fabia had hatchback, estate (called Fabia Combi), and saloon (called Fabia Sedan) versions. Since 2007, only hatchback and estate versions are made. The third generation Fabia was introduced in 2015.

The national flag of Anguilla, a British overseas territory, has a blue background with the British flag in the top left corner. It also features Anguilla's coat of arms on the right side. The coat of arms shows three dolphins in a circle, representing friendship, wisdom, and strength. The white part stands for peace, while the blue symbolizes the sea, and also represents faith, youth, and hope. Anguilla has used three different flags. The first was a red flag with the island's name and two mermaids. Variants of this flag also existed. This flag was unpopular and was replaced by the dolphin flag when Anguilla briefly had its own independence. The dolphin flag had a white background with a blue band at the bottom and three golden dolphins. The blue ensign was adopted in 1990 and is used on land and by government vessels. For civilian ships, Anguilla uses the standard red ensign. On land, the dolphin flag is commonly used as a general flag. The governor's flag is the Union Jack with Anguilla's coat of arms. This flag helps Anguilla show its identity and connection to Britain.

Badfinger were a Welsh/English rock band formed in Swansea, active from the 1960s to the 1980s. Their main members were Pete Ham, Mike Gibbins, Tom Evans, and Joey Molland. They are known for their influence on the 1970s power pop music. The band started as a group called The Ivys in 1961. In 1968, The Ivys changed their name to Badfinger after a Beatles song title. From 1968 to 1973, Badfinger recorded five albums and toured a lot. Their songs "Come and Get It," "No Matter What," "Day After Day," and "Baby Blue" became big hits. Their song "Without You" was famous and later made number one by Harry Nilsson and Mariah Carey. After Apple Records ended in 1973, Badfinger had many problems like legal and financial issues. In 1975, Pete Ham took his own life. The band members faced more issues, and their later albums were not as successful. Joey Molland and Tom Evans had conflicts. In 1983, Tom Evans also took his own life.
Challis is the biggest city in Custer County, Idaho, United States. It is the county seat. In 2010, the population was 1,081, an increase from 909 in 2000.

In physics, chemistry, and electronic engineering, an electron hole is a missing electron in an atom or atomic lattice. Holes are not actual particles but quasiparticles, unlike positrons, which are electron antiparticles. In a normal atom or crystal, electrons and atomic nuclei have equal charges, so a hole creates a positive charge. Holes in metals or semiconductors can move through the lattice like electrons, acting like positively charged particles. They are crucial for semiconductor devices like transistors, diodes, and integrated circuits. When an electron is excited, a hole is left behind. This concept is used in techniques like Auger electron spectroscopy and computational chemistry. In crystals, electronic band structure calculations give electrons a negative effective mass at the band's top. This negative mass is hard to understand, but thinking about a positively charged particle with a positive mass makes it easier to grasp.

Bob Kelly Abreu, born on March 11, 1974, is a former professional baseball player from Venezuela. He is known by the nicknames "El Comedulce" and "La Leche." Abreu played in Major League Baseball for several teams, including the Houston Astros, Philadelphia Phillies, New York Yankees, Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim, Los Angeles Dodgers, and New York Mets. He was a two-time All-Star. Abreu also won a Rawlings Gold Glove Award and a Silver Slugger Award. He was the single-season leader in games played twice, and he also led in doubles and triples. By 2014, he was leading active ballplayers in doubles (565), walks (1,456), and outfield assists (136). He was also in the top five for runs scored (1,441) and stolen bases (400), in the top seven for extra-base hits (911) and on-base percentage (0.396), and in the top ten for runs batted in (1,363).

Kishi is known for his harsh rule over Manchukuo, a Japanese puppet state in northeastern China. He was called "devil of Shōwa." After World War II, Kishi was imprisoned for three years as a suspect in Class A war crimes. However, the U.S. government released him, thinking he was the best leader for a pro-American Japan. In the 1950s, Kishi worked to strengthen Japan's conservative group against the socialist party. He helped create the "1955 system," where the Liberal Democratic Party became the dominant political party in Japan for a long time.

Antonín Leopold Dvořák, born on September 8, 1841, and died on May 1, 1904, was a Czech composer. He was one of the first to gain worldwide fame. Following the example of his predecessor, Bedřich Smetana, Dvořák often used rhythms and aspects of Moravian and Bohemian folk music. People say his style was "the best mix of his country's music and the symphonic tradition, using folk music in a new and effective way." Dvořák showed musical talent early, learning the violin well from the age of six. His first public performances were in Prague in 1872 and 1873, when he was 31. He tried to get recognition in Germany by submitting his first symphony to a prize competition but didn't win. It was found again many years later. In 1874, Dvořák entered a contest for the Austrian state prize. Johannes Brahms, who was on the jury, was very impressed and helped Dvořák get his music published. This helped Dvořák become well-known internationally. In 1880, Dvořák wrote a religious piece called "Stabat Mater," which was successful in London in 1883. He visited England nine times, often conducting his own works. He wrote the "Dumky Trio" in 1890-91, a piece that was popular. In 1891, Dvořák became a professor at the Prague Conservatory. In 1892, he moved to the United States and became the director of the National Conservatory of Music in New York. In the U.S., he wrote his most famous works, including the "New World Symphony," which made him famous worldwide, and his most respected cello concerto. He also wrote the "American String Quartet." Problems with his salary and homesickness led him to return to Bohemia in 1895. All of Dvořák's nine operas, except the first, have Czech librettos and aim to show Czech spirit. His most successful opera is "Rusalka." His "Humoresque" and the song "Songs My Mother Taught Me" are also often performed. He is described as "the most versatile composer of his time."

The Imja Khola is a river in Nepal. It flows into the Dudh Kosi. The Imja Khola comes from the slopes of Mount Everest. The Khumbu Glacier melts into the Lobujya River, which becomes the Imja Khola. The Imja Khola then flows south to meet the Dudh Kosi at a place called Tengboche. The Imja Glacier feeds the Imja Khola through a valley called Dingboche.

Video cameras used special tubes called cathode ray tubes before the 1980s. These tubes helped capture images for television. Different types of these tubes were used from the early 1930s until the 1980s. In these tubes, a beam would scan across the image to be broadcast. The brightness of the image affected the resulting current. The beam was very small compared to the image, allowing 483 lines for NTSC format or 576 lines for PAL format.

"Sunday Bloody Sunday" is a song by the Irish rock band U2. It is the first song on their 1983 album "War" and was released as the third single on March 21, 1983, in the Netherlands and West Germany. This song has a strong military beat, a harsh guitar sound, and a melodic part. It is one of U2's most political songs. The lyrics describe the bad things that happened during the troubles in Northern Ireland, especially the Bloody Sunday incident in Derry in 1972 when British soldiers killed unarmed protest marchers. Along with "New Year's Day," this song helped U2 become more popular. Critics liked the song when it came out and it became a regular part of U2's live shows. During early performances, it caused some controversy, but lead singer Bono often talked about the message against violence. Today, it is one of U2's most famous songs and has been performed by many artists. It was ranked 272nd on Rolling Stone's list of the 500 greatest songs of all time.

Fort Scott is a city in Bourbon County, Kansas, United States. It is south of Kansas City and sits by the Marmaton River. In 2010, it had 8,087 people living there. The city is known for the Fort Scott National Historic Site and the Fort Scott National Cemetery. It is named after General Winfield Scott.
Ernie is a boy's name. It is often a shorter version of Ernest. It can be:
Moutiers-sur-le-Lay is a commune in Vendée, which is in the Pays de la Loire region in western France.

Eli Lilly and Company is an American drug company based in Indianapolis, Indiana. They have offices in 18 countries and sell their products in about 125 countries. Founded in 1876 by Eli Lilly, a chemist who served in the American Civil War, the company made history by producing the first mass-produced polio vaccine and insulin. Lilly was among the first to make human insulin using recombinant DNA, creating products like Humalog and Humulin. They also produce Prozac, Dolophine, Cymbalta, and Zyprexa. According to John Marks, the company made LSD for a CIA project called MKUltra. In 2019, Lilly was ranked 123rd on the Fortune 500 list and 221st on the Forbes Global 2000 list. They are also considered one of America's best employers. As of 1997, Eli Lilly was the largest corporation and biggest charitable donor in Indiana.

The penalty shootout is a way to decide a winner in games that end in a tie. The rules can be different for each sport and even for different competitions. But generally, it works like this: One player kicks the ball from a specific spot, and the only defender is the goalkeeper. If the game is still tied after this, the shootout continues with players taking turns to kick. The team that scores a goal that the other team doesn't match is the winner. This might go on until every player has kicked, and if it's still tied, extra kicks happen until the tie is broken. It's also called "sudden death."

Kavala, or "Kavála," is a city in northern Greece. It's the main seaport in eastern Macedonia and the capital of the Kavala regional unit. Kavala is located on the Kavala bay, facing the island of Thasos. It's also on the Egnatia Motorway, about 1.5 hours from Thessaloniki to the west, 40 minutes from Drama to the north, and 40 minutes from Xanthi to the east. It is approximately 150 kilometers west of Alexandroupoli. Kavala is an important economic center in northern Greece. It is a hub for commerce, tourism, fishing, and oil-related activities. It used to be a major place for trading tobacco.

Morissen used to be a separate municipality in the Surselva district of the Swiss canton of Graubünden. On January 1, 2013, Morissen joined with seven other municipalities—Cumbel, Degen, Lumbrein, Suraua, Vignogn, Vella, and Vrin—to form a new municipality called Lumnezia.
Marcy is a commune in the Aisne department, which is in Hauts-de-France, in northern France.

Hans Modrow, born on January 27, 1928, is a German politician. He is famous as the last communist leader of East Germany. When the peaceful revolution was happening, he became the acting leader in late 1989 and early 1990, trying to stop Germany from becoming one country. After East Germany changed, the new government said he did wrong things in the election. In 1995, the Dresden court found him guilty of cheating and lying. He used to be an important leader of the Party of Democratic Socialism. Since 2007, he has been the president of the council of elders for the Left Party.

How to Murder Your Wife is a 1965 American black comedy film. It was produced by George Axelrod and directed by Richard Quine. Jack Lemmon, Virna Lisi, and Terry-Thomas starred in the movie. Quine directed Lemmon in other films as well, such as "My Sister Eileen," "It Happened to Jane," "Operation Mad Ball," "The Notorious Landlady," and "Bell, Book and Candle." The film featured comic strip art by Mel Keefer, who also drew "Perry Mason," "Mac Divot," and "Rick O'Shay." Alex Toth made a teaser comic strip in Keefer's style for ten days before the film's theater release.
Hiroshi Umemura was born on February 22, 1972. He is a Japanese mixed martial artist. He competed in bantamweight and featherweight divisions.

Lynne Carol, born Josephine Caroline Gertrude Mary Faith Harber on June 29, 1914, and died on June 30, 1990, was an actress. She was born in Wales, but was often described as English. She acted mainly in TV series and telemovies. She was famous for playing Martha Longhurst, a busybody character, in the soap opera "Coronation Street" from the show's second episode in 1960 until 1964 when her character was killed off.
Newark is a city in Tarrant and Wise counties, Texas. The population was 1,005 in 2010.
In math, the lowest common denominator (LCD) is the smallest number that can be the denominator for a set of fractions. It helps when you need to add, subtract, or compare fractions.

A prefix is an affix placed before a word's main part, or stem. Adding a prefix changes one word into another. For example, adding "un-" to "happy" makes "unhappy." In language study, a prefix is also called a preformative, as it changes the word's form. Prefixes can be inflectional or derivational. Inflectional prefixes create a word with the same basic meaning and category but with a different role in the sentence. Derivational prefixes make new words with different meanings and sometimes new categories. Like other affixes, prefixes are usually bound morphemes. In English, there are no inflectional prefixes; suffixes are used instead for that purpose. The word "prefix" comes from the Latin "fix" (meaning "attach") and the Latin "pre-" (meaning "before").

The Lamborghini Huracán, named after a hurricane, is a sports car made by Lamborghini, an Italian car company. It replaced the Gallardo, which had a V10 engine. The Huracán first showed to the world at the 2014 Geneva Auto Show and came out in the second quarter of 2014. Its model name, LP 610-4, means it has 610 horsepower and uses all four wheels for driving. The "LP" stands for "Longitudinale posteriore," referring to its engine being placed in the middle, towards the rear of the car.

Suuwanee is a city in Gwinnett County, Georgia. In 2010, it had about 15,355 people. By 2019, the number grew to around 20,907. Suwanee used to be where the Atlanta Falcons played football from 1979 to 2001. In 2007, it was named one of the top 10 places to live according to Money magazine. In 2012, Kiplinger said it was the third best place in America for families. In 2013, Family Circle listed Suwanee as one of the top 10 towns for families. In 2018, Niche ranked Suwanee number one for places with the best public schools in Georgia. Some areas in Forsyth and Fulton counties share Suwanee's mailing address.
Sajid Nawaz Khan was born on March 25, 1975. He is a Pakistani politician. Sajid Nawaz Khan was a member of the National Assembly of Pakistan from June 2013 to May 2018.

Action Comics is an American comic book series that introduced Superman, one of the first major superhero characters. The publisher was originally called National Allied Publications, then National Comics Publications, and later National Periodical Publications. It changed its name to DC Comics. The original series ran from 1938 to 2011 and is one of the longest-running comic books. A second volume of Action Comics, starting with issue #1, ran from 2011 to 2016. Action Comics returned to its original numbering, starting with issue #957 in August 2016.

Keitele is a large lake in central Finland, with an area of 493.59 km², making it the 9th largest in the country. The lake is split into three parts: Ylä-, Keski-, and Ala-Keitele, with Keski-Keitele being the biggest. The water is clear and very clean. The towns of Äänekoski and Viitasaari are near Keitele. The northern part is called Ylä-Keitele and part of it is protected under the Natura 2000 program because of its clear water and natural condition. A famous Finnish painter, Akseli Gallen-Kallela, painted Keitele in 1904. This was his third and most detailed painting of the lake, and he showed it in Helsinki that year. He signed the painting with his Swedish name, but later used his Finnish name, which is more well-known. The painting is now in the National Gallery in London. The lake is also mentioned in a book called "A Corpse in the Koryo" by James Church, published in 2006.
The Centre Étienne Desmarteau is a multi-purpose building in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. It has two ice rinks.

The Gaslight Anthem was an American rock band from New Brunswick, New Jersey, formed in 2006. The band members are Brian Fallon (lead vocals, rhythm guitar), Alex Rosamilia (lead guitar, backing vocals), Alex Levine (bass guitar, backing vocals), and Benny Horowitz (drums, percussion). They released their first album, "Sink or Swim," in May 2007, through XOXO Records. Their second album, "The '59 Sound," came out in August 2008, through SideOneDummy Records. The third album, "American Slang," was released in June 2010. Their fourth album, "Handwritten," was released in July 2012, through Mercury Records. The lead single from "Handwritten," "45," was their most successful and well-known song. The band released their fifth album, "Get Hurt," on August 12, 2014, through Island Records. They took a break after their European tour in 2015 and played a few shows in 2018 to celebrate the 10th anniversary of "The '59 Sound." After that, they went on indefinite hiatus.
Giron or girón can mean: A place name A measurement, like an area

Arctic Monkeys are an English rock band formed in Sheffield in 2002. They have four members: Alex Turner (sings, plays guitar and keyboards), Jamie Cook (plays guitar and keyboards), Nick O'Malley (plays bass guitar and sings backup), and Matt Helders (plays drums and sings backup). A former member, Andy Nicholson (played bass and sang backup), left the band in 2006 after their first album was released. They have made six main albums: "Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not" (2006), "Favourite Worst Nightmare" (2007), "Humbug" (2009), "Suck It and See" (2011), "AM" (2013), and "Tranquility Base Hotel & Casino" (2018), plus one live album, "At the Apollo" (2008). Their first album sold the fastest of any new band in the UK. In 2013, Rolling Stone magazine said it was the 30th-best first album ever. The band has won seven Brit Awards, including Best British Group and Best British Album three times. They were nominated for five Grammy Awards. They also won the Mercury Prize in 2006 for their first album, and were nominated in 2007, 2013, and 2018. Arctic Monkeys played at the Glastonbury Festival twice—once in 2007 and again in 2013. People think they were one of the first bands to get famous online, and might show how new bands can be promoted differently.

Matthew Tyler Oakley, born on March 22, 1989, is an American YouTuber, actor, activist, and author. He often talks about LGBTQ+ rights, health care, education, and preventing suicide among young LGBTQ+ people. Oakley makes videos on topics like queer politics, pop culture, and humor. He started making videos in 2007 and his first video got over 517,000 views in 2020. His YouTube channel has over 682 million views, and at its peak, he had over 8 million subscribers. Oakley, who is openly gay, used to be part of a group called "5awesomegays" and made a video every Friday. He was in a TV report called "Generation Like" in 2014. His YouTube channel was rated as 224th in terms of subscribers, 2,010th in video views, and 33,897th overall on a website called Socialblade. He also had many followers on Twitter and Instagram. Oakley hosted a show called "Top That!" with Becca Frucht from March to October 2013. He voiced Mr. McNeely in a comedy series called "The Most Popular Girls in School" in 2013-2014. He has many followers on Facebook and Tumblr. In 2015, he wrote a book of funny stories called "Binge." Oakley hosted his own show, "The Tyler Oakley Show," on Ellen DeGeneres' platform. In 2017, he was one of "Forbes" 30 under 30. In March 2020, Oakley became a landlord, which caused a lot of people to criticize him.

Jacob Tremblay, born on October 5, 2006, is a Canadian actor. He became famous for playing Jack Newsome in the movie "Room" in 2015. For this role, he won an award for best young performer and was nominated for another award. In 2017, he played August Pullman, a boy with Treacher Collins syndrome, in "Wonder." In 2019, he starred in the comedy "Good Boys."

Dr. Hannibal Lecter is a character in books by Thomas Harris. He is a famous doctor who helps catch bad guys, but he also eats people. After he is caught and put in jail, he helps the FBI find other dangerous criminals. Lecter first appeared in "Red Dragon" in 1981. He is one of the main bad guys in "Red Dragon" and "The Silence of the Lambs" from 1988. In "Hannibal" in 1999, he becomes one of the main good guys. His story as a bad guy continues in "Hannibal Rising" in 2006. The first movie based on Harris' books, "Manhunter," came out in 1986. Brian Cox played Lecter, with a different spelling. Anthony Hopkins won an Oscar for his role in "The Silence of the Lambs" in 1991 and acted as Lecter again in "Hannibal" in 2001 and "Red Dragon" in 2002. The last movie was "Hannibal Rising" in 2007, with Gaspar Noeul playing Lecter. Harris wrote the screenplay for this film. A TV show called "Hannibal" began in 2013, focusing on Dr. Lecter and FBI agent Will Graham. Mads Mikkelsen played Lecter and won a Saturn Award for his performance. In 2003, Hopkins' Lecter was named one of the greatest villains in American cinema. In 2010, "Entertainment Weekly" listed him as one of the 100 greatest characters of the last 20 years. In 2019, Mikkelsen's Lecter was ranked as the 18th greatest villain on TV by "Rolling Stone."

The speaker of the Spanish senate is called the president of the senate. This is the upper house of Spain's cortes generales. After the monarch (head of state), the prime minister (head of government), and the president of the congress of deputies (speaker of the lower house), it is the fourth most important position in the country. The senate speaker is chosen by the senators themselves. If unable to serve, a vice president of the senate replaces them. While the senate speaker and the congress president both represent the cortes generales, the constitution gives more power to the congress president because of Spain's special type of bicameralism. As a result, the senate speaker usually works in the background. The current senate speaker role was created by the 1978 constitution. However, the position has existed for almost 200 years since 1834 when it was called president of the house of peers. As of now, Pilar Llop holds this position. She represents Madrid for the socialist party.

Miikka Sakari Kiprusoff, nicknamed Kipper, was born on October 26, 1976. He is a Finnish former ice hockey goalie. Kiprusoff played for the Calgary Flames and San Jose Sharks in the NHL. He was picked 116th in the 1995 NHL draft by the San Jose Sharks. He also played for TPS in the Finnish SM-liiga and for AIK IF and Timrå IK in the Swedish Elitserien. Kiprusoff played for Finland in international tournaments. He won silver medals in the ice hockey world championships in 1999 and 2001. He helped Finland finish second in the 2004 World Cup of Hockey and won a bronze medal at the 2010 Winter Olympics in Vancouver, Canada. Kiprusoff started his pro career with TPS in 1994. He was the best goalie and best player of the playoffs in 1999, helping TPS win the SM-liiga championship. In 1999, he went to North America and played in the American Hockey League (AHL) for two seasons before joining the San Jose Sharks in the NHL. He was often a backup goalie there. In 2003-2004, Kiprusoff was traded to the Calgary Flames, where he became the starting goalie. He set a modern NHL record with the lowest goals against average at 1.69, helping the Flames reach the 2004 Stanley Cup Final. He won the Vezina Trophy as the best goalie in the NHL in 2006 and the William M. Jennings Trophy for giving up the fewest goals in the league. Kiprusoff was in his first NHL All-Star Game in 2007 and holds the Flames' franchise records for wins and shutouts.

Docetism is a belief in early Christianity. It says that Jesus appeared to be human, but he was not truly human. The word "docetai" meaning "illusionists" was used by Bishop Serapion of Antioch around 197-203 AD. He found this belief in a text called the Gospel of Peter. Serapion did not like this idea and said it was fake. This belief came about because of disagreements about a sentence from the Gospel of John: "The word was made flesh." The First Council of Nicaea in 325 AD clearly said that Docetism was wrong. Today, most churches, including the Catholic Church, Eastern Orthodox Church, and some Protestant churches, agree that Docetism is not correct.
The list includes all known Atlantic hurricanes from 1700 to 1799. Not all data for each storm exist, but some coastal areas provided information about hurricanes that occurred.

Paktika is one of the 34 provinces in Afghanistan. It is in the eastern part of the country. Paktika has about 413,800 people, and most are ethnic Pashtuns. Sharana is the provincial capital. Uргун is the most populous city.

Stephen Lewis, born on December 17, 1926, and known early in his career as Stephen Cato, was an English actor, comedian, director, and writer. He is famous for playing Inspector Cyril "Blakey" Blake on the TV show "The Buses," Clem "Smiler" Hemmingway in "Last of the Summer Wine," and Harry Lambert in "Oh, Doctor Beeching!" He also appeared in many stage and film roles.

In chemistry, a leaving group is a part of a molecule that leaves during a reaction. It can be a negatively charged ion (anion), a positively charged ion (cation), or a neutral molecule. For it to leave, the leaving group must be able to handle extra electrons. Common negative ions that can leave include chloride (Cl), bromide (Br), iodide (I), and tosylate (TOS). Fluoride (F) can also leave in certain nerve agent reactions. Common neutral molecules that can leave are water and ammonia. Positive ions, such as hydrogen (H) that leaves during benzene nitration, are also leaving groups. These are called electrofuges.

Alfred Lothar Wegener, born on November 1, 1880, and died in 1930, was a German scientist who studied the polar regions, geophysics, and meteorology. During his life, he was known for his work in meteorology and as a leader in polar research. However, today he is best known for suggesting that the continents were slowly moving around the Earth. He proposed this idea in 1912. His idea was controversial and not widely accepted by most geologists at the time. It wasn't until the 1950s, when new discoveries like palaeomagnetism showed strong support for his theory, that his idea gained more acceptance. Wegener went on several trips to Greenland to study air circulation before the jet stream was discovered. During these expeditions, they made many weather observations and were the first to spend a winter inside the Greenland ice sheet and the first to take ice cores from a moving Arctic glacier.
Paul Konrad Müller, born on March 11, 1923, in Neuchâtel, is a Swiss actor. He mostly appeared in Italian films. He acted in movies for 51 years in Europe.

Northport is a historic maritime village on Long Island, New York. In the 17th century, English colonists called it Great Cow Harbour. It was officially renamed Northport in 1837. In 1894, Northport became a village to have its own local government. Northport is famous for its Victorian-era village center, which still has trolley tracks from an old streetcar line. This line once took residents to the East Northport train station. The main street of Northport runs from the village green by the harbor to what used to be Vernon Valley. Today, Vernon Valley is part of East Northport. In 2010, Northport had about 7,401 people living there. The Northport-East Northport School District takes care of the education in the area.

Togiola Talalelei A. Tulafono, born on February 28, 1947, is an American Samoan politician and lawyer. He was the 56th governor of American Samoa and a member of the Democratic Party. Tulafono served as lieutenant governor from January 3, 1997. He became acting governor on March 26, 2003, after Governor Tauese Pita Fitu Sunia died. Tulafono officially became governor on April 7, 2003. In 2004, he was elected governor for a full 4-year term. He was re-elected in 2008. Tulafono did not run in 2012 because he was term-limited and could not seek a third term. In 2014, he tried to become a representative for American Samoa but did not succeed.

Baked beans are a dish made from white beans. These beans are first parboiled and then baked at a low temperature for a long time in a sauce. This is how people usually make them in the United States, except when using canned beans. In the United Kingdom, they might be baked or stewed. Canned baked beans are not baked; they are steamed instead. The dish came from Native American food. English colonists in New England started using it in the 1600s. Cookbooks in the 1800s helped spread this dish to other parts of the United States and Canada. In New England, people still use local beans like Jacob's cattle, soldier beans, yellow-eyed beans, and navy beans. Native Americans originally sweetened the dish with maple syrup. English colonists started using brown sugar in the 1600s. In the 1700s, people began using American-made molasses to avoid taxes on sugar. Boston baked beans use a molasses and salt pork sauce, which made Boston famous as "Beantown." Today, baked beans are often eaten with barbecue food or at picnics. You can find beans in a sauce made with brown sugar, sugar, or corn syrup, sometimes with tomato. Bush Brothers and Company makes the most baked beans in the United States. Canned baked beans are a quick food. They are made from navy beans in a sauce and can be eaten hot or cold straight from the can. They were first made in 1895 by the H.J. Heinz Company. By the early 1900s, they became popular in the United Kingdom as part of a typical full English breakfast.

Caliban is the second-largest retrograde irregular moon of Uranus. It was found on September 6, 1997, by Brett J. Gladman, Philip D. Nicholson, Joseph A. Burns, and John J. Kavelaars using the 200-inch Hale telescope. Sycorax, another moon, was also discovered at the same time. It was first called S/1997 U 1. Later, it was named Uranus XVI. The name comes from a character in William Shakespeare's play "The Tempest."

Valente Rodriguez, born on February 14, 1964, is an American actor. He is famous for playing the character Ernie Cárdenas in the TV show "George Lopez." He also acted as César in "Happily Divorced," a sitcom on TV Land. He appeared as a guest in shows like "Yes, Dear," "Mad About You," and "ER." He also had a role in the movie "Suckers" from 2001.

Ryan Prosser, born on July 10, 1988, is a professional rugby player. He plays as a hooker. In June 2008, he played for Wales in the Under 20 Junior World Cup. Ryan got engaged to Hayley Thomas on January 2, 2018. He is also friends with actor Fin Samadin. In January 2010, Ryan joined the Cornish Pirates from Bristol.

The flag of Germany is a tricolor with three equal horizontal bands: black, red, and gold. It was first used as the national flag in 1919 during the Weimar Republic, until 1933. Before that, from the mid-19th century, Germany had two color traditions: black-red-gold and black-white-red. Black-red-gold represented the 1848 revolutions, the Weimar Republic (1919–1933), and the Federal Republic since 1949. The German Democratic Republic (1949–1990) used black-red-gold with an additional coat of arms starting in 1959. Black-white-red appeared in 1867 in the North German Confederation and was used in the German Empire from 1871 until 1918. After 1918, black-white-red became a symbol of the right. Nazi Germany used these colors with their own swastika flag in 1933. After World War II, black-white-red was still used by some conservative groups or far-right groups, but it is not banned like Nazi symbols. Black-red-gold is the official flag of Germany. It is protected as an official symbol of the country, with penalties for defaming it.

The conservation movement, also called nature conservation, aims to protect animals, plants, and their habitats for the future. It uses science to make conservation efforts more effective. This movement began with managing fisheries and wildlife, protecting water, soil, and forests. Later, it focused on preserving natural resources and wilderness areas. Today, it also protects biodiversity. Some people see conservation as part of a larger environmental movement. Others believe they are different in ideas and practices. In the U.S., conservation is mainly about preserving nature for humans to use in a sustainable way. Elsewhere, conservation includes more about the environment.

A hose is a flexible tube used to carry fluids from one place to another. People sometimes call it a "pipe," but a pipe is usually rigid, while a hose is flexible. Hoses often have a round shape. Hose design depends on the use and performance needed. Factors include size, pressure, weight, length, straightness, coiling, and the fluid it will carry. Common materials for hoses are nylon, polyurethane, polyethylene, PVC, rubber (synthetic or natural), and special polyethylene. Recently, hoses can also be made from PTFE (Teflon) or metal like stainless steel.
Bell is a town in the Mayen-Koblenz district of Rhineland-Palatinate, which is in western Germany.

Matthew Quiny `` Matt '' Daddario, born on October 1, 1987, is an American actor. He is famous for playing Alec Lightwood in the TV show `` Shadowhunters '' from 2016 to 2019. He has a sister, actress Alexandra Daddario.

betrayal happens when someone breaks a promise or trust, causing conflict in a relationship. This can occur between people, organizations, or between individuals and organizations. Betrayal might mean supporting a rival group or doing something against what was expected or agreed upon. People who betray others are often called traitors. Betrayal is often used in stories, movies, and TV shows as a surprise plot twist.
Francisco Ibáñez Talavera was born on March 15, 1936. He is a Spanish comic book artist and writer.

Blythburgh is a village and civil parish in East Suffolk, England. It is west of Southwold and southeast of Halesworth, located near the River Blyth. The A12 road goes through the village, splitting it into two parts. In the 2011 census, 297 people lived in the parish. The parish includes the hamlets of Bulcamp and Hinton. Blythburgh is famous for its church, Holy Trinity, known as the cathedral of the marshes. Since the 1960s, the church has been lit up at night, making it easy to see for drivers on the A12. The village has a priory site. It was founded by monks from St Osyth's Priory in Essex in the 12th century. The priory was closed in 1537, and some ruins remain. Blythburgh is part of the Suffolk Coast and Heaths Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, known as the Suffolk Sandlings. It is near the Suffolk Heritage Coast, close to marshes and mud-flats by the River Blyth. These areas were flooded in 1940 as part of wartime preparations.

Appenzeller cheese is a hard cheese made from cow's milk in the Appenzell region of northeast Switzerland, specifically in the cantons of Appenzell Innerrhoden and Appenzell Ausserrhoden. While the cheese cures, a herbal brine, sometimes including wine or cider, is used to flavor and preserve it, and also to form its rind. Cheese from the Appenzell region has a long history, dating back at least 700 years and first mentioned in a document from 1282. The making process was likely quite different then. Today, about 75 dairies produce Appenzeller cheese, each with its own recipe for the brine wash, most of which are trade secrets. The cheese is straw-colored, has small holes, and a golden rind. It has a strong smell and a taste that can be nutty or fruity, ranging from mild to tangy, depending on how long it ages. Three types of Appenzeller cheese are available.

Keiunta Denard Span was born on February 27, 1984. He was an American professional baseball player who played as a center fielder. Span played for several MLB teams: the Minnesota Twins, Washington Nationals, San Francisco Giants, Tampa Bay Rays, and Seattle Mariners. He batted and threw left-handed. At his best, Span was famous as one of the top leadoff hitters due to his excellent on-base percentage.

The Toronto Maple Leafs, also called the Leafs, are a professional ice hockey team in Toronto. They play in the National Hockey League (NHL) in the Atlantic Division. The team is owned by Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment, Ltd., and Larry Tanenbaum is the chairman. They are broadcast by BCE Inc. and Rogers Communications. The Leafs first played at Mutual Street Arena for 14 seasons before moving to Maple Leaf Gardens in 1931. They now play at Scotiabank Arena, which used to be called the Air Canada Centre, since 1999. The Toronto Maple Leafs were founded in 1917 as the Toronto Arenas and were renamed the St. Patricks in 1919. In 1927, under new ownership, the team became the Maple Leafs. They are one of the "original six" NHL teams that have existed since the league's founding. The team has won 13 Stanley Cup championships, second only to the Montreal Canadiens. The Maple Leafs have two famous periods of success: from 1947 to 1951, and from 1962 to 1967. They haven't won a championship since 1967, making their 51-year gap the longest among NHL teams without a championship. The Leafs have rivalries with the Boston Bruins, Detroit Red Wings, Montreal Canadiens, and Ottawa Senators. They have retired numbers for 19 players, including the first in professional sports. Some important people from the team are also in the Hockey Hall of Fame. The Toronto Maple Leafs have partnerships with the Toronto Marlies, an AHL team, and the Newfoundland Growlers, an ECHL team.

Gangwon-do is a province in South Korea, with its capital in Chuncheon. It lies to the east of the Sea of Japan and borders Gyeonggi Province to the west. To the south, it borders North Gyeongsang and North Chungcheong provinces. Its northern boundary is the military demarcation line separating it from North Korea's Kangwŏn province. Before 1945, Gangwon and Kangwŏn were one province. Pyeongchang County hosted the 2018 Winter Olympics and Winter Paralympics. Gangwon will host the 2024 Winter Youth Olympics.
Unterschächen is a municipality in the canton of Uri in Switzerland. It is located in the Upper Schächen Valley.

Benjamin Franklin, born on January 17, 1706, was a brilliant American who did many things. He was a writer, printer, political thinker, government official, Freemason, mailman, scientist, inventor, and funny man. He also worked to help set up new communities and ran important groups like libraries and fire departments. Franklin was very important as a diplomat and helped America get help from France during the American Revolution. Franklin was known for his honesty and good values, like being hardworking, smart, and caring for his neighbors. He believed in letting people make their own choices. He was a leader in publishing, running newspapers, and making money. He also helped create important schools, like the University of Pennsylvania. As a diplomat, Franklin worked hard to get Britain to stop taxing the colonies. He was a top diplomat in France and helped make America and France close friends. He also helped America get supplies from France during the war. Franklin became the main person in charge of mail delivery in the colonies and helped set up the first national mail system. He was governor of Pennsylvania from 1785 to 1788. He once owned slaves but later changed his mind and worked to end slavery and help African Americans. Franklin's name is remembered in many ways, like on money and buildings, and people still talk about him today.

Salvador Vilar Braamcamp Sobral, born on December 28, 1989, is a Portuguese singer. He won the Eurovision Song Contest 2017 with the song "Amar pelos Dois," which his sister Luísa wrote and composed. This win gave Portugal its first victory in the contest since it started in 1956. It ended the longest winless streak for a country in Eurovision history—53 years. Salvador and his song hold the record for the highest score in Eurovision history, earning 758 points. This score came from both the jury vote and the televote.
Île-d’Eau is a commune in the Vendée department, which is in the Pays de la Loire region of western France.

Anna Kavan, born Helen Emily Woods on April 10, 1901, and died on December 5, 1968, was a British writer and painter. She first wrote under the name Helen Ferguson when she was married. In 1939, she changed her name to Anna Kavan not just as a pen name but also legally.

Hamont-Achel is a municipality in the Belgian province of Limburg. It was created in 1977 by combining the city of Hamont and the village of Achel. As of January 1, 2006, Hamont-Achel had 13,770 people living there. The area covers 43. 66 square kilometers, which means there are about 315 people for each square kilometer. The town has a Trappist abbey called Achel, part of which is a brewery named De Achelse Kluis, one of 11 Trappist breweries. A professional tennis player named Elise Mertens (ranked WTA 35 in 2017) lives in Hamont-Achel.

The election for the U.S. House of Representatives speaker happened on October 29, 2015, during the 114th U.S. Congress. John Boehner, who was the speaker, was leaving his position on October 30. This was the 124th election since 1789. Republican Paul Ryan won with 236 votes. Nancy Pelosi, the Democrat, got 184 votes. To win, you needed 217 votes. Ryan, the youngest speaker since 1869, became the new speaker. On October 29, Ryan was chosen, and he was sworn in by John Conyers on October 30. Before this, Boehner was speaker from January 5, 2011. Many Republicans wanted the job, but Kevin McCarthy withdrew. Paul Ryan was asked to run but didn't want it. However, after getting support from all groups, he agreed. He won on October 28 and was elected the next day.

Mccomb is a city in Pike County, Mississippi, United States. It is south of Jackson. In 2010, the city had 12,790 people. Mccomb is the main city in the Mccomb, Mississippi micropolitan statistical area.

The Phoenix Dwarf is a dwarf irregular galaxy. It was found in 1976 by Hans-Emil Schuster and Richard Martin West. At first, it was mistaken for a globular cluster. Now, it is 1.44 million light-years away from Earth. The galaxy got its name because it is part of the Phoenix constellation.

Vauxhall Gardens is a park in Kennington, London, on the south bank of the River Thames. From 1785 to 1859, it was a popular place for entertainment. Originally called New Spring Gardens, it opened before 1660, as mentioned by Samuel Pepys in 1662. The gardens had trees and paths. Initially, entry was free, with food and drink sold. People reached the gardens by boat until the Vauxhall Bridge was built in the 1810s. As London grew, the area became part of the city. In 1785, it became known as Vauxhall Gardens, and entrance fees were charged. The gardens attracted large crowds and had tightrope walkers, hot-air balloons, concerts, and fireworks. There was a "Turkish Tent" and a "Rotunda" that became famous. A statue of George Frideric Handel was later moved to Westminster Abbey. In 1817, a Waterloo re-enactment was held with 1,000 soldiers. It closed in 1840 due to financial problems but reopened in 1841. Ownership changed in 1842, and it closed permanently in 1859. The land was later developed, but part of the original site was turned into a public park in the late 20th century. It is now called Vauxhall Pleasure Gardens and managed by Lambeth. Vauxhall Gardens are also shown in a tile design at Vauxhall tube station.
Hansi Müller, born on July 27, 1957, in Stuttgart, was a German football player. He played as a midfielder.

Promenade concerts were musical performances in London's pleasure gardens during the 18th and 19th centuries. People would walk around while listening to the music. The word "promenade" comes from the French word "se promener," meaning "to walk." Today, "promenade concert" often refers to the Proms, a summer classical music series that started in 1895. Robert Newman and conductor Henry Wood founded the Proms.

Stanley Norman Cohen was born on June 30, 1935, in Perth Amboy, New Jersey, United States. He is an American geneticist and works as the Kwoh-Ting Li Professor at Stanford University School of Medicine. Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer were the first to move genes from one living thing to another. This discovery is very important for genetic engineering. Many products, like human growth hormone and the hepatitis B vaccine, were developed using their method. Microbiologist Hugh McDevitt said, "Cohen's DNA cloning technology has helped scientists in almost every field." Without this technology, "biomedicine and biotechnology would look very different today."

Knuts Skujenieks, born on September 5, 1936, in Riga, is a Latvian poet, journalist, and translator from fifteen European languages. He grew up near Bauska, in Zemgale, southern Latvia. Skujenieks studied at the University of Latvia in Riga and the Maxim Gorky Literature Institute in Moscow. In 1962, he was convicted for anti-Soviet activities and spent seven years in a prison camp in Mordovia, Russia. Despite being a prolific poet, his first poetry collection wasn't published until 1978. His poems from the time he was in prison were released in 1990. Skujenieks' poetry has been translated into many European languages. His books have been published in Sweden and Ukraine. In 2008, he won the Baltic Assembly Prize for Literature. Director Ivars Tontegode is making a documentary about his life called "The Deviant/Nepareizais."

The second inauguration of Andrew Jackson as the president of the United States happened on Monday, March 4, 1833, in the House Chamber of the U.S. Capitol. This inauguration marked the beginning of Jackson's second four-year term and Martin Van Buren's first four-year term as vice president. When Jackson arrived at the east front of the Capitol, John Peter Van Ness, the mayor of Washington, and the council of corporation members welcomed him and Vice President Martin Van Buren. They escorted them to the House Chamber before the swearing-in ceremony began. At noon, Chief Justice John Marshall swore Jackson and Van Buren into their positions in the House Chamber. This was different from the previous inauguration, which was held in the east portico, because of the snowy weather and the cold temperature of 29ºF. Jackson's poor health also made the swearing-in happen inside the House Chamber. Judges, the House Speaker, the Senate President, senators, foreign ministers, Andrew Jackson Donelson, and House members attended the ceremony. Jackson then took his seat as the Speaker of the House. After the cheering crowd quieted down, Jackson stood up and was sworn in as president. His private secretary, Andrew Jackson Donelson, stood on his right, and Martin Van Buren was on his left. This was the last time Chief Justice John Marshall administered the oath for a president. After taking the oath, Jackson gave his inaugural speech to the people in the House of Representatives hall. He said he was honored to be re-elected and would try to help improve the lives of Americans. Jackson also said the United States was not in any wars with other countries and emphasized the importance of a strong, unified country and cooperative state and federal governments. After his speech, two inaugural balls were held. These were the first such events with more than one ball in U.S. history. One was at Central Masonic Hall, and the other at Carusi's. On the day of the inauguration, Boston Republicans planned 50-gun salutes at 9:00 a.m. and 12:00 p.m., as directed by Captain Hoppin.

Rayon is a man-made fiber created from natural materials like wood and agricultural products. It is similar to cellulose fiber. Rayon can feel and look like natural fibers such as silk, wool, cotton, and linen. This is why it is called art silk. Rayon is made from cellulose, which has the same molecules as cellulose. Some types of viscose, a type of rayon, can feel and look like silk. These are often called artificial silk. Rayon is used to make clothes and other items.
Beaulencourt is a commune in the Pas-de-Calais department, which is in the Hauts-de-France region of northern France.

The ARIA charts, styled as ARIA Charts since November 2018, are Australia's main music sales charts. They are published weekly by the Australian Recording Industry Association. The charts list the top-selling songs and albums in various genres in Australia. ARIA became Australia's official music chart in June 1988. Before that, the Kent Music Report was Australia's national music sales chart from 1974.

Eurovision: Europe Shine a Light was a live TV show. It was organized by the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) and produced by Dutch broadcasters AVROTROS, NOS, and NPO. This replaced the Eurovision Song Contest 2020, which was supposed to take place in Rotterdam, Netherlands, but was cancelled because of the COVID-19 pandemic. The show aired live from Hilversum, Netherlands, on May 16, 2020, and lasted about two hours. Chantal Janzen, Edsilia Rombley, and Jan Smit hosted it. They were originally chosen to present the Eurovision Song Contest 2020 before it was cancelled.
St. Francis is a city in Clay County, Arkansas, United States. It is next to the St. Francis River. In 2010, the city had 250 people.
