The Academy Awards for best dance direction were given from 1935 to 1937. Then, it was stopped.
Monsignor Bernardino Piñera Carvallo was a bishop in the Catholic Church from Chile. He lived from September 22, 1915, to June 21, 2020.

Jean-Martin Charcot, born on November 29, 1825, and died on August 16, 1893, was a French doctor who studied the nervous system and taught about diseases. He is famous for his research on hypnosis and a condition called hysteria. He worked closely with a patient named Louise Augustine Gleizes. Charcot is known as the founder of modern neurology. His name is linked to at least 15 medical terms, like Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease and Charcot disease. Charcot is often called the father of French neurology and a pioneer in the field. His work had a big impact on neurology and psychology. Many ideas in psychiatry came from his research and the work of his students. He was considered the top neurologist in France during the late 1800s and was called the Napoleon of the neuroses.
Gigondas is a town in the Vaucluse department, which is in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region of southeastern France.

Sylvia Robinson, born May 29, 1935, and died September 29, 2011, was an American singer, musician, record producer, and record label executive. She had two R&B chart toppers: "Love Is Strange" with Mickey & Sylvia in 1957 and her solo record "Pillow Talk" in 1973. Later, she founded and was CEO of Sugar Hill Records, a hip-hop label. Robinson is known for her work as the driving force behind two important hip-hop singles: "Rapper's Delight" by the Sugarhill Gang in 1979, and "The Message" by Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five in 1982. This earned her the nickname "the mother of hip-hop." In 2000, she received a Pioneer Award at the 11th annual Rhythm and Blues Awards gala for her career and founding Sugarhill Records.

Jw-jones, born on July 15, 1980, is a Canadian blues guitarist, singer, songwriter, and band leader. He won an International Blues Challenge award in 2017 for his album "High Temperature." Jones signed his first recording contract with Crosscut Records in Germany in 2000. He released his first seven CDs in Europe through this label. Later, he worked with Northernblues Music in Toronto, releasing his first six recordings with them. He also worked with Ruf Records in the USA and Blind Pig Records. Jones has released nine studio albums and one live album. He has performed in 23 countries across four continents and continues to tour widely. He lives in Ottawa, Ontario, and has played at blues festivals, theaters, and clubs in Canada, the USA, Europe, the UK, Russia, Australia, and Brazil. In 2014, Jones received a Forty Under 40 award from the Ottawa Business Journal/Ottawa Chamber of Commerce, recognizing his business achievements and community involvement.

The Royal Academy of Dramatic Art (RADA) is a drama school in London, England, teaching acting for film, TV, and theatre. It is in the Bloomsbury area of central London, near the University of London's Senate House. RADA is part of the Federation of Drama Schools and is one of the oldest in the UK, founded in 1904 by Herbert Beerbohm Tree. It moved to Gower Street in 1905. In 1920, it got a royal charter. RADA opened a new theatre on Malet Street in 1921. It received its first government money in 1924. Today, RADA has five theatres and a cinema. It offers basic, college, and advanced acting courses. These courses are linked to King's College London. Edward Kemp is the school's leader. Kenneth Branagh is the president, replacing Richard Attenborough after his passing in 2014. Queen Elizabeth II is the patron.
The following is a list of notable deaths in April 2014. Each day's entries are listed alphabetically by last name. A typical entry includes the following information in order:

Jules Henri Poincaré, born on April 29, 1854, and died on July 17, 1912, was a French mathematician, physicist, engineer, and philosopher. He was a polymath, excelling in all fields of mathematics. Poincaré contributed significantly to pure and applied mathematics, physics, and celestial mechanics. In his study of the three-body problem, he was the first to find a chaotic system, a key step in modern chaos theory. He is also known as one of the founders of topology. Poincaré focused on how laws of physics remain unchanged under different transformations. He presented the Lorentz transformations in their modern form. He also discovered the remaining relativistic velocity transformations and wrote to Hendrik Lorentz in 1905. This work helped establish the theory of special relativity. In 1905, he proposed gravitational waves, which travel at the speed of light. The Poincaré group, used in physics and mathematics, is named after him. In early 20th century, he proposed the Poincaré conjecture, which remained unsolved until 2002–2003 by Grigori Perelman.

The vertical bar is a symbol used in math, computing, and printing. It has many names, like Sheffer stroke (in logic), verti-bar, vbar, stick, vertical line, vertical slash, bar, pike, or pipe. It is sometimes called a broken bar.

Wellin is a municipality in Wallonia, Belgium, located in the province of Luxembourg. On January 1, 2007, it had 2,958 people living there, which is about 44 people for every square kilometer. The municipality includes Wellin, Chanly, Halma, Lomprez, and Sohier. Other smaller areas in Wellin are Barzin, Froidlieu, Fays-Famenne, and Neupont.

Common wheat, also called bread wheat, is a type of cultivated wheat. Almost all wheat grown worldwide—about 95%—is common wheat. It is the most widely grown crop and the cereal with the highest value.

Genealogy, which means the making of a family tree, is the study of families and their histories. Genealogists use interviews, records, and genetic analysis to learn about family connections and create family trees. Genealogical work can be shown in charts or written stories. Family history covers more than just family lineages; it also includes stories about family and community life. A genealogy focuses on tracing descendants, while a family history focuses on tracing ancestors. But people often use these terms interchangeably. A family history might include more information like personal stories and family traditions. People do family history research for different reasons, like understanding their family's place in history, wanting to keep the past for future generations, or just enjoying telling accurate stories. Genealogy research is also done for academic or legal purposes.

Lynwood is a city in Los Angeles County, California. In 2010, it had about 69,772 people, a little less than the 69,845 in 2000. It is near South Gate and Compton, in the southern part of the Los Angeles basin. Lynwood became a city in 1921. It is named after Lynn Wood Sessions, wife of Charles Sessions, a local dairyman. The local railroad siding and later Pacific Electric Railway station were also named after the dairy.

Churchill College is part of the University of Cambridge in England. It mainly focuses on science, engineering, and technology but also supports the arts and humanities. In 1958, a trust was set up with Sir Winston Churchill as the chairman to build a college for 60 fellows and 540 students as a memorial to him. The college received approval from the Queen in August 1960. It is located on the outskirts of Cambridge, near the university's new development zone, which now includes the Centre for Mathematical Sciences. This new area is often considered the city's center. Churchill College has the largest grounds of all Cambridge colleges. It was the first all-male college to accept women students, and began admitting women in 1972. By 1987, all other male colleges had followed. The college is known for being less formal than other Cambridge colleges and admits a higher percentage of students from state schools. Its motto is "forward," which Churchill took from his famous "blood, toil, tears, and sweat" speech.
Puget can mean: Puget
Trachselwald is a municipality in the Emmental region of the Swiss canton of Bern.

Flensburg, in Danish "Flensborg," in Low Saxon "Flensborg," in North Frisian "Flansborj," and in South Jutlandic "Flensborre," is a town in the northern part of Germany's Schleswig-Holstein state. It is an important town in the southern Schleswig region. Flensburg is the third largest town in Schleswig-Holstein after Kiel and Lübeck. In May 1945, Flensburg became the location of the last government of Nazi Germany. Known as the Flensburg Government, it was led by Karl Dönitz and lasted for one week, from May 1, the day Hitler was reported dead, until German troops surrendered, when Allied forces took over the town. The government was officially dissolved on May 23. The nearest larger towns are Kiel to the south and Odense in Denmark to the northeast. The city center of Flensburg is about 3 kilometers from the Danish border. Flensburg is famous in Germany for

In geometry, a line segment is a part of a line that starts and ends at two different points. It includes all the points between these two points. A closed line segment has both starting and ending points included, while an open line segment does not include both. A half-open line segment includes one of the endpoints. Examples of line segments include the sides of a triangle or square. If both endpoints are corners of a shape, the line segment is an edge if the corners are next to each other, or a diagonal if they are not. If both endpoints are on a curved line like a circle, the line segment is called a chord.

James Edward Westcott was born on January 20, 1922, and passed away on March 29, 2019. He was an American photographer. During the Manhattan Project and the Cold War, he worked with the United States government in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. He was one of the few people allowed to have a camera in Oak Ridge during the Manhattan Project. He took many pictures of the construction and operation of the Oak Ridge facilities, as well as civilian life in the community.
Virginia is a city in Cass County, Illinois, United States. In 2010, it had 1,611 people. Virginia is also the county seat of Cass County.

Madonna Louise Ciccone, born on August 16, 1958, is an American singer, songwriter, actress, author, and record executive. Known as the "queen of pop," she is one of the most influential figures in music. Madonna is famous for constantly changing her style and being talented in music production and performances. Her work covers many themes and has both been praised and criticized. She was born and grew up in Michigan and moved to New York City in 1978 to dance. She first sang in rock bands Breakfast Club and Emmy, then signed with Sire Records in 1982. Her first album came out in 1983. Some of her most popular albums include "Like a Virgin" (1984), "True Blue" (1986), "Ray of Light" (1998), and "Confessions on a Dance Floor" (2005). She has many hit songs, like "Like a Virgin," "Vogue," and "Hung Up." Madonna acted in films such as "Desperately Seeking Susan" (1985), "Dick Tracy" (1990), "A League of Their Own" (1992), and "Evita" (1996). While "Evita" won her a Golden Globe, other films got bad reviews. She started her own company, Maverick, in 1992, which includes a record label. She has also done fashion, books, health clubs, and movies. She helps charities and started the Ray of Light Foundation in 1998 and Raising Malawi in 2006. Madonna has sold over 300 million records worldwide, making her the best-selling female artist of all time. She is also the most successful solo artist on Billboard's Hot 100 chart. She is the top-selling female solo touring artist, earning over $1.4 billion. In 2008, she was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. VH1 named her the greatest woman in music, and Rolling Stone put her on their lists of the greatest artists and songwriters of all time.

Love & Basketball is a 2000 American movie about romance and sports. It was made by 40 Acres and a Mule Filmworks. Sanaa Lathan and Omar Epps star in it. The story is about Quincy McCall, played by Omar Epps, and Monica Wright, played by Sanaa Lathan. They are neighbors in Los Angeles and play basketball. They also fall in love. The movie was the first one Gina Prince-Bythewood directed. It came out on April 21, 2000, in the United States. Critics said good things about it.
The duped journalist is a 1914 Hungarian silent film. It was directed by Alexander Korda and Gyula Zilahi.

"Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS" and "Super Smash Bros. for Wii U" are like other games in the "Super Smash Bros." series. Players use attacks to make opponents weaker and knock them out of the arena. These games bring characters, items, music, and stages from many Nintendo and some other game series together. The games started making in 2012 and were announced at a big gaming event in 2013. The gameplay is a mix between the fast, competitive "Super Smash Bros. Melee" and the slower, easier "Super Smash Bros. Brawl". New things in these games include up to eight players fighting at once on the Wii U version, support for Nintendo's special toys that work with the games, using custom-made characters as fighters, and getting new fighters and stages through the internet after the game is bought. Some old features, like the story mode in "Brawl", were removed. Critics liked how the games improved, but had some complaints about playing online. Both versions did well, selling more than nine million copies of the 3DS version by 2017 and over five million of the Wii U version. In 2018, a new version called "Super Smash Bros. Ultimate" was released for Nintendo Switch.
Beverly Hills is a city in McLennan County, Texas, United States. In 2010, it had 1,995 people. The city is near Waco and is part of the Waco metropolitan area.

Pir Sultan Abdal lived around 1480 to 1550. He was a Turkish Alevi poet. His simple and clear language, rich imagination, and beautiful poems made him loved by many Turks. Pir Sultan Abdal described the everyday life of people. He was a humanist and wrote about God, Islam, Muhammad, Ali, the twelve Imams, resistance, love, and peace. He also rebelled against strict rulers, which got him in trouble with the Ottoman government.
Frances Winfield was an American writer and speaker.
Guttet-Feschel is a municipality in the Leuk district of the Valais canton in Switzerland. It was created by combining the towns of Guttet and Feschel in 2000.
Carol Greitzer was born on January 3, 1925. She is an American politician. Carol served in the New York City Council from 1969 to 1991. She was the first president of NARAL Pro-Choice America.
Midland City is a town in Dale County, Alabama, United States. In 2010, it had 2,344 people. It became a town in 1890. It is in the Ozark micropolitan area.

Marian Jurczyk, born on October 16, 1935, and died on December 30, 2014, was a Polish politician and activist for the Solidarity trade union. He served as a senator in the Polish Senate from 1997 to 2000 and as the mayor of Szczecin from November 18, 1998, to January 24, 2000. He was again elected mayor on November 21, 2002, and held the position until December 4, 2006. People criticized Jurczyk for many reasons. He had to pay the city 10 million zlotys because of a canceled land deal. He also had little formal education and made several mistakes, such as forgetting the name of the deputy he had just nominated or quoting Jesus in a speech to the city council. These errors led to calls for him to be recalled. On March 23, 2004, the recall committee received enough signatures to start the process. A recall referendum was held on May 23, 2004. However, only 19% of voters turned up, which was not enough to meet the 30% turnout requirement. Despite this, 92% of those who voted wanted Jurczyk to be recalled.

Irvington is a town in Lancaster County, Virginia, United States. The population was 432 in 2010. It is on a piece of land called the Northern Neck. Irvington is also known as a historic district. In the late 1800s, there was a school called the Chesapeake Academy there. One of its students, Claybrook Cottingham, later worked as an assistant principal at the same school. Later in his career, he became the president of Louisiana College and Louisiana Tech University.

Rafael Alkorta Martínez, born on September 16, 1968, is a retired Spanish footballer. He mainly played as a central defender. Currently, he works as the sporting director for Athletic Bilbao. Alkorta played for Athletic Bilbao and Real Madrid for 17 years. He played in 370 La Liga matches and scored 8 goals. He won three trophies with Real Madrid. Alkorta also played for the Spanish national team in three World Cups during the 1990s.
Hideo Tanaka can be about: -

Topfreedom is a movement for changes in laws. It wants women to be able to be topless in public places where men can be bare-chested. This is to make genders more equal. The movement aims to remove laws that stop women from not wearing a top all the time in public. Also, it supports letting mothers feed their babies in public.
Leandro Grimi was born on February 9, 1985. He is from Argentina and plays football. He plays as a left back for Club Atlético Huracán.

Ryland Heights is a city in Kenton County, Kentucky, in the United States. According to the 2010 census, it had 1,022 people, an increase from 799 in the 2000 census. It is part of the Cincinnati metropolitan area.

The Gibson Les Paul is a solid body electric guitar. It was first sold by Gibson Guitar Corporation in 1952. It was designed by Ted McCarty, John Huis, and their team, with input from guitarist Les Paul. The guitar typically has a solid mahogany body and a carved maple top, a mahogany neck that fits into the body, a rosewood fingerboard, and two pickups with separate volume and tone controls. There is also a bridge. Early versions had gold finishes and two P-90 pickups. In 1957, humbucking pickups were added, and sunburst finishes came in 1958. The 1958-1960 sunburst Les Paul became well-known, but sales were low. In 1961, the Les Paul was redesigned into the Gibson SG. The original Les Paul style was brought back in 1968. Since then, many versions have been made. Along with the Fender Telecaster and Stratocaster, the Les Paul was one of the first mass-produced solid-body electric guitars. It is used in many music genres, like rock, country, pop, soul, blues, jazz, reggae, punk, and heavy metal.

Ioannis Veryvakis was a Greek army officer who became a full general. He held important posts, including chief of the Hellenic Army General Staff and chief of the Hellenic National Defence General Staff. He was born on November 3, 1930, and died on June 19, 2019.

Anna Jókai (born on November 24, 1932, and died on June 5, 2017) was a Hungarian author, poet, and teacher. She started writing in 1974. In the 1980s, she joined a movement to help Hungary become free. From 1990 to 1992, she led the Hungarian Writers' Union.

Hans Schneider was born on January 24, 1927, in Vienna, Austria, and died on October 28, 2014. He was a British-American mathematician. Schneider became the James Joseph Sylvester Emeritus Professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. He was the first president of the International Matrix Group from 1987 to 1990, and later the president of the International Linear Algebra Society from 1990 to 1996. The society established the Hans Schneider Prize in 1993. Schneider was a founding editor of the journal "Linear Algebra and Its Applications" from 1968 to 1972 and later became its editor-in-chief until 2012. He was also an advisory editor for the "Electronic Journal of Linear Algebra." Schneider received his Ph.D. in 1952 from the University of Edinburgh, with Alexander Craig Aitken as his advisor. He taught at Queen's University of Belfast until 1959, when he moved to the University of Wisconsin, where he retired in 1993. Schneider wrote over 160 research papers. His work covered various topics in linear algebra, including Perron Frobenius theory and inertia theory. Later in his career, he studied max algebra. For more about his experiences from 1938 to 1940, see the Kindertransport site. Schneider died of cancer at 87 years old. He was the grandfather of YouTube musician/producer Kurt Hugo Schneider.

Lohengrin is a character in German Arthurian stories. He is the son of Parzival and a knight of the Holy Grail. Lohengrin appears in a boat pulled by swans to save a lady who cannot ask about his name. This story first appeared in a book called "Parzival" by Wolfram von Eschenbach. The story was later made into two other stories. Later, a famous opera called "Lohengrin" was based on his legend, created by Richard Wagner in 1848.

Barbour County is in north-central West Virginia, US. In 2010, it had 16,589 people. The county seat is Philippi, which was made official in 1844. Both the county and the city are named after Philip Pendleton Barbour (1783-1841), a former U.S. congressman and associate justice of the U.S. Supreme Court. The county was formed in 1843 when the area was still part of Virginia. In 1871, a small part of Barbour County became part of Tucker County. The Battle of Philippi, known as the "Philippi Races," happened in June 1861. This was the first land battle of the American Civil War. Alderson Broaddus University, a Baptist school, is in the county. The university's Physician Assistant program is one of the oldest and best in the world.

Africa is the world's second-largest and second-most populous continent, after Asia. It covers about 30.3 million square kilometers, which is 6% of Earth's total surface area and 20% of its land area. As of 2023, Africa has around 1 billion people, making up about 16% of the world's population. The continent's average age is young, with a median age of 19.7 in 2012, compared to the world's median age of 30.4. Despite having many natural resources, Africa is the least wealthy per person, partly due to historical European colonization. However, recent economic growth and its large, young population make Africa an important economic market. Africa is surrounded by the Mediterranean Sea to the north, the Red Sea to the northeast, the Indian Ocean to the southeast, and the Atlantic Ocean to the west. It includes Madagascar and several archipelagos. There are 54 fully recognized countries, plus eight territories and two self-declared independent states. Algeria is the largest country by area, and Nigeria is the largest by population. African nations work together through the African Union, headquartered in Addis Ababa. Africa has a wide range of climates and is home to much biodiversity. It has the largest number of megafauna species and was least affected by the extinction of Pleistocene megafauna. However, it faces environmental issues like desertification, deforestation, and water scarcity, which are expected to worsen with climate change. Africa is considered the most vulnerable continent to climate change. Africa, especially Eastern Africa, is believed to be the place where humans and hominids originated. Ancient human civilizations, like ancient Egypt and Phoenicia, emerged in North Africa. Over a long history of migrations and trade, Africa now has many ethnicities, cultures, and languages. In the last 400 years, European influence increased, driven by trade, including the trans-Atlantic slave trade. This created large African diaspora populations in the Americas. By the late 19th century, almost all of Africa was colonized by European countries, which exploited local resources and communities. Most of Africa's current states emerged from the decolonization process in the 20th century.

Human cloning means creating a copy that is genetically identical to a person. It usually refers to artificial cloning, which involves reproducing human cells and tissues. This is different from naturally born identical twins. Cloning a person has caused many debates. Laws have been made in some countries to address the legality of human cloning. Two main types of human cloning are often discussed: therapeutic cloning and reproductive cloning. Therapeutic cloning uses cells from a person for medical purposes, like transplants. This is a field of active research, but it's not used in medicine anywhere yet. Common methods include somatic-cell nuclear transfer and more recently, pluripotent stem cell induction. Reproductive cloning aims to create a whole cloned human, not just specific cells or tissues.
Dorothea Sally Eilers was an actress. She lived from December 11, 1908, to January 5, 1978. She was American.

A satellite state is a country that appears independent but is heavily influenced or controlled by another country. The term comes from the idea of smaller planets orbiting larger ones. During the Cold War, it mostly referred to Central and Eastern European countries in the Warsaw Pact and Mongolia or Tannu Tuva between 1924 and 1990. For these countries, it meant they were under Soviet control. In some cases, it also described North Korea before 1953 and Cuba after joining Comecon in 1972. Usually, Western countries only use this term for Soviet satellite states. In Soviet times, it also applied to states influenced by Nazi Germany, Fascist Italy, and Imperial Japan. The phrase "satellite state" was first used in English in 1916. During conflicts, satellite states can act as a buffer between an enemy and the controlling nation. The term is sometimes used instead of "puppet state" or "neo-colony." A satellite state shows strong loyalty to the controlling power, while a puppet state shows political and military dependence, and a neo-colony shows economic dependence. A country can fit into more than one category depending on the type of control.

The car-free movement is a large, informal group of people and organizations, including activists, planners, and engineers. They believe that cars and other motorized vehicles are too common in cities. The goal is to make cities where cars are used less often, if at all. They want to change roads and parking spaces for other uses and create compact cities where people can easily reach most places by walking, cycling, public transport, personal transporters, or sharing rides.

George Peter Alexander Healy was an American painter who lived from July 15, 1813, to June 24, 1894. He painted many portraits and was very famous during his lifetime. He painted important people of his time.

Fort Wayne is a city in Indiana, the U.S., and the largest city in Allen County. Located in northeastern Indiana, it is near the Ohio border and south of Michigan. As of 2010, it had 253,691 people, making it Indiana's second-largest city and the 75th-largest in the U.S. It is the main city of the Fort Wayne metropolitan area, which includes Allen, Wells, and Whitley counties, with a population of 419,453 as of 2011. Fort Wayne is important for the culture and economy of northeastern Indiana. The combined statistical area includes Adams, DeKalb, Huntington, Noble, and Steuben counties, with about 615,077 people. Fort Wayne was founded in 1794 by the U.S. Army, named after General Anthony Wayne. It grew into a trading post for pioneers where the St. Joseph, St. Marys, and Maumee rivers meet. The city was laid out in 1823 and saw a lot of growth with the Wabash and Erie Canal and the arrival of railroads. It used to be a big manufacturing town, part of what became known as the Rust Belt. Now, its economy focuses on distribution, transportation, healthcare, professional services, tourism, and finance. Many people work in the defense industry, and there are also jobs at local healthcare providers like Parkview Health and Lutheran Health Network. Fort Wayne has won the All-America City Award in 1982, 1998, and 2009. It was also recognized by the U.S. Conference of Mayors with an Outstanding Achievement City Livability Award in 1999.

Matthias Lukas Ginter was born on January 19, 1994. He is a German football player. He plays as a centre back. He plays for Borussia Mönchengladbach in the Bundesliga. He also plays for the Germany national team.

J. Whyatt Mondesire was a reporter at "The Philadelphia Inquirer" early in his career. When he died, he owned the "Philadelphia Sun" newspaper. He also led the Philadelphia branch of the NAACP for more than ten years.
A consumer is a person or group who buys goods, products, or uses services mainly for personal, social, family, or household needs, not for business purposes.
Wide awake or wide awake may refer to:
Peristeri is a suburb in the northwest part of the Athens area in Greece. It has about 139,981 people living there, which makes it the seventh-largest city in Greece by population.
The national emblem of Algeria is a seal used by the government. It is similar to how other countries use coats of arms.

Ana Lila Downs Sánchez, born on September 9, 1968, is a Mexican singer-songwriter and actress. She performs her own songs and others in many music styles, including traditional and popular Mexican music. She also includes music from indigenous groups like Mixtec, Zapotec, Mayan, Nahuatl, and Purépecha. Born in Oaxaca, she studied at the Oaxaca Institute of Arts before attending the University of Minnesota for a short time. She focused on her music career and began performing in traditional Oaxaca City music scenes. Her first album, "Ofrenda," came out in 1994. In 1999, her album "La Sandunga" was a big success. In 2001, her album "Border" made her famous in Mexico and Latin America. Her 2011 album, "Pecados y Milagros," was very popular, and so was her 2015 album, "Balas y Chocolate." In 2017, she released "Salón Lágrimas y Deseo." Downs started performing in school, showing her talent with traditional and modern music. She can speak Spanish, Mixtec, and English. Downs works to save Mixtec and other indigenous Mexican languages. She is inspired by artists like Chavela Vargas, Mercedes Sosa, Lucha Villa, and Amparo Ochoa. Downs is known for her colorful and diverse music, reflecting Mexican indigenous cultures. She has won one Grammy and three Latin Grammys. Besides music, she works on helping people and fighting for indigenous rights in Latin America.

Stephen Wochy, born Wojciechowski, was born on December 25, 1922. He is a retired ice hockey player from Canada. He played 54 games for the Detroit Red Wings in the National Hockey League. He was born in Fort William, Ontario. After Jim Conacher died in April 2020, he became the oldest living former NHL player. Before playing in the NHL, Wochy was on the Port Arthur Bearcats in 1942 and played in the 1942 Allan Cup. Wochy played 10 seasons in the American Hockey League for the Indianapolis Capitals, Philadelphia Rockets, Cleveland Barons, and Buffalo Bison. In 1952, he was named a first-team AHL all-star.

Diving Machine G5 is a roller coaster at Janfusun FancyWorld in Taiwan. It was built in 2000 by Swiss company Bolliger & Mabillard. This was the second dive coaster they made; the first was Oblivion at Alton Towers in the UK. Diving Machine G5 is in the Sky Plaza area of the park. It looks very similar to Oblivion. Diving Machine G5 is named after the strong g-forces felt during the drop. Like Insane Speed, it does not have any theme. With the Ku Ku roller coaster, it is one of three roller coasters at the park. It is close to the entrance, so it often has long lines in the morning but shorter waits in the afternoon and evening.

Patmos is a town in Hempstead County, Arkansas, United States. In 2010, it had 64 people. This town shares its name with a Greek island where the Book of Revelation was written. Patmos is also part of the Hope micropolitan statistical area.

James W. Hardy III was born on December 24, 1985. He played American football as a wide receiver. He was chosen by the Buffalo Bills in the second round of the 2008 NFL Draft. He also played for the Baltimore Ravens. Hardy went to Indiana University to play college football. He passed away around June 7, 2017.

Mackenzie Christine Foy, born on November 10, 2000, is an American actress and model. She is famous for playing Renesmee Cullen in the 2012 film, which got her a Young Artist Award nomination for best supporting young actress in a feature film. She also acted as young Murphy in the 2014 space movie "Interstellar," receiving a Saturn Award for best performance by a younger actor and other nominations. In Disney's "The Nutcracker and the Four Realms," she played the character Clara.

The 1935–36 NHL season was the 19th season of the National Hockey League. The St. Louis Eagles left the league, so there were now eight teams. The Detroit Red Wings won the Stanley Cup. They beat the Toronto Maple Leafs in four games.
Koenigsegg Automotive AB makes fast sports cars. They are in Ängelholm, Skåne County, Sweden.

Jonsered is a small town in Partille Municipality, Västra Götaland County, Sweden. It had 930 people living there in 2010. Jonsered is an old industrial town near the Säve River, outside of Gothenburg. In 1834, Scotsman William Gibson started factories in Jonsered. One of their first products was sail canvas. In 1856, the first Swedish state railway connected Gothenburg and Jonsered, eventually reaching Stockholm. Until the 1920s, the Gibson family ruled Jonsered. However, the company continued to be the main force in the community. They owned most of the land until the 1970s. By the 1880s, Jonsered began making wood-processing machinery, which is still one of their products today. In the 1950s, Jonsered started making chainsaws. These became very successful worldwide. When the textile industry closed in the late 1960s, chainsaw production helped the company survive. Jonsered was once a factory town. In 1979, Electrolux bought the company and moved production to Husqvarna, closing the local plant in 1984. Since then, Jonsered has changed. It is now a suburb where people commute to work in Gothenburg and Partille. You can reach Jonsered by train from the station, which opened in 2000.

Alfredo Félix Alcón was an actor born in Buenos Aires on March 3, 1930. He worked in over 50 films, starting with "Love Never Dies" in 1955. He was a very important Argentine actor of the 20th century and received many awards, including the Silver Condor, Martin Fierro Award, and the 1981 Diamond Konex Award. Alfredo Félix Alcón died on April 11, 2014, at the age of 84.

Uzbekistan first joined the Olympic Games as an independent country in 1994. They have sent athletes to every Olympic Games since then. Before that, Uzbek athletes competed for the Soviet Union from 1952 to 1988. After the Soviet Union ended, Uzbekistan joined the Unified Team in 1992. Uzbek athletes have won 26 medals in the Summer Olympics, mostly in wrestling and boxing. They won 1 medal in the Winter Olympics. The Uzbekistan Olympic Committee was formed in 1992 and was recognized by the International Olympic Committee in 1993.

Richard Andrew Gephardt, born on January 31, 1941, is an American politician. He was a U.S. representative from Missouri from 1977 to 2005. A member of the Democratic Party, Gephardt was the House Majority Leader from 1989 to 1995 and the Minority Leader from 1995 to 2003. He tried to get the Democratic nomination for president in 1988 and 2004 but was not successful. People talked about him as a possible vice president in 1988, 1992, 2000, 2004, and 2008. After leaving politics, Gephardt started a public affairs firm called Gephardt Government Affairs in Washington. He also set up a labor consultancy in Atlanta named the Gephardt Group. He works for DLA Piper, FTI Consulting, and Goldman Sachs as a consultant. Gephardt is also part of the Reformers Caucus of Issue One.

Brendan Halligan was born on July 5, 1936, and passed away on August 9, 2020. He was an Irish economist and politician. Halligan founded and led the Institute of International and European Affairs, a think tank that discusses European and international issues. He was also the president of the Ireland China Institute, which was based in Dublin and launched in October 2019. Halligan's career included working in both the public sector and the private sector. At different times, he was the general secretary of the Labour Party, a Teachta Dála (TD), a senator, and a Member of the European Parliament (MEP).

Robert Costanza, born on September 14, 1950, is an economist who focuses on ecology. He teaches public policy at the Australian National University. He is a fellow in Australia's Social Sciences Academy and a member of the Club of Rome.

Ofteriswaing is a town in southern Germany, in Oberallgäu, Bavaria. It is known for winter sports, hosting World Cup alpine events. Ofteriswaing is famous for skiing and other sports. Traditionally, the area was used for farming. The town has a church with a World War II memorial and small chapels. Tourism is important in the region. In winter, people ski, and in summer, they hike, mountain bike, or fly with parachutes. Tourists also enjoy the "dorfsabend," a village evening with Bavarian costumes, dancing, food, and beer.

José Sarney de Araújo Costa, born José Ribamar Ferreira de Araújo Costa on April 24, 1930, is a Brazilian politician, lawyer, and writer. He was Brazil's 31st president, serving from April 21, 1985, to March 15, 1990. At 92, he is the oldest former Brazilian president still alive, and one of only two former presidents not elected directly by voters; the other is Michel Temer. Sarney became involved in politics in his home state of Maranhão in the 1950s as part of the "Bossa Nova generation" of UDN politicians. They were young and idealistic, wanting to clean up government and remove corruption. During Brazil's military dictatorship, which only allowed two parties, Sarney joined the government party, Arena, and became its president in 1979. However, when Arena split over choosing Paulo Maluf as their candidate, Sarney joined the opposition and helped form the Liberal Front Party. He ran for vice president with Tancredo Neves of PMDB. When Neves won the election but died before taking office, Sarney became president. His term started well, but his popularity dropped due to economic problems like the Brazilian debt crisis and the failure of Plan Cruzado to control inflation. His presidency is seen as very bad, and he was known for giving favors to friends, which had long-lasting effects on Brazil after the military dictatorship ended. Over time, Sarney and his family gained a lot of power in Maranhão. He is seen as the most powerful person among Brazil's "oligarchs." He owns the biggest newspapers and TV stations in Maranhão and still has a big influence there. Sarney has also been accused of giving jobs to family members and other corrupt practices. In 2009, The Economist called his election as Senate president "a victory for semi-feudalism." A columnist for Veja magazine said Sarney was "the perfect oligarch." Despite this, Sarney is also a good writer and a member of Brazil's Academy of Letters.

The Louisville/Jefferson County metro government (balance) is a statistical group in Kentucky. It covers the part of the combined city and county of Louisville-Jefferson County that isn't included in 83 separate towns or cities. This includes most of Jefferson County that used to be Louisville before 2003, plus some areas outside of towns. In 2010, the balance had 597,337 people. The whole metro area had 741,096 people in 2010. This area is also part of the Louisville-Jefferson County, KY-IN Metropolitan Statistical Area.
Frank Fakaotimanava was born on November 19, 1935. He used to be the premier of Niue, a Pacific island country.

Selhurst Park is a football stadium in the London area of Selhurst, in the Croydon borough. It is where Crystal Palace football team plays. The stadium was designed by Archibald Leitch and opened in 1924. It has hosted one international match and games during the 1948 Summer Olympics. A part of the stadium has a Sainsbury's store. From 1985 to 1991, Charlton Athletic shared the stadium. Then, from 1991 to 2003, Wimbledon shared it.

The Cheongyang chili pepper, also known as Dang Jo Cheongyang, is a medium-sized chilli. It belongs to the species "Capsicum annuum" and has a heat level of 10,000 Scoville units. This pepper looks similar to regular Korean chili peppers but is much spicier. It is a special local product from Cheongyang County in South Korea. However, it was developed by Dr. Yoo Il-woong by mixing local Jeju Island chili with Thai chili from Cheongsong and Yeongyang counties. The unripe fruits are either light purple or green. As they ripen, the peppers turn a deep red color. Even when dried, they keep their dark red color.
grimbosq is a commune in Calvados, which is in the Normandy region in northwestern France.

Saliva, often called spit, is a liquid produced by glands in the mouth. In humans, it is mostly water, with small amounts of salts, mucus, cells, enzymes, and agents that fight infections. Saliva contains enzymes like amylase and lipase, which start breaking down food. It also has lysozymes that help protect teeth from decay. Saliva helps with digestion by breaking down starches and fats. It also moistens food and starts the swallowing process. Additionally, it keeps the mouth moist. Some animals use saliva for special purposes. Swifts use their sticky saliva to build nests. Certain snakes, like cobras and vipers, use venomous saliva to catch their prey. Some caterpillars produce silk from their saliva.
Schortens was an independent municipality and is now a town in the Friesland district of Lower Saxony, Germany.

The British Rail Class 52 were 74 diesel-hydraulic locomotives made for the western region of British Rail between 1961 and 1964. Each locomotive got a two-word name, starting with "Western." So, these locomotives were called Westerns.
Springdale is a city in Hamilton County, Ohio, in the United States. It is a suburb of Cincinnati. In 2010, the population was 11,223.

Larkana district is in Sindh province, Pakistan. Its main city is Larkana. Two former Pakistani prime ministers, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Benazir Bhutto, come from Larkana. Sohai Ali Abro, an actress, and folk singer Abida Parveen also come from Larkana. A cricket team called the Larkana Bulls was formed in 2013. Other towns in the district are Ratodero, Dokri, Bakrani, and Naodero. In 2005, during Pervez Musharraf's time as Pakistan's leader, the district was split into two new districts: Qamber and Shahdadkot.

The Cat in the Hat is a children's book by Dr. Seuss, published in 1957. It features a tall cat wearing a red and white-striped hat and a red bow tie. On a rainy day, the cat visits the house of Sally and her brother. They have no mother at home. Despite their fish's warnings, the cat does a few tricks to entertain them. However, he and two mischievous friends, Thing One and Thing Two, cause a lot of trouble in the house. The children and the fish become very worried. But then the cat uses a cleaning machine to tidy everything up before their mother comes home. Dr. Seuss wrote this book to help teach children to read. He was asked to make a fun book by William Spaulding, a friend he met during World War II. Houghton Mifflin published a version for schools, and Random House published one for bookstores. To create the story, Seuss looked at a list of words he could use. He chose "cat" and "hat" because they rhymed. The book became very popular right after it was published. It sold over a million copies in three years. In 2001, it was on the list of best-selling children's books of all time. The Cat in the Hat's success led to the creation of beginner books, a series of books for young readers. In 1971, it was turned into an animated TV show, and in 2003, a live-action movie was made.

The Eurocopter (now Airbus helicopters) EC120 Colibri, also known as "hummingbird," was a small helicopter that could carry five people. It had one engine and was used for general purposes. Eurocopter, along with China National Aero-Technology Import & Export Corporation (CATIC), Harbin Aviation Industries (Group) Ltd (HAIG), and Singapore Technologies Aerospace Ltd (ST Aero) jointly designed and developed this helicopter. Eurocopter assembled it in France and Australia. In China, the helicopter is produced as the HC120 by Harbin Aircraft Manufacturing Corporation (HAMC). In 2004, HAMC started making the HC120 in Harbin, a city in northern China. In China, both the People's Liberation Army and several local police forces bought HC120 helicopters.

Nigel John Taylor, born on June 20, 1960, is a musician, singer, songwriter, producer, and actor. He was the bass guitarist in the band Duran Duran, which he helped start. Duran Duran was very popular in the 1980s because of their videos shown on early MTV. Taylor was with Duran Duran from 1978 to 1997, then left to make solo music and films. He made twelve solo albums and acted in movies. Since 2001, he has been playing with Duran Duran again. The current members of Duran Duran are Simon Le Bon (singer), John Taylor (bass guitarist), Nick Rhodes (synthesizer), and Roger Taylor (drums). Taylor was also part of two other bands, The Power Station and Neurotic Outsiders.

Last of the Summer Wine is a British sitcom created by Roy Clarke and broadcast by the BBC from 1973 to 2010. It started as part of "Comedy Playhouse" on January 4, 1973, and its first series aired on November 12, 1973. Alan J. W. Bell produced and directed all episodes from 1983 to 2010. The BBC stopped making new episodes on June 2, 2010, and the 31st series was the last. The final episode was broadcast on August 29, 2010. All 295 episodes, including films and specials, were released on DVD. The show is shown on Gold, Yesterday, and Drama in the UK and in over 25 countries, including some PBS stations in the U.S. and VisionTV in Canada. It is the longest-running comedy show in Britain and the world. The series is set in Holmfirth, West Yorkshire, and follows three old men and their funny adventures. Sometimes, new actors replaced one of the main characters. The show gained popularity for its positive portrayal of older people and family-friendly humor. It received many nominations and won awards. There were 21 Christmas specials, three TV films, and a documentary about the series. The show inspired other adaptations, like a prequel and stage productions.

The museum, previously called the Japanese Currency Museum, is about Japanese money. It is located in front of the Bank of Japan building in Chūō, Tokyo. The museum opened in November 1985. In 2010, there was an exhibition of wallets from the Edo period (1603–1867) and the Meiji era (1868–1912).

Charles Henry Pitman Sr. was born on October 20, 1935. He was a lieutenant general in the United States Marine Corps. He worked as deputy chief of staff for aviation. He retired in 1990. Pitman died in 2020 from cancer. He was also part of the 1980 Operation Eagle Claw.

The Mercator projection is a map made by Gerardus Mercator in 1569. It is a cylindrical projection used for navigation. This map shows north always at the top and south always at the bottom, and it keeps the shapes and directions of areas true. It is called conformal because of this. However, the map enlarges areas away from the equator. This enlargement is slight near the equator but gets bigger as you go towards the poles. At the poles, the enlargement becomes very large. For example, Greenland and Antarctica look much bigger than they actually are, while areas near the equator, like Central Africa, appear smaller on the map.

Shakargarh is the capital of Shakargarh tehsil and a city in the northeastern part of Narowal district, Punjab, Pakistan. It is next to Jammu to the north and Sialkot to the west. Shakargarh has a very high literacy rate over 85%, which is the highest among all tehsils. The city is at 32°16' north latitude and 75°10' east longitude, and it lies on the western side of the Ravi River. The tehsil is divided into 35 union councils, with three of them forming the capital, Shakargarh.

Madeleine Vionnet was a French fashion designer. She trained in London and then returned to France. In 1912, she opened her first fashion house in Paris. It had to close in 1914 during World War I but reopened after the war. Vionnet became one of Paris's top designers between 1919 and 1939. In 1939, she had to close her house and retired in 1940. Known as the "queen of the bias cut" and the "architect among dressmakers," Vionnet is famous for her elegant Grecian-style dresses and for popularizing the bias cut in fashion. She inspired many modern designers.
Kuthwal is one of 51 union councils in Abbottabad district, which is in the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan. It is situated northwest of Abbottabad city, which is the district capital.

Whidbey Island, also spelled as Whidby, Whitbey, or Whitby, is the biggest island in Island County, Washington, in the United States. Next to it is Camano Island, which is also large and lies to the east. Whidbey Island is about north of Seattle and is between the Olympic Peninsula and the I-5 corridor. It borders Puget Sound. Whidbey Island has a military base called Naval Air Station Whidbey Island. In 2000, it had about 67,000 people living there, with 29,000 of them living in rural areas. The island is about long when measured along roads and about wide when measured from north to south. It covers an area of and is the 40th largest island in the United States. It is the fourth longest and largest island in the contiguous United States, after Long Island in New York, Padre Island in Texas, and Isle Royale in Michigan. In Washington state, Whidbey Island is the largest island, followed by Orcas Island.

Blount County is a county in Alabama. As of 2010, it had 57, 322 people. The county seat is Oneonta. Blount County allows alcohol sales in some areas. In 2012, people voted against allowing alcohol sales everywhere in the county, but some towns already allowed it. Blount County has many old covered bridges. More old covered bridges are in Blount County than in any other county in Alabama. Each autumn, Oneonta hosts a covered bridge festival to celebrate the bridges.
Hermann Baumann was born on January 23, 1921. He is a retired Swiss wrestler. Baumann won a bronze medal in the lightweight class at the 1948 Summer Olympics in London.

John Norman Haynes was born on October 17, 1934, and passed away on October 18, 2005. He was an English football player who played for the national team. He made 56 appearances, with 22 as captain. He was chosen for three World Cup finals teams, playing in the last two. Known as "the maestro," Haynes was famous for his attacking play, using both feet, good vision, and skillful touches. He is considered Fulham's best player ever, staying loyal for 20 years without winning a major trophy, though he reached two FA Cup semi-finals. In 1961, when the £20 wage limit was lifted, Haynes became the first player to earn £100 a week. He played briefly for Toronto City in 1961 and finished his career at Durban City, winning the only trophy of his career there.

Yoshihide Kozai was born on April 1, 1928, and died on February 5, 2018. He was a Japanese astronomer who studied celestial mechanics. Kozai and Michael Lidov discovered the Kozai mechanism together. Kozai received the Imperial Prize from the Japan Academy in 1979. From 1988 to 1991, he was the president of the International Astronomical Union. In 1989, he got the Brouwer Award from the American Astronomical Society. In 2009, the Japanese government awarded him the Decoration of Cultural Merit. An asteroid was named 3040 Kozai in his honor.
Planomicrobium flavidum is a bacterium in the Planomicrobium genus. It was found in a marine salt pond.

Joshua Reynolds, born on July 16, 1723, and died on February 23, 1792, was an English painter who painted portraits. John Russell said he was one of the best painters in Europe during the 18th century. Reynolds promoted the "grand style" in painting, which means making imperfect things look perfect. He helped start the Royal Academy of Arts and became its first president. King George III made him a knight in 1769.

Chicka Chicka Boom Boom is a popular children's book. It was written by Bill Martin Jr. and John Archambault and illustrated by Lois Ehlert. The book came out in 1989 with Simon & Schuster. The letters in the story are given human traits. It appeared on The New York Times bestseller list for children's books in 2000.

This list includes current cities, towns, and communities in New York, the U.S. state. It also gives the county names and numbers where each place is located. If there are zip codes, the lowest and highest ones are shown too.

Andrus Ansip, born on October 1, 1956, is an Estonian politician. He has been a member of the European Parliament since 2014. From 2005 to 2014, he was the prime minister of Estonia. He was also a vice president of the European Commission. Before politics, Ansip trained as a chemist and worked in banking and business. He joined parliament in 2004, became minister of economic affairs, and then prime minister in April 2005. He became a member of the European Commission in November 2014.

Lynching is when a group of people kill someone without a fair trial. It often happens to punish someone they think has done something wrong or to scare others. Sometimes, they show the killing to others as a warning. Lynchings can be found in many societies. In the United States, there were many lynchings of African Americans in the South after the Reconstruction Era, especially during a time when race relations were very bad. Lynchings still occur in some places today, like Brazil, Guatemala, and South Africa, especially where crime is high.

The King and I is the fifth musical by Richard Rodgers and Oscar Hammerstein II. It is based on Margaret Landon's novel "Anna and the King of Siam," which came from Anna Leonowens' memoirs. Anna Leonowens was a British governess who taught the children of King Mongkut of Siam in the early 1860s. The musical tells Anna's story as a teacher hired to help modernize the king's country. The king and Anna have a complicated relationship with conflict and unspoken love. It first played on Broadway from March 29, 1951, and ran for almost three years, making it the fourth longest-running Broadway musical. The musical was successful, winning Tony Awards for best musical, best actress, and best featured actor. Actress Gertrude Lawrence starred as Anna until her death, after which other actresses took over the role. The musical was also a hit in London and on tours. In 1956, Yul Brynner won an Academy Award for his role as the king. Later, Brynner starred in a successful national tour. Broadway and West End revivals have continued to win Tony Awards. People still perform the musical regularly.

Illapel is a city in Chile. It is the capital of the Choapa province, which is in the Coquimbo region. Illapel is next to the Illapel River and is the narrowest point in the country along a line that is 94 km long. It is located east of Los Vilos.

Michael Jagmin is an American singer. He was the lead singer of a post-hardcore band called A Skylit Drive. He used to sing for a metal band named Odd Project. Jagmin is famous for his high-pitched voice. He has a high tenor voice and can sing over three octaves.

Gillingham Football Club is a professional soccer team in Gillingham, Kent, England. The only Kent-based club in the Football League, they play at Priestfield Stadium. The team is in League One, which is the third level of English football. The club was started in 1893 and joined the Football League in 1920. They left the league in 1938 but returned 12 years later when the league grew to 92 clubs. In the late 1980s, they almost went up to the second tier but later declined and narrowly avoided going down to the Football Conference in 1993. Between 2000 and 2005, they were in the second tier for the first time in their history, finishing eleventh in 2002-03.

Universal Studios Japan is in Osaka and is one of six Universal Studios theme parks. It is owned and operated by a company that is part of NBCUniversal. The park opened on March 31, 2001. In its first year, more than 11 million people visited, making it the world's fastest amusement park to reach 10 million guests. Each year since, around 8 million people visit. Most visitors are from Japan, South Korea, China, and some Western tourists. In 2005, a company called Goldman Sachs became the largest shareholder. To celebrate the park's 10th anniversary in 2011, they had special events. By then, 88 million people had visited. In June 2012, there were 700,000 people with annual passes. In 2012 and 2013, the park got more popular. In 2013, they opened new rides like the Hollywood Dream roller coaster and the new Spider-Man ride. The Family Area, Universal Wonderland, also attracted families. Recent additions include special attractions based on video games and anime, like Biohazard, Monster Hunter, and One Piece. In 2014, they opened the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. The Harry Potter ride was updated to 3D. The park invested 45 billion yen in this area, expecting it to bring 5 trillion 60 million yen to Japan over 10 years. In 2012, the park welcomed its 100 millionth visitor. In 2014, it was the fifth most visited theme park worldwide, with 11.8 million visitors. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Universal Studios Japan closed from February 27, 2020, to June 19, 2020.

Antony Passage is a small village in southeast Cornwall, England, UK. It is next to the tidal part of the River Lynher. The River Lynher is a smaller river that flows into the River Tamar. Antony Passage is on the other side of the River Lynher from Antony Village.

Daniel Hudson Burnham, born on September 4, 1846, and died on June 1, 1912, was an American architect and urban planner. He supported the "Beaux-Arts" style and is considered one of the most successful leaders in American architecture. As a famous Chicago architect, he worked on the 1892-93 World's Columbian Exposition, known as "the White City." Burnham also created plans for cities like Chicago, Manila, Baguio, and the center of Washington, D.C. He designed several well-known buildings, including skyscrapers in Chicago, the triangular Flatiron Building in New York City, Union Station in Washington D.C., Selfridges department store in London, and San Francisco's Merchants Exchange Building. While famous for his skyscrapers and city planning, Burnham also built many shops, comprising almost one-third of his total work.

Lexington is the second-largest city in Kentucky and the 60th-largest city in the United States. It is known as the "horse capital of the world" and is at the center of the state's bluegrass region. Notable places in the city include the Kentucky Horse Park, Red Mile and Keeneland race courses, Rupp Arena, Transylvania University, the University of Kentucky, and Bluegrass Community and Technical College. Lexington has a high rate of college education, with 39.5% of its residents having at least a bachelor's degree. In 2019, the city had 323,152 people, while the metropolitan area had 517,056 people, and the combined statistical area had 745,033 people. Lexington is the 28th largest city by land area in the United States. It is in Fayette County and is part of the county. The city has a mayor-council government with 12 districts and three elected members, one of whom is the vice mayor.

Ramón Gómez Castillo, often called Ramón Valdés, was a Mexican actor born on September 2, 1923, and passed away on August 9, 1988. He is famous for playing Don Ramón. He was also considered one of Mexico's best comedians. Ramón was born in Mexico City and grew up in a big, poor family. At two years old, his family moved to Ciudad Juárez. Valdés started acting in 1949 in a movie called "Tender Pumpkins." His brother Germán, known as Tin-Tan, was already a famous actor. Together, they appeared in films during the golden age of Mexican cinema. Ramón had two other brothers who were also actors: Manuel, known as "Manuel the Crazy Valdés," and Antonio, known as "Ratón Valdés." In 1968, Ramón met Roberto Gómez Bolaños, known as Chespirito. They worked together on shows like "Los Supergenios de la Mesa Cuadrada," "Chespirito," and "El Chapulín Colorado." Ramón gained international fame for his role as Don Ramón in Chespirito's sitcom "El Chavo del Ocho." He left the show in 1979 but came back in 1981 for his last year. In 1982, Ramón acted in a Venezuelan show called "Federrico" with Carlos Villagrán. In 1987, he was in another show called "Ah Que Kiko." Neither of these shows became very popular.
Vezot is a commune in Sarthe department, which is in the Pays de la Loire region of northwest France.

The secretary of defense (SecDef) leads the U.S. Department of Defense, which manages the armed forces. The SecDef's power over the military is next to the president. This role is similar to a defense minister in other countries. The SecDef is chosen by the president, with Senate approval, and usually joins the cabinet. By law, the SecDef is part of the National Security Council. The SecDef has the authority to control and direct the Department of Defense, as long as the president gives directions. The SecDef is also the president's main helper on matters related to the Department of Defense. The SecDef cannot be appointed for seven years after being an active officer in the regular armed forces. The SecDef, only following the president's orders, controls all military forces, including the army, marines, navy, air force, and space force. The SecDef can also control the U.S. Coast Guard when its command is transferred to the Department of Defense. The SecDef is the only one who can transfer military control between the three main military departments and the ten combatant commands. Because of this, some call the SecDef a "de facto" deputy commander-in-chief. The SecDef, along with the secretary of state, attorney general, and secretary of the treasury, is often seen as one of the most important cabinet positions. Mark Esper became the 27th SecDef on July 23, 2019.

The Richmond football club, known as the Tigers, is a professional Australian rules football team in the Australian Football League (AFL), the top competition. The club started in Richmond, Melbourne, in 1885 and won two premierships before 1907. They then joined the Victorian Football League (now AFL) in 1908 and have won twelve premierships, most recently in 2019. Richmond's main base and training are at the Punt Road Oval, near the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG), their home ground since 1965. The team wears black guernseys with yellow stripes. Their song, "We're from Tigerland," has the famous "yellow and black" part. Richmond is led by coach Damien Hardwick and has Trent Cotchin as captain. Five Richmond players—Kevin Bartlett, Jack Dyer, Royce Hart, Kevin Sheedy, and Ian Stewart—are famous "Legends" in Australian football.

"Right Behind You (Mafia)" is a song by the Canadian alternative rock band Our Lady Peace. It came out in July 2001 as their third and last single from their fourth album, "Spiritual Machines." The single didn't do well, so they stopped its release and its music video. It was also the last single released when Mike Turner, the band's founding guitarist, was still part of the group. Matt Cameron from Pearl Jam played drums for this song while Our Lady Peace's drummer, Jeremy Taggart, was hurt.

Rascal Flatts is an American country music group formed in Columbus, Ohio, in 1999. The members are Gary Levox (lead vocals), Jay DeMarcus (bass guitar, background vocals), and Joe Don Rooney (lead guitar, background vocals). Jay DeMarcus is Gary Levox's second cousin and has been married to a sister of country singer James Otto. He was also in a Christian music group called East to West. From 2000 to 2010, they were with a record label called Disney's Lyric Street. They made six albums during this time, all of which were very popular and certified platinum or higher by the Recording Industry Association of America. Their albums were: "Rascal Flatts" (2000), "Melt" (2002), "Feels Like Today" (2004), "Me and My Gang" (2006), "Still Feels Good" (2007), and "Unstoppable" (2009). After Lyric Street closed in 2010, they joined Big Machine Records. They made five more albums and one Christmas album with Big Machine: "Nothing Like This" (2010), "Changed" (2012), "Rewind" (2014), "The Greatest Gift of All" (2016), and "Back to Us" (2017). Rascal Flatts had forty hit songs. Sixteen of these were number one hits on the Billboard Hot Country Songs, Country Airplay, and Canada Country charts. Their song "Bless the Broken Road" stayed at number one for five weeks in 2005. In 2006-2007, "What Hurts the Most" was a big hit, reaching number one on both the Hot Country Songs and Adult Contemporary charts, and peaked at number six on the Billboard Hot 100. On January 7, 2020, the band said they would end their group after 21 years with a farewell tour. However, the tour was postponed indefinitely on May 19, 2020, because of the coronavirus.
Bizen's original center was in modern Okayama. Bizen was a major place for making swords from an early time in Japan.
Phillipsburg is a city in Kansas, United States. It is also the county seat of Phillips County. According to the 2010 census, the city had 2,581 people.

The Coral Sea is a part of the South Pacific Ocean, located off Australia's northeast coast. It is considered an interim Australian bioregion. The Coral Sea stretches along Australia's northeast coast. During World War II, the Coral Sea was the site of a major naval battle between Japan, the United States, and Australia. This sea has many islands and reefs, including the Great Barrier Reef, which is the world's largest reef system. UNESCO declared the Great Barrier Reef a World Heritage Site in 1981. Oil exploration in the Great Barrier Reef area was stopped in 1975, and fishing is limited in some areas. The Coral Sea's reefs and islands are home to a variety of birds and sea life, making it a popular tourist destination both within Australia and internationally.

A drumstick is a type of percussion mallet used to play the snare drum, drum kit, and some other percussion instruments. They are especially used for unpitched percussion. Some other percussion instruments, like a triangle, use different beaters called metal beaters or "wands," while tuned percussion instruments such as the xylophone and timpani use mallets, but these are not called drumsticks. Drumsticks usually have these features:

Michael Lawrence Marrow, known as Phase 2 and Lonny Wood, was an American artist who used aerosol paint. He lived from August 2, 1955, to December 12, 2019, and was based in New York City. He was most active in the 1970s and is known for creating the "bubble letter" style of aerosol writing, also called "softies." Phase 2 also played an important role in the early hip hop scene.

Yandobinskoye rural settlement is in the Alikovsky district of the Chuvash Republic, Russia. It is in the middle of the district. The administrative center is Yandoba, a small village. In 2006, it had about 1,081 people. Yandobinskoye has twelve small villages. A road runs through its area.
