In the body, compound sugars break down into simple sugars. Longer chains of simple sugars are not called sugars and are called oligosaccharides or polysaccharides. Some substances, like glycerol and sugar alcohols, taste sweet but are not considered sugars. Sugars are found in most plants, with honey and fruit being natural sources of simple sugars. Sugarcane and sugar beets are rich in sucrose, used to make refined sugar. In 2016, these crops produced about two billion tonnes. Maltose is made from malting grain, and lactose is found only in milk and some dairy products. Corn syrup, a cheap source of sugar, is made from corn starch. Sugar is used in baked goods and added to processed foods and drinks. People also use it as a sweetener. On average, a person consumes about 50 kilograms of sugar yearly, or more than 260 food calories daily in developed countries. As sugar consumption increased in the late 20th century, researchers looked at whether a high-sugar diet, especially refined sugar, harmed human health. Excessive sugar intake may cause obesity, diabetes, heart disease, dementia, and tooth decay. The World Health Organization suggests reducing sugar intake to less than 10% of total energy intake and ideally below 5%.

Jessica Mauboy, born on August 4, 1989, is an Australian singer, songwriter, and actress. She grew up in Darwin, a city in the Northern Territory. Mauboy became famous in 2006 by coming second on "Australian Idol" and then signed with Sony Music Australia. She released her first album, "Been Waiting," in 2007. It had her first number-one single, "Burn," and became one of the top-selling albums that year. Her next album, "Get 'Em Girls," came out in 2010. It had four platinum singles and had a harder sound. In 2013, she released "Beautiful," which included popular songs like "Pop a Bottle (Fill Me Up)," "Never Be the Same," and "Can I Get a Moment?" Mauboy also acted in films like "Bran Nue Dae" (2010) and "The Sapphires" (2012), winning an AACTA Award. She starred in the TV show "The Secret Daughter" from 2016 to 2017. Her 2019 album "Hilda" was number one on the charts. Mauboy has worked with many famous singers and performed at important events. She also competed in the Eurovision Song Contest in 2018.

Red Bank is a borough in Monmouth County, New Jersey. It was incorporated in 1908 and is located near the Navesink River. As of 2010, the population was 12,206, which was an increase from 11,844 in 2000 and 10,636 in 1990. Red Bank originally became a town in 1870 from part of Shrewsbury Township. In 1879, it was renamed Shrewsbury City but returned to its original name in May of the same year. On March 10, 1908, it officially became a borough. Red Bank got its name from the red soil near the Navesink River.

George of the Jungle is an American animated TV series. It was made by Jay Ward and Bill Scott, who also created "The Rocky and Bullwinkle Show." The character George came from a story about Tarzan and a cartoon drawing of George Eiferman. George Eiferman was known as Mr. America, Mr. Universe, and a hall of famer from the IFBB. The cartoon was drawn by a cook on a ship during World War II. The series aired on Saturdays, from September 9 to December 30, 1967, on the ABC network.

Michael Andrew Gove, born Graeme Andrew Logan on August 26, 1967, is a British politician. He has been the Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster since 2019 and Minister for the Cabinet Office since 2020. He has been the Member of Parliament (MP) for Surrey Heath since 2005. A member of the Conservative Party, Gove served as Education Secretary from 2010 to 2014, Chief Whip from 2014 to 2015, Justice Secretary from 2015 to 2016, and Environment Secretary from 2017 to 2019. He tried to become leader of the Conservative Party twice, in 2016 and 2019, but finished third both times. Gove went to Robert Gordon's College and Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford. He worked as an author and journalist for The Times before becoming an MP in 2005. In 2007, he became the shadow secretary of state for Children, Schools, and Families under David Cameron. In 2010, he became Education Secretary. As Education Secretary, he ended the Building Schools for the Future program, changed A-level and GCSE exams, and dealt with the Trojan Horse scandal. Teachers' unions passed motions against his policies in 2013. In 2014, Gove became Chief Whip. After the 2015 election, he became Justice Secretary and Lord Chancellor. In 2016, he was a key figure in the Brexit referendum, helping the Vote Leave campaign. He later ran for Conservative Party leader, but came third. He was removed from the cabinet in 2016. In 2017, he became Environment Secretary. He tried again to be party leader in 2019 but came third. After Boris Johnson became prime minister in 2019, Gove became Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster. He now also handles preparations for a no-deal Brexit.

Dodge is an American car brand made by FCA US LLC, which is based in Auburn Hills, Michigan. Dodge makes fast cars, but for most of its history, it was Chrysler's mid-priced brand, above Plymouth. Dodge was started in the early 1900s by brothers Horace and John Dodge. At first, it supplied parts to car makers in Detroit. In 1914, Dodge began making complete cars under its "Dodge Brothers" name, before Chrysler was founded. The factory was in Hamtramck, Michigan, and operated until January 1980. Both Dodge brothers died from the Spanish flu in 1920. Their families sold the company to Dillon, Read & Co. in 1925, and then to Chrysler in 1928. Dodge mostly made trucks and large cars in the 1970s. They also produced some smaller cars, like the Dart from 1963 to 1976, and midsize cars like the Coronet and Charger from 1965 to 1978. The 1973 oil crisis helped Chrysler create the K platform for small to midsize cars starting in 1981. One of these cars was the Dodge Caravan. From 1998 to 2009, Dodge went through several ownership changes, including a short merger with Daimler-Benz AG from 1998 to 2007. It was then sold to Cerberus Capital Management, got a bailout from the U.S. government in 2009, went bankrupt, and was bought by Fiat. In 2011, Dodge separated from its model sub-brands, Dodge Ram and Dodge Viper. Dodge said Viper would be an SRT product, and Ram would be a separate brand. In 2014, SRT was merged back into Dodge. That year, Chrysler Group changed its name to FCA US LLC, along with the merger of Fiat S.p.A. and Chrysler Group into Fiat Chrysler Automobiles.
The following is a list of notable deaths in December 2017. Each day's entries are arranged alphabetically by last name. A typical entry includes the following information:

The governor of Tasmania represents Queen Elizabeth II, who is the Queen of Australia. In Tasmania, the governor does the same jobs as the governor-general does across the whole country. Usually, the governor follows advice from the premier, the leader of the government. But the governor can still use some special powers if needed, including dismissing the premier. For more on governors in Australia, see "Governors of the Australian States." The governor lives in Government House, which is in the Queen's Domain. Sir Stanley Burbury was the first Tasmanian-born governor in 1973, and Sir Guy Green was the first Tasmanian-born governor born in Tasmania in 1995. Since Burbury, all Tasmanian governors have been born in Australia, except for Peter Underwood, who was born in Britain but moved to Australia when he was young. In 2014, there was no governor for over five months because Peter Underwood died suddenly. Alan Blow, the chief justice and lieutenant-governor, acted as governor during this time. On November 10, 2014, Premier Will Hodgman said Kate Warner, a university professor, would become the first female governor of Tasmania. Kate Warner was sworn in on December 10, 2014. Since Kate Warner became governor, the Queen, based on the premier's suggestion, gave her and all future governors the title "The Honourable" for life.

Frode Johnsen, born on March 17, 1974, was a Norwegian former professional footballer. He played for teams like Odd and Rosenborg in Norway and Nagoya Grampus and Shimizu S-Pulse in Japan. He played in different positions, but was often used as a striker or midfielder. Johnsen is 188 cm tall and was good at heading the ball. In his last season with Odd in 2015, he won the Kniksen's honour award for his long football career. He retired at the age of 41. In 2013, he became the top scorer in the Tippeligaen, making him the oldest top scorer in a European league.

Leslie David Reed, born on July 24, 1935, and passed away on April 15, 2019, was an English songwriter, arranger, musician, and leader of a light orchestra. His main songwriting partners were Gordon Mills, Barry Mason, and Geoff Stephens. He also wrote songs with other artists like Roger Greenaway, Roger Cook, Peter Callander, and Johnny Worth. Reed wrote about sixty charting songs, and is well-known for "It's Not Unusual," "Delilah," "The Last Waltz," and "Marching on Together." His songs received many gold discs and Ivor Novello awards. In the mid-1960s, it was unusual for a British singles chart not to include a song by Leslie Reed. He received the British Academy Gold Badge of Merit in 1982.

Duttaphrynus stomaticus, also known as the Indian marbled toad, Punjab toad, Indus Valley toad, or marbled toad, is a species of toad found in Asia. It is in areas like eastern Iran, Pakistan, Afghanistan, and Nepal, extending into peninsular India and Bangladesh. This toad does not have bony bumps on its head. The space between its eyes is wider than its upper eyelid. Its ear has a membrane that is about two-thirds the size of its eye. The first and second fingers are nearly the same length, and there is one small bump under each of these fingers. A bony ridge is found on the toes. There is a gland on the shin and the swelling behind the eye is longer than it is wide. Three dark lines run across the inside of the arm. The underside is light with dark spots on the throat.

Mahavira, also known as Vardhamana, was the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism. He followed Parshvanatha, the 23rd Tirthankara. Mahavira was born in the early 6th century BC into a royal Kshatriya Jain family in present-day Bihar, India. His mother's name was Trishala, and his father's name was Siddhartha. They were followers of Parshvanatha. At about 30 years old, Mahavira gave up all his possessions and became an ascetic, searching for spiritual awakening. He practiced intense meditation and severe austerities for 12 and a half years. After this, he gained omniscience. Mahavira preached for 30 years and attained salvation in the 6th century BC. He taught that following the vows of non-violence, truth, non-stealing, chastity, and non-attachment are necessary for spiritual liberation. He also taught the principles of many-sided reality, known as anekantavada. Mahavira's teachings were passed down by his chief disciple, Indrabhuti Gautama, as the Jain Agamas. The texts, originally passed orally by Jain monks, were mostly lost by the 1st century AD. Only some versions of the Agamas are used by the Svetambara tradition, and their authenticity is debated by the Digambara tradition. Mahavira is often shown sitting or standing in a meditative pose, with a lion underneath him. The earliest depictions of Mahavira come from archaeological sites in the north Indian city of Mathura, dating from the 1st century BC to the 2nd century AD. Mahavir Janma Kalyanak celebrates his birth, and Diwali marks his salvation.

CAAMA, the Central Australian Aboriginal Media Association, was started in 1980. Its goal is to share Aboriginal music and culture with all of Australia. Located in Alice Springs, CAAMA involves the local Indigenous community in its work. CAAMA makes radio, TV, and recordings.

Harvey Spector, born on December 26, 1939, is an American record producer, musician, and songwriter. He created the Wall of Sound, a music production method that he saw as a grand approach to rock and roll, similar to Wagner's style. Spector is seen as a very important person in pop music history and is known as the first artist to have full control over the recording process. After being inactive for about 30 years, he was found guilty of killing actress Lana Clarkson in 2009 and is serving a prison sentence of 19 years, with parole possible in 2025. Born in the Bronx, Spector started his career in 1958 as part of the Teddy Bears, a band he co-founded. They had a big hit with "To Know Him Is to Love Him." In 1960, he helped start Philles Records and was the youngest record label owner in the U.S. at 21. During the 1960s, he wrote, co-wrote, or produced records for the Ronettes, the Crystals, and Ike & Tina Turner. He often worked with arranger Jack Nitzsche, engineer Larry Levine, and a band called "The Wrecking Crew." In 1966, Spector stopped making music for a while. In 1969, Spector came back and produced the Beatles' album "Let It Be" (1970) as well as albums by John Lennon and George Harrison. In the mid-1970s, he helped make eighteen top 10 US hits for different artists, though he became less active later. His famous songs include "You've Lost That Lovin' Feelin'" (1964), "The Long and Winding Road" (1970), and "My Sweet Lord" (1970). According to BMI, "You've Lost That Lovin' Feelin'" was the most played song on American radio in the 20th century. Spector's work influenced the way studios were used and mixed pop art with music. His 1963 Christmas record is considered one of the best of all time. In 1965, he was called the "First Tycoon of Teen" by Tom Wolfe. Spector won a Grammy Award in 1973 and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1989 and the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 1997. In 2004, Rolling Stone magazine ranked him 63rd on their list of the 100 greatest artists of all time.

Azerbaijan Airlines, also known as Azal, is the main and biggest airline in Azerbaijan. It is based in Baku, next to Heydar Aliyev International Airport. The airline flies to places in Asia, CIS, Europe, and the USA. Azerbaijan Airlines is part of a global airline group. The airline started in 1992, becoming Azerbaijan's first national airline after the country became independent.

The adrenal glands, also called suprarenal glands, are endocrine glands that make hormones such as adrenaline and steroids like aldosterone and cortisol. These glands are located above the kidneys. Each gland has two main parts: an outer cortex and an inner medulla. The adrenal cortex, or outer part, is divided into three zones: The zona glomerulosa produces hormones that help regulate blood pressure and electrolyte balance. The zona fasciculata makes glucocorticoids like cortisol and cortisone, which control metabolism and affect the immune system. The zona reticularis, the innermost layer, produces androgens, which become sex hormones in other parts of the body. Making steroid hormones is called steroidogenesis, a process that happens in the cortex cells. The medulla, the inner part of the gland, makes catecholamines, which prepare the body to respond quickly during stress. Some diseases involve problems with the adrenal glands. Too much cortisol leads to Cushing's syndrome, while too little causes Addison's disease. Congenital adrenal hyperplasia is a genetic condition that affects how the endocrine system works. Tumors can also develop in the adrenal tissue and are often found when looking for other medical issues.
Del Norte is a town in Colorado, United States. It is the county seat of Rio Grande County. The town's name is usually said as "Del Nor-te". In 2010, the town had 1,686 people.

Cryptosporidium, often called crypto, is a type of parasite that can cause illness in the lungs and intestines. It can lead to watery diarrhea and, sometimes, a persistent cough. This can happen to both people with a healthy immune system and those with a weak one. The main treatment for this illness involves keeping hydrated and replacing lost salts and managing pain. For people with a healthy immune system, the drug nitazoxanide is approved to treat cryptosporidium. Adding zinc supplements might help, especially for those who might lack zinc, especially if they have recurring or persistent infections. Cryptosporidium oocysts are tiny, measuring 4 to 6 micrometers in size, and they can be partly stained with an acid-fast stain. They need to be distinguished from other similar-looking organisms like Cyclospora cayetanensis.

Kuala Terengganu, often called K.T., is a city in Terengganu, Malaysia. It is the main city, where the government and the king live, and where the money of the state comes from. Kuala Terengganu is also the capital of Kuala Terengganu district and has the most people in the state. It is about 440 kilometers northeast of Kuala Lumpur on Malaysia's east coast. The city sits at the Terengganu River's mouth, facing the South China Sea. Kuala Terengganu got the title "Waterfront Heritage City" on January 1, 2008. The city is important for politics and the economy. It is also a main entrance to many tourist spots in the state. Places to visit include Chinese Village, Kedai Payang Market, Terengganu State Museum, and Batu Buruk Beach. Even though the city has modern changes, it still has strong Malay influences due to its long history as a port.
Angels in the outfield can mean: Players in the outfield.

Publius Cornelius Tacitus, or Gaius Cornelius Tacitus, was a Roman historian and politician. He is considered one of the best Roman historians by modern scholars. Living during the Silver Age of Latin literature, Tacitus was known for his short and clear writing and deep understanding of power politics. His two major works, the "Annals" and the "Histories," cover the rule of emperors like Tiberius, Claudius, Nero, and those in the year of the four emperors in 69 AD. These works start from 14 AD, when Augustus died, and end in 70 AD, during the first Jewish–Roman war. Parts of his works are missing, especially a long gap in the "Annals." Tacitus also wrote about speaking skills, Germania, and his father-in-law, Agricola, who was responsible for many Roman conquests in Britain.

Pratval was a former municipality in the Hinterrhein district of the Swiss canton of Graubünden. On January 1, 2015, Pratval joined with four other former municipalities—Almens, Paspels, Rodels, and Tomils—to form the new municipality of Domleschg.

Kaoru Moto was born on April 25, 1917, and died on August 26, 1992. He was in the United States Army. After he died, he was given the Medal of Honor. This award is the highest decoration given by the United States military. Kaoru received it for his brave actions during World War II.
In the 1957-58 Dutch Eerste Divisie, 32 teams played. They were split into two groups. Willem II and SHS won the championship.

Cameron Barker was born on April 4, 1986. He is a professional ice hockey player who plays as a defenseman. Currently, he is not signed to any team. Most recently, he played for the Ilves Tampere in Finland. Barker was chosen third in the 2004 NHL entry draft by the Chicago Blackhawks. He played for the Blackhawks for four seasons before being traded to the Minnesota Wild in 2010. He also played for the Canadian national team. Barker won gold medals twice in the world junior championships in 2005 and 2006. People often think he should have been drafted better.

Karnali Zone was one of the fourteen zones in Nepal's mid-western development region. The headquarters of Karnali Zone was in Jumla. It was one of the poorest and most remote areas in Nepal, with poor road access. There were airfields in all districts except Kalikot, which is linked to Jumla Airport by road only during certain seasons. Karnali Zone was the largest zone in Nepal and had two national parks. Shey Phoksundo National Park, containing Phoksundo Lake—the deepest lake in Nepal—was Nepal's largest park, covering 3,555 km². Rara National Park, which surrounds Rara Lake—the largest lake in Nepal at 10.2 km²—was known as the "pearl of Nepal." Karnali Zone was split into five districts, and since 2015, these districts have been called Karnali Pradeshs.

Grandval is a town in the Jura Bernois area of the canton of Bern in Switzerland. It is in the French-speaking part of the Bernese Jura. Grandval was also known as Granfel or Granfelden in German, but these names are not used much now.

Mario Altmann, born on November 4, 1986, is an Austrian ice hockey player. He plays for EHC Black Wings Linz in the Austrian Hockey League (EBEL). Before this, he played for EC VSV for five seasons. On April 16, 2015, Altmann signed a one-year contract with EHC Black Wings Linz, his Austrian rival. Altmann has been part of the Austria men's national ice hockey team since 2009. He played in the 2009, 2011, and 2011 IIHF World Championships and also in the 2014 Winter Olympics.

Cee Lo Green's "Magic Moment" is his first Christmas album and the fourth studio album released in 2012. It came out on October 29 in the UK and October 30 in the US. His versions of "Mary, Did You Know?" and "What Christmas Means to Me" reached number 22 and 23 on the US R&B chart in December 2012. The album sold 181,000 copies in the US that year. This is the first time his solo album doesn't have a parental advisory label.
Jimmy Morales was born on March 18, 1969, as James Ernesto Morales Cabrera. He is a Guatemalan politician, actor, and comedian. Jimmy Morales served as Guatemala's president from 2016 to 2020.

The Yukon River is a big river in northwestern North America. It starts in British Columbia, Canada, and flows through the Canadian Yukon Territory, named after the river. Later, it goes through Alaska and empties into the Bering Sea at the Yukon–Kuskokwim Delta. The river is very long, with an average flow of 227,000 feet per second and a drainage area of 832,700 square kilometers, with 323,800 square kilometers in Canada. It's the longest river in Alaska and Yukon, and was a main way for people to travel during the Klondike Gold Rush from 1896 to 1903. A part of the river in Yukon, called "The Thirty Mile" section, is a national heritage river and part of the Klondike Gold Rush International Historical Park. Riverboats used the river until the 1950s when the Klondike Highway was built. After the U.S. bought Alaska in 1867, the Alaska Commercial Company built some posts along the Yukon River. The Yukon River has had some pollution from military bases, dumps, and other sources, but it's not listed as an impaired watershed by the Environmental Protection Agency. The U.S. Geological Survey shows good levels of water quality, with low turbidity, metals, and dissolved oxygen. Compared to other rivers in Siberia, the Yukon River has much less suspended sediment. A group called the Yukon River Inter-Tribal Watershed Council, made up of 70 tribes from Alaska and Canada, works to clean up the river and make its water safe to drink again by checking government data.

Rancho Palos Verdes, also called RPV or Palos Verdes, is a coastal city in Los Angeles County, California. It sits on the bluffs of the Palos Verdes Peninsula. Neighboring cities include Palos Verdes Estates, Rolling Hills, and Rolling Hills Estates. Known for its views of the Pacific Ocean, Santa Catalina Island, and Los Angeles, it also has top-ranked schools, many horse and hiking trails, and expensive homes.

Ratnasambhava means "jewel-born." He is one of the five dhyani buddhas in Vajrayana or tantric Buddhism. Ratnasambhava focuses on developing equality and equanimity. In Vajrayana, he helps to overcome greed and pride. His female partner is Mamaki, and he rides a horse or a pair of lions.

Swatch Internet Time, or.beat time, was introduced in 1998 by Swatch. It uses a decimal system instead of hours and minutes. Each day is divided into 1000 parts called.beats. Each.beat lasts 1 minute and 26.4 seconds. Time is shown as a 3-digit number out of 1000 after midnight. For example, 248 means 248.beats after midnight, which is about 5 hours and 57 minutes. Swatch Internet Time doesn't have different time zones. Instead, it uses Biel Meantime (BMT), based on Swatch's headquarters in Biel, Switzerland. BMT is the same as Central European Time, West Africa Time, and UTC+01. Unlike civil time in Switzerland and many other countries, Swatch Internet Time does not change for daylight saving time.

The covalent radius, "r," measures an atom's size in a covalent bond. It is usually measured in picometers (pm) or angstroms (Å), where 1 Å equals 100 pm. The covalent bond length between two atoms, "r" (ab), is typically the sum of their covalent radii: "r" (ab) = "r" (a) + "r" (b). Different radii can be used for single, double, and triple bonds, though they are not always exact due to varying chemical environments. For bonds between different atoms (heteroatomic), ionic effects might be involved. Polar covalent bonds are often shorter than expected based on covalent radii alone. Covalent radii values in tables are usually averages or idealized, but they can still be useful in different situations. Bond lengths "r" (ab) are often measured using X-ray diffraction or neutron diffraction. For homonuclear bonds (same atoms), the covalent radius is half the single bond length, such as in hydrogen (H-H = 74.14 pm, so H's radius = 37.07 pm). In practice, an average value from various covalent compounds is usually used. Recently, Sanderson published covalent radii for main-group elements, but bond lengths from the Cambridge Crystallographic Database are now more commonly used.

Osvaldo Bayer was an Argentine writer and journalist. He lived in Buenos Aires. In 1974, during Isabel Perón's presidency, he went to live in Linz am Rhein, Germany. This was during the dictatorship from 1976 to 1983.

The December 2010 North American blizzard was a major snowstorm from December 5 to 29, 2010. It affected the United States and parts of Canada. From January 4 to 15, the storm was called "Windstorm Benjamin" in Europe. It was the first big winter storm of the 2010-11 season and the fifth blizzard in North America that year. The storm hit many big cities in the Northeast, including Norfolk, Philadelphia, Newark, New York, Hartford, Providence, and Boston. It brought lots of snow to these areas.
Carol Cleveland was born on January 13, 1942. She is an actress and comedian from Britain and America. People know her especially for her work with Monty Python.
Sandslån is a small place in Kramfors municipality, Västernorrland county, Sweden. It had 272 people living there in 2010.

Muscular dystrophy (MD) is a group of diseases that cause muscles to weaken and break down over time. Different types affect different muscles, cause varying degrees of weakness, worsen at different rates, and begin at different ages. Many people eventually lose the ability to walk. Some types can also affect other organs. There are about 30 types of muscular dystrophy, usually grouped into nine categories. The most common is Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), which usually starts in boys around age four. Other types include Becker muscular dystrophy, facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy, limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, and myotonic dystrophy. These conditions are caused by changes in genes that make muscle proteins. Changes can be passed from parents or happen during early development. Some types are inherited while others are not. Doctors often diagnose muscular dystrophy through blood tests and genetic testing. There is no cure. Treatments may include physical therapy, braces, and corrective surgeries to help with symptoms. For those with breathing muscle weakness, assisted ventilation might be needed. Medications like steroids can slow muscle breakdown, while others control seizures and delay damage to dying muscle cells. Duchenne muscular dystrophy, which makes up about half of all cases, affects about one in 5,000 boys at birth. Muscular dystrophy was first described in the 1830s by Charles Bell. The term "dystrophy" comes from the Greek "dys," meaning "difficult," and "trophic," meaning "to nourish." Gene therapy is currently in early stages of human study as a treatment.

In Norse mythology, Sigyn is a goddess and Loki's wife. She is mentioned in the "Poetic Edda," compiled in the 13th century from older sources, and in the "Prose Edda," written by Snorri Sturluson in the 13th century. In the "Poetic Edda," not much is known about Sigyn except that she helps Loki when he is captured. In the "Prose Edda," she helps Loki again during his time in captivity. She appears in various poetic sayings, and her role as a goddess is mentioned twice. Some people think Sigyn is shown on the Gosforth Cross, and she has been the subject of many theories and cultural references.
Bluebells, or bluebelle, can mean:

Rain is a town in the Donau-Ries district of Bavaria, Germany. It is by the River Lech, near where it meets the Danube, about 11 km east of Donauwörth. Rain is on the B16 road and has a train station on the Ingolstadt–Neuoffingen railway, part of the Danube Valley Railway. The town was first mentioned in a document from 1257, when it was called a "ducal town." It was likely founded during the reigns of Duke Otto II (1248-1253) or Duke Louis II (1253-1294). Rain was built for economic and strategic reasons, protecting Bavaria and collecting taxes from the Lech bridge. In 1632, during the Thirty Years' War, the Battle of Rain took place. Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden's army defeated Johann Tserclaes von Tilly's army. Tilly died in Ingolstadt from an infected wound. A monument to Tilly stands in front of Rain's Rococo town hall. Rain has a Roman Catholic church with Gothic paintings from about 1480. Other historic buildings include the Schwabian Gate, a hospital with a chapel, and a former castle. Rain has three museums: the Lachner Brothers Museum, the Homeland Museum, and the Jean-Duprai Museum. The Lachner brothers were 19th-century German composers born in the town. Notable residents include Johann Bayer, a lawyer and astronomer, Georg Tannstetter, a humanist, and Michael Raucheisen, a pianist. Rain is the home of the Dehner chain of garden centers, which employs 1,100 people. The town also has a sugar refinery with about 240 to 280 workers. Rain is twinned with Tougan, the capital of the Sourou province in Burkina Faso.
Heinrich Ludwig Futterer was an athlete from Germany. He mainly ran in sprint events. He was born on October 14, 1931, and died on February 10, 2019.

Viktor Fedorovych Yanukovych, born on July 9, 1950, was a Ukrainian politician. He became the fourth president of Ukraine in 2010. He was removed from office during the 2014 Ukrainian revolution and now lives in Russia. Yanukovych worked as the governor of Donetsk Oblast, an eastern province in Ukraine, from 1997 to 2002. He was also Ukraine's prime minister twice, first from November 21, 2002, to December 7, 2004, and again from December 28, 2004, to January 5, 2005, under President Leonid Kuchma. In 2004, Yanukovych ran for president. He won the first round of the election but lost the second round to Viktor Yushchenko. There were complaints about election cheating. This led to protests and the Orange Revolution. The Ukrainian Supreme Court nullified the second round and held a new election. Yanukovych lost again to Yushchenko. Yanukovych served as prime minister for a second time from August 4, 2006, to December 18, 2007, under President Yushchenko. In 2010, Yanukovych won the presidential election against Yulia Tymoshenko. International observers said the election was fair. In November 2013, Yanukovych refused a European Union association agreement and instead chose a Russian loan and closer ties with Russia. This angered people, who protested and occupied Kyiv's Independence Square. These events became known as the Euromaidan. In January 2014, violent clashes occurred, and Yanukovych left Kyiv. He fled to Kharkiv, then to Crimea, and eventually to Russia. On February 21, 2014, the Ukrainian parliament removed Yanukovych from his position and issued an arrest warrant for him. After his departure, Yanukovych said he was still the legitimate president. In June 2015, the Ukrainian parliament took away his title. In January 2019, he was sentenced to 13 years in prison for high treason, even though he was not in the country.

To catch a killer is a TV movie from 1992. Eric Till directed it, and Brian Dennehy and Michael Riley acted in it. The story is based on the real events of catching John Wayne Gacy, an American serial killer.

The Schwarzschild radius, sometimes called the gravitational radius, is a special distance. It defines the event horizon of a Schwarzschild black hole, which is a solution to Einstein's field equations. This radius is related to any mass. It was named after Karl Schwarzschild, who figured out this solution in 1916. The Schwarzschild radius can be calculated using this formula: Sch. r = (2 × G × M) / (c²) Here, "G" is the gravitational constant, "M" is the object's mass, and "c" is the speed of light.
This is a list of important people who were born, grew up in, or live in the state of Florida, USA.

João Teixeira de Faria, also known as João de Deus, was born on June 24, 1942. He is a Brazilian man who calls himself a medium and a psychic surgeon. He was also found guilty of sexually abusing people. He lived and worked in Abadiânia, Brazil. His place, Casa de Dom Inácio de Loyola, claimed to offer spiritual healing. He was on TV shows like CNN, ABC News, and The Oprah Winfrey Show. However, James Randi and Joe Nickell said his healing tricks were just like carnival tricks, and the benefits people reported were probably just because they believed in them. In 2018, he admitted to more than 600 sexual abuse accusations. In December 2019, he was found guilty and given a 19-year and four-month sentence for raping four women. On January 20, 2020, he was sentenced to 40 more years in prison for raping five women. This was his third time being found guilty. In total, his sentences add up to 63 years and four months.
Oxford is a town in Oxford County, Maine, United States. In 2010, it had 4,110 people. Oxford has a speedway, a fair, and a casino. The town also includes Welchville.

In the year 235 BC, it was known as the time when consuls Torquatus and Bulbus served. Some also called it the 519th year since the founding of Rome. People started using 235 BC to date this year a long time ago, when counting years from the birth of Jesus became common in Europe.

Princess Amelia of the United Kingdom was born on August 7, 1783, and died on November 2, 1810. She was the fifteenth and last child, and the sixth daughter, of King George III and Queen Charlotte of Mecklenburg-Strelitz. She was their first daughter to pass away, and the third child to die before them.
Gianni Morandi, born on December 11, 1944, is an Italian singer, actor, and entertainer.

San Carlos is a community in Hidalgo County, Texas. According to the 2010 United States Census, its population was 3,130. It is part of the McAllen-Edinburg-Mission metropolitan area. San Carlos is located northeast of McAllen.

The pedal steel guitar is a type of steel guitar that uses pedals and knee levers to change string pitches. This lets players make more complex music than before. Like other steel guitars, it can slide notes smoothly and create deep vibrato sounds, just like a human voice. It is mostly used in American country music. In the 1950s, pedals and knee levers were added to steel guitars. This let performers play a major scale without moving the bar. They could also play chords and push pedals at the same time, making passing notes blend with other notes. This unique sound became popular in country and western music. The steel guitar originated in Hawaii in the 19th century. It gained popularity in the United States during the early 20th century. Various instruments were developed to be played horizontally, like the lap steel and the resonator lap steel. The electric guitar pickup, invented in 1934, helped steel guitars be heard equally with other instruments. Later, the electrified lap steel, console steel, and finally the pedal steel guitar were created. Playing the pedal steel requires coordinated use of both hands, feet, and knees. Only the American reed organ has similar demands. Key developers include Buddy Emmons, Bud Isaacs, Zane Beck, and Paul Bigsby. Besides country music, the pedal steel is used in sacred music in the eastern and southern United States, jazz, and Nigerian music.

Twiztid is an American horrorcore duo from Detroit, Michigan. They were formed in 1997 and consist of Jamie Spaniolo and Paul Methric, who use the stage names Jamie Madrox and Monoxide. Spaniolo and Methric used to be in a group called House of Krazees, which stopped performing in 1997. They made their first album in 1997. Twiztid worked with a record company called Psychopathic Records from 1997 until 2012 when they left. After that, they started their own label in 2014 called Majik Ninja Entertainment. Twiztid makes horrorcore rap music and has released 12 studio albums, 12 EPs, 10 compilation albums, and 1 mixtape.
Gabriel Pereira de Castro (1571-1632) was a Portuguese priest, lawyer, and poet.

Crystal Palace FC is a professional football club in Selhurst, South London, England. They play in the Premier League, the top level of English football. The club was officially founded in 1905 but claims to be a continuation of an earlier amateur club established in 1861 by the same company. This would make Crystal Palace one of the oldest professional football clubs in the world. Both the amateur and professional clubs were founded at Crystal Palace exhibition building and played there until 1915 when they had to move due to the war. They moved to their current home, Selhurst Park, in 1924. The amateur club was one of the first members of the Football Association in 1863 and took part in the first FA Cup in 1871–72, reaching the semi-finals. They stopped appearing in records after 1875. In 1905, the club became professional and tried to join the Football League but were rejected, instead playing in the Southern League. They joined the Football League in 1920 and mostly competed in the top two tiers of English football. Since 1964, they have only been in the third tier for three seasons between 1974 and 1977. Crystal Palace had a successful time in the 1980s and early 1990s, finishing third in the old First Division in the 1990–91 season. They almost qualified for the UEFA Cup that year. The club became a founder member of the Premier League in 1992. Crystal Palace have been in the FA Cup final twice, losing to Manchester United both times in 1990 and 2016. The team's colors used to be brown and blue until 1973, when they changed to the red and blue vertical stripes they wear today. Crystal Palace has a long rivalry with Brighton & Hove Albion, and also with Millwall and Charlton Athletic, south London clubs.
A gag is a tool made to stop someone from speaking. Sometimes, "gag" can also mean the acronym "gag."

The great seal of Connecticut has been its coat of arms since May 1784. It shows three grapevines and a ribbon below. The ribbon has a Latin motto: "Qui transtulit sustinet" (which means "He who transplanted sustains"). Around the design, it says "Sigillum reipublicæ connecticutensis," which means "Seal of the State of Connecticut."

Gomillion vs. Lightfoot, 364 U.S. 339 (1960), was a big court case. The Supreme Court said that creating voting district boundaries to keep black people from voting was wrong. This violated the Fifteenth Amendment.

Richard Falk was born on November 13, 1930. He is an American professor who retired from Princeton University. He has written 20 books and coauthored another 20. In 2008, he became a United Nations special rapporteur. His job was to report on human rights in the Palestinian territories since 1967.

Horace Ward Martin Tavares Silver was an American jazz pianist, composer, and arranger, known for his hard bop style, which he helped create in the 1950s. Born on September 2, 1928, and passed away on June 18, 2014. Silver started playing piano and saxophone in Connecticut. In 1950, his trio was chosen to play with Stan Getz, which was a big break. He moved to New York City and gained fame for his bluesy piano style. His work with Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers brought him more attention. Their album "Horace Silver and the Jazz Messengers" included his first hit song, "The Preacher." After leaving Blakey in 1956, Silver formed his own quintet, with a typical group of tenor saxophone, trumpet, piano, bass, and drums. Their performances and recordings for Blue Note Records made him popular. His best-known album was "Song for My Father," recorded in 1963 and 1964. In the early 1970s, he disbanded his group to focus on composing and added lyrics to his music. His interest in spiritualism also grew, leading to less successful releases. Silver left Blue Note after 28 years and started his own record label. He reduced his touring in the 1980s and relied on income from his compositions. In 1993, he returned to major record labels and released five albums before gradually retiring due to health issues. As a player, Silver played hard bop with a focus on melodies, using clear and humorous right-hand lines with dark left-hand notes. His compositions were catchy but sometimes contained dissonant harmonies. Many of his songs, like "Doodlin'," "Peace," and "Sister Sadie," became jazz standards still played today. His influence on other pianists and composers, along with nurturing young jazz talents over four decades, is part of his legacy.

Leo Keith Thorsness was born on February 14, 1932, and died on May 2, 2017. He was a colonel in the United States Air Force. Thorsness received the Medal of Honor for his actions in the Vietnam War. He was awarded this medal for an air engagement on April 19, 1967. Two weeks later, he was shot down and became a prisoner of war in North Vietnam for six years. After his military service, Thorsness served one term in the Washington State Senate.
Saint-Vigor-des-Mézerets was a small town in Calvados, Normandy, France. On January 1, 2017, it joined with another town to form Terres de Druance.

Rex Taylor Reed was born on October 2, 1938. He is an American film critic and sometimes acts in movies. Rex was also a co-host on the TV show "At the Movies." He writes a column called "On the Town with Rex Reed" for The New York Observer.

Consumer confidence is an economic measure that shows how optimistic people feel about the economy and their finances. If people feel good about the economy and their money, they are more likely to spend. When consumer confidence is high, people buy more things. When it's low, people save more and buy less. Consumer confidence changes over time, showing what people think about job opportunities and their financial situation. It usually goes up when the economy gets better and down when the economy worsens. In the United States, consumer confidence often follows the stock market after a while.

Lawrenceville is a city in Lawrence County, Illinois, United States. It is the county seat and is near the Embarras River. In 2010, there were 4,348 people living there. Lawrenceville is in southeast Illinois, close to Vincennes, Indiana. The city's high school basketball team, the Lawrenceville Indians, won state championships in 1972, 1974, 1982, and 1983. They won 68 games without losing in those two seasons. The coach, Ron Felling, later became an assistant coach at Indiana University.

Sheikh Ahmed Ismail Hassan Yassin (1937-2004) was a Palestinian imam and politician. He founded Hamas, an Islamist Palestinian paramilitary organization and political party. Yassin was the spiritual leader of Hamas. Hamas gained support in Palestinian society by setting up charities to fund hospitals, education, libraries, and other services. However, it was also responsible for several attacks on Israeli civilians and was labeled a terrorist group by many countries, including the European Union, Israel, Japan, Canada, and the United States. Yassin became a quadriplegic and nearly blind after a sports accident at age 12. He used a wheelchair. He was killed when an Israeli helicopter fired a missile at him during early morning prayers. The attack also killed his bodyguards and nine bystanders. Yassin's death was condemned internationally. Over 200,000 Palestinians attended his funeral.

Alfred Gomolka was a German politician born on July 21, 1942, and died on March 24, 2020. He was a member of the European Parliament representing Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. Additionally, he worked as the Minister President of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.

In Norse mythology, the megingjörð is a belt worn by the god Thor. This name means "power-belt" in Old Norse. The megin in Old Norse means power or strength, and gjörð means belt. In the Prose Edda, the belt is one of Thor's main possessions, along with his hammer Mjölnir and iron gloves Járngreipr. When worn, the belt doubles Thor's already great strength. In a poem called Þórsdrápa, written in the 10th century by Eilífr Göðrúnarson, there's a line that refers to Thor's power-belt. The line "njótr njarðgjarðar" means "he who benefits from the mighty belt," which refers to Thor's magical belt of strength, the megingjörð. In Gylfaginning, part of Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda, verse 45 mentions Thor's power-belt. In the story, when dawn came, Thor went outside. He was just a short distance from the forest. He fell asleep and slept strongly. Thor then realized what had happened during the night. He girded himself with his belt of strength, and his divine strength grew. He woke up quickly and was ready to use his hammer.

John Francis Welch Jr. was born on November 19, 1935, and died on March 1, 2020. He was an American businessman, chemical engineer, and writer. Welch was the chairman and CEO of General Electric (GE) from 1981 to 2001. When he left GE, he got a severance payment of $417 million, which was the largest such payment in business history. In 2006, Welch's net worth was estimated to be $720 million.

Soy milk, also called soya milk or soymilk, is a plant-based drink made from soaking and grinding soybeans. You mix it with water, boil it, and then strain it to remove the solids. It is a mixture of oil, water, and protein, similar to an emulsion. This drink is originally made during the tofu-making process. It first appeared in East Asia but became popular in Europe and North America later in the 20th century. Its taste and texture were improved to be more like regular milk. Soy milk, like almond or rice milk, can be used as a dairy milk substitute by vegans or people who can't tolerate lactose. Some people also choose to drink it for environmental or health reasons.

Terneuzen is a city and municipality in the southwestern part of the Netherlands, in Zeeland province, in the middle of Zeelandic Flanders. It has more than 55,000 people living there, making it the largest city in Zeeland.

"March On, Bahamaland" is the national anthem of the Bahamas. Timothy Gibson wrote the music and the lyrics. The Bahamas adopted this anthem in 1973 after gaining independence from the United Kingdom. Before this, "God Save the Queen" was used as the royal anthem.

The Queanbeyan River is a constant stream that belongs to the Molonglo catchment area in the Murray–Darling Basin. It is found in the Monaro and Capital Country regions of New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory, in Australia. The river is about long and has a catchment area of. The Queanbeyan River and the Cotter River provide clean water for the Canberra and Queanbeyan region. Their water quality is protected by federal laws. It is thought that the local Aboriginal Ngarigo people called this river "Queanbeyan," meaning "clearwater."

Hannah Dominique E. John-Kamen, born on September 7, 1989, is an English actress. She is famous for playing Yalena "Dutch" Yardeen in the TV show "Killjoys," Orela in "Game of Thrones," F'nale Zandor in "Ready Player One," Ava Starr/Ghost in "Ant-Man and the Wasp," and the main character in "The Stranger," a mystery series on Netflix.

William Shakespeare (1564-1616) was part of a theater company called the King's Men for most of his career. Before 1603, the company was known as the Lord Chamberlain's Men. When King James I became the new ruler in 1603, the company changed its name. A royal letter on May 19, 1603, listed the main actors: Lawrence Fletcher, William Shakespeare, Richard Burbage, Augustine Phillips, John Heminges, Henry Condell, William Sly, Robert Armin, and Richard Cowley. The nine named actors also became chamber servants. On March 15, 1604, each of these nine men received four and a half yards of red cloth for a special procession.

The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic in the Philippines is part of the global pandemic caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). The first case was found on January 30, 2020, involving a 38-year-old Chinese woman at San Lazaro Hospital in Metro Manila. A 44-year-old Chinese man was confirmed dead from the virus on February 1, making the Philippines the first country outside China to record a death from this disease. The Philippines did not report any new cases for over a month. However, on March 7, the country confirmed its first local transmission. Since then, the virus spread to all 17 regions of the country. Socio-economic status is linked to the number of cases across the country. As of August 21, there were 182,365 confirmed cases, with 114,519 recoveries and 2,940 deaths. The Philippines has the highest number of confirmed cases in Southeast Asia, surpassing Indonesia and Singapore. It ranks 9th in Asia and 22nd globally. On August 10, the Department of Health reported the highest daily increase of 6,958 new cases. Initially, the Philippines had a lower testing capacity compared to its Southeast Asian neighbors, especially during the early months of the pandemic. Testing had to be done outside the country due to a lack of testing kits. This led to controversies involving government officials undergoing tests without qualifying according to the Department of Health's guidelines. By the end of January 2020, the Research Institute for Tropical Medicine (RITM) in Muntinlupa, Metro Manila, began testing operations and became the country's first subnational laboratory. Since then, multiple laboratories have been accredited by the Department of Health. As of August 19, the country has 109 subnational laboratories capable of detecting the virus and has conducted 2,193,448 tests on over 2,051,983 unique individuals.
Cheshire is a county in England. It can also refer to:

Cardboard refers to strong paper-based products that are thicker and more durable than regular paper. These products can be foldable, rigid, and able to withstand impacts. Cardboard can be a thick sheet called paperboard or corrugated fiberboard, which consists of multiple layers. Although commonly used in English and French, the term cardboard is not precise enough for business and industry. In these fields, professionals use more specific terms.

Kalmar BTK is a table tennis club in Kalmar, Sweden. It was founded on June 14, 1960. The club won the Swedish national men's team championship in 1996, 1999, 2000, and 2002. Jan-Ove Waldner played for the club from 1996 to 2006.

Westville is a village in Georgetown Township, Vermilion County, Illinois, United States. It is part of the Danville, Illinois metropolitan area. In 2010, the population was 3,202. In 2018, it was 2,990.

Borno is a state in northeastern Nigeria. Its capital and biggest city is Maiduguri. The state was created in 1976 from a split in the northeastern region. Until 1991, it included what is now Yobe state. Borno's motto is "Home of Peace." This area is home to the Kanuri people and other groups. Borno has been where Boko Haram, an Islamist group, started their attacks in 2009. In 2009, there were clashes between Boko Haram and government forces, where Boko Haram's leader, Mohammed Yusuf, was reportedly caught. A few days later, Mohammed Yusuf was said to have died while trying to escape. After years of conflict that hurt the economy and daily life, Borno's governor, Babagana Umara Zulum, in 2019 started a plan to use 10,000 people with supposed magical abilities to help defeat the insurgents.

In the United States, a "Terry" stop lets police briefly detain someone based on a hunch they might be involved in a crime. This hunch needs to be better than just a guess but not as strong as the proof needed for an arrest. When police stop and search someone walking, it's usually called a "stop and frisk." When they stop a car, it's often a "traffic stop." If police stop a car for small driving issues but really want to look for other crimes, it's called a "pretextual stop." Police stops on a bus have extra rules. One officer stopping one person is called a "Terry" stop. But if a whole police department or city uses this a lot, it can hurt trust between police and the community and might be seen as targeting people because of their race. The Supreme Court has made many rules about how police can search people without breaking the Fourth Amendment. But Congress hasn't set basic guidelines for how police should act. Some states have made laws and rules about this, and some cities have passed their own laws. This article mostly talks about these issues at a national level. Local and state laws might differ, but that's rare.
Hartberg-Fürstenfeld is a district in Styria, Austria. It started on January 1, 2013, when the districts of Hartberg and Fürstenfeld combined.

"Frenzy" is a 1972 British thriller film directed by Alfred Hitchcock. It's his last major film in his long career. The story is based on a 1966 novel by Arthur La Bern, adapted by Anthony Shaffer. The main actors include Jon Finch, Alec McCowen, Barry Foster, Billie Whitelaw, Anna Massey, Barbara Leigh-Hunt, Bernard Cribbins, and Vivien Merchant. Ron Goodwin composed the music. The film tells the story of a serial killer in modern London and an ex-Royal Air Force (RAF) serviceman who is accused. Early in the film, there is a scene mentioning two real London serial murders: the Christie murders in the 1950s and the Jack the Ripper murders in 1888. To prepare for his role, Barry Foster studied books about Neville Heath, an English serial killer who often pretended to be an RAF officer. This was Hitchcock's third and final film shot in Britain after moving to Hollywood in 1939. The other two were "Under Capricorn" in 1949 and "Stage Fright" in 1950. Hitchcock's last film in Britain before moving to America was "Jamaica Inn" in 1939. The film was shown at the 1972 Cannes Film Festival but did not compete in the main event.

Saline, also called saline solution, is a mixture of salt and water. It is used in medicine for several purposes. When applied to the skin, it helps clean wounds, removes contact lenses, and treats dry eyes. Saline can also be given through a vein to treat dehydration, such as from gastroenteritis or diabetic ketoacidosis. It is used to mix other medications for injection. Too much saline can lead to fluid overload, swelling, acidosis, and high blood sodium. For people with low blood sodium, using too much saline may cause a problem called osmotic demyelination syndrome. Saline belongs to a group called crystalloid medications. The most common type is a 0.9% salt solution, known as normal saline, which has a slightly acidic pH. The medical use of saline began around 1831. It is considered one of the essential medicines needed in health systems and costs about $0.60 to $4.20 per liter in developing countries. In the U.S., sodium, which is used to make saline, was the 225th most commonly prescribed medication in 2017, with over two million prescriptions.

Inversnaid, in Scottish Gaelic "inbhir snàthaid," is a small rural community on the east side of Loch Lomond in Scotland. It's near the northern end of the loch. Inversnaid has a pier and a hotel. The West Highland Way passes through the area. There is a small passenger ferry that goes from Inversnaid to Inveruglas and Tarbet. Another seasonal ferry connects Ardlui and Ardleish, which are close to Inversnaid. To get to Inversnaid by car, you need to drive from Aberfoyle. Nearby, there is a cave called Rob Roy's Cave, which is said to be where Rob Roy MacGregor hid. The cave is hard to reach, but you can see the location marked with white paint on Loch Lomond.

Oona Castilla Chaplin, born on June 4, 1986, is a Spanish-British actress. She played Talisa Maegyr in the HBO series "Game of Thrones." In "The Crimson Field," she acted as Kitty Trevelyan. In "Taboo," she played Zilpha Geary. Oona is part of the Chaplin family. She is the daughter of actress Geraldine Chaplin and the granddaughter of filmmaker and actor Charlie Chaplin. She is also the great-granddaughter of American playwright Eugene O'Neill. Oona was named after her maternal grandmother, Oona O'Neill, who was Charlie Chaplin's wife.

Andry Nirina Rajoelina, born on May 30, 1974, is a Malagasy politician and businessman. He is currently the president of Madagascar. His career began in the private sector. He first organized events on the island, like live concerts. Then, he invested in advertising businesses such as Injet, billboards, and print. He also worked in media, including Viva TV and radio. Rajoelina was the mayor of Antananarivo from December 2007 to February 2009. From March 21, 2009, to January 25, 2014, he served as the president of the High Transitional Authority of Madagascar until the 2013 general elections. After leaving this position, he stayed as the head of the majority party, Mapar. He won the 2018 presidential election and was inaugurated as president on January 19, 2019.
René Angélil was a Canadian who made music, managed talent, and sang. He worked as Céline Dion's manager from 1981 to 2014 and was her husband from 1994 until his death in 2016.

Alfred Pleasonton was born on July 7, 1824, and died on February 17, 1897. He was an officer in the United States Army and a major general of volunteers in the Union cavalry during the American Civil War. He led the cavalry corps of the Army of the Potomac during the Gettysburg Campaign. This campaign included the Battle of Brandy Station, the largest cavalry battle of the war. In 1864, he moved to the Trans-Mississippi Theater. There, he defeated Confederate General Sterling Price in two important battles, including the Battle of Mine Creek, which was the second largest cavalry battle of the war. This victory helped end the war in Missouri. Alfred Pleasonton was the son of Stephen Pleasonton and the younger brother of Augustus Pleasonton.

The Metre Convention, also called the Treaty of the Metre, is an international agreement signed on May 20, 1875, in Paris. It was signed by representatives from 17 countries: Argentina, Austria-Hungary, Belgium, Brazil, Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, Peru, Portugal, Russia, Spain, Sweden and Norway, Switzerland, the Ottoman Empire, the United States, and Venezuela. This treaty created the International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM), an organization managed by the General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM) and overseen by the International Committee for Weights and Measures (CI蓬M). The BIPM helps with international measurement standards and the metric system. The convention also set rules for funding and managing the BIPM. The BIPM has three main parts. Only countries can join the convention. In 1999, the CGPM created a new status called Associate of the CGPM. This allows states and economic entities to join through their national metrology institutes (NMIs). Countries that don't pay membership fees can be removed from the agreement. Initially, the Metre Convention only dealt with mass and length. In 1921, at the 6th CGPM meeting, it was expanded to cover more areas of physics. In 1960, at the 11th CGPM meeting, the system of units it created was named the International System of Units (SI).

The king's gambit is a chess opening where White gives up a pawn to move the black pawn on e-file. If Black accepts, White has two main plans. One is to play d4 and bxf4, taking back the pawn and controlling the center. The other is nf3 and bc4, followed by 0-0. This creates an open file on f, allowing White to attack Black's pawn on f7. To keep the gambit pawn, Black might need to play moves like...g5 or put pieces in strange positions. A downside is that White's king becomes weaker and more exposed to checks like...qh4+. With a Black pawn on f4, White can't respond with g3 to avoid the check. If Black's king must move, White can't castle. The king's gambit is an old opening, first studied by Italian player Giulio Cesare Polero in the 17th century. It appeared in Luis Ramirez de Lucena's "Repetición de Amores y Arte de Ajedrez" from 1497. This gambit was popular until the late 19th century but is now rarely seen at high levels. Black has good defenses, but it's still popular among amateurs.

In military tactics, a strongpoint is a crucial area in a defense system. It helps hold a line and is usually made of structures like redoubts, bunkers, or trenches. The main idea is that it should be hard to take over and cannot be easily avoided. A good choice is a blocking position on high ground that controls key paths, like a hill. Examples from history include Thermopylae, where ancient Greeks stopped a much bigger Persian army, and Monte Cassino, which was important in the Winter Line during World War II.

A hedgehog is a spiny mammal in the family Erinaceidae. There are 17 species of hedgehogs in five groups, found in parts of Europe, Asia, Africa, and New Zealand. There are no native hedgehogs in Australia or the Americas, although there used to be some in North America. Hedgehogs are related to shrews and possibly to gymnures. They have not changed much over the past 15 million years and live mostly at night. Their spines are similar to those of porcupines and echidnas.

Kembangan MRT station is an above-ground train station on the East West Line in Bedok, Singapore. It is located where Sims Ave East meets Jalan Kembangan. Part of the station is built above the Siglap Canal. The station's name means "expansion" in Malay.

The Industrial and Mining Water Research Unit (IMWARU) is part of the School of Chemical and Metallurgical Engineering at the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg. It does research and helps supervise master’s and doctorate students. It also offers advice to businesses.

Madison County is in Arkansas, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 15, 717 people. The county seat is Huntsville. Madison County was created on September 30, 1836. It was named after James Madison, the fourth president of the United States. Madison County is part of Northwest Arkansas.

Mary Fallin, born on December 9, 1954, is an American politician. She was the 27th governor of Oklahoma from 2011 to 2019. A Republican, Fallin was elected governor in 2010 and re-elected in 2014. Fallin began her political career by being elected to the Oklahoma House of Representatives in 1990. She served there until 1995. In 1994, she was elected as Oklahoma's 14th Lieutenant Governor and served for two terms until 2007, working with two different governors. In 2007, Fallin was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives for Oklahoma's 5th congressional district, serving from 2007 to 2011. She was elected twice. In 2010, Fallin ran for governor. She won the Republican primary with 54% of the votes and the general election with 60% against the Democratic nominee, Lieutenant Governor Jari Askins. She was re-elected in 2014 against Oklahoma State Representative Joe Dorman. Fallin's time as governor was difficult. She faced many controversies, accusations of being hypocritical, and claims of overstepping her authority. In October 2018, a Morning Consult poll showed her approval rating at 17%, the lowest among all governors. She could not seek a third term due to term limits, and Kevin Stitt became the new governor.

In algebra, a nested radical is a square root or other root that contains another root expression. For example, a nested radical like appears in studying a regular pentagon. More complex examples exist as well.

"Baby, Don't Forget My Number" is a song by the German dance-pop group Milli Vanilli. It came out in December 1988 as the second single from their album "Girl You Know It's True." In 1989, it became their first number one hit on the Billboard Hot 100 chart. In 1992, Weird Al Yankovic made fun of this song and another one, "Blame It on the Rain," by creating "The Plumbing Song" for his album "Off the Deep End." The single was also certified gold in the USA by the RIAA.

Echinoderm is a term used for any animal in the phylum Echinodermata, which comes from the Greek words "echinos" meaning "hedgehog" and "derma" meaning "skin." These animals are mostly found in the ocean and have a five-part symmetrical body. Some examples include starfish, sea urchins, sand dollars, and sea cucumbers. There are about 7,000 living species of echinoderms, making them the second-largest group of deuterostomes after chordates, which include animals like birds, fish, mammals, and reptiles. Unlike some other groups, echinoderms do not have any freshwater or land-based representatives. The first clear examples of these animals appeared at the beginning of the Cambrian period. Some Cambrian echinoderms, like the cinctans, had external gills for filtering food, similar to those found in other animals. Echinoderms are important for their abundance in the deep sea and for their ability to reproduce and regrow body parts. Their hard skeletons are also crucial in the formation of limestone and provide clues about the geological environment. In the 19th and 20th centuries, echinoderms were widely used in scientific studies of regeneration. Some scientists believe their development was key to the Mesozoic Marine Revolution.

Ahattat Atun was a former prime minister of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus. He was prime minister from 1994 to 1996. Born in 1935 in Famagusta, he studied engineering at Istanbul Technical University in 1959. He also studied urban planning in Manchester and Nottingham. From 1961 to 1975, Atun held several public jobs. In 1963, he was the regional director of Limassol-Paphos planning. By 1975, he was the undersecretary of housing. Atun became an MP in 1976, 1981, 1985, and 1990, representing the National Unity Party. He served in various ministries, including settlement and rehabilitation, economy and finance, and national education. He was also the secretary general of the National Unity Party. In 1983, Atun joined the Constituent Assembly and became the minister of settlement in the first republican government. From 1985 to 1993, he was the speaker of the Assembly of the Republic. In 1992, he became the president of the Democratic Party. He was elected to parliament in 1993 and was prime minister until August 1996. In 1996, he was again elected as the speaker. Later, he did not participate in parliament. He is the honorary president of the Democratic Party. He speaks English and some Greek. He is married with two children. He is the nephew of Derviş Eroğlu, the third president of TRNC.

Scorpion is Drake's fifth album. It came out on June 29, 2018. Drake made it with his own company and two others. Scorpion is two albums combined, with 25 songs. The first part is mainly hip hop, while the second has R&B and pop songs. Drake produced the album himself, with help from a friend named 40 and his manager. It has guest artists like Jay-Z and Ty Dolla Sign, and some singers who died, like Michael Jackson and Static Major. Drake sings about fame, relationships, and his success in the album. The music has sounds from soul, R&B, pop, and other genres. Seven singles came from the album: "God's Plan," "Nice for What," "I'm Upset," "Don't Matter to Me," "In My Feelings," "Nonstop," and "Mob Ties." All reached the top 20 on the Billboard Hot 100, with three at number one. Scorpion broke records on Spotify and Apple Music on its first day. It sold 732,000 units in the US, with 160,000 from regular sales. As of January 2019, it was five times platinum. Scorpion got five Grammy nominations, won Best Rap Song for "God's Plan," and helped Drake win the Top Billboard 200 Album at the 2019 Billboard Music Awards.

Exology Chapter 1: The Lost Planet is the first live album by the South Korean-Chinese boy band EXO. It came out on December 22, 2014, from SM Entertainment. The album has two CDs with 36 songs in total (18 songs on each CD). It includes individual songs from each member and remixes of some of their songs in both Korean and Mandarin. The album was released in both a normal version and a special version.

An ofrenda is a collection of objects placed on a ritual display during the annual and traditional Mexican "Día de Muertos" celebration. An ofrenda can be large and fancy. It is usually created for someone who has died and is meant to welcome them to the altar.
Chidester is a city in Ouachita County, Arkansas, United States. In 2000, it had 335 people. It is part of the Camden micropolitan area.
The weather is getting warmer. People are starting to wear lighter clothes. Birds are building nests. Trees are growing new leaves.

Guatemala is one of 22 departments in the country. The capital is Guatemala City, which is also the national capital. This department includes Guatemala City and some nearby suburbs. It covers an area of several thousand square kilometers and had about 3 million people living there in 2018.
Hardancourt is a commune in the Vosges department, which is in the Grand Est region of northeastern France.

William Grant "Bill" Moggridge, who was born on June 25, 1943, and passed away on September 8, 2012, was a British designer, writer, and teacher. He co-founded a design company called ideo. He also worked as the director of the Cooper-Hewitt, National Design Museum in New York. Moggridge was a leader in focusing on people when designing products. He is known for creating the term "interaction design." He designed the first laptop computer, called the Grid Compass. Moggridge received awards for his life's work, including the National Design Award and the Prince Philip Designer Prize. He once said, "The main idea behind everything I've done is my love for people and how they use things."

Lady Susan is a short novel by Jane Austen. It was likely written in 1794 but not published until 1871. This early complete work was never sent to be published by the author. The story is about the schemes of the title character.

The Vickers Viscount is a British medium-range airliner. It first flew in 1948. Vickers-Armstrongs designed it based on a requirement from the Brabazon Committee. Service began in 1953, and it was the first airliner with a turboprop engine. Passengers liked the Viscount because of its good cabin conditions, including pressurization, reduced vibrations and noise, and large windows. Many were built, and it was one of the most successful post-war transport aircraft. A total of 445 Viscounts were made for customers in different countries, including some in North America.

The Blossoms are an American girl group from California. In the 1960s, they were most known for Darlene Love, Fanita James, and Jean King. Although they recorded songs on their own, they are best remembered for singing backing vocals on many top hits of that time. They also recorded the hit song "He's a Rebel," which was credited to The Crystals by producer Phil Spector. The Blossoms were like the Sweet Inspirations on the West Coast and the Andantes for Motown.

TESOL International Association, formerly known as Teachers of English to Speakers of Other Languages, is the largest organization for teachers of English as a second or foreign language. It was founded in 1966 and is based in Alexandria, Virginia, United States. In 2018, it had 10,113 members worldwide and was affiliated with 109 language education organizations, most of which were outside the United States. TESOL has around 44,000 members in total, including members from affiliated organizations. The organization publishes two academic journals: "TESOL Quarterly" and "TESOL Journal". During the summer, TESOL holds professional development seminars called "TESOL Academies" across the United States. It also organizes an annual convention.

Neptune Beach is a beach city in Duval County, Florida, east of Jacksonville. In 1968, most communities in Duval County joined Jacksonville. However, Neptune Beach, along with Jacksonville Beach, Atlantic Beach, and Baldwin, stayed almost independent. These towns have their own government. Even so, the people of these towns vote for the mayor of Jacksonville and are represented on the Jacksonville city council. The town had 7,037 people in 2010. Neptune Beach is part of the Jacksonville beaches area.

The Plymouth Fury was a car made by Plymouth from 1955 to 1989. It first came out in 1956 as part of the Belvedere series, but became its own separate model in 1959. The Fury was a full-size car from 1959 to 1961. Then, it became a mid-size car from 1962 to 1964. It was again a full-size car from 1965 to 1974 and a mid-size car from 1975 to 1978. From 1975 to 1977, the Fury was sold together with the Gran Fury, which was a full-size car. In 1978, the Fury was the largest Plymouth. In 1979, there were no large Plymouths. To fix this, in 1980, the Gran Fury returned with the R-body. In 1982, the M-body Fury was introduced. Production of the last V8, rear-wheel-drive Plymouth Fury ended in Kenosha, Wisconsin, on December 23, 1988. Unlike its sister brand, Dodge, Plymouth did not survive the revival of large, V8/rwd sedans. The last Plymouth car was made in 2001.

Franzobel is the pen name of Austrian writer Franz Stefan Griebl. He was born on March 1, 1967, in Vöcklabruck. In 1997, he won the Wolfgang Weyrauch Prize. In 1998, he got the Kassel Literary Prize. He has received many other literary awards. In 2017, he won the Nicolas Born Prize and was a finalist for the German Book Prize for his novel "Das Floß der Medusa." Now he lives in Vienna.

County Westmeath is a county in Ireland. It is in the province of Leinster and part of the Midlands region. It used to be part of a kingdom called Meath, which meant "middle" because it was in the center of Ireland. Westmeath is run by a council, and the main town is Mullingar. In 2016, there were 88,770 people living in the county.

Graves' disease, also called toxic diffuse goiter, is an autoimmune condition affecting the thyroid. It often leads to hyperthyroidism, which means the thyroid makes too much hormone. This can cause the thyroid to become larger. Symptoms of hyperthyroidism might include feeling irritable, having weak muscles, sleeping problems, a rapid heartbeat, difficulty with heat, loose stools, and unintentional weight loss. Some people may also have thickened skin on their shins and bulging eyes due to Graves' ophthalmopathy. About 25 to 80 percent of those with the disease develop eye problems. The exact cause isn't clear but it seems to involve both genes and environmental factors. If someone in your family has the disease, you're more likely to get it. If one twin has it, there's a 30 percent chance the other twin will too. Stress, infections, giving birth, and other autoimmune conditions like type 1 diabetes or rheumatoid arthritis can trigger the disease. Smoking can increase the risk and make eye problems worse. The disease happens when the body makes antibodies that mimic thyroid-stimulating hormone, causing the thyroid to produce too much hormone. This can be diagnosed through symptoms, blood tests, and radioactive iodine uptake. Blood tests usually show high levels of thyroid hormones and low thyroid-stimulating hormone, with increased uptake in the thyroid and antibodies. Treatment options include radioiodine therapy, medications, and surgery. Radioiodine therapy involves taking iodine-131, which destroys part of the thyroid over several weeks to months. This can lead to hypothyroidism, treated with thyroid hormones. Medications can help control symptoms, while antithyroid drugs like methimazole can provide temporary relief. Surgery can remove the thyroid gland. Eye problems often need extra treatment. Graves' disease affects about 0.5 percent of men and 3 percent of women, with women four times more likely to be affected. It usually starts between ages 40 and 60 but can occur at any age. It's the leading cause of hyperthyroidism in the U.S., accounting for about 50 to 80 percent of cases. The disease is named after Irish surgeon Robert Graves, who first described it in 1835. Earlier descriptions also exist.
