Earl Wilbur Sutherland Jr. was born on November 19, 1915, in Burlingame, Kansas. He was an American pharmacologist and biochemist. In 1971, Sutherland won a Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. He was honored for discovering how hormones, like epinephrine, work through second messengers, specifically cyclic AMP.
Gevelsberg is a town in Ennepe-Ruhr-Kreis district, in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.

Francisco Waldir Pires de Souza was a Brazilian politician born on October 21, 1926, and died on June 22, 2018. He worked as the Minister of Defence under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. However, he was fired because of his poor performance and inaction during Brazil's aviation crisis in 2006–2007. Some people in Brazil thought he was getting senile. After he was fired, Nelson Jobim, who was previously the president of the Supreme Court, took his place. During this time, Souza was also in charge of Brazil's mission in Haiti as part of MINUSTAH. This mission caused chaos in the country after the president, Jean-Bertrand Aristide, was removed by a rogue police chief.

Patrick James Riley, born on March 20, 1945, is an American basketball executive. He used to be a coach and player in the NBA. Riley has been the Miami Heat's team president since 1995. He coached the Heat from 1995 to 2003 and again from 2005 to 2008. As a player, Riley was part of the Lakers' championship team in 1972. He is considered one of the best NBA coaches. Riley led five championship teams, including four with the Los Angeles Lakers during their successful period in the 1980s, and one with the Heat in 2006. He won Coach of the Year three times, as head coach of the Lakers, New York Knicks, and Heat. Riley was the head coach of the NBA All-Star game team nine times, mostly for the Western Conference. He is the first North American sports figure to win championships as a player, assistant coach, head coach, and executive. Riley was named one of the 10 greatest coaches in NBA history in 1996. He won the 2012 and 2013 NBA championships as the Heat's team president. In 2012, Riley received the Chuck Daly Lifetime Achievement Award from the NBA coaches association.

Bloomsburg is a town in Columbia County, Pennsylvania, United States. It is southwest of Wilkes-Barre and located near the Susquehanna River. Bloomsburg is the county seat of Columbia County and the only Pennsylvania town called a "town." In 2010, the town had about 14,855 people, and in 2019, the population was around 13,811. Bloomsburg is part of the Bloomsburg-Berwick, PA micropolitan area, which also includes Montour County. This area had a total population of 85,562 in the 2010 census.
Walala TJapaltjarri (born Walala TJapangati) is an Australian Aboriginal artist.

The United States has many types of laws, with the most important being the Constitution. The Constitution forms the basis of the federal government and protects civil liberties. Federal laws include acts of Congress, treaties, regulations, and court decisions. The United States Code contains permanent federal laws. Federal laws and treaties, as long as they follow the Constitution, can override state laws in the 50 states and territories. However, the federal government's power is limited, and states can make different laws as long as they do not violate the Constitution. Most laws that affect everyday citizens, like those related to contracts, torts, property, criminal matters, and families, are state laws. Federal and state laws are mostly based on the common law system from English law, used when the American Revolutionary War began. American law has changed a lot from its English roots in both rules and procedures, and has also added some new ideas from civil law.

Meresankh I, who loved life, was an ancient Egyptian king's wife and the mother of King Sneferu. She might have been married to King Huni, the last king of the 3rd dynasty. Her name appears on a fragment of the Palermo Stone, and an estate of hers may be mentioned in the tomb of Pehernefer in Saqqara. She and her son Sneferu are named in graffiti found in the Pyramid Temple at Meidum. This graffiti dates back to the time of Tuthmosis III from the 18th dynasty. The text there says a "hetep di nesu" for King Sneferu and Queen Meresankh.

Gerald Göttig was a German politician. He led the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) in East Germany from 1966 to 1989. Göttig was the president of the People's Chamber from 1969 to 1976. He also worked as the deputy chairman of the State Council of East Germany from 1960 to 1989. He was born on June 9, 1923, and died on May 19, 2015.

In economics, a free market is a system where prices for goods and services are set by the open market and consumers. In a free market, the government and other authorities don't intervene, and there are no special economic advantages or monopolies. Those who support the idea of a free market see it as different from a regulated market where governments use methods like tariffs to protect their own economy. In an ideal free-market system, prices are determined by supply and demand, and the government doesn't interfere. Experts compare free markets to coordinated markets, studying them in areas like political economy, new institutional economics, economic sociology, and political science. These fields highlight the role of external rule-making institutions in current market systems, giving space for supply and demand to work. While free markets are often linked to capitalism, they have also been supported by anarchists, socialists, and some cooperative advocates. Critics of the free market theory argue that significant market power, unequal bargaining power, or information asymmetry make markets less free. They believe that regulation is necessary to balance these issues and help markets work better and achieve more desirable social outcomes.

Lipscomb County is in Texas, United States. In 2010, it had 3,302 people. The county seat is Lipscomb. It was created in 1876 and organized in 1887. The county is named after Judge Abner Smith Lipscomb, who was the secretary of state of the Republic of Texas.
Didier Bezace was a French actor. He was born on February 10, 1946, and died on March 11, 2020.

Nadap is a village in Fejér county, central Hungary. It has 460 people living there. The village is surrounded by low hills. It starts tours of the countryside. There is a tall stone called "Ancient Mark of Nadap" nearby, at 173. 8 meters high. This stone helps as a reference point. Mihály Vörösmarty, a famous writer, was baptized in the church of Saint Rosalia in Nadap. The baptismal font is still kept in the church.

Surya Bahadur Thapa, born on March 21, 1928, and died on April 15, 2015, was Nepal's only five-time prime minister. He served under three different kings over a career lasting more than 50 years. In 1955, he began his career as a temporary prime minister for four days but became well-known later. In 1959, he was elected to the upper house. From 1963 to 1964, he was the leader of the council. He went on to serve as prime minister four more times: 1965 to 1969, 1979 to 1983, 1997 to 1998, and in 2003. In November 2004, he left his Rastriya Prajatantra party and became the leader of the Rastriya Janashakti party. He died from breathing problems during surgery.

A mast cell, also called a mastocyte or labrocyte, is a type of cell in connective tissue. It has lots of granules filled with histamine and heparin. Mast cells come from myeloid stem cells and are part of the immune and neuroimmune systems. They were first discovered by Paul Ehrlich in 1877. Mast cells are important for both protection and healing. They help in healing wounds, growing new blood vessels, and keeping the blood-brain barrier healthy. While best known for their role in allergies and anaphylaxis, they also protect the body against harmful invaders. Mast cells look and act a lot like basophils, another kind of white blood cell. However, they do not come from the same source as basophils, so they are not the same cells.

Amanda Michelle Seyfried, born on December 3, 1985, is an American actress, singer, and model. She grew up in Allentown, Pennsylvania. Seyfried started modeling when she was 11 and acting at 15. She had roles as Lucy Montgomery in "As the World Turns" (1999-2001) and as Joni Stafford in "All My Children" (2003). Her first big role was in the movie "Mean Girls" (2004). She also starred in "Veronica Mars" (2004-2006). Seyfried then had parts in films like "Nine Lives" (2005), "Alpha Dog" (2006), and "Big Love" (2006-2011). She later got more main roles, such as in "Mamma Mia!" (2008), "Solstice" (2008), "Jennifer's Body" (2009), "Chloe" (2009), "Dear John" (2010), "Letters to Juliet" (2010), "Red Riding Hood" (2011), "In Time" (2011), "Les Misérables" (2012), "Gone" (2012), "Lovelace" (2013), "The Big Wedding" (2013), and more. She also did voice work in movies like "Epic" (2013) and "Scoob!" (2020).
Ellen Marie Elze Anthing Vogel was a Dutch actress. She lived from January 26, 1922, to August 5, 2015. She acted in films, on stages, and on television.

The question mark is a punctuation mark used to show a question. It is also called an interrogation point, query, or eroteme in journalism. This mark is used for direct questions, not indirect ones. Sometimes, it is used to represent missing or unknown information. In Unicode, it is encoded there.
In the politics and government of the United States, the term "presidential nominee" has two different meanings.

Alois Hitler Sr., born Alois Schicklgruber, was born in 1837 and died in 1903. He was an Austrian civil servant and the father of Adolf Hitler, who later became the dictator of Nazi Germany. Alois was born without a father's name. His parentage was never confirmed, leading some to say he might have been related to his mother, Klara, who was Adolf's mother. Because of this, Adolf could not prove his family background and his "Aryan descent." Later, Alois got a job promotion and changed his last name to Hitler, using his stepfather's name. No one knows why he did this. Alois and Adolf had a bad relationship. Alois often punished Adolf severely.

Rock of Ages Corporation is a granite quarrying and finishing company in Graniteville, Vermont. It started in 1885. The company has about 230 workers. In 2009, they made about $800,000 in profit from sales of $21.6 million. That was an improvement from losing over $2 million in 2008. In October 2010, Swenson Granite in New Hampshire agreed to merge with Rock of Ages. Swenson paid Rock of Ages' shareholders $39 million. On September 16, 2016, Polycor Inc. in Quebec, Canada, bought Swenson Granite and Rock of Ages. This made Polycor the largest producer of marble and granite in North America. They also took over Rock of Ages' division in Stanstead, Quebec. Rock of Ages runs the world's largest "deep hole" granite quarry, called the E.L. Smith Quarry. They mine Devonian Barre granite there. Initially, they used simple tools like hand saws and explosives. Today, they use more advanced methods like diamond-tipped wire saws and water jets. Visitors can watch workers cutting granite at the quarry. Rock of Ages also has a factory and gift shop. The company was featured in a 2005 PBS documentary called "A Cemetery Special" that highlighted cemetery-related businesses.

The mighty Bosstones, often called the Bosstones, are an American ska punk band from Boston, Massachusetts. They started in 1983. Since then, the band has had the same main members: lead singer Dicky Barrett, bassist Joe Gittleman, tenor saxophonist Tim Burton, and dancer Ben Carr. Other members include drummer Joe Sirois, saxophonist Leon Silva, guitarist Lawrence Katz, keyboardist John Goetchius, and trombonist Chris Rhodes. The Bosstones are known as pioneers of ska punk and creators of ska-core, a mix of ska with punk and hardcore. Their first album, "Devil's Night Out," came out in 1989. Throughout the 1990s, they toured and recorded a lot, helping make ska punk popular. Their biggest hit was "The Impression That I Get" from their 1997 album "Let's Face It." By December 2003, they had released seven studio albums, three EPs, and a live album before taking a break. In 2007, the band reunited and have since made three more studio albums. From 1994 to 2002, and again since 2007, they host an annual music festival called the Hometown Throwdown in Boston around Christmas.

The Regional Representative Council, or DPD, is one of two parts of Indonesia's parliament. Along with the DPR, or Dewan Perwakilan Rakyat, it makes up the national legislative body known as the MPR. According to Indonesia's constitution, the DPD focuses on regional issues and can suggest bills to the DPR but does not have the power to make laws directly. Members of the DPD are often referred to as senators.
An antacid is a substance that makes your stomach less acidic. It helps to ease heartburn, indigestion, or an upset stomach.

Taiwan, officially known as the Republic of China (ROC), is a country in East Asia. It borders the People's Republic of China (PRC) to the northwest, Japan to the northeast, and the Philippines to the south. The main island of Taiwan is large, with mountain ranges covering the eastern two-thirds and plains in the western third where most people live. Taipei is the capital and largest city, with other major cities including New Taipei, Kaohsiung, Taichung, Tainan, and Taoyuan. Taiwan has 23.7 million people, making it one of the most crowded countries. It is also the most populous and largest economy among countries not in the United Nations. People from indigenous groups lived in Taiwan about 6,000 years ago. In the 17th century, Dutch people started to colonize the island and Han Chinese began moving there. In 1683, the island was taken by the Qing dynasty of China and later given to Japan in 1895. After Japan's defeat in World War II in 1945, the Republic of China, which had replaced the Qing dynasty in 1911, took control of Taiwan. In 1949, the ROC government moved to Taiwan after losing control of mainland China to the Communist Party of China. Since 1950, the ROC has controlled Taiwan and some smaller islands. In the 1960s, Taiwan's economy grew quickly, becoming one of the world's 21 largest economies, with industries like steel, machinery, electronics, and chemicals. Taiwan is a developed country, with high levels of education and health care, and a strong economy. Taiwan's status remains unclear. The ROC is not a UN member and is recognized by only 14 out of 193 UN member states. The PRC claims Taiwan and refuses diplomatic relations with countries recognizing the ROC. Taiwan has unofficial ties with some countries through representative offices. Domestically, the main political debate is between those who support eventual Chinese reunification and those who promote Taiwanese independence.
Aulnois-sous-Laon is a village in the Aisne department, which is in Hauts-de-France, a region in northern France. People who live there are called Aulnoisiens or Aulnoisiennes.

Jacques Houplain was a French painter and engraver. He was born on September 10, 1920, and died on February 22, 2020.

Mahākāla is a deity in Hinduism, Buddhism, and Sikhism. In Hinduism, Mahākāla is a form of Shiva and the husband of Mahākālī. He is mainly found in the Shaktism sect. In Vajrayana Buddhism, especially in Tibetan traditions, he is known as Citipati. He is also a protector in Chinese and Japanese Buddhism. In Chinese, he is called "大黑天" (dàhēitiān), in Cantonese "daaih'hāktīn", in Korean "대흑천" (daeheukcheon), in Vietnamese "đại hắc thiên", and in Japanese "大黒天" (daikokuten). In Sikhism, Mahākāla is known as Kal, who controls Maya.

The Gulf of Gonâve is a large part of the Caribbean Sea near Haiti. Haiti's main city, Port-au-Prince, is on the Gulf's coast. Other cities on the coast include Gonaïves, Saint-Marc, Miragoâne, and Jérémie. There are also several islands in the Gulf. The largest is Gonâve Island, with Cayemites being much smaller.

Fillmore is a small city in Ventura County, California. It is in the Santa Clara River Valley. Fillmore is in an agricultural area with rich, fertile soil. The city has a historic downtown. The town was named after J. A. Fillmore, who was a general superintendent for the Southern Pacific Company. The railroad was built through the valley in 1887. The population grew from 13,643 in 2000 to 15,002 in 2010.

Ivy Queen, born Martha Ivelisse Pesante Rodríguez on March 4, 1972, is a Puerto Rican singer, songwriter, rapper, actress, and record producer. She gained attention as part of the Noise group in Puerto Rico, performing their first song "Somos Raperos Pero No Delincuentes" (We Are Rappers, Not Delinquents). In 1996, she went solo and released her first album "En Mi Imperio (In My Empire)," which Sony Discos later distributed in 1997. Her second album "The Original Rude Girl" came out in 1998, with the hit single "In the Zone." However, she became famous after moving to an independent label for her third album "Diva" in 2003. Her albums "Diva," "Flashback," and "Sentimiento" were all certified gold and platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America. In 2010, she released "Drama Queen," which had a top ten single "La Vida Es Así." Her album "Musa" in 2012 was nominated for a Grammy. Ivy Queen's music often talks about empowering women and relationships. She is known as the queen of reggaeton. She has also acted in plays and created a doll based on her appearance. In 2012, she appeared in Eve Ensler's play "The Vagina Monologues." In 2017, she was one of the wealthiest reggaeton artists with a net worth of $10 million.

In mathematics, a real number is a value that can show a distance on a line or be shown as an endless decimal. The term "real" was first used in the 17th century by René Descartes to distinguish between real and imaginary numbers. Real numbers include rational numbers, like -5 and 4/3, and irrational numbers, like the square root of 2. Transcendental numbers, such as pi (3.14159265...), are also real numbers. Real numbers can measure various things, like time, weight, and speed. They can be seen as points on an endless number line. Each real number can be written as an endless decimal, like 8.632, where each digit is ten times smaller than the one before it. Real numbers are part of complex numbers and can be seen as a part of the complex plane. These descriptions of real numbers are not fully precise according to modern math. Defining real numbers correctly was a significant development in 19th-century math. Today, real numbers are seen as the only ordered field that is Dedekind-complete, up to an isomorphism. They can also be defined as equivalence classes of Cauchy sequences of rational numbers, Dedekind cuts, or infinite decimals, with precise rules for operations and order. The set of real numbers is uncountable, meaning there's no way to match each real number with a natural number one-to-one. The size of the set of real numbers is denoted by $\mathfrak{c}$, while the size of natural numbers is $\aleph_0$. The Continuum Hypothesis states that there is no set whose size is strictly between that of the natural numbers and the real numbers. It is neither provable nor refutable using the standard rules of math. Some math models accept the Continuum Hypothesis, while others do not.

This list shows the presidents of Djibouti. Since 1977, there have been two presidents. The president is in charge of the country, leads the government, and is in command of Djibouti's armed forces. The current president is Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, since 1999.

Affoltern district, also called Knonaueramt or Säuliamt, is one of the twelve districts in the German-speaking part of the canton of Zurich, Switzerland. The capital of this district is the city of Affoltern am Albis.

The Co-operative Party is a center-left political party in the United Kingdom that supports co-operative values. It was founded in 1917 by co-operative societies to campaign for fair treatment of co-operative businesses and to elect 'co-operators' to Parliament. Its roots go back to an 1881 parliamentary committee of the Co-operative Union. Since 1927, the Co-operative Party has had a pact with the Labour Party, where they agree not to run against each other. Instead, candidates from both parties use the 'Labour and Co-operative Party' description when contesting elections. The Co-operative Party is a separate legal entity from the Labour Party and is registered with the Electoral Commission. Members of the Co-operative Party cannot belong to any other UK political party except the Labour Party or Northern Ireland's Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP). The Co-operative Party has 26 Members of Parliament, making it one of the larger parties in the House of Commons. It also has representatives in the House of Lords, the Scottish Parliament, the Senedd, the London Assembly, and local government. Although its MPs are part of the Parliamentary Labour Party, they are still considered a separate group. The party does not have a leader. Instead, Joe Fortune serves as the general secretary, and Jim McMahon is the chair of the Co-operative Party group in Parliament.
Rickenbach is the name of several places. In Germany, there is none. In Switzerland, there are some.

Jessie Lawrence Ferguson was an American actor. He lived from June 8, 1941, to April 26, 2019. He is most famous for his role as a police officer who was very hard on himself in the movie "Boyz n the Hood," which was directed by John Singleton and was nominated for an Academy Award.
ebnat-kappel is a municipality in Toggenburg, which is a constituency in the canton of St. Gallen, Switzerland.

The movie "Riding in Cars with Boys" is a 2001 American film. It is based on the autobiography by Beverly Donofrio. The story is about a woman who overcame challenges, including being a teen mother, and later earned a master's degree. The film covers the years 1961 to 1986. It stars Drew Barrymore, Steve Zahn, Brittany Murphy, and James Woods. It was the last film directed by Penny Marshall. While Beverly Donofrio co-produced the movie, many of its details differ from the book.

Dargai is an administrative area in the Malakand District of Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. Another area is Batkhela. Dargai is on the main highway from Peshawar to Swat, Dir, and Chitral. It's known as a trade center between the upper regions of Pakistan and the lower regions of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The town is important for selling timber and is also the last train station into northern Pakistan. Dargai was part of the Malakand Agency Tribal Area until 1970. That year, Chitral, Dir, and Swat were joined to form the Malakand Division. This division was divided into districts, including the Malakand Protected Area, which is now known as Malakand District. In 2000, the Malakand Division was abolished. Despite changes in the constitution since 1970, the term "Malakand Agency" is sometimes still used to refer to the entire area.

A gravitational singularity is a point in space where gravity becomes extremely strong. This happens because the density of matter is very high, making measurements of the gravitational field infinite. These singularities are mainly studied in the context of black holes and the beginning of the universe. In a black hole, a singularity is hidden by an event horizon, and general relativity suggests that all matter inside this point has infinite density. The Penrose-Hawking singularity theorems say that singularities occur when paths of particles (geodesics) can't be extended smoothly. The end of these paths is considered the singularity. At the start of the big bang, the universe itself is thought to have been a singularity. However, the big bang involved expanding space, unlike the collapse of a star into a black hole, so the rules that apply to black holes may not fully describe the early universe. Current theories in physics, like general relativity and quantum mechanics, can't precisely describe what happened during the very first moments of the big bang. Quantum mechanics suggests that particles can't exist in spaces smaller than their wavelengths.

Mirosława Litmanowicz, born Kałęcka on September 6, 1928, and passed away on August 18, 2017, was a Polish chess player. She won the Polish women's chess championship in 1968. She became a FIDE Woman International Master in 1967.

Throckmorton County is in Texas, United States. In 2010, it had 1,641 people. The county seat is Throckmorton. It became a county in 1858 and was organized in 1879. It is named after William Throckmorton, who was an early settler in Collin County. Throckmorton County is one of six dry counties in Texas.

Dmitry Vladimirovich Strakhov, born on May 17, 1995, is a Russian professional racing cyclist. He rides for a UCI team. In 2017, he competed in a point race at the UCI Track Cycling World Championships. In May 2019, he was listed to start in the 2019 Giro d'Italia. On March 11, 2020, it was reported that Strakhov had been infected with the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which causes COVID-19. He was hospitalized in an Abu Dhabi hospital after being placed in quarantine following the 2020 UAE Tour.

The Limbourg brothers, Herman, Paul, and Johan, were famous Dutch miniature painters who lived around 1385 to 1416. They came from Nijmegen. In the early 15th century, they worked in France and Burgundy. Their art style was called International Gothic. They are most well-known for creating the "Très Riches Heures du Duc de Berry," which is a famous late medieval illuminated manuscript.

A hypodermic needle is a thin, hollow tube with a sharp tip, used to inject or draw fluids. It is part of a group of tools called sharps, used to enter the skin. The needle is often used with a syringe, which has a plunger to push medicine into the body. It can be used to put medicine or liquid into a vein or to take blood. Large hypodermic needles are useful for giving quick treatment in emergencies or when medicine cannot be taken by mouth, like insulin. Common places to insert the needle are in the arm. In research, hypodermic needles are important because they help keep things clean. They reduce contamination during experiments by having a smooth surface that doesn’t trap germs and by being very sharp, which makes small holes that stop larger germs from getting in.

Melissa Suzanne McBride, born on May 23, 1965, is an American actress and former casting director. Her big break came when she played Carol Peletier in the AMC series "The Walking Dead" from 2010 to the present. She has been highly praised for her role and has won several awards and nominations. At first, she was in a small part and only mentioned in the credits after the main ones. Over time, her role grew, and she became a main cast member. As of 2020, she is the second person shown in the opening credits, and one of only two actors to appear in every season of the show, along with Norman Reedus.

A.C. Moore was an American store that sold arts and crafts. It was owned by Nicole Crafts. A.C. Moore had 145 stores in the eastern part of the United States. Its main office was in Berlin, New Jersey. On November 25, 2019, A.C. Moore said it would close all its stores and sell some of its stores and other things to a competitor named Michaels.

Pori is a city and municipality on Finland's west coast. It is near the Gulf of Bothnia, at the mouth of the Kokemäenjoki river, west of Tampere, north of Turku, and northwest of Helsinki, Finland's capital. Pori was founded in 1558 by Duke John, who later became King John III of Sweden. The city has about 66,000 people. Its land area is 68 square kilometers, with 20 square kilometers of water. Pori has about 980 people per square kilometer. The city only speaks Finnish. It is the largest city in Finland and the seventh largest urban area. Pori is the capital of the Satakunta region, which has 224,000 people, and the Porikunta sub-region, which has 136,905 people.

Clannad is a Japanese visual novel by Key, released on April 28, 2004, for Windows PCs. Unlike the company's earlier works, "Kanon" and "Air," which were first released for adults and later made for younger audiences, Clannad was suitable for all ages from the start. It was later released on various gaming consoles, including PlayStation 2, PlayStation Portable, Xbox 360, PlayStation 3, PlayStation Vita, PlayStation 4, and Nintendo Switch. An English version came out in 2015 on Steam by Sekai Project. Clannad tells the story of Tomoya Okazaki, a high school student, who meets and helps five girls during his final year. The game lets you choose how to interact with the characters and focuses on the five girls. Clannad was very popular, ranking as the best-selling PC game in Japan when it was released and appearing in the top 50 national charts many times. In 2005, Key made an adult spin-off called "The Reed Warbler," which expanded the story about one of the girls, Tomoyo Sakagami. Clannad has been adapted into several other media. Four manga adaptations were published by different companies, along with comic anthologies, light novels, art books, audio dramas, and music albums. In 2007, an animated film was released, followed by two anime series with original video animation episodes. Both series were licensed by Sentai Filmworks and shown in North America. The anime and films were well-received in Japan and abroad.

The national flag of Bolivia was first used in 1851. It has three horizontal stripes: red, yellow, and green. In the middle, there is a coat of arms. Some say the red color represents brave soldiers, green symbolizes fertility, and yellow shows the country’s mineral wealth. Bolivia shares this unique feature with a few other countries: the Dominican Republic, Haiti, Afghanistan, Ecuador, Costa Rica, and El Salvador. Since 2009, the wiphala has also been an official flag in Bolivia.

The Saturn Relay is a minivan made by General Motors. It was introduced in 2005 and was built with the Buick Terraza, Chevrolet Uplander, and Pontiac Montana SV6 in Doraville, Georgia. It was the first Saturn minivan without plastic side panels. It was also the first Saturn model rebadged from a Chevrolet or Pontiac. The Relay was the only minivan made by Saturn. It had a 3.5-liter V6 engine that could go from 0 to 60 miles per hour in about 9 seconds. In 2006, a 3.9-liter V6 engine was added, which was faster and more powerful. In 2007, the 3.5-liter engine was removed, leaving the 3.9-liter as the only option. The optional all-wheel drive system was also dropped because it couldn't handle the power of the 3.9-liter engine. The 2007 Relay could use a special fuel type, but only for company use. The Relay got high scores in safety tests. In terms of fuel efficiency, it was rated for city and highway driving. It started at $22,850. There were three types: 1, 2, and 3. All had seats for seven people, with folding second and third-row seats. Standard features included OnStar and a DVD entertainment system. Navigation was optional on type 3. Side airbags were optional too. The Relay was no longer made after 2007 and was replaced by the Saturn Outlook.
Willis David Gradison Jr., born on December 28, 1928, is an American politician from Ohio. He worked in the United States House of Representatives from 1975 to 1993.

The Samsung Galaxy Note 10 is a line of large Android phones. Samsung Electronics makes and sells these phones as part of the Galaxy Note series. They were shown to the public on August 7, 2019, as replacements for the Samsung Galaxy Note 9. Before their announcement, people knew many details about the phones. In 2020, Samsung also released a cheaper version called Galaxy Note 10 Lite, with fewer features.

Companion planting in gardening and farming involves putting different plants close together for various reasons. These reasons can include keeping pests away, helping with pollination, attracting good insects, using space better, and improving crop growth. Companion planting is a type of growing several crops together. People who grow crops, both in developed and developing countries, use this method for many purposes. Some ideas for companion planting were around long ago. They were used in old English gardens and in forests in Asia. Many of these ideas were even older, dating back thousands of years in a place called Mesoamerica.
Melano is a municipality in the Lugano district of the Ticino canton in Switzerland.

The 1983–84 NHL season was the 67th season of the National Hockey League. The Edmonton Oilers beat the New York Islanders, who had won the Stanley Cup four times in a row, in the finals, winning four games to one.

In physics, angular velocity describes how quickly an object turns or moves around another point, or how its orientation changes over time. There are two kinds: spin angular velocity, which is how fast a rigid body spins about its center, and orbital angular velocity, which measures how fast a point revolves around a fixed point. Spin angular velocity is the same no matter where you measure it, unlike orbital angular velocity. Angular velocity is measured in angles per unit time, such as radians per second. The standard unit is radians per second, often just stated as 1/s. It is represented by the symbol omega (ω). Clockwise rotation is negative, while counter-clockwise is positive. For example, a geostationary satellite orbits the Earth once every 24 hours, or 360 degrees in 24 hours. Its angular velocity is ω = 360° / 24 h = 15°/h, or approximately 0.26 rad/h. With a radius of 42,000 km, the satellite's speed is about 11,000 km/h. In three dimensions, angular velocity is a vector that points perpendicularly to the plane of rotation. Its magnitude shows the rate of rotation, and it is positive for counter-clockwise rotation from above the north pole.
Hinton is a town in Caddo County, Oklahoma, United States. In 2010, the population was 3,196, which was more than in 2000 when it was 2,175. It is roughly west of Oklahoma City.

Ronald Tauranac, born on January 13, 1925, and died on July 17, 2020, was a British-Australian engineer and racing car designer. He co-founded the Brabham team with Formula One driver Jack Brabham in 1962. After Brabham stopped racing at the end of the 1970 season, Tauranac ran the Brabham team until 1972, when he sold it to Bernie Ecclestone. In 1973, Tauranac worked on redesigning a racing car chassis for Frank Williams and helped Trojan develop a Formula One version of their Formula 5000 car. He took a short break in Australia before returning to England in 1973 to create the Ralt racing team. He and his brother had used the Ralt name earlier in the 1950s. The Ralt RT1 chassis was successful, winning the European Formula Three championship in 1975 with Australian driver Larry Perkins. The chassis also won the 1978 European Formula Three championship for Jan Lammers. Tauranac designed the Theodore F1 car for the 1978 season. For the 1979 season, he created the RT2 for Formula Two and the RT3 for Formula Three. The RT3 won the 1983 European F3 championship for Pierluigi Martini and five consecutive British F3 titles. A joint venture with Honda produced the RH6 chassis, which won titles in 1981, 1984, and 1985. In October 1988, Tauranac sold the Ralt business to March Engineering for £1.25 million. He continued to work in racing, developing Honda racing school cars, designing a Formula Renault car, and consulting for the Arrows Formula One team. He also worked with Honda and was a design judge at the Formula SAE Australia competition. In 2002, Tauranac was awarded the Officer of the Order of Australia for his contributions to motor racing. He passed away on July 17, 2020, at the age of 95.
Lovelock is the biggest town in Big Horn County, Wyoming, in the United States. According to the 2010 census, it had 2,360 people.

Gustavo José Joaquín Noboa Bejarano was born on August 21, 1937, in Guayaquil, Ecuador. He is an Ecuadorian politician. Noboa was the president of Ecuador from January 22, 2000, to January 15, 2003. He also served as vice president during Jamil Mahuad's government.

Vandervoort is a town in Polk County, Arkansas, United States. In 2000, it had 120 people. The town is named after the mother of a significant railway businessman from the early 20th century. Her name was Jan de Goeijen, and her maiden name was Van der Voort.

This list shows the 33 counties in New Mexico. In 1852, there were nine counties. One of them, Santa Ana County, was added to Bernalillo County in 1876. Each county has a code, known as the FIPS code. New Mexico's code is 35, and when combined with a county code, it looks like 35xxx. Clicking on the FIPS code for a county will take you to its census data.

Jock Sturrock, born on May 14, 1915, in Melbourne, and passed away on July 11, 1997, in Noosa Heads, was an Australian yachtsman. He won over four hundred yachting races in international, national, state, and club championships.

The bleating tree frog, also called Keferstein's tree frog, is a type of tree frog. It belongs to the family Pelodryadidae. This frog lives along the coast in eastern Australia, from south-eastern Queensland to Eden, in New South Wales.

The National Symphony Orchestra (NSO), started in 1930, is a symphony orchestra in the United States. It is based in Washington, D.C. and usually performs at the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. The NSO played in the National Memorial Day concert and the Capitol Fourth event.

A neural network is a system of connected nodes, either artificial or biological. In modern usage, it refers to artificial neural networks used for AI problems. These networks have nodes that mimic real neurons, where connections are represented as weights. Positive weights show excitatory connections, while negative ones show inhibitory connections. Each input is changed by a weight and then combined. This is called a linear combination. An activation function then controls the output, usually between 0 and 1 or -1 and 1. These networks can be trained with data to make predictions, control systems adaptively, and learn from experience to handle complex information.

On July 15, 2020, between 8:00 PM and 10:00 PM UTC, about 130 important Twitter accounts were taken over by outside people to spread a Bitcoin scam. Twitter and other news sources said that the criminals used Twitter's tools to make changes and send messages directly. It seems they tricked Twitter employees to get access to these tools. On July 31, 2020, three people were caught and charged with fraud, money laundering, identity theft, and using Twitter without permission because of the scam. The criminals asked people to send Bitcoin to a specific wallet, promising to double the money as a gift. Within minutes, over 320 transactions had happened on one wallet address, and the scam messages were removed quickly by Twitter. Also, some message history from eight non-verified accounts was stolen. Cybersecurity expert Dmitri Alperovitch called it "the worst hack of a major social media platform yet." Law enforcement agencies, including the FBI, are looking into the scam and Twitter's security. People worry that this trick might affect the use of social media in important discussions, like before the 2020 U.S. presidential election.

Madelaine Gail Kahn, born Madeline Gail Wolfson on September 29, 1942, and died on December 3, 1999, was an American actress, comedian, voice actress, and singer. She was famous for her funny roles in movies directed by Peter Bogdanovich and Mel Brooks, such as "What's Up, Doc?" (1972), "Young Frankenstein" (1974), "High Anxiety" (1977), "History of the World, Part I" (1981), and "Blazing Saddles" (1974), which got her nominated for an Academy Award. Kahn first appeared on Broadway in "Leonard Sillman's New Faces of 1968." She was nominated for a Tony Award for the play "In the Boom Boom Room" in 1974 and for the musical "On the Twentieth Century" in 1978. She starred in the short-lived TV show "Oh Madeline" (1983-1984) and won a Daytime Emmy Award in 1987 for an "ABC Afterschool Special." Kahn was nominated for a Tony Award again in 1989 for the play "Born Yesterday" and won in 1993 for the best actress in the comedy "The Sisters Rosensweig." Some of her film roles included "The Cheap Detective" (1978), "City Heat" (1984), "Clue" (1985), and "Nixon" (1995).

An oar is a tool used to move boats through water. It has a flat blade at one end, and rowers hold it at the other. Oars are only used for rowing. In rowing, the oar is connected to the boat with a pivot point, either an oarlock or a thole. Most of the oar is outside the boat, and the rower pulls on the part inside. This makes the oar blade move through the water. The oar acts like a second class lever, with the water acting as the fulcrum, the oarlock as the load, and the rower providing the force. Oars increase the small movement of the rower's hand into a larger movement of the boat. The rower applies a strong force over a short distance, while the water applies a smaller force over a longer distance, meaning the work done by the rower is equal to the work done by the water. Paddles, on the other hand, are held in both hands and are not attached to the boat. Rowers face the back of the boat, reach towards the stern, and place the paddle blade in the water. As they lean back, the paddle blade pivots in the water, pushing the boat forward. For thousands of years, boats were moved by either sails or rowers. Some ancient boats used both oars and sails, depending on the wind direction and speed.

A medical abortion uses pills to end a pregnancy. First, you take mifepristone. Then, you take misoprostol. This combination is safe and effective at different stages of pregnancy. If mifepristone is not available, misoprostol alone can be used.

Ji Guobiao was a Chinese chemical engineer and an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering. He lived from March 1932 to September 2019. Ji was a pioneer in chemical fiber engineering technology in China.
The Berowra division is an Australian area where people choose their representatives. It is in the state of New South Wales.

phosphorus pentafluoride, or pf, is a type of phosphorus halide. It is a colorless, toxic gas that produces fumes when it mixes with air.

Ksenia Arturovna Tripolitova was born on May 7, 1915, in Vilna, Russian Empire, and died on April 9, 2020, in Paris, at the age of 104. She was a Russian-born French ballet dancer. She studied dance with Lyubov Yegorova. Ksenia performed with her husband in the 1930s and 1940s. During World War II, she danced in France when the Nazis were fighting there. In 1949, she performed in Switzerland. In the 1950s, she and her husband formed a vocal and dance group called "Troika." From 1954 to 1955, she worked at an opera theater in Tunisia. In 1957, she danced with the Ural Cossack Choir in Spain. She celebrated her 100th birthday in 2015.

The Allen Telescope Array (ATA), previously called the One Hectare Telescope (1HT), is a radio telescope used for astronomy and searching for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI). It is located at the Hat Creek Radio Observatory in Shasta County, near San Francisco, California. Originally, it was a joint project between the SETI Institute and the Radio Astronomy Laboratory at the University of California, Berkeley. Paul G. Allen, co-founder of Microsoft, provided the initial funding of $11.5 million, and later added another $13.5 million to complete the first two phases. Although Paul Allen invested over $30 million in total, the project did not build the originally planned 350 6.1-meter dishes. The array had a break in operations due to lack of funds between April and August 2011, but resumed after that. In 2012, the University of California, Berkeley withdrew from the project. SRI International now manages the facility. The SETI Institute uses the ATA from 6 PM to 6 AM daily. In August 2014, the installation faced a forest fire but managed to continue operations largely unharmed.

The British Association for Applied Linguistics (BAAL) is a group based in the UK. It helps people who are interested in language and applied linguistics. BAAL holds regular meetings for its members in different places in the UK. They also publish conference papers, send out a newsletter, and give scholarships to students. There is an elected committee that represents the members' interests. Dawn Knight is the current chair (2018-2021). BAAL has more than 1200 members from around the world and is a registered charity in the UK.

An airliner is a plane that carries passengers and cargo. Airlines operate most of these planes. Typically, an airliner is a commercial airplane meant for multiple passengers or cargo. The largest ones are wide-body jets, also called twin-aisle planes, which have two aisles from front to back and are used for long flights between big cities. Smaller, more common airliners are narrow-body or single-aisle planes, used for shorter flights with fewer passengers. Regional airliners usually hold fewer than 100 passengers and may use turbofans or turboprops. They connect smaller airports to main hubs. These regional planes help feed passengers into larger airline hubs. Regional routes form the spokes of the hub-and-spoke model in air transport. Light planes, like the Beechcraft 1900 with 19 seats, are called commuter aircraft, commuterliners, feederliners, or air taxis, depending on their size, engines, marketing, region, and seating.

Duck Commander is a brand for duck calls and a company in West Monroe, Louisiana, United States. The company makes duck calls and hunting gear for ducks, as well as merchandise for deer and turkeys under different brand names. Phil Robertson, who used to play football, started the business. He made calls in an old boat for 25 years using cedar trees from Louisiana. Willie Robertson, Phil's son, is now the CEO. He has grown the company into a large business. The Robertson family and their business are shown on a reality TV show called "Duck Dynasty" on A&E. Before that, they were featured on the Outdoor Channel's "Duck Commander" show.

Halabja is a city in the Kurdistan region, and it is the capital of Halabja governorate. It is located in Iraq, northeast of Baghdad and near the Iranian border. The city is part of the greater Hewraman region, which spans across the Iran-Iraq border. To the northeast of Halabja, there are Hawraman and Shnrwe ranges. To the south, there is the Balambo range, and to the west, there is the Sirwan river. Most people in Halabja speak the Sorani dialect of Kurdish. However, some people in nearby villages speak the Hewrami dialect.

The Meissner effect is when a superconductor, like tin or lead, expels magnetic fields when cooled below a certain temperature. In 1933, Meissner and Ochsenfeld found this by cooling these metals and seeing a change in the magnetic field. This shows superconductors do more than just conduct electricity perfectly—they also repel magnetic fields. This effect is important because it helps define the superconducting state. Superconductors can be type I or type II. In type I, superconductivity stops when a strong magnetic field is applied. In type II, superconductors can allow some magnetic field penetration but still conduct electricity with no resistance. Most pure metals, like niobium, are type I, while impure or compound superconductors are type II.

"Sadness" is a song by the American band Maroon 5. It came out on June 22, 2010, through A&M Octone Records. This was the first song from their album called "Hands All Over," which was released in 2010.

North Macedonia has 34 cities. Five of these cities have more than 50,000 people. Twelve towns have fewer than 10,000 people. The capital city, Skopje, has about 25% of the country's population. As of 2002, 59.5% of people lived in towns. Twelve towns are very small, with populations like this: Demir Hisar (2,593), Peševo (3,237), Demir Kapija (3,275), Makedonski Brod (3,740), Valandovo (4,402), Makedonska Kamenica (5,147), Kruševo (5,330), Bogdanci (6,011), Kratovo (6,924), Berovo (7,002), Probishpit (8,714), and Resen (8,748). These towns are often called "small towns." North Macedonia has five large cities: Skopje (506,926), Bitola (74,550), Kumanovo (70,842), Prilep (66,246), and Tetovo (86,580). There are also 17 medium-sized towns, including Veles (43,716), Stip (43,652), Ohrid (42,033), Gostivar (35,847), Strumica (35,311), Kavadarci (29,188), Kočani (28,330), Kičevo (27,067), Struga (16,559), Radoviš (16,223), Gevgelija (15,685), Debar (14,561), Kriva Palanka (14,558), Sveti Nikole (13,746), Negotino (13,284), Delčevo (11,500), and Vinica (10,863).
Cool is a town in Parker County, Texas, United States. In 2010, the town had 157 people.

The Russian Empire, which lasted from 1721 to 1917, grew across Europe, Asia, and North America. It was the third-largest empire in history, after the British and Mongol empires. The empire expanded by taking over neighboring rivals like Sweden, Poland, Persia, and the Ottoman Empire. It was at its largest during the 19th century, stretching from the Arctic to the Black Sea, and from Western Europe to parts of North America. The Romanov family ruled the empire from 1721 until 1917. The empire was very diverse, with many different economies, ethnic groups, languages, and religions. There were many rebellions and assassinations, watched by the secret police, with thousands of people sent to Siberia. The empire was mostly about farming. Many people worked on large farms called estates. These people were called serfs and were tied to the land. Serfs were freed in 1861, but the landowning nobles kept control. The economy slowly got better with help from foreign investments in railways and factories. Ivan III, who ruled from 1462 to 1505, started the empire. He made the land much bigger and improved the Kremlin. Peter the Great, who ruled from 1682 to 1725, made the empire bigger and turned it into a major European power. He moved the capital to a new city called Saint Petersburg and brought in western ideas. Catherine the Great, who ruled from 1762 to 1796, expanded the empire by taking over more land and made it more modern. Alexander II, who ruled from 1855 to 1881, freed the serfs in 1861 and tried to protect Orthodox Christians in the Ottoman Empire. During World War I, the empire had problems. The last emperor and his family were killed by the Bolsheviks in 1918. The Bolsheviks took power in 1922 and created the Soviet Union, while many nobles were forced into exile or killed.

Ongar railway station is on the Epping Ongar railway heritage line. It used to be a London Underground station in Chipping Ongar, Essex. The station opened in 1865 by the Great Eastern Railway. It became part of London Transport in 1949. The station closed in 1994. Until then, it was the easternmost point of the Central Line. It is still the starting point for measuring distances on the London Underground.

Roberts County is in Texas, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 929 people, making it the least populous county in Texas. The county seat is Miami, the only incorporated town. Roberts County was formed in 1876 and officially organized in 1889. It's named after Oran Milo Roberts, a former Texas governor. Currently, Roberts County is one of six dry counties in Texas.

Eye contact is when two animals look directly into each other's eyes at the same time. In humans, it's a way of communicating without talking and is believed to affect social behavior significantly. The term "eye contact" was first used in the 1960s and is seen as a sign of confidence and respect. The importance and meaning of eye contact can vary a lot between different cultures due to religious and social differences. This study of eye contact is sometimes called "oculesics."

pavement lights, also known as vault lights in the US, floor lights, or sidewalk prisms, are flat-topped lights that you can walk on. They are usually set into sidewalks or floors to let sunlight into the space below. Often, they use special prisms to spread light sideways under the building. These lights were developed in the 19th century but became less popular with the introduction of cheap electric lights. Older cities and small towns around the world still have or once had these lights. Most such lights are about a century old, although some new buildings are installing them too.

Lancaster is a city in Fairfield County, Ohio. It is located in the south-central part of the state. According to the 2010 census, Lancaster had a population of 38,780. The city is near the Hocking River. It is southeast of Columbus and southwest of Zanesville. Lancaster is the county seat of Fairfield County.

The Korean peninsula has many mountains along its eastern side. Therefore, most of its rivers flow westward, emptying into the Yellow Sea. Some rivers pass through artificial reservoirs before reaching the coast, as there are no natural lakes on the mainland. A few rivers flow south into the Korea Strait, and a few small rivers flow east toward East Korea Bay. These eastern rivers are usually just small streams. Here is a list of tributaries, organized by the main river they flow into, in upstream order. The list goes counterclockwise, starting from the Amnok River to the Duman River.

chopicallqui, possibly from Quechua "chawpi" meaning "center" and "kallki" meaning "ravine," is a mountain in the Cordillera Blanca area of the Andes in Peru. At an elevation above sea level, it is one of the highest peaks in the Cordillera Blanca. This mountain is in Yungay province, in the region of Ancash. It is located between Huascarán and Contrahierbas mountains.

Ilkka Olavi Suominen, born on April 8, 1939, in Nakkila, is a Finnish politician from the National Coalition Party. He was the president of the Nordic Council in 1992. Suominen was a member of the parliament from 1970 to 1975 and from 1983 to 1994. He was the chairman of the National Coalition Party from 1979 to 1991. Suominen served twice as the speaker of the parliament in 1987 and 1991 to 1994. He was a minister of trade and industry from 1987 to 1991 in the Holkeri cabinet. After leaving parliament, Suominen became the CEO of Alko, a state monopoly. He was elected to the European Parliament (MEP) for one term from 1999 to 2004, representing the EPP. Suominen was also the chairman of the Parliamentary Assembly of the OSCE from 1992 to 1994.

Wofford Heights is a census-designated place in southern Sierra Nevada, Kern County, California, United States. It is in the West Kern River Valley, south-southwest of Kernville. The area is at an elevation. In 2010, the population was 2,200, down from 2,276 in 2000.

Shakib Khan, born on March 28, 1979, is a Bangladeshi film actor, producer, singer, and media personality. Known by the initialism SK, Khan has been active in the film industry for about 20 years. He is called "King Khan" and "King of Dhallywood" and is famous as "Number One Shakib Khan" (No1SK). He is also known as "Bhaijaan of Dhallywood" due to his 2018 film. Khan is the highest-paid actor in Bangladesh. Khan first appeared in the 1999 film "Ananta Bhalobasha" but didn't gain widespread fame until later. In 2008, he starred in "Priya Amar Priya," a successful film that earned him a lot of money. His 2016 film "Shikari" was very popular, and "Swatta" and "Nabab" were also big successes in 2017. "Swatta" won many awards, including national awards. "Nabab" was the highest-grossing film in 2017 and one of the highest-grossing films of all time. Khan earned 50 lakh for the 2019 film "Nolok," which was the highest-paid performance in Bangladeshi cinema history. Khan has acted in many films, including "Shuva" (2006), "Amar Praner Swami" (2007), "Bhaijaan Elo Re" (2018), and "Bir" (2020). He also sang in "Moner Jala" in 2011 and started producing films in 2014, including "Password" (2019) and "Bir" (2020). Khan has received many awards, including four national film awards, eight Meril Prothom Alo awards, three Bachsas awards, and five CJFB performance awards. He won the national film award for best actor four times for the films "Bhalobaslei Ghor Bandha Jay Na" (2010), "Khodar Pore Ma" (2012), "Aro Bhalobashbo Tomay" (2015), and "Swatta" (2017).

Wanrong, also known as the Xuantong Empress, was the empress of China's last emperor, Puyi. She lived from November 13, 1906, to June 20, 1946. In 1932, when Japan set up a fake government in Manchuria and made Puyi its leader, Wanrong became the empress of this fake government. During the war in 1945, Soviet forces invaded Manchuria. Communist Chinese guerrillas captured Wanrong and moved her to different places. Finally, she was put in a prison camp in Yanji, Jilin. She died in the prison around June or August 1946, but her body was never found. On October 23, 2006, Wanrong's younger brother, Runqi, had a burial ceremony for her in the Western Qing Tombs.

Uzlovac is a long mountain in Bosnia and Herzegovina, located east of the Maslovare-Vrbanjci-Kotor Varoš-Cелинac line. It stretches from southeast to northwest through mountainous areas, from Kruševica River (west of Borja Mountains) to Jošavka. The mountain is very rich in mixed forests and hunting wildlife, including Bosnian endemic quarry mammals. Its forests include diverse species like deciduous oak and beech. Uzlovac also has many water resources such as springs, streams, and rivers. Many tributaries of the Vrbas and Bosna rivers rise on the mountain.

Thixotropy is a property where certain gels or fluids become thinner and less viscous over time when shaken or agitated. They then take some time to become thicker again. Some fluids, like ketchup, become less thick quickly and are called pseudoplastic. Others, like yogurt, take longer to return to a thicker state. Many gels and colloids are thixotropic, appearing solid when still but becoming fluid when moved. Thixotropy happens because particles or structured materials need time to organize. Some fluids, known as anti-thixotropic, become thicker when constantly stressed. These fluids are called rheopectic. Examples and studies of anti-thixotropic fluids are less common.

Arjen Anthony Lucassen, born on April 3, 1960, in Hilversum, Netherlands, is a Dutch singer, songwriter, musician, and record producer. He is famous for creating the progressive metal/rock opera project Ayreon. Lucassen started his music career in 1980 as the guitarist and backup singer of the band Bodine, performing under the name Iron Anthony. In 1984, he joined Vengeance and stayed for eight years. After leaving the band, he released an unsuccessful solo album in 1991 called "Pools of Sorrow, Waves of Joy." In 1995, Lucassen released an album titled "Ayreon: The Final Experiment," singing, writing songs, and playing most of the instruments. This led to the creation of Ayreon. His third album, "Into the Electric Castle," gained attention and praise, making Lucassen known for composing rock operas. Since Ayreon's success, Lucassen has worked on many other projects. He is the creator and composer of Star One, Guilt Machine, and The Gentle Storm, and was once a guitarist in Ambeon and Stream of Passion. He also writes songs and sometimes shares lyrics with his musical partners. Lucassen plays many instruments, including guitar and keyboards, but also bass and banjo. Throughout his career, he has released 26 studio albums, four live albums, two EPs, and 17 singles. He has also participated in several other artists' albums, appearing in over 50 albums. Lucassen gained recognition in the rock and metal scene, with many critics calling him a "genius." In a review of "01011001," Allmusic reviewer Cosmo Lee said the music was so outstanding that it was hard to criticize.

Rod Piazza, born on December 18, 1947, in Riverside, California, is an American blues harmonica player and singer. He started playing with his band, The Mighty Flyers, in 1980. Honey Piazza, his pianist wife, helped form the band. Their music has a boogie style that mixes jump blues, West Coast blues, and Chicago blues.

A disposable product is made to be used once and then recycled or thrown away. Sometimes, it refers to items that can last for several months, like disposable air filters, to set them apart from items that can last forever, like washable air filters. The term "disposables" shouldn't be confused with "consumables." In the mechanical world, consumables include things like welding rods, tips, nozzles, and gas, which are used until they wear out. Consumables are needed for processes, such as inks for printing or welding rods for welding. On the other hand, disposables are items that can be thrown away when they are damaged or no longer useful.

Tiko, formerly known as 'keka' by the Bakweri people, is a town and important port in Cameroon's southwest region. It grew as a market town for fishermen, farmers, and hunters from nearby areas like Molyko, Bwenga, Bulu, and Bokova. The main parts of Tiko include streets 1 to 7, Motombolombo, Down Beach, the New Quarter, P&T Quarter, New Layout, Long Street, Likomba, Golf Club, Mutengene, and Ombe. In 2010, Tiko had around 55,914 people living there. It is a popular place for tourists visiting Cameroon. Tiko is also an industrial area with the Cameroon Development Corporation (CDC) producing rubber, banana, and palm oil. The town hosts the Tiko Golf Club, a favorite spot for golfers. The Likomba Golf Course in Likomba has 18 holes and hosts major tournaments during the dry season. This is one of only two golf courses in Cameroon. Tiko also has a special forces unit that provides safety for its people. Mutengene, a small town to the west of Tiko, is a crossroads leading to Buea and Limbe, which used to be called Victoria.

Hugo Boss AG, often called Boss, is a German luxury fashion company based in Metzingen, Baden-Württemberg. They make clothes, accessories, shoes, and perfumes. Hugo Boss is one of the largest German clothing companies, with sales of €2.9 billion in 2019. Its stock is part of the MDAX. The company was started in 1924 by Hugo Boss and initially made common clothing. During the 1930s, when the Nazi party became powerful, Boss started making and selling uniforms for the Nazis. This boosted sales significantly. After World War II and Hugo Boss's death in 1948, the company shifted focus to making men's suits. Hugo Boss went public in 1988 and launched a fragrance line that same year. In 1997, they added men's and women's wear lines. They introduced a full women's collection in 2000 and children's clothing in 2006-2007. Since then, Hugo Boss has become a major global fashion company. As of now, they operate over 1,113 retail stores worldwide.

Nystagmus is a condition where the eyes move involuntarily or voluntarily, often starting in infancy or later. It can lead to reduced vision. Because the eyes move without control, it's sometimes called "dancing eyes." In normal vision, as the head turns, the eyes adjust in the opposite direction, keeping the focus steady. The inner ear helps sense the head movement and sends signals to the brain, which tells the eye muscles to focus on objects while the head moves. Nystagmus happens when the inner ear is stimulated, making the eyes move even when the head is still. The direction of eye movement depends on which part of the inner ear is involved. There are two main types of nystagmus: pathological and physiological. Each type has different causes. Nystagmus can be caused by birth defects, lack of sleep, diseases, medicines, alcohol, or spinning movements. In recent years, some drugs have been found to help treat nystagmus, and it can sometimes be linked to dizziness.

In the Roman Empire from the 2nd to 4th centuries, taurobolium was a practice involving the sacrifice of a bull. After the mid-2nd century, this practice became linked with worshipping the great mother of the gods. Earlier, it wasn't exclusive to her worship. Starting in 159 AD, all private inscriptions about taurobolium mentioned the "magna mater."
The Bas-Rhin department has five arrondissements.

Ugur Yucel, born on May 26, 1957, is a Turkish actor, producer, and director. He studied theater at the Istanbul Municipality Conservatory. From 1975 to 1984, he performed in plays at Kenter Theatre, Tef Kabare Theatre, Dormen Theatre, and Şan Musikholu. He became known for his roles in "Selamsiz Bandosu" and "Muhsin Bey" in 1987. He then found more success in the 1996 film "Eşkıya."

The Murray was an Australian electoral division in Victoria. It was in the northern part of the state, next to the Murray River, which forms the border between Victoria and New South Wales. The division had towns like Shepparton, Echuca, Cobram, Yarrawonga, Boort, and Bridgewater. In 2018, the division changed its name to Nicholls and this change was applied for the 2019 federal election.

Calhoun County is a name used for several counties in the United States. These counties are named after John C. Calhoun, who was a U.S. Vice President.

Challakere Kareem Jaffer Sharief (born November 3, 1933, died November 25, 2018) was an Indian politician. He was one of the most experienced leaders in the Indian National Congress party. He served as the Railway Minister of India from 1991 to 1995.

The Brooks Range, also called "gwazhał" in Athabaskan, is a mountain range in northern North America, stretching from west to east across northern Alaska and into Canada's Yukon Territory. Its highest peak is Mount Isto, and the range is about 126 million years old. In the U.S., the range is seen as part of the Rocky Mountains, but in Canada, it's considered separate, with the northern border of the Rocky Mountains being the Liard River in British Columbia. Most of the range is uninhabited. However, the Dalton Highway and Trans-Alaska Pipeline go through Atigun Pass (1,415 meters, 4,643 feet) on their way to Prudhoe Bay on Alaska's north slope. The only settlements are the Alaska Native villages of Anaktuvuk and Arctic Village, and small communities like Coldfoot, Wiseman, Bettles, and Chandalar. Near the Wulik River in the De Long Mountains, there's the Red Dog mine, the world's largest zinc mine. The range was named after Alfred Hulse Brooks, the chief USGS geologist for Alaska from 1903 to 1924. It has also been known by other names like the Arctic Mountains, Hooper Mountains, Meade Mountains, and Meade River Mountains. In Canada, the range is officially called the British Mountains. Ivvavik National Park is in the British Mountains in Canada.

The monk parakeet, also called the quaker parrot, is a small, bright-green parrot. It has a greyish breast and a greenish-yellow belly. These parakeets usually live for 20 to 30 years. They come from areas in South America, like Argentina and nearby countries. They can now be found in the wild in many places, especially in North America and Europe.

Greifswald, officially named the University and Hanseatic City of Greifswald, is a city in northeastern Germany. It is in the state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, roughly equally distant from Germany's two biggest cities, Berlin and Hamburg, and about 80 kilometers from the Polish border. Located in Western Pomerania, the city is near the Baltic Sea and has a small river called the Ryck flowing through it. It is close to Germany's two largest islands, Rügen and Usedom, and nearby are three of Germany's 14 national parks. Since September 2011, Greifswald has been the capital of the new district of Vorpommern-Greifswald. Along with Stralsund, it is one of the four main urban centers in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. The city's population was about 55,659 in 2013, including many of the 12,500 students and 5,000 employees of the University of Greifswald. Greifswald attracts international attention because of the university, the biocon valley around it, the Nord Stream gas pipeline, and the Wendelstein 7-x nuclear fusion project.

Balkrishna Vithaldas Doshi, born on August 26, 1927, is an Indian architect. He is an important figure in Indian architecture and is known for his work in shaping architectural discussions in India. He has worked with famous architects Le Corbusier and Louis Kahn and is a pioneer in modernist and brutalist architecture in India. Some of his famous designs include IIM Bangalore, IIM Udaipur, NIFT Delhi, Amdavad Ni Gufa, CEPT University, and Aranya low-cost housing in Indore. The Aranya project won the Aga Khan Award for Architecture. In 2018, he became the first Indian architect to receive the Pritzker Architecture Prize, which is a very important prize in the field. He has also been given the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan awards.

Kraftwerk is a German band formed in Düsseldorf in 1970 by Ralf Hütter and Florian Schneider. They are known as pioneers of electronic music. Kraftwerk started in West Germany’s experimental music scene in the early 1970s and later focused on electronic instruments like synthesizers and drum machines. They became very popular with albums such as "Autobahn" (1974), "Trans-Europe Express" (1977), "The Man-Machine" (1978), and "Computer World" (1981). These albums had a style called "robot pop" that mixed electronic music with pop tunes and simple arrangements. They wore matching suits as part of their look. Wolfgang Flür left the band in 1987, and Karl Bartos followed in 1990. Florian Schneider left in 2008. Kraftwerk’s music has influenced many artists and genres, including synth-pop, hip hop, post-punk, techno, ambient, and club music. In 2014, they won a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award. They also won a Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Album in 2018. The band keeps performing as of 2020.

Putnam County is in New York, U.S. The 2010 census showed its population was 99,710. The county seat is Carmel. Putnam County was created in 1812 from Dutchess County and is named after Israel Putnam, a hero in the French and Indian War and a general in the American Revolutionary War. It is part of the New York-Newark-Jersey City, NY-NJ-PA metropolitan area and is in the Lower Hudson River Valley. It's about a one-hour drive from midtown Manhattan and a one-hour, 20-minute train ride from Grand Central Terminal. Putnam County is one of the wealthiest in America, ranked 21st by median household income and 43rd by per-capita income, according to data from 2012 and 2009-2013 American Community Surveys.

Lee Hyo-ri, born on May 10, 1979, is a singer from South Korea. She also works as a record producer, activist, actress, and television presenter. During her early career, she was known as "the nation's fairy." Lee first joined the girl group Fin.K.L but later became a solo artist. In 2003, she released her first solo album called "Stylist" and won several "artist of the year" awards. In 2006, she became the highest-paid female singer in South Korea when she signed a contract with Mnet Media.

Violet Brown (née Mosse; born March 10, 1900, died September 15, 2017) was a Jamaican person who lived for over 117 years. She became the oldest known living person in the world after Emma Morano died on April 15, 2017. Violet Brown passed away on September 15, 2017. At the time of her death, she was the fifth-oldest person in history and was one of only two people known to have been born in the 19th century.

Here is a list of the 67 counties in Pennsylvania. The city of Philadelphia is the same as Philadelphia County. In 1854, the cities there combined. A vote in 1951 made Philadelphia County's county government part of the city. Eight of the ten most populous counties are in the southeast part of the state. Four of the top five most populous counties are there. Eight out of the top ten most populous counties are in either the Philadelphia or Pittsburgh areas.

João Ubaldo Ribeiro was a Brazilian writer, journalist, screenwriter, and teacher. He lived from January 23, 1941, to July 18, 2014. Many of his books and short stories were made into movies and TV shows in Brazil. Ribeiro became a member of the Brazilian Academy of Letters in 1994. When he died, many people thought he was Brazil's best novelist of his time.

Zvečan is a town and municipality in Mitrovica District in Kosovo. As of 2015, it has 16,650 people living there. The area covers 16.65 square kilometers and includes the town and 35 villages. Zvečan is in North Kosovo. This area has many Serb people and functions mostly separately from the rest of Kosovo, where Albanians are the main ethnic group. After the 2013 Brussels Agreement, the municipality became part of the group of Serb municipalities.

Neopterygii comes from the Greek words "neos" meaning new and "pteryx" meaning fin. It is a group of ray-finned fish (actinopterygii). Very few changes happened as neopterygians evolved from earlier actinopterygians. They first appeared in the late Permian period, before the time of dinosaurs. Neopterygians moved faster than their ancestors. Their scales and skeletons became lighter, and their jaws grew stronger and more efficient. Unlike other fish, neopterygians lost the ability to sense electricity, even though some later fish, like gymnotiformes and catfish, developed this sense again. A key development in neopterygians was gaining better control of their dorsal and anal fins. This improved their swimming. They also got changes in their skull, which helped them find new ways to feed and live in different habitats. These improvements made neopterygii the main group of fish, and thus, of vertebrates in general. Neopterygii includes teleosts, which are most of today’s fish.

Numidia existed from 202 BC to 40 BC and was located in what is now Algeria, a small part of Tunisia, and a small part of Libya in the Maghreb region. At first, it was divided into two areas: Massylii in the east and Masaesyli in the west. During the Second Punic War (218–201 BC), King Masinissa of the Massylii defeated Syphax of the Masaesyli and unified Numidia into one kingdom. The kingdom started as an independent state and later became either a Roman province or a Roman client state. At its largest extent, Numidia was bordered by the kingdom of Mauretania to the west, Africa Proconsularis (now part of Tunisia) to the east, the Mediterranean Sea to the north, and the Sahara to the south. It is seen as one of the first major states in Algerian and Berber history.
