Harads is a small village in Boden Municipality, Norrbotten County, Sweden, about 50 kilometers south of the Arctic Circle. It had 501 people living there in 2010. Harads is the main village in the Edefors parish. Edefors Church, built in 1928, is a key site in the municipality. The church was designed by John Åkerlund, an architect from Stockholm. It has a mix of styles, combining simplified Nordic classicism with more national romantic elements. It replaced an older church from 1888 that was destroyed by fire in 1918. Harads is also known for the Treehotel, created by entrepreneur Kent Lindvall in 2010. The hotel's rooms are built high in a pine forest, connected by walkways. Each room, designed by a different architect, has a unique name, like Mirrorcube, UFO, Blue Cone, and Bird's Nest. Lindvall believes the hotel's design is based on the idea of sustainability.

Angelo Peruzzi, born on February 16, 1970, is an Italian football coach and former goalkeeper. He won the Serie A Goalkeeper of the Year award three times. Currently, he is the team manager for Lazio. Peruzzi is seen as one of the best goalkeepers of his time in both Italy and globally. During his career, he played for several Italian clubs: Roma, Hellas Verona, Juventus, Internazionale, and Lazio. Peruzzi had a very successful time with Juventus, where he won three Serie A titles, the Coppa Italia, the UEFA Cup, and the UEFA Champions League. He also won a second Coppa Italia with Lazio before retiring from professional football in 2007. Internationally, Peruzzi played 31 times for Italy's national team, making his debut in 1995. He was part of the Italian team that won the 2006 FIFA World Cup. He also represented Italy in the 1992 Olympics, the 1996 UEFA Euro, and the 2004 UEFA Euro.

Alfred A. Bianchi was born on March 26, 1932, and died on October 28, 2019. He was from the United States. Alfred A. Bianchi worked in basketball as a player, coach, general manager, consultant, and scout.
Ambrières-les-Vallées is a town in the Mayenne department in western France. It is near Normandy.

Fernando James Ferrer was born on April 30, 1950. He is an American politician. From 1987 to 2001, he was the borough president of the Bronx. In 2001, he ran for mayor of New York City. In 2005, he was the Democratic Party candidate for mayor.

Montluçon is a town in central France, by the Cher River. It is the biggest town in the Allier department, but the department's main town, Moulins, is smaller. People who live there are called "montluçonnais." Montluçon is in the traditional region called Bourbonnais and was once part of a medieval duchy named Bourbon.

Hurricane Erin was the first hurricane to hit the United States since Hurricane Andrew in 1992. It was the fifth tropical cyclone, fifth named storm, and second hurricane of the very active 1995 Atlantic hurricane season. Erin started near the southeastern Bahamas on July 31 and moved northwest, becoming a Category 1 hurricane near Rum Cay about a day later. On August 1, Erin turned slightly north-northwest and moved over the northwestern Bahamas, including the Abaco Islands and Grand Bahama. Early on August 2, it hit Vero Beach, Florida, with winds of 85 mph (140 km/h). The hurricane weakened as it crossed Florida and became a tropical storm before entering the Gulf of Mexico later that day. Early on August 3, Erin became a Category 1 hurricane again and briefly strengthened to a Category 2. At Fort Walton Beach, Florida, it had maximum sustained winds of 100 mph (155 km/h). The storm weakened slightly before hitting Pensacola Beach, Florida, with winds of 85 mph (140 km/h) on August 3. After moving inland, it quickly became a tropical storm over Mississippi early on August 4, and then a tropical depression a few hours later. Erin moved northeast and then east across the eastern United States, eventually merging with a front in West Virginia on August 6. The outer bands of Erin caused seven deaths in Jamaica, five from a plane crash and two from lightning strikes. The Bahamas, particularly the islands between Mayaguana and Grand Bahama, were hit by the storm. Damage was generally minor, totaling about $400,000 (1995 USD). In Florida, wind speeds of up to 86 mph (138 km/h) were recorded at Sebastian Inlet, and gusts reached 101 mph (163 km/h) at Pensacola Naval Air Station. Over 1 million people lost electricity during the storm. More than 5,000 homes and buildings in Florida suffered some damage, mostly in Brevard County and the western Florida Panhandle. Nine deaths occurred in Florida, six from drowning and three from other causes. In Alabama, the storm damaged over 100 homes and 50 to 75 percent of pecan crops in Baldwin County. Other states reported minor flooding and wind damage. Overall, Hurricane Erin caused about $700 million in damage, mostly in Florida.

The Sea of Marmara, also called the Marmora Sea, connects the Black Sea and the Aegean Sea. It is inside Turkey and separates Turkey's Asian and European parts. It has straits called the Bosphorus and the Dardanelles. The Bosphorus also divides Istanbul into Asian and European sides. The Sea of Marmara is a small sea with an area of about 11,350 square kilometers and some dimensions. Its deepest part is about 4,150 meters deep.

Warcraft II: Beyond the Dark Portal is an expansion for a real-time strategy game. It was made by Blizzard Entertainment and Cyberlore Studios and came out in 1996. To play it, you need to have the original game first.

Jean-Michel Larrasket (1950-2018) was a French professor and engineer. He was also a vice president for the French Basque Country in the Basque Studies Society. He promoted projects to help the social and economic development of the French Basque Country. He was one of the founders of "Eticoop," a cooperative that encourages entrepreneurship in the area.

Ingram Olkin was born on July 23, 1924, and died on April 28, 2016. He was a professor and the chair of statistics and education at Stanford University and the Stanford Graduate School of Education. Olkin developed statistical methods to evaluate policies, especially in education. He also made important contributions to meta-analysis, statistics education, multivariate analysis, and majorization theory.

The People's Party was a political party in the United States. It was founded in 1971 by several smaller parties. It wanted to present an anti-war platform in elections. The People's Party ran for president twice. In 1972, Dr. Benjamin Spock, a doctor and author, was their candidate. In 1976, Margaret Wright was their candidate. Dr. Spock was also their vice presidential candidate. After the 1976 election, the party became a loose group. Most of its smaller founding parties also disappeared. The party's papers are now at the University of Missouri–St. Louis.

Ramo Peter Ceresino, born on April 24, 1929, and passed away on May 1, 2015, was a Canadian ice hockey player. He played as a left winger for the Toronto Maple Leafs, an NHL team. Ramo married Lorraine Giardetti on June 2, 1953, and they stayed married for 62 years. In 1962, Ramo moved his family to California and settled in Los Angeles. He worked as a mortgage broker there. Later, he retired to San Diego. He had three children, one of them named Gordon Ceresino.

tagetes is a group of plants that are either grown for one season or come back year after year. They are mostly green and leafy. Carl Linnaeus, a scientist, named this group in 1753. These plants are originally from southern Mexico, but some species now grow naturally in other places too. One type, called t. minuta, can be a problem in some areas because it grows too much.

China uses a single time zone, which is eight hours ahead of UTC. Even though China has five different geographical time zones, the whole country follows the same time. The official time is called "Beijing Time" in China and "China Standard Time" internationally. China stopped using daylight saving time in 1991.

Allosaurus is a type of meat-eating dinosaur from the late Jurassic period, about 155 to 145 million years ago. The name "allosaurus" means "different lizard." It was a large, two-legged predator with a big skull full of sharp teeth. Its forelimbs were small compared to its powerful hindlimbs, and it had a long, heavy tail for balance. Discovered in 1877 by Othniel Charles Marsh, allosaurus is one of the first well-known theropod dinosaurs, known outside paleontological circles. Allosaurus lived in North America and Portugal. For over 50 years, it was known as "antrodemus," but "allosaurus" became more famous after studying remains from the Cleveland-Lloyd Dinosaur Quarry. Allosaurus was one of the biggest predators in its ecosystem, feeding on large plant-eating dinosaurs like sauropods, stegosaurids, and ornithopods. Some scientists think allosaurus hunted in groups, while others believe they fought each other and gathered at carcasses.

Joseph Thomas Elliott Jr., born on August 1, 1959, is an English singer-songwriter, musician, record producer, and radio presenter. He is famous for being the lead singer and a founding member of the English rock band Def Leppard. Elliott has also sung as the lead in tribute bands for David Bowie's band, The Cybernauts, and Mott the Hoover's cover band, Down 'n' Outz. He is one of two original members of Def Leppard and has performed on every Def Leppard album. Known for his unique, raspy voice, he can sing over a wide range.

White Colne is a village and parish in Essex, England. It is on the north side of the River Colne, opposite Earls Colne, and on the Colchester road. It is 4 miles east-southeast of Halstead. White Colne has a long history, dating back to the Domesday Book. People lived in the area during the Paleolithic and Mesolithic eras. The village has a church dedicated to Saint Andrew. There is a railway station called White Colne on the Colne Valley and Halstead railway line. Anton Diffring, a German film actor, is buried in the churchyard.
Stapleford Tawney is a village and civil parish in Epping Forest, Essex, England. It is roughly southwest of Chipping Ongar and southwest of Chelmsford, the county town.
lignerolles is a commune in central France, in the Allier department.

Nadine Vanessa Dorries, born on May 21, 1957, is a British politician. She has been the minister for mental health, suicide prevention, and patient safety since 2019. Dorries is from the Conservative Party and has been representing Mid Bedfordshire as an MP since 2005. She is considered to be on the right side of the Conservative Party. Dorries grew up in Liverpool from a working-class family. She began her career as a nurse and later worked as a medical representative. She spent a year in Zambia as the head of a community school. After returning to the UK, she started a company called Kids Ltd, which provided childcare services for working parents. She sold the company in 1998. In 2005, Dorries won her seat in Parliament for Mid Bedfordshire during a general election, getting 11,355 more votes than the next candidate. As a new MP, she tried to pass some unsuccessful bills, such as changing the abortion time limit and rules for counseling. She also wanted girls to stay abstinent in sex education. Dorries was against John Bercow, the Speaker of the House of Commons, and tried to get him removed. She had disagreements with David Cameron and George Osborne, calling them "arrogant posh boys." In 2012, Dorries was suspended from the Conservative Party for participating in a reality TV show, "I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here!" without permission. In 2013, she was allowed back into the party. In July 2019, Boris Johnson appointed Dorries as the parliamentary under-secretary of state for the Department of Health and Social Care, focusing on mental health, suicide prevention, and patient safety. In February 2020, she was the first MP to be diagnosed with COVID-19 during the pandemic. In May of that year, she was promoted to the position of minister of state.

Abel Ferrara, born on July 19, 1951, is an American filmmaker. He makes movies with surprising and sometimes controversial themes. His films often use dark and city settings. He has been making independent films for a long time. Some of his well-known movies are "Ms. 45" from 1981, "King of New York" from 1990, "Bad Lieutenant" from 1992, and "The Funeral" from 1996.

Minnie Mouse is a cartoon character created by Ub Iwerks and Walt Disney. She and Mickey Mouse were first drawn in 1928. In a comic strip from 1942, Minnie's full name was given as Minerva Mouse, but this is not used often. In another comic strip from 1930, Minnie's father, Marcus Mouse, and her unnamed mother, were introduced. The same comic featured photos of Minnie's uncle, Milton Mouse, and his family, as well as her grandparents, Marvel and Matilda Mouse. However, her most well-known relatives are her uncle, Mortimer Mouse, and her twin nieces, Millie and Melody Mouse. Usually, just Melody appears. In many stories, Minnie is Mickey Mouse's girlfriend, a close friend of Daisy Duck, and a friend of Clarabelle Cow. In 2018, Minnie got her own star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.
Louis Réard, a French engineer and clothing designer, introduced the modern two-piece bikini in July 1946. He ran a bikini shop for 40 years.

Manchukuo was a state in northeast China and Inner Mongolia from 1932 to 1945. It was controlled by Japan. Before 1934, it was called Manchuria. In 1934, it became the Empire of Manchuria. Japan ruled it, but some people thought it was a real kingdom. Manchuria was home to the Manchus, including the last emperor of China. In 1931, Japan took control after an incident. They put a pro-Japan government in place with the last Qing emperor as a symbol of leadership. Manchukuo ended in 1945 when Japan lost World War II. The area was taken by the Soviet Union first, then given to China. Manchus made up a small part of the population. Han Chinese were the largest group. Koreans, Japanese, Mongols, and other groups lived there. Mongol areas had their own rules. Dalian on the Liaodong Peninsula stayed under Japanese control.

Jane Child, born on February 15, 1967, is a Canadian singer, songwriter, and record producer. She is famous for the song "Don't Want to Fall in Love." She also has a special and unusual fashion style, like spikes in her hair and long braids reaching her ankles. She also has a nose chain.

Pope Gregory XVI, born Bartolomeo Alberto Cappellari, was the leader of the Catholic Church and the Papal States from February 2, 1831, until his death in 1846. He took the name Mauro when he joined the Camaldolese religious order. Gregory XVI was very traditional and conservative. He opposed democratic and modern changes in the Papal States and across Europe, seeing them as a threat from revolutionaries. He worked to strengthen the power of the Papacy and supported religious and political authority (known as ultramontanism). In a document called "Mirari vos," he said that letting people choose their own beliefs was wrong. He also supported spreading Catholicism in other countries and opposed the slave trade. However, his strict rules, spending money a lot, and not taking care of people at home made him very unpopular. He was the last pope to use the name "Gregory" and the last non-bishop to become pope. Before Pope Francis in 2013, he was the last pope who was a member of a religious order.
returns, in economics and political economy, are payments given to people who provide goods or services.

Patrik Jonas Andersson, born on August 18, 1971, is a Swedish former football player who played as a defender. His father, Roy Andersson, and his younger brother, Daniel Andersson, also played professional football.

Colonization has been a global phenomenon throughout history. Ancient and medieval colonialism was practiced by the Phoenicians, Greeks, and Crusaders. Modern colonialism began during the "Age of Discovery," led by Portuguese and Spanish explorers who discovered the Americas and parts of Africa, the Middle East, India, and East Asia. The Portuguese and Spanish empires were the first global empires, expanding across continents and covering large areas. Between 1580 and 1640, both empires were ruled by Spanish monarchs. During the late 16th and 17th centuries, England, France, and the Dutch Republic also created their own overseas empires, competing with each other. In the late 18th and early 19th centuries, the first era of decolonization started. Most of the European colonies in the Americas, including those of Spain and France, gained independence. Britain, France, Portugal, and the Dutch focused on other areas, like South Africa, India, and Southeast Asia, where they already had coastal enclaves. The Second Industrial Revolution, in the 19th century, led to the "era of new imperialism." This period saw rapid colonization, especially the "scramble for Africa," involving Belgium, Germany, and Italy. Conflicts between colonial powers and revolutions in colonized areas shaped control and led to the establishment of independent nations. During the 20th century, the colonies of defeated World War I powers were given to victors as mandates. However, it wasn't until the end of World War II that the second phase of decolonization truly began.

World music is a category in Western music that includes many types of music from other parts of the world. It covers music that is considered ethnic, indigenous, or folk music, as well as music that mixes non-Western and Western popular traditions. While it doesn't have a clear definition, the idea of interest in different cultures is at its core. This term became popular in the 1980s for marketing non-Western traditional music. Now, it includes subgenres like ethnic fusion.

Ophthalmosauridae is an extinct family of ichthyosaurs from the Middle Jurassic to the Early Late Cretaceous. They lived in Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and South America. The oldest known ophthalmosaurid is "Mollesaurus" from Argentina. It lived during the early Bajocian period. "Mollesaurus" was named by George H. Baur in 1887. This includes basic ophthalmosaurid species like "Ophthalmosaurus." In 1956, Appleby named the group Ophthalmosauria, but this name is a synonym of Ophthalmosauridae, which has priority.

Everett Lee was born on August 31, 1916. He is an American conductor and violinist. He made history as the first African American to conduct a Broadway musical. He was also the first to lead an established symphony orchestra below the Mason-Dixon Line. Additionally, he conducted a performance by a major American opera company for the first time.

Rodney Adolphus Wilkes, born on March 11, 1925, and died on March 24, 2014, was a weightlifter from Trinidad and Tobago. Known as "the mighty midget," he became famous for winning a gold medal at the 1946 Central American and Caribbean Games in Barranquilla, Colombia. His best lifts included a press of 67.5 kg, a snatch of 62.5 kg, and a clean and jerk of 75 kg. In 1948, he went to the Olympics in London. He was the first athlete from Trinidad and Tobago to win an Olympic medal, getting a silver behind Mahmoud Fayad from Egypt. At the 1951 Pan American Games in Buenos Aires, Wilkes won the gold in the featherweight division. He went to the 1952 Olympics in Helsinki, winning the bronze medal behind two Soviet athletes, Rafael Chimishkyan and Nikolai Saksonov. After a short break, Wilkes returned in 1954 and won gold at the British Empire and Commonwealth Games in Vancouver. Four years later, he won bronze at the games in Cardiff. His last Olympic appearance was in 1956 in Melbourne, where he came in fourth place. He continued competing until 1960 but stopped when he missed the West Indies team for the 1960 Rome Olympics. After retiring, Wilkes worked as an electrician in his hometown of San Fernando, Trinidad and Tobago. He passed away in a San Fernando hospital in 2014 at the age of 89, due to prostate cancer.

Gorillaz are a British virtual band created in 1998 by Damon Albarn and Jamie Hewlett. The band has four animated members: 2-D, Murdoc Niccals, Noodle, and Russell Hobbs. They use music videos, interviews, and cartoons to show their world. Albarn is the only permanent musician, but they work with other artists too. In 2016, Remi Kabaka Jr. joined as the producer and became an official member. Albarn started Gorillaz with different kinds of music, like hip hop, electronic, and world music. Their first album, "Gorillaz," came out in 2001 and was very successful. Their second album, "Demon Days," in 2005, also did well. "Plastic Beach" in 2010 had more pop music and talk about the environment. Their fourth album, "The Fall," was released in 2010. "Humanz" came out in 2017 after a break. "The Now Now" in 2018 had simpler music. Their current project is "Song Machine," where they release new songs every month with different artists. Gorillaz have played in different ways, like hiding the live band or using computer graphics. They have won some awards and sold over 20 million records. They are the most successful virtual band, according to Guinness World Records.

Mortality rate is a way to measure how many deaths happen in a group of people, per year, for every 1,000 people. For example, if a population of 1,000 people has a mortality rate of 9.5, that means about 9.5 people out of 1,000 will die each year, or 0.95%. This is different from "morbidity," which talks about how often a disease appears or how many people have it. An important measure of mortality rate is the crude death rate, which looks at deaths from all causes in a certain time period for a specific population. For instance, the CIA estimates the global crude death rate is about 7.7 deaths per 1,000 people each year. Mortality rates can be calculated using a formula: (number of deaths / population size) × conversion factor. The conversion factor changes the result into a rate per 1,000 people, for example.

The Kama is a long river in Russia. It is the longest left tributary of the Volga and the largest in terms of water flow. At the place where the Kama meets the Volga, the Kama is even bigger than the Volga. The Kama begins in the Udmurt Republic, near Kuliga. It flows northwest for a distance, then turns northeast near Loyno and flows another distance. It then turns south and west in Perm Krai, going through the Udmurt Republic and the Republic of Tatarstan. In Tatarstan, the Kama joins the Volga. Before trains, people could travel between the Kama and the Northern Dvina and Pechora river basins. In the early 1800s, a canal called the Northern Ekaterininsky Canal connected the upper Kama with the Vychegda River, which is a tributary of the Northern Dvina. However, the canal was not used much and was mostly abandoned after a few years. The Kama river was featured in a 2013 Russian movie called "The Geographer Drank His Globe Away." A significant scene in the movie showed the challenging rapids of the Kama.

William Edgar Buchanan II was born on March 20, 1903, and passed away on April 4, 1979. He was an American actor who worked in both film and television for many years. Today, he is best known for his role as Uncle Joe Carson in the television shows "Petticoat Junction," "Green Acres," and "The Beverly Hillbillies," which were popular in the 1960s.

Steven Ralph Schirripa, born on September 3, 1957, is an American actor, producer, author, and voice artist. He is famous for playing Bobby Baccalieri in "The Sopranos" and Detective Anthony Abetemarco in "Blue Bloods." Schirripa produces and hosts two shows on Investigation Discovery: "Karma's a B*tch!" and "Nothing Personal." He was also a regular actor in "The Secret Life of the American Teenager." Schirripa voices the character Roberto in the "Open Season" movies. He has also appeared in commercials for Lamisil, Dick's Sporting Goods, and McDonald's.

Mamasani County is in Fars Province, Iran. Its capital, Nurabad, is 180 kilometers from Shiraz. People there speak Luri, a southern Luri dialect. In 2006, the county had 162,694 people, 45,145 families. Excluding some parts, the population was 166,317, in 26,011 families. Mamasani County has three districts: central, Mahvarmilani, and Doshman Ziar. It includes three cities: Nurabad, Khumeh Zar, and Baba Monir. Mamasani is home to the ancient Luri tribe and its many sub-tribes. This tribe lives in Iran, Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Iraq. The main Luri tribe in Iran is in Mamasani County, Fars Province. Another group, Sistani Mamasanis, lives in Sistan and Baluchistan. Muhammad Hasani Mamasanis are in Baluchistan, Iran, Pakistan, and Afghanistan’s Nimrus and Helmand regions.

The Arrondissement of Perpignan is in France, in the Pyrénées- Orientales department, which is in the Occitanie region. Northern Catalonia is another name for this area. It includes 39 towns. In 2016, it had about 285,077 people.

Rameswaram is a town in Tamil Nadu, India. It is on an island called Pamban, separated from the mainland by the Pamban Channel. The town is about 40 kilometers from Mannar Island in Sri Lanka and is located at the tip of the Indian peninsula in the Gulf of Mannar. Rameswaram is connected to the mainland by the Pamban Bridge. It is a major railway station and the end of a train line from Chennai and Madurai. Rameswaram is very holy for Hindus and part of the Char Dham pilgrimage. According to the Ramayana, Rama and his companion Hanuman built a bridge to Sri Lanka to rescue Rama's wife Sita. The Ramanathaswamy temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva, is central to the town and important for Shaiva pilgrims. Rameswaram is the nearest point in India to Sri Lanka, and some say it was once connected by land. The town has been in the news due to the Setusamudram shipping canal project, Kachchatheevu issues, and reports of local fishermen being captured by Sri Lankan forces. Rameswaram has been a municipality since 1994. In 2011, it had 44,856 people living in an area of about 6 square kilometers. Most people work in tourism or fishing.
Wolfgang Feiersinger was born on January 30, 1965. He is from Austria and played football as a defender. He is now retired.

Lil' Kim's "La Bella Mafia" is her third album. It came out on March 4, 2003, through Atlantic Records. The album started strong, reaching number five on the US Billboard 200 chart. In the United States, it sold more than one million copies, making it platinum, and worldwide, it sold over two million copies. Critics praised the album, highlighting Kim's skill and strong presence. Two songs from the album did well on music charts. "The Jump Off" hit number 17 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and reached number 16 in the UK. "Magic Stick," featuring 50 Cent, peaked at number two on the Billboard Hot 100. "Magic Stick" and "Came Back for You" got Kim nominated for Grammy Awards.

Priscilla Moran was an American actress who worked in silent films. She was born on November 23, 1917, in Sedalia, Missouri. She began her acting career in 1922 and stopped in 1937, when she was 20 years old. During her career, she appeared in 14 films.
This NHL player list includes players who have played at least one game from 1917 to now and have last names starting with "M". The list was updated for the 2018–19 NHL season.

Arianism is a belief that Jesus Christ is the son of God, created by God the Father, and is different from the Father. However, the son is also considered god. This belief first appeared with a man named Arius, who lived in Alexandria, Egypt. People called this group "Arians" because of Arius. The Arian belief was against other Christians who believed that the Father and Son were the same in nature. Arianism suggested that Jesus did not exist forever but was created by God the Father. There was a disagreement about whether Jesus was divine in the same way as God. One group, called Homoousians, believed in the Trinity. The other, Arians, believed differently. Both groups tried to explain their ideas. At first, both beliefs were seen as correct, but later, there were arguments about which was the true Christian belief. The First Council of Nicaea, called by Emperor Constantine in 325, declared Arianism a heresy. However, ten years later, Constantine supported Arian bishops, including Eusebius of Nicomedia. In 335, Constantine called a meeting of 310 bishops to discuss Athanasius, who was accused of various crimes. Athanasius was sent away, and Arianism was still seen as a heresy. Later, in 381, Athanasius and other leaders met again at the First Council of Constantinople with 150 bishops. Arianism was condemned once more. Some rulers and leaders, like Constantius II, Valens, and Odoacer, supported Arianism. It spread in places like Italy, Spain, and North Africa. Other nontrinitarian beliefs, like Semi-Arianism, also existed during this time, with different views on Jesus' nature.

Marc Angéle Vanderlinden, or van der Linden, was born on February 4, 1964, in Merksem. He is a former Belgian footballer. He started his career with SC Merksem, a local team. In 1982, he joined Royal Antwerp FC. After seven seasons there, he moved to R.S.C. Anderlecht in 1989. Two years later, he went to K.A.A. Gent. In 1995, he played in Israel for Hapoel Ironi Rishon Lezion F.C. and then Hapoel Herzliya F.C. He returned to Merksem in 1997 and continued to play there until 2002 when he retired. He played 19 times for the Belgium national football team, scoring nine goals. He was also part of the 1990 FIFA World Cup.

In physics, specifically in celestial mechanics, escape velocity is the minimum speed needed for an object to leave the gravitational pull of a massive body. This means the object will go very far away and never come back. Escape velocity depends on the mass of the body and its distance from the center. For a rocket, it can escape without reaching this speed because it keeps getting more speed from expelling its fuel. It can escape at any speed, given enough fuel and propulsion. The escape velocity from Earth’s surface is about 11.2 kilometers per second. It's the speed at which an object's kinetic and gravitational energy equal zero. Once an object achieves escape velocity, it will keep moving away, slowing down but never stopping. The escape velocity from Earth is around 11.2 kilometers per second. Once it's achieved, the object will keep moving away, slowing down but never stopping. The distance to Earth will get bigger and bigger, and the object will never return. The formula to find the escape velocity from a massive body, like a planet or star, is: \[ v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times G \times m}{r}} \] where \( v_e \) is the escape velocity, \( G \) is the universal gravitational constant, \( m \) is the mass of the massive body, and \( r \) is the distance from the center of the massive body. If an object starts from infinity and falls towards a massive body, it will hit the body with the same speed as its escape velocity. If given a speed higher than the escape velocity, the object will move away, slow down, and approach zero speed as it moves infinitely away, never returning. Atmospheric drag and other forces are not considered in these calculations.

Lichtervelde is a municipality in the Belgian province of West Flanders. It includes only the town of Lichtervelde. On January 1, 2006, Lichtervelde had 8,400 people. The town covers 25. 93 square kilometers, making the population density 324 people per square kilometer. There is a church that is 64 meters tall. A famous inventor, Charles Joseph van Depoele, was born in this town.
Plains is a town and the county seat of Yoakum County in western Texas, United States. It is in the southern part of the Panhandle. The population was 1,481 in 2010.
Gillespie is a city in Macoupin County, Illinois, in the United States. It is part of the Metro East region of the St. Louis area. In 2010, the population was 3,319.

Bernard Verlhac, known as Tignous, was a French cartoonist. He worked for the French satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo for a long time. Tignous was killed on January 7, 2015, during the Charlie Hebdo shooting.

This list covers only domestic cat breeds and mixes of domestic cats with wild cats. It includes breeds officially recognized by cat registries, new breeds, and those being developed into official breeds. It also mentions distinct domestic populations that are not actively being bred, and extinct breeds. As of 2019, TICA recognizes 71 breeds, CFA 44, and FIFE 43. Differences in breed classification mean a cat could be considered a different breed in different registries, depending on its background. For instance, TICA’s Himalayan is seen as a type of Persian by CFA, while the Javanese (or Colorpoint Longhair) is a variation of the Balinese in both TICA and CFA. WCF groups these into a single "mega-breed" called Colorpoint. Similarly, the term "Colorpoint Longhair" can refer to different breeds in other registries. Many cat breed names come from Western breeders who choose exotic-sounding terms, often unrelated to the breeds' origins. Examples include Balinese, Javanese, and Himalayan. The domestic short-haired and domestic long-haired cats are not breeds but terms used to describe mixed breeds based on coat length. Some registries allow them to be bred, and they have been used to create other breeds. They should not be confused with official breeds that share similar names, like the British Shorthair and Oriental Longhair.

The Rubik's Revenge, also known as the Master Cube, is a 4×4×4 version of the Rubik's cube. It came out in 1981. It was invented by Péter Sebestény. It was almost named the Sebestény cube but the name was changed right before release to appeal to people who liked the original Rubik's cube. Unlike the original cube and some other odd-numbered cubes, the Rubik's Revenge has movable center pieces. You can't use the center pieces to identify the colors, as they can move to different positions. However, methods to solve the 3×3×3 cube can work for the edges and corners of the 4×4×4 cube, as long as you correctly identify the colors.
The middle angles were an important group in Mercia, a larger kingdom in England during the Anglo-Saxon period.

Robert Michael Schneider, born on October 31, 1963, is an American actor, comedian, screenwriter, and director. He performed stand-up comedy and was part of the NBC show "Saturday Night Live." He has acted in several comedy films, including "The Animal," "The Hot Chick," "The Benchwarmers," and "Grown Ups." Schneider is the father of singer Elle King.

Alexander Smart was born on May 29, 1918, and died on April 18, 2005. He was a Canadian ice hockey player who played as a forward. He played one season for the Montreal Canadiens in the National Hockey League. Most of his career, however, was in the Quebec Senior Hockey League.

Charles Anthony Ryan Silvera, known as Swede, was born on October 13, 1924, and died on September 7, 2019. He was an American who played baseball in the Major League and also coached. He was part of six World Series championships with the New York Yankees.

Hamilton County is in the southwestern part of Ohio. As of 2010, it had 802,374 people, making it the third largest county in Ohio. The main city is Cincinnati, which is also the county seat. Hamilton County is named after Alexander Hamilton, the first U.S. Secretary of the Treasury. The county is part of the Cincinnati-Middletown metropolitan area.
Palmer is a city in Washington County, Kansas, United States. In 2010, the city had 111 people living there.

Norman Steven Maciver, born on September 1, 1964, is from Canada. He used to play ice hockey professionally and is now an assistant general manager for the Chicago Blackhawks in the NHL. As a player, he played defense for six different NHL teams over thirteen years.

Hiragana and katakana are both kana systems. Each syllable in Japanese is represented by one character or a pair of characters in these systems. This can be a vowel like "a" (hiragana あ), a consonant followed by a vowel like "ka" (か), or a nasal sound that can sound like "m," "n," or "ng." Because kana characters represent syllables rather than single consonants (except for "n"), they are called syllabic symbols. Hiragana is used to write suffixes (okurigana) that follow kanji, such as verb endings. It also writes particles, miscellaneous native words, and some kanji when the meaning is unclear or formal. Authors may choose to use hiragana for an informal tone. Hiragana can also be used for furigana, which are small readings next to kanji to show their pronunciation. Hiragana has two main ordering systems: the old iroha ordering and the more common gojūon ordering.
San Diego is a city in Texas, United States. It is mainly in Duval County and is the county seat. The population was 4,488 in 2010.

Michel Suleiman was born on November 21, 1948. He was the president of Lebanon from 2008 to 2014. Before becoming president, Suleiman was the commander of the Lebanese Armed Forces from 1998 to 2008. He replaced Emile Lahoud as commander of the Lebanese Armed Forces in December 1998. Suleiman then became president and was officially sworn in on May 25, 2008.

Ivan's Childhood, sometimes called My Name Is Ivan in the US, is a 1962 Soviet war drama film. Andrei Tarkovsky directed it and co-wrote it with Mikhail Papava, with uncredited input from Tarkovsky himself. The film is based on Vladimir Bogomolov's 1957 short story "Ivan." In the film, child actor Nikolai Burlyayev plays Ivan, an orphan whose parents were killed by German forces during World War II. The film also stars Valentin Zubkov, Evgeny Zharikov, Stepan Krylov, Nikolai Grinko, and Tarkovsky's wife Irma Raush. Ivan's Childhood tells the story of an orphaned boy named Ivan during World War II. Unlike many films of that time, it focuses on the human cost of war and does not glorify the war experience. In a 1962 interview, Tarkovsky said he wanted to show his hatred of war and chose childhood because it contrasts most with war. This was Tarkovsky's first feature film. It gained him critical acclaim and made him known internationally. The film won the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival and the Golden Gate Award at the San Francisco International Film Festival in 1962. Although it was nominated for the best foreign language film at the 1962 Academy Awards, it was not accepted as a nominee. Famous filmmakers, including Ingmar Bergman, Sergei Parajanov, and Krzysztof Kieślowski, praised the film and cited it as an influence on their work.
Sannes is a commune in Vaucluse department, which is in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region in southeastern France.

Linux Mint is a community-driven Linux distribution based on Ubuntu or Debian. It includes many free and open-source applications. Users can choose to add some proprietary software, like multimedia codecs, by ticking one box during installation. This provides full multimedia support. The project was started by Clément Lefèbvre and is developed by the Linux Mint team and community.

Crooked Island is an island and district. It is part of a group of Bahamian islands. These islands form a large, shallow lagoon called the Bight of Acklins. The largest islands in this group are Crooked Island in the north and Acklins in the south-east. There are also smaller islands, like Long Cay (formerly known as Fortune Island) in the north-west, and Castle Island in the south.

Vientiane is the capital and largest city of Laos. It is located near the Mekong River, close to the border with Thailand. Vientiane became the capital in 1573 because of worries about a Burmese invasion. It was later attacked and destroyed in 1827 by the Siamese (Thais). During French rule, Vientiane was the administrative capital. Due to recent economic growth, it is now Laos's main economic center. The city had 820,000 people as of the 2015 census. Vientiane is famous for That Luang, a major national monument that is a symbol of Laos and a key Buddhist icon. Other important Buddhist temples can also be found there, like Haw Phra Kaew, which used to house the Emerald Buddha. The city hosted the 25th Southeast Asian Games in December 2009, marking 50 years since the games began.
A crescent is a shape that represents the moon. It may also refer to:

Our Band Could Be Your Life: Scenes from the American Indie Underground, 1981–1991 is a book by Michael Azerrad. The book tells the stories of some underground rock bands. These bands didn't get much attention from mainstream music, but they were very important in making American alternative and indie rock popular. They achieved this by touring almost constantly and releasing records on small, local independent record labels. Azerrad spoke with many band members and also read old fanzines, as well as mainstream newspapers and books to research their history.

Everland is South Korea's biggest theme park. It is in Yongin, a city in Gyeonggi-do. Everland gets about 5. 85 million visitors each year and was the 19th most visited park in the world in 2018. The park has attractions, a zoo, and a water park called Caribbean Bay. Everland is run by Samsung C&T Corporation, part of the Samsung Group. The park used to be called "Jayeon Nongwon," which means "Natural Farm." Its old English name was "Farmland."

Dr. Strangelove, or How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb, is a 1964 black comedy film. It makes fun of fears during the Cold War about a nuclear war between the Soviet Union and the United States. The movie was directed and written by Stanley Kubrick. Peter Sellers, George C. Scott, Sterling Hayden, and Slim Pickens acted in it. The filming took place in the United Kingdom. It was based on Peter George's book Red Alert from 1958. The story is about a crazy U.S. Air Force general who starts a nuclear attack on the Soviet Union. Meanwhile, the U.S. president, his advisors, military leaders, and a British officer try to stop the plane from bombing the Soviets and causing a big nuclear disaster. Many people think it is one of the best comedies and one of the greatest films ever made. In 1998, the American Film Institute ranked it 26th among the best American movies (in 2007, it was 39th). In 2000, it was the third funniest American film. In 1989, the U.S. Library of Congress preserved it as one of the first 25 films with cultural, historical, or aesthetic importance.

Warendorf is a district in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is in the northern part of the state. Neighboring districts include Steinfurt, Osnabrück, Gütersloh, Soest, Hamm, Coesfeld, and Münster, which are all district-free cities.

Frank Cloud Cooksey was born on June 3, 1933. He is an American public servant. In the 1950s, he was the president of the student body at the University of Texas. He worked as an attorney in different places: the Civil Rights Division of the U.S. District Attorney, the Texas Attorney General's office under John Hill, and in private practice. He was the mayor of Austin, Texas, from 1985 to 1988. He is also an environmental activist, and is known for being progressive during his time as mayor.

Zonia Baber, born Mary Arizona Baber on August 24, 1862, in Clark County, Illinois, lived until January 10, 1956. She was an American geographer and geologist. Baber is famous for creating ways to teach geography. Her teachings focused on learning by doing, especially through field work and experiments.

José Hugo Garaycoa Hawkins was born on June 2, 1930, in Peru. He became a priest in 1961. From 1982 to 1991, he worked as a bishop in Peru. Specifically, he was the auxiliary bishop of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Lima. After that, from 1991 to 2006, he served as the bishop of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Tacna y Moquegua in Peru. He passed away on March 27, 2018.

The London, Brighton and South Coast Railway (LB&SCR) was a railway company in the United Kingdom from 1846 to 1922. It covered an area shaped like a triangle. London was at the top, the whole coast of Sussex was at the bottom, and much of Surrey was in between. It bordered the London and South Western Railway (L&SWR) on the west side. The L&SWR provided a different route to Portsmouth. On the east side, the LB&SCR was next to the South Eastern Railway (SER). The SER later became part of the South Eastern and Chatham Railway (SE&CR) and offered routes to Bexhill, St Leonards-on-Sea, and Hastings. The LB&SCR had the shortest routes from London to several seaside towns on the south coast, like Brighton, Eastbourne, Worthing, Littlehampton, and Bognor Regis. It also served the ports of Newhaven and Shoreham-by-Sea. The railway connected to inland towns and cities such as Chichester, Horsham, East Grinstead, and Lewes. It shared routes with Croydon, Tunbridge Wells, Dorking, and Guildford. At the London end, there were many railway lines coming from London Bridge and Victoria. The LB&SCR was created by merging five smaller companies in 1846. In 1921, it joined with the L&SWR, SE&CR, and some smaller railway companies. They formed the Southern Railway on January 1, 1923.

The Colombo crime family is the youngest of the five families that control organized crime in New York City. It is part of the American mafia. Joseph Profaci started this family in 1928 with a bootlegging gang. Profaci was in charge until the late 1950s. The family had three major internal conflicts. The first war happened in the late 1950s when Joe Gallo rebelled against Profaci. But it slowed down after Gallo was arrested and Profaci died of cancer in the early 1960s. In 1960, Joseph Colombo took control. In 1971, a second war began after Gallo was released from prison and shot Colombo. Colombo's supporters, led by Carmine Persico, won this war by 1975 when the remaining Gallo members went to the Genovese family. From 1975 to 1991, the family was peaceful. In 1991, a third and bloodiest war broke out. Victor Orena tried to take power from the imprisoned Carmine Persico. This split the family into two groups loyal to Orena and Persico. This lasted two years, until 1993. It ended with 12 family members dead and Orena in prison. Persico became the boss again. Persico ran the family until 2019, but the family never recovered from the war. In the 2000s, many family members were caught in federal cases and became informants. Many think the Colombo family is the weakest of the five New York City families. Carmine Persico died in prison on March 7, 2019.

Prunella Margaret Rumney West Scales, born on June 22, 1932, is an English actress. She is famous for playing Basil Fawlty's wife, Sybil, in the BBC comedy "Fawlty Towers." She also acted as Queen Elizabeth II in "A Question of Attribution," a 1991 BBC production by Alan Bennett, for which she was nominated for a BAFTA award.
Beyrie-en-Béarn is a village in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department, located in southwestern France.

Achim Mentzel was born on July 15, 1946, in Berlin, and died on January 4, 2016, in Cottbus. He was a German musician, TV host, and actor. Mentzel was famous for his TV show "Achim's Hit Parade" from 1989 to 2006, and he worked with Oliver Kalkofe on "Kalkofe's Record Player." He made 23 singles and 7 albums between 1978 and 2010. He was also part of a cover band called Fritzens Dampferband with Nina Hagen. Mentzel appeared in films like "The Legend of Paul and Paula" (1973) and "The Wixxer" (2004), and in TV shows "Das Amt" and "Leipzig Homicide." He got married four times and had eight children. Mentzel was 69 years old when he died due to a heart attack or stroke.

Age Fridtjof Hareide, born on September 23, 1953, is a Norwegian football manager. He recently led the Denmark national football team. In his playing career, he played for Hødd and Molde in Norway, and Manchester City and Norwich City in England. He was also a national player, getting 50 caps for Norway. As a coach, Hareide won league titles in all Scandinavian countries. He won with Helsingborgs IF in Sweden in 1999, Malmö FF in 2014, Brøndby in Denmark in 2001-02, and Rosenborg in Norway in 2003. Hareide managed the Norway national team from 2003 to 2008.

Arsène Lupin is a made-up gentleman who steals things and can change his appearance. He was created in 1905 by a French writer named Maurice Leblanc. At first, his name was Arsène Lopin, but he changed it because a local politician had the same name. Leblanc first introduced Lupin in a series of short stories in a magazine called "Je Sais Tout." The first story came out on July 15, 1905. Lupin appeared in 17 novels and 39 short stories written by Leblanc, which were later collected into 24 books. If you count a 1923 novel called "The Secret Tomb," there are 25 books in total. In this novel, Lupin does not appear, but the main character, Dorothée, solves one of Lupin's four fantastic secrets. The character of Lupin has also been in many books by other writers, as well as films, TV shows, stage plays, and comic books. In the 1970s, two famous mystery writers, Boileau and Narcejac, wrote five books that continue the story of Lupin.

Tuili is a "municipality" in South Sardinia, which is in Italy. It is located north of Cagliari and northeast of Sanluri. Tuili borders these municipalities: Barumini, Gesturi, Las Plassas, Pauli Arbarei, Setzu, and Turri.

Bussigny-sur-Oron was a former municipality in the district of Lavaux-Ovron, in the canton of Vaud, Switzerland. On January 1, 2012, Bussigny-sur-Oron joined with châtillens, chesalles-sur-Oron, ecoteaux, oron-la-ville, oron-le-châtel, palézieux, les tavernes, les thioleyres, and vuibroye to form the new municipality of Oron.

Jack Klugman, born on April 27, 1922, and died on December 24, 2012, was an American actor. He started acting in 1950. In 1957, he acted in "12 Angry Men," and in 1958, in "Cry Terror!" In the 1960s, he appeared in many TV shows. He won his first Primetime Emmy for his role in "The Defenders" in 1964. He was also in "The Twilight Zone" four times from 1960 to 1963. In 1965, he took over the role of Oscar Madison from Walter Matthau in "The Odd Couple." He played the same character in a TV show from 1970 to 1975, opposite Tony Randall. He also played Henry Willows in "You Again?" from 1986 to 1987. Klugman won two more Primetime Emmys and a Golden Globe for "The Odd Couple." From 1976 to 1983, he was the main actor in "Quincy, M.E.," for which he was nominated four times for Primetime Emmy Awards.

Alain Emile Louis Marie Poher was born on April 17, 1909, and died on December 9, 1996. He was a French centrist politician. He first worked with the Popular Republican Movement and later joined the Democratic Centre. Poher was a senator for Val-de-Marne from 1946 to 1995. He was the president of the Senate from October 3, 1968, to October 1, 1992. During his time as president of the Senate, he served as a temporary president of France twice. In 1969, he was a main candidate for the presidency but lost to Georges Pompidou in the second round of voting.

Cipriano de Rore, sometimes called Cypriano, lived from about 1515 or 1516 to between September 11 and 20, 1565. He was a composer from France and Flanders during the Renaissance. He worked in Italy and was a key figure in the generation of composers who moved to Italy after Josquin des Prez. He was also one of the top composers of madrigals in the mid-16th century. His music was experimental, used a lot of chromatic tones, and was very expressive. His style had a big impact on how madrigals developed after him.

Luis Maldonado Venegas was a Mexican politician and lawyer who lived from November 19, 1956, to April 30, 2019. He was a member of the Party of the Democratic Revolution. Maldonado served as a federal deputy in the LXIII legislature of the Mexican Congress. He represented Mexico City and the fourth electoral region. Additionally, he was the national president of the Convergencia political party and was involved in both houses of Congress.

Abigail Kathleen Breslin, born on April 14, 1996, is an American actress and singer. She grew up in New York City. Breslin started acting in commercials when she was three. She was in her first movie, "Signs," at age five, in a science fiction horror film by M. Night Shyamalan. She got a Young Artist Award nomination for this role. After playing in movies like "Raising Helen" and "The Haunted Tree" in 2004, she got great reviews for her part as Olive Hoover in "Little Miss Sunshine" in 2006. For this, she was nominated for Screen Actors Guild, BAFTA, and Academy Awards. She won the Screen Actors Guild award for best cast in a movie and Critics' Choice Movie Award for best young performer. Breslin became known as a top child actress with roles in "No Reservations" in 2007, where she was nominated for Critics' Choice Award, "Nim's Island" and "Definitely, Maybe" both in 2008, "My Sister's Keeper" in 2009, "Zombieland" and "Rango" both in 2011, "The Call" in 2013, and "Star Trek Into Darkness" also in 2013, where she got a Screen Actors Guild Award nomination. She also starred in "Ender's Game" in 2013 and "A Star Is Born" in 2019. Between 2015 and 2016, Breslin acted in the horror-comedy TV show "Scream Queens" on Fox, her first regular role on TV.

Boyd County is in Nebraska. In 2010, there were 2,099 people living there. The main town is called Butte. Boyd County became a county in 1891 and was named after James E. Boyd, who was Nebraska's governor at that time. In 1922, Boyd County's license plate started with 63. At the 2010 census, there were only a few small towns with very few people. Anoka had 6 people, Gross had 2 people, and Monowi had just 1 person. Monowi was the only town in the United States with just one person living there in 2010.
Kurt Paul Schmitt was born on October 7, 1886, in Heidelberg. He died on November 2, 1950, in Heidelberg. He was a German economic leader and served as the Reich Economy Minister.

Plymouth County is in Massachusetts, U.S. The 2010 census showed a population of 494, 919. The county seats are Plymouth and Brockton. In 1685, Plymouth County was created by the Plymouth General Court, the legislature of Plymouth Colony, before it joined the Massachusetts Bay Colony. Plymouth County is part of the Boston-Cambridge-Newton metropolitan area.
pectinina is a group for saltwater clams. These clams belong to a suborder called pectinina, which is part of a larger group named pectinida. Pectinida is in the order of marine bivalve molluscs.

The Spanish treasure fleet, also known as the West Indies fleet, was a group of ships that transported goods between Spain and its American territories from 1566 to 1790. These ships carried many items like food, wood, metals, including silver and gold, jewels, pearls, spices, sugar, tobacco, silk, and other items from the Spanish colonies to Spain. Goods like oil, wine, cloth, books, and tools were sent from Spain to the colonies. This fleet was the first permanent trade route between the Atlantic. Similarly, the Manila galleons were the first permanent trade route in the Pacific.

Mclaren Racing Limited is a British racing team based at the Mclaren Technology Centre in Woking, Surrey, England. They are famous for racing in Formula One and have also competed in American open wheel racing. Mclaren won the Canadian-American Challenge Cup (Can-Am) sports car racing championship. The team is the second oldest and second most successful Formula One team after Ferrari, having won races, 12 drivers' championships, and eight constructors' championships. It is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Mclaren Group. Mclaren was founded by Bruce McLaren from New Zealand in 1963. They won their first grand prix at the 1968 Belgian Grand Prix and were dominant in Can-Am from 1967 to 1971. They also won the Indianapolis 500 twice, in 1972 and 1974. After Bruce McLaren died in 1970, Teddy Mayer took over. They won their first Formula One constructors' championship in 1974, with Emerson Fittipaldi and James Hunt as drivers. That year also marked the start of a long-standing sponsorship by Philip Morris's Marlboro cigarette brand. In 1981, Mclaren merged with Ron Dennis's Project Four Racing. Dennis became the team principal and took full control. This began their most successful era. With Porsche and Honda engines, Niki Lauda, Alain Prost, and Ayrton Senna won seven drivers' championships, and the team took six constructors' championships. Prost and Senna were particularly dominant, winning all but one race in 1988. Later, their rivalry led to Prost leaving for Ferrari. During this period, the English team Williams offered the most consistent challenge. The two teams won every constructors' title between 1988 and 1992. By the mid-1990s, Honda withdrew from Formula One, Senna moved to Williams, and Mclaren went three seasons without a win. With Mercedes-Benz engines, West sponsorship, and Adrian Newey from Williams as a designer, Mclaren won further championships with Mika Häkkinen. During the 2000s, Mclaren were consistent front-runners, and Lewis Hamilton won their latest title in 2008. Ron Dennis retired as team principal in 2009, handing over to long-time Mclaren employee Martin Whitmarsh. However, after the team's worst season since 2004 in 2013, Whitmarsh was removed. In 2013, Mclaren announced they would use Honda engines from 2015 onwards, replacing Mercedes-Benz. They raced as Mclaren Honda for the first time since 1992 at the 2015 Australian Grand Prix. In 2017, Mclaren returned to the Indianapolis 500 as a partner to Andretti Autosport. They announced in August 2019 that they would run in the full IndyCar series with Arrow Schmidt Peterson Motorsports, starting in 2020. The combined entry would be named Arrow McLaren SP.

Flushing is a neighborhood in the middle part of the New York City borough of Queens. It's the fourth-largest business area in the city. The downtown area, which is busy with shops and stores, is near Main Street and Roosevelt Avenue. This area is the third-busiest in the city, after Times Square and Herald Square. Flushing started as a settlement on October 10, 1645. It was called Vlissingen, named after a city in the Netherlands. In 1664, the English took over New Amsterdam, and when Queens County was created in 1683, the town of Flushing was one of the first towns in Queens. In 1898, Flushing joined New York City. In the early 1900s, the area grew because of new bridges and public transportation. Many immigrants, mainly Chinese and Korean people, moved to Flushing in the late 1900s. There are many smaller neighborhoods in Flushing, and it has a mix of different groups of people living there. The area has train stations and subway stops. Flushing is in Queens Community District 7 and has zip codes 11354, 11355, and 11358. The New York City Police Department’s 109th Precinct patrols the area.
maspie-lalonquère-juillacq is a commune in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department in southwestern France.
Hydro is a town in Oklahoma. It is located in Caddo and Blaine counties. According to the 2010 census, the town had 969 people.

A doctor of science degree, often shortened to Sc.D., D.Sc., S.D., or D.S., is an academic research degree given in many countries. In some places, a doctor of science is the regular science doctorate. In other countries, it is a higher doctorate, meaning a more advanced degree. It is awarded for a big, long-lasting contribution to science. Sometimes, it is given as an honorary degree.

In South Africa, rivers often have the word "rivier" in their names, which comes from Afrikaans. Another common ending is "-kamma," from a Khoisan word for "river." Sometimes, the English word "river" is also added. Zulu uses the word "amanzi" for water, which is part of some river names. In Afrikaans, "spruit" means small river, like a stream.

Return to Never Land is a 2002 American animated movie about Peter Pan. It's a sequel to the 1953 film and is based on J. M. Barrie's 1911 novel. The movie was produced by Walt Disney Television Animation and released by Walt Disney Pictures, with distribution by Buena Vista Pictures. It came out on February 15, 2002. The film made $115 million worldwide. Critics say it has forgettable songs and a weak story. The story is about Wendy's daughter who doesn't believe in Peter Pan's stories during the London Blitz. By mistake, she is brought to Never Land by the pirates. To go back home, she meets Peter Pan, Tinker Bell, and the Lost Boys. They help her learn to fly and believe in the stories.

Elizabeth I ruled England and Ireland from 1558 to 1603. Sometimes called the Virgin Queen, she was the last of the Tudor monarchs. She was the daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn. Anne was executed two years after Elizabeth's birth. Henry then annulled his marriage to Anne, making Elizabeth illegitimate. Her half-brother Edward VI ruled until 1553, leaving the throne to Lady Jane Grey and ignoring his half-sisters Mary and Elizabeth. Mary became queen and had Lady Jane Grey removed. During Mary's reign, Elizabeth was briefly imprisoned. In 1558, Elizabeth became queen after Mary's death. She relied on trusted advisers, led by William Cecil. She established England's Protestant church, becoming its supreme governor. Elizabeth remained unmarried and never had children. She was succeeded by her cousin, James VI of Scotland. Elizabeth tried to avoid war, maintaining a balance with France and Spain. She supported some military campaigns, but they were not successful. In the 1580s, England went to war with Spain. In 1588, England defeated the Spanish Armada. Elizabeth was known for her virginity and was celebrated in art and literature. Her rule, known as the Elizabethan era, saw the rise of English drama and naval power. Some saw her as a good ruler, while others thought she was sometimes indecisive. Towards the end of her reign, Elizabeth faced economic and military problems. However, her long rule provided stability to England and helped shape its identity.

Jonathan Edgar Nichols was an American politician. He was born on November 14, 1965, and died on June 5, 2019. Nichols served in the Oklahoma Senate from 2000 to 2012. He was part of the Republican Party. Before that, Nichols worked as a lawyer and was an assistant district attorney.

Morgan County is in the central part of Missouri, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 20, 565 people. The county seat is Versailles. Morgan County was created on January 5, 1833, and was named after General Daniel Morgan from the American Revolutionary War.

Friedrich Hermann Hund was a German physicist born on February 4, 1896, and died on March 31, 1997. He was from Karlsruhe and is known for studying atoms and molecules.

freethe20 is a campaign to highlight women who are political prisoners worldwide. The campaign focuses on twenty women who are unjustly imprisoned. Samantha Power, the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, started the campaign to mark the twentieth anniversary of the Beijing Declaration. The goal is to ask governments to stop imprisoning women and to support the women and their families. The campaign announced one woman per day for twenty days, starting from the anniversary of the Beijing Declaration. In September 2015, a bipartisan "freethe20" bill was introduced to the U.S. Senate. All twenty female senators from both major political parties supported the bill.

Siġġiewi, also known as Città Ferdinand, is a city and local council in southern Malta. It is the third largest council in Malta by size, after Rabat and Mellieħa. Located on a plateau, it is a few kilometers away from Mdina, the old capital, and Valletta, the current capital. As of March 2014, it had 8,367 people living there. In the past, most people in Siġġiewi worked in nearby fields. The city chose the motto "labore et virtute" meaning "work and virtue" in 1993.

Hot Spring County is a county in Arkansas, U.S. In 2010, it had 32, 923 people. The county seat is Malvern. Hot Spring County was created on November 2, 1829, from part of Clark County. It was named for the hot springs in Hot Springs, Arkansas, which moved to Garland County in 1874. Today, Hot Spring County doesn't allow alcohol. It includes the Malvern, AR micropolitan area, part of the Hot Springs-Malvern, AR combined statistical area.

Bhagat Singh Koshyari, born on June 17, 1942, is an Indian politician. He serves as the governor of Maharashtra and acts as the governor of Goa. A veteran of the RSS, Koshyari worked as the national vice president of the BJP and was the party's first state president for Uttarakhand. He also served as the second chief minister of Uttarakhand from 2001 to 2002. After that, he was the leader of the opposition in the Uttarakhand legislative assembly from 2002 to 2003. Koshyari was also an MLC in the Uttar Pradesh legislative council (when Uttarakhand was part of the larger Uttar Pradesh) and an MLA in the Uttarakhand legislative assembly. Later, he served as an MP in the Rajya Sabha from 2008 to 2014 for Uttarakhand and then as an MP in the 16th Lok Sabha from the Nainital-Udhamsingh Nagar constituency. This made him unique as he served in both houses of the state legislature and both houses of the national parliament.

Arnaldo Pagliarini, known as Arnie Lerma, was born on November 18, 1950, and passed away on March 16, 2018. He was an American writer and activist. Lerma used to be a Scientologist but later criticized the organization. He appeared in TV, media, and radio interviews. Lerma was the first to share an important court document called the Fishman Affidavit, including the Xenu story, on the internet through a Usenet newsgroup called alt.religion.science.

Silicon is a chemical element with the symbol Si and atomic number 14. It is hard, brittle, and has a blue-grey, shiny surface. It is a metalloid and a semiconductor, belonging to group 14 in the periodic table, just below carbon and above germanium, tin, and lead. Silicon is not very reactive. In 1823, Jöns Jakob Berzelius prepared and identified pure silicon. It forms oxides called silicates, and has the second-highest melting and boiling points among metalloids and nonmetals, after boron. Silicon is the eighth most common element in the universe. However, it is rarely found as pure silicon on Earth. Instead, it is found in minerals, rocks, and in space as silica or silicates. About 28% of the Earth's crust is made of silicate minerals, making it the second most abundant element after oxygen. Most silicon is used in its natural form without much processing. It is used in construction with clay, sand, and stone. Silicates are used in cement, concrete, and ceramics. Silicon compounds are used as abrasives and in high-strength ceramics. Silicon is crucial for modern technology, especially in semiconductors. Very pure silicon is used in transistors and chips in computers and cell phones. It is also used in steel making, aluminum casting, and making chemicals. Silicon is important in biology, though animals only need small amounts. Some sea sponges, microorganisms, and plants use silicon to build their structures.

The Hotchkiss School is a boys and girls school in Lakeville, Connecticut. It is part of the Eight Schools Association, the Ten Schools Admission Organization, and the G30 Schools Group.

Jimmy Eat World is an American rock band formed in 1993 in Mesa, Arizona. The band members are lead singer and guitarist Jim Adkins, rhythm guitarist and backup singer Tom Linton, bassist Rick Burch, and drummer Zach Lind. They have made ten studio albums. The current lineup has been together since 2001. Their biggest success came from the album "Bleed American" in 2001. Four songs from this album did well, with "The Middle" reaching number one on the Alternative Songs Chart. Their next album, "Futures" (2004), had "Pain" as its number one song. The "Bleed American" album was certified platinum by the RIAA, meaning it sold over a million copies. The "Futures" album was certified gold, selling over 500, 000 copies. Their sixth album, "Chase This Light" (2007), was their most successful, reaching number five on the Billboard 200 chart. Jimmy Eat World released their tenth album, "Surviving," in October 2019.

"All Quiet on the Western Front" is a novel by Erich Maria Remarque, a German soldier who fought in World War I. The book talks about how the German soldiers were very tired and stressed during the war. After the war, many of these soldiers felt distant from regular life. The book was first published in a German newspaper in November and December 1928. It came out as a book in January 1929. "All Quiet on the Western Front" and its sequel, "The Road Back," were among the books the Nazis banned in Germany. The book sold over 2.5 million copies in 22 languages in just 18 months. In 1930, it was made into a film, which won an Academy Award. Another film version came out in 1979, starring Richard Thomas and Ernest Borgnine.

Sinodelphys was an extinct mammal from the early Cretaceous period. It is the oldest known metatherian fossil, about 125 million years old. Scientists discovered and described it in 2003. The fossil was found in the Yixian Formation of Liaoning Province, China. The team included Zhe-xi Luo and John Wible.
The Loire department in France has 323 communes. As of 2020, these communes work together in the following intercommunalities.

Vincenzo "Enzo" Daniele Scifo, born on February 19, 1966, is a retired Belgian football midfielder. He is considered one of Belgium's greatest football players. He also managed the Belgium national under-21 team and several Belgian club teams. He played for clubs in Belgium, France, and Italy, winning multiple domestic titles. Internationally, he was part of the Belgian national team, playing in four FIFA World Cups. He was one of only three Belgian players to achieve this.
Peggy Webber was born on September 15, 1925. She is an American actress and writer. Peggy has worked in film, theater, television, and old-time radio. Now she is retired.

Kari Peter Conrad von Bagh (born August 29, 1943, died September 17, 2014) was a Finnish film historian and director. He worked as the head of the Finnish Film Archive and edited a magazine called "Filmihullu." Von Bagh also co-founded and directed the Midnight Sun Film Festival. Since 2001, he was the artistic director of the Film Festival in Bologna. Von Bagh was part of the jury at the 2004 Cannes Film Festival. Von Bagh directed films that were shown at important film festivals. In 2012, his works were showcased at the Rotterdam International Film Festival and the Festival Internacional de Cine Independente in Buenos Aires. In 2013, his films were shown at the Tromsø International Film Festival. Von Bagh produced about 40 non-fiction books mostly about cinema, and about 60 films for both cinemas and television. Some of his famous films include "Helsinki, Forever" (2008), "Sodankylä, Forever" (2010-2011, a documentary series), "Song of Finland" (a 2003-2004 television series and 2007 book), "Elokuvan historia" (History of Cinema, a 1975 radio series and 1998 book), and "Tähtien kirja" (The Book of Stars, 2006). He also wrote a book about Aki Kaurismäki that was translated into several languages. Von Bagh died in 2014 at the age of 71.
