Princeton, originally called Vermilion Forks, is a town in southern British Columbia, Canada, in the Similkameen region. It is located east of the Cascade Mountains, which continue south into Washington, Oregon, and California. The Tulameen and Similkameen rivers meet here. In 2016, the town's population was 2,828. Princeton has its main businesses on seven blocks of Bridge Street and five blocks on Vermilion Avenue. There are also businesses along British Columbia Highway 3. Historically, mining has been the main industry. Princeton has copper, gold, coal, and some platinum mines. The town's biggest employers are the Copper Mountain Mine and a sawmill owned by Weyerhaeuser, along with a few smaller timber companies like Princeton Wood Preservers and Princeton Post and Rail.

Ingvar Axel Harald Ericsson was born on August 31, 1927, and died on May 14, 2020. He was a Swedish runner who ran the 1500 meters. He took part in the 1952 and 1956 Summer Olympics. In 1952, he finished eighth. At the European Championships, he placed seventh in 1950 and fourth in 1954. Ericsson won the national 1500 meters title three times: in 1952, 1954, and 1955. He also set a new national record in 1956. His job was to be a firefighter.

A medical school teaches medicine and gives professional degrees to doctors and surgeons. It offers degrees like bachelor of medicine, bachelor of surgery, doctor of medicine, or doctor of osteopathic medicine. Some schools also provide other advanced degrees or programs. Medical schools can do medical research and run teaching hospitals. These schools have different rules, teaching methods, and programs. Getting in is tough; they use tests, grades, and leadership roles to pick students. In most countries, you study medicine as an undergraduate, meaning you don't need a specific background. But more schools are accepting graduates who finished another undergraduate degree. In the U.S. and Canada, almost all medical schools require several years of university study before entering. After graduating, you study for 5 or more years for an undergraduate degree or 4 years for a graduate degree before getting a medical degree. Many schools teach basic sciences and clinical skills from the start. Preclinical classes cover topics like biochemistry, genetics, pharmacology, and anatomy. Clinical rotations involve specialties such as internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, psychiatry, and obstetrics. Doctors need more than just a medical degree. They must pass tests, get background checks, and complete further training before they can practice medicine legally. Each country regulates medical schools, and the World Directory of Medical Schools lists them. This directory came from combining two other directories.
Domingo Nicolás Fuentes Zegarra was born on December 20, 1941, and died on October 28, 2015. He was a Peruvian football player who played as a left-back.

LeFlore is a town in LeFlore County, Oklahoma, United States. It is in the Fort Smith, Arkansas-Oklahoma metropolitan area. In 2010, the population was 190, up from 168 in 2000. Although the town is spelled "LeFlore" legally, the official name for the town and the postal address is just "LeFlore."

Wilbert Francisco Cobbs, born on June 16, 1934, is an American actor. He is famous for his roles in movies like "The Hitter" (1979) where he played Louisiana Slim, and "The Brother from Another Planet" (1984) where he acted as water. He also appeared as Lewis Coleman in the TV show "I'll Fly Away" from 1991 to 1993, and as Jack in "The Michael Richards Show" in 2000. He has also appeared as a guest in shows like "Walker, Texas Ranger" and "The Sopranos." In 2020, he won a Daytime Emmy Award for his performance in the daytime series "Dino Dana."

Freedom riders were activists who rode buses into the southern United States in 1961 and after to challenge segregation. They wanted to enforce court decisions from 1946 and 1960, which said segregation on buses was not allowed. In 1961, the first freedom ride began in Washington, D.C., on May 4th, and was supposed to reach New Orleans on May 17th. In 1960, the Boynton ruling said restaurants and waiting rooms in bus stations should be open to everyone. Before this, in 1955, the ICC said the "separate but equal" rule was wrong for interstate buses, but didn't enforce it. Freedom riders mixed different races on buses to challenge segregation laws. Their rides and the attacks on them showed how much people cared about civil rights. Police arrested riders for minor offenses but sometimes did nothing when white mobs attacked them. The Congress of Racial Equality (CORE) mostly organized the rides, with some help from the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee (SNCC). The rides followed other civil actions in the south, like sit-ins and boycotts. The Boynton ruling said people could ignore local segregation rules when traveling across state lines. Local and state police arrested freedom riders, and sometimes even helped violent groups attack them.

Christian Science is a belief system linked to members of the Church of Christ, Scientist. People who follow this belief are often called Christian Scientists or students of Christian Science, and the church is sometimes called the Christian Science Church. It began in the 19th century in New England with Mary Baker Eddy. In her 1875 book, "Science and Health," Eddy said sickness could be healed through prayer. This book became the church's main text, along with the Bible. By 2001, it had sold more than nine million copies. Eddy and 26 people got permission in 1879 to start the Church of Christ, Scientist. In 1894, they built the first Mother Church in Boston, Massachusetts. Christian Science grew quickly in the U.S., reaching nearly 270,000 members by 1936, but this number dropped to over 100,000 by 1990 and to less than 50,000 by 2009. The church makes a newspaper called "The Christian Science Monitor," which won seven Pulitzer Prizes from 1950 to 2002. They also run reading rooms worldwide. Eddy saw Christian Science as a return to early Christianity and its healing practices. Christian Science teaches that reality is spiritual, not material, and that the physical world is an illusion. They believe sickness is caused by wrong thoughts, not physical problems, and should be treated with prayer instead of medicine. The church doesn't ask its members to avoid all medical care. However, they think Christian Science prayer works best when not used with medicine. Critics say this can be dangerous, as several members and their children died between the 1880s and 1990s due to not receiving medical treatment.
wayne county is in the state of georgia, u.s. In 2010, it had 30,099 people. Jesup is the county seat. Wayne county includes the jesup, georgia micropolitan area.

Carovello National Park is a big park in Costa Rica. It is on the Osa Peninsula, in the southwest part of the country. The park was created in 1975. It is the largest national park in Costa Rica and covers a big part of the Osa Peninsula. People think it is one of the most important parks in the country because it has a lot of different types of plants and animals. National Geographic calls it "the most biologically intense place on earth in terms of biodiversity." The park is very popular with scientists who study tropical ecosystems. Visitors can see many animals there. Carovello National Park has the largest primary forest on the American Pacific coast and one of the last big areas of lowland tropical forests in the world. Logging used to happen in lowland areas because the trees there are easier to reach and bigger. But these areas are also important for biodiversity. With only about half of the original lowland forests left, the remaining areas are too small to support all the animals that need them. Larger animals, especially, need a lot of space without human activity. This means that even tourism, which is good for the economy, can threaten the park's long-term biodiversity. The waters in Carovello National Park are calm and rich in life. Cano Island Biological Reserve is one of the areas along the coast that are protected. These areas are important for humpback whales that come to breed and feed each winter. Ballena National Marine Park is specially designed for these whales. Other whales, like Bryde's whales, also visit the area. Spinner and rough-toothed dolphins, and smaller cetaceans like false killer and killer whales, live there too. People can go whale watching in these areas. Manatees, which were hunted in the past, are rare now, but can be seen occasionally at beaches like Manzanillo, Talamanca, and Limón.

Thomas Andrews, Jr., was born on February 7, 1873, and died on April 15, 1912. He was a businessman who worked in shipbuilding. Thomas Andrews was in charge of designing ships at a company called Harland and Wolff in Belfast, Ireland. In 1912, he was on a big ship called an ocean liner for its first trip across the Atlantic Ocean. The ship hit an iceberg and sank. Sri Lanka's S11 train is a diesel multiple-unit (DMU) train. It was made by Integral Coach Factory and bought through RITES Ltd. This company works for the Indian government. The S11 DMUs were bought to replace older locomotive-hauled trains. Twenty S11 DMUs were ordered to help with long-distance travel between Colombo and Matara.

Javier García Portillo, born on March 30, 1982, is a retired Spanish footballer who played as a forward. He began his career at Real Madrid but only played in 59 competitive games, scoring 17 goals. In La Liga, he also played for Gimnàstic, Osasuna, and Hércules, making 131 appearances and scoring 21 goals. He also played professionally in Italy and Belgium. During his 14-year senior career, he represented Hércules at all three major levels of Spanish football.

Gertrude Himmelfarb, also known as Bea Kristol, was an American historian who lived from August 8, 1922, to December 30, 2019. She led conservative ways of understanding history. She wrote a lot about how great ideas developed, especially focusing on Britain and the Victorian era. She also wrote about modern times and society.

Syed Mir Jafar Ali Khan Bahadur (– February 5, 1765) was a military leader who became the first nawab under the British East India Company. His rule began the British presence in India and played a crucial role in British control over a large part of India. Mir Jafar was the commander of the Bengali forces for Siraj Ud-Daulah, the nawab of Bengal. However, he betrayed Siraj during the Battle of Plassey in 1757 and took over as nawab after the British won. The British supported Mir Jafar until 1760 but later found out he had made a secret agreement with the Dutch in 1758. This led to a battle. In October 1760, the British forced him to give his position to Mir Qasim, his son-in-law, who was supposed to act as deputy subahdar. Mir Qasim had his own plans and wanted to get rid of the British. He was overthrown, and Mir Jafar was reinstated as nawab with the British support in 1763. However, Mir Qasim fought against the British and was defeated. Mir Jafar ruled until his death on February 5, 1765, and is buried in Jafarganj cemetery in Murshidabad, West Bengal. Mir Jafar is seen differently in history; some see him as a traitor, while others view him as a symbol of betrayal among Bengalis.

Chris Harris, born on December 14, 1942, and passed away on April 30, 2014, was an English actor, director, and writer. He was in several UK TV shows, such as "Into the Labyrinth" and "Hey Look That's Me." He also worked in pantomimes, playing the role of a pantomime dame. Additionally, he directed and wrote for theaters, including the Bristol Old Vic and the Theatre Royal, Bath. He lived in Portishead, in North Somerset.

Kate Harcourt, born on June 16, 1927, is a New Zealand actor. She is known professionally as Kate Harcourt. Kate hosted a radio show called "Listen with Mother" for young children. This led to her working on television, hosting a version of "Junior Magazine" in Wellington. Over her long career, she has acted in comedy and drama in theater, film, and television.

Aquarius is a constellation in the zodiac, between Capricornus and Pisces. It means "water-carrier" or "cup-carrier" in Latin. Its symbol is (Unicode ♒), which looks like water. Aquarius is one of the oldest constellations and was listed by Ptolemy in the 2nd century. It is still one of the 88 modern constellations. This constellation is part of a region called the sea, as it has many stars associated with water, like Cetus the whale, Pisces the fish, and Eridanus the river. Beta Aquarii, with an apparent magnitude of 2.9, is the brightest star in Aquarius.

Kareby is a small place in Kungälv municipality, in Västra Götarland county, Sweden. It had 292 people living there in 2010. Kareby has four sports teams. The women's team won the Swedish bandy championship in 2016.

A lifeguard watches over swimmers, surfers, and people doing water sports to keep them safe. They work in places like swimming pools, water parks, beaches, spas, rivers, and lakes. Lifeguards learn to swim and know first aid. They use different tools and equipment for rescuing people in the water, depending on where they work. In some places, lifeguards help with emergencies. In some communities, they are the main emergency help.

Nuclear espionage means giving state secrets about nuclear weapons to other countries without permission. Throughout the history of nuclear weapons, there have been known cases of nuclear espionage, as well as suspected cases. Because nuclear weapons are considered very important secrets, countries with nuclear weapons have strict rules against sharing information about how they are designed, how many they have, how they are delivered, and where they are stored. Countries are also limited in how much they can share about their nuclear weapons due to non-proliferation agreements.

The word "seneschal" can mean different things, all related to supervising or managing in history. Most often, a seneschal was a high-ranking official appointed by the king, duke, or noble in a royal, ducal, or noble household during the Middle Ages and early modern period. In a medieval royal household, the seneschal managed the home and servants, overseeing hundreds of workers and their tasks. This role gave the seneschal a lot of power in the community, especially since much of the local economy depended on such a household. In late medieval and early modern France, a seneschal was a royal officer in charge of justice and administration in certain southern regions called seneschalties. This position was similar to a northern French bailiff. In the United Kingdom, seneschal is a church term, referring to an official at a cathedral.
Lütschental is a village and a municipality in the Interlaken-Oberhasli area, which is in the canton of Bern, Switzerland.

The battle happened on September 24, 1877, in Kagoshima, Japan. It was the last fight of the Satsuma Rebellion. Saigō Takamori led samurai who were much fewer in number against troops from the Imperial Japanese Army. The army was commanded by generals Yamagata Aritomo and Kawamura Sumiyoshi. Saigō's army was completely destroyed, and Saigō died. This ended the Satsuma Rebellion. The Imperial Army's win made their power stronger, and there would be no more internal fighting.

Jenna Bush Hager, born on November 25, 1981, is an American news personality, author, and journalist. She co-hosts "Today with Hoda & Jenna," part of NBC's morning news program "Today," starting in the fourth hour. Jenna and her twin sister Barbara are the children of former U.S. President George W. Bush and former First Lady Laura Bush. They are the first and only twin children of a U.S. president. After her father's presidency, Jenna became an author and worked for NBC, including as a correspondent and contributor on "The Today Show."

Fakenham is a market town and civil parish in Norfolk, England. It is located near the River Wensum, about northwest of Norwich. The town is at the intersection of several local roads, including the A148 from King's Lynn to Cromer, the A1067 to Norwich, and the A1065 to Swaffham. The civil parish covers an area of about and had a population of 7,357 in 3,292 households in the 2001 census, with the population growing to 7,617 by the 2011 census. For local government purposes, Fakenham is part of the North Norfolk district. Fakenham has been a market town since 1250, especially famous for trading corn, barley, and wheat. In the 19th century, it became known for printing. Fakenham Racecourse, a thoroughbred horse racing venue to the south of the town, has Prince Charles as its patron. Fakenham's long name, "Fakenham Lancaster," comes from the ownership of the manor in 1377 passing to John of Gaunt, the Duke of Lancaster. This name is still used today, appearing on history trail plaques around the town. The two wards for electing councillors to the North Norfolk District Council are called Lancaster North and Lancaster South.

Hartselle is the second biggest city in Morgan County, Alabama, United States. It is located south of Decatur. Hartselle is part of the Decatur metropolitan area and the Huntsville-Decatur combined statistical area. In 2010, the city's population was 14,255. Hartselle was founded in 1870 when the South and North Alabama Railroad came. The city is named after George Hartsell, one of the railroad owners. The post office opened in 1873, and the city became officially incorporated on March 1, 1875. Many old buildings were destroyed in a big fire in 1916.

Western romance languages are part of a group based on the La Spezia–Rimini line. They include Gallo-Romance and Iberian-Romance branches, along with Northern Italian. These languages use "s" for plurals, have some weakened consonants, and pronounce "soft c" as /t͡s/ or /s/, unlike in Italian and Romanian. However, Italian and French are more similar than French and Spanish, and Italian and Spanish dialects share more similarities in terms of words, writing, and sounds than Italian and French. According to Dalby, twelve languages fit into this group: Portuguese, Spanish, Asturian-Leonese, Aragonese, Catalan, Galician, Gascon, Provencal, Gallo-Wallon, French, Franco-Provencal, Romansh, and Ladin. This classification is problematic because Italo-Romance and Iberian languages are more easily understood by each other than by Gallo-Romance languages. Some groups include Italo-Dalmatian, making a clade called Italo-Western Romance, while others place Italo-Dalmatian with Eastern Romance. Sardinian is different and may have separated before Western or Eastern Romance. Today, the four most widely used Western romance languages are Spanish (about 410 million native speakers, around 125 million second-language speakers), Portuguese (about 220 million native, another 45 million second-language speakers, mainly in African countries that speak Portuguese), French (about 80 million native, another 70 million second-language speakers, mostly in African countries that speak French), and Catalan (about 7.2 million native). Many of these languages are spoken by non-native speakers, especially French, which is widely used in West Africa as a common language.

Cleaner shrimp are a type of swimming crab that help other sea creatures. They belong to three families: Hippolytidae, which includes the Pacific cleaner shrimp; Palaemonidae, which includes the spotted shrimp; and Stenopodidae, which includes the banded coral shrimp. Cleaner shrimp are called so because they clean fish of parasites. The fish get rid of parasites, and the shrimp eat the parasites. They also clean the wounds of injured fish, helping them heal faster. This cleaning makes the fish less stressed. At cleaning stations in coral reefs, groups of cleaner shrimp gather. Some species, like Urocaridella, live in caves and don't usually clean fish. However, when fish come near, these shrimp do a dance to attract them. At night, shrimp like Urocaridella antonbruunii clean sleeping fish to avoid competition. Cleaner shrimp are kept in home aquariums for their cleaning ability and colorful appearance.

Mount Vernon is a city in Posey County, Indiana, United States. It is in the southwest corner of the state. It is the westernmost city in Indiana. The southernmost point in the state is Rockport, which is near the Ohio River. Mount Vernon had 6,687 people in 2010. The city is in Black Township and is part of the Evansville metropolitan area, which had 358,676 people in 2010.

Runa Laila, born on November 17, 1952, is a well-known Bangladeshi playback singer and composer. She started her career in the Pakistan film industry in the late 1960s. Runa's singing style is inspired by Pakistani singer Ahmed Rushdi. She replaced Mala and later paired with Rushdi. Runa's voice can be heard in films like "The Rain" (1976), "Jadur Banshi" (1977), "Accident" (1989), "Ontore Ontore" (1994), "Devdas" (2013), and "Priya Tumi Shukhi Hou" (2014). For her work in these films, she won seven Bangladesh National Film Awards for best female playback singer. Additionally, she won a best music composer award for the film "Ekti Cinemar Golpo" (2018).

Cebuano, also known as Bisaya or Binisaya, is a language spoken in southern Philippines, mainly in Central Visayas, Western Eastern Visayas, and most of Mindanao. It comes from the island of Cebu and is used by Visayan groups like Cebuanos. In the 1950s to the 1980s, it had the most native speakers among Philippine languages. It is the most widely spoken Visayan language and one of the main Philippine languages. Its name comes from the island of Cebu, where it originated. In Central Visayas, Cebuano is a common language, and it is also used in parts of Palawan and Mindanao. It is the primary language in some areas of Western Leyte, such as Ormoc and nearby towns. People there often call it by local names like "Ormocanon" or "Albuerahanon." Cebuano uses the ISO code CEB and is spelled as Sebwano by the Komisyon ng Wikang Filipino. It is one of five main groups of Visayan languages, including dialects like Boholano.

ʿilm al-kalām, usually shortened to kalām, is about studying Islamic beliefs. It was created to explain and protect these beliefs against those who doubt them. Scholars who study this are called mutakallimūn. Kalām means "speech" in Arabic, and it refers to talking about God's word as mentioned in the Quran. Mutahhari says kalām is about discussing and defending important Islamic beliefs. One reason for its name could be that it debates whether God's word in the Quran is part of His nature and not created, or if it is like normal speech and created.

Eden Sonja Jane Riegel, born on January 1, 1981, is an American actress and dialogue director. She played Bianca Montgomery in the daytime drama "All My Children." Bianca became famous as a gay icon and a popular character. Eden was nominated many times for her role. She won a Daytime Emmy Award for Bianca in 2005. Besides "All My Children," Eden appeared in other TV shows and films. She also played a character named Eden in the web series "Imaginary Bitches." Eden acted as Heather Stevens on "The Young and the Restless" from April 2010 to November 2011. Additionally, she works as the voice director for Disney's animated TV series "Amphibia" and "The Owl House."

Dhayam is a 2017 Tamil thriller film made in India. Kannan Rangaswamy wrote and directed it, and A. R. S. Sunder produced it. The entire film was shot inside one room. Santhosh Prathap, Jayakumar, Aanchal Singh, Sandhu Samaira, and Iraa Agarwal starred in the film. Sathish Selvam composed the music, A. Packiaraj handled the cinematography, and R. Sudharsan did the editing. It was first shown in theaters on March 24, 2017.

Mystery Science Theater 3000 (MST3K) is an American comedy TV show created by Joel Hodgson. It was produced by Alternaversal Productions, LLC. The show first aired on KTMA-TV in Minneapolis, Minnesota, on November 24, 1988. It ran for seven seasons on The Comedy Channel/Comedy Central until 1996. Later, it was shown on The Sci-Fi Channel for three seasons until 1999. A 60-episode package called "The Mystery Science Theater Hour" was produced in 1993 and aired in 1995. In 2015, Hodgson led a crowd-funded revival with 14 episodes in its eleventh season, first released on Netflix in 2017. Another six-episode season followed in 2018. The show has 217 episodes and two live tours. The story follows Joel Robinson, a janitor, who is trapped by two mad scientists on the "Satellite of Love." Joel watches bad movies and uses his invention, a robot named Tom Servo, to keep him company. Tom, along with Crow T. Robot and Gypsy, makes fun of the movies as they play. Each episode features a single movie, often shortened, with Joel, Tom, and Crow watching in silhouettes from the bottom of the screen. The show had a new cast, including Mike Nelson, Trace Beaulieu, and Josh Weinstein. The 2017 revival has a new cast, including Jonah Ray as the new character Jonah Heston and Patton Oswalt as one of the mad scientists. This revival also features Baron Vaughn, Hampton Yount, and Rebecca Hanson voicing Tom Servo, Crow T. Robot, and Gypsy, respectively. Originally, the show didn't get many viewers. However, its popularity grew through online fan communities, repeats, and home media. The show was named one of the best TV shows of all time by Time magazine in 2007 and one of the top cult TV shows by TV Guide. MST3K won a Peabody Award in 1993 and was nominated for two Emmy Awards. It was influential in social television and inspired similar projects. The show also brought attention to some forgotten bad movies.

Sir David Tang, born on August 2, 1954, and passed away on August 29, 2017, was a businessman, philanthropist, and socialite from Hong Kong. He is famous for starting Shanghai Tang, a fashion chain in 1994. He sold it to Richemont in 1998.

Seminole County is in Oklahoma, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 25, 482 people. The county seat is Wewoka. Most of the county is part of the Seminole Nation reservation, while a small part in the east belongs to the Muscogee (Creek) Nation. Seminole County is known for the Greater Seminole Field, one of the most important oil fields. It still produces oil and extends into nearby counties. When oil was first discovered, many workers and people came to the county. The population almost tripled. As oil production decreased later, people and jobs left the area.

Granzymes are enzymes that kill cells. They are found in special cells called cytotoxic T cells and natural killer cells. Granzymes help get rid of cells that are cancerous or infected by viruses or bacteria. They can also kill bacteria and stop viruses from copying themselves. Granzymes are stored in small parts of the cell called cytotoxic granules, along with another substance called perforin. When these cells attack a target cell, the granzymes enter the target cell. Perforin helps granzymes get inside. Granzymes are a type of enzyme family. They are similar to other enzymes produced by immune cells, like neutrophil elastase and cathepsin G. Granzyme B, a specific type of granzyme, triggers cell death by activating caspases, especially caspase-3. This cuts many proteins, including caspase-activated DNase, to start cell death. Granzyme B also cuts proteins like Bid, which bring other proteins to the mitochondria, making the cell membrane leaky. This releases cytochrome c and other proteins that activate caspase-9 and suppress inhibitor proteins. Granzymes can kill both cells and intracellular pathogens. Granzyme B cuts parts of bacteria's electron transport chain, causing damage. It also cuts viral proteins to stop viruses from copying. Granzymes A and B can also cut DNA and RNA, affecting proteins that bind to these molecules. Granzymes are not just in T cells. They can also be found in dendritic cells, B cells, and mast cells. In some non-immune cells like keratinocytes, pneumocytes, and chondrocytes, granzymes are expressed. These cells do not always have perforin or form immunological synapses, so granzyme B can be released outside the cell. In diseases with chronic inflammation, granzyme B outside the cell can damage the extracellular matrix, affecting tissue healing and repair. This has been linked to problems like atherosclerosis, aneurysms, and skin aging.

The East Midlands is one of nine official regions in England. It includes Derbyshire, Leicestershire, Lincolnshire (excluding North and North East Lincolnshire), Northamptonshire, Nottinghamshire, and Rutland. The region covers an area and had more than 4.5 million people in 2011. The main urban centers are Derby, Leicester, Lincoln, Mansfield, Northampton, and Nottingham. Other towns include Boston, Chesterfield, Corby, Grantham, Hinckley, Kettering, Loughborough, Newark-on-Trent, Skegness, Wellingborough, and Worksop. Its location near London and being on major roads helps the East Midlands to be a strong economic area. Nottingham and Leicester are known as sufficient-level world cities. The main airport is East Midlands Airport, located between Derby, Loughborough, and Nottingham.

Muskmelon, also known as "cucumis melo," is a type of melon that has been grown into many different varieties. These include smooth-skinned ones like honeydew, crenshaw, and casaba, and different netted ones such as cantaloupe, Persian melon, and Christmas melon. There are many cultivated types in this species, similar to wild cabbage, although the differences are not as many. It belongs to a fruit type called pepo. The origin of muskmelons is unknown. Researchers found that seeds and rootstocks were traded along ancient caravan routes. Some scientists think muskmelons came from the Levant and Egypt, while others believe they originated in India or Central Asia. Some researchers even suggest an African origin, and today, wild muskmelons can still be found in some African countries.
Elitserien is the top division for men's volleyball in Sweden. It usually happens in late February or early March. After that, there is a Swedish national championship playoff.

John Walton was an Australian actor born in 1952 in St. Ives, Sydney. He acted on stage, television, and in films. He is best known for his role in the TV show "The Young Doctors." He passed away on July 17, 2014.

Northern California is the top part of California in the U.S. It covers 48 counties in the north. The main cities are San Jose, San Francisco, Oakland, Sacramento, and Fresno. There are forests with redwood trees and mountains like the Sierra Nevada. Yosemite Valley and Lake Tahoe are popular places here. The central valley, a big area for farming, is also part of northern California. The area includes cities like Fresno and Sacramento and parts of the San Francisco Bay Area. Another important area is Lake Tahoe and Reno. The first people to live there were Native Americans about 19, 000 years ago. Spanish settlers arrived in the 1770s, starting with a mission in Monterey.

M'sila is a province in northern Algeria. It has about 1 million people and covers an area of 18,718 square kilometers. The capital, also named M'sila, has around 100,000 inhabitants and is home to M'sila University. Some local places include Bou Saada and Maadid. There's a salt lake called Chott el Hodna nearby. Most of the area is semi-arid and not well developed. M'sila is known for farming. It was also the place for a government project that turned nomadic Algerians into settled villagers using local materials. This project, now finished, is called Maader and includes houses, public areas, trading spots, and a mosque.

Dominique Baudis was a French defender of rights, also known as an ombudsman. He was born on April 14, 1947, and passed away on April 10, 2014. Before his role as an ombudsman, he was a journalist and a politician. He also served as the mayor of Toulouse. Later, he became a member of DL and then joined the leading centre-right party, Union for a Popular Movement.

The Hawthorn football club, nicknamed the Hawks, is a professional Australian rules football team in the Australian Football League (AFL). Founded in 1902, it is one of the younger Victorian-based AFL teams and has won thirteen premierships. It is the only club to have won premierships in each decade from the 1960s to the 2010s. The Hawks play in brown and gold striped uniforms. The club's motto is "let us be judged by our acts." The Hawks started in Hawthorn, an area in Melbourne, and used to have a training base at Glenferrie Oval. Matches haven't been played there since 1973. In 2006, the club moved its training and administrative facilities to Waverly Park, which is 21 km from the city center and closer to its main supporters. Since 2007, the Hawks have played four games a year at York Park in Launceston, Tasmania, and the rest at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Hawthorn's current VFL affiliate team is the Box Hill Hawks.
